# Support matrix

This file is the authoritative statement of what CloudBurrow supports.

**Three separate things are tracked separately**, because conflating them is how a tool
over-promises:

| Dimension | Question | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **GCP API compatibility** | Does an official Google SDK call behave correctly? | §Services below |
| **Native Kubernetes portability** | Do ordinary manifests, Helm charts and operators work? | §Native Kubernetes |
| **Knative feature coverage** | Which Cloud Run v2 behaviors does the adapter actually map? | §Cloud Run |

A component being adopted from upstream does not make its operations supported. **Upstream
behavior still has to be demonstrated through an official SDK** before it is promoted here. It is not a roadmap
and not an aspiration. If an operation is not listed as `Verified` here, CloudBurrow does not
support it, regardless of what any other document, README, or commit message says.

## Status values

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Planned` | Not implemented. May return `UNIMPLEMENTED`, or may not be routed at all. |
| `Partial` | Implemented with documented gaps. The gap is named in the Notes column; an unexplained `Partial` is a documentation bug. |
| `Verified` | Implemented **and** exercised by a merged test that drives it through an official Google client library. |
| `UNVERIFIED` (an error code) | The call is Verified, but an error code the test asserts is one **Google does not document**. It is implemented as the most plausible code and marked `// unverified:` in the test, so [docs/coverage](coverage/README.md) lists it and a row that relies on it says `(error code UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/status-codes>))`. It stays so until a recorded observation pins it; see [test/compat/README.md](../test/compat/README.md#unverified-error-codes). |

**The promotion rule.** An operation moves off `Planned` only in a PR that adds a test using
an official Google SDK — `cloud.google.com/go/...`, `google-cloud-*` for Python, and so on.
A curl invocation, a handwritten HTTP request, or an internal unit test is not sufficient
evidence, because those test our understanding of the API rather than the client's.

**Control plane vs data plane.** These are tracked separately because they fail
independently, and conflating them is the standard way an emulator overstates itself.
Creating a Cloud Run service and receiving a well-formed `Service` response says nothing
about whether a container ran. A service is described as supported only when both columns are
`Verified`.

**Backing component** is recorded per service, from the
[upstream reuse audit](upstream-evaluation.md). Inherited limitations are listed with the
service — an upstream gap is still our gap as far as a user is concerned.

**Verified** rows below are backed by `test/compat`, run against a live `cloudburrow up` on
2026-09-20. Everything else remains `Planned`: exercised-by-hand is not evidence, and an
operation a test merely touches in cleanup is not asserted.

### What CI does not run, and why

Every merge runs `test/compat` against a live instance. A test that skips there is not evidence,
so each one that still skips is listed here with its reason (#346). The acceptance workflow
(`test/e2e`) and `test/k8s` run too, on an instance of their own (the
`official SDK compatibility (acceptance)` job), and none of them may skip: the job fails unless
every one passes (#596).

| Tests | Why they skip in the main compat run |
|---|---|
| `TestDatastoreAcrossRestart`, `TestFirestoreAcrossRestart`, `TestMemorystoreAcrossRestart`, `TestCloudSQLMySQLAcrossRestart`, `TestCloudSQLAcrossRestart`, `TestKMSAcrossRestart`, `TestSecretManagerAcrossRestart`, `TestTasksAcrossRestart`, `TestSchedulerAcrossRestart`, `TestStorageAcrossRestart` | They read what an earlier process wrote. They run, and must pass twice each, in CI's restart probe after `stop`/`up` (persistent mode) and `up --mode ephemeral`, each in the shard that serves it; `TestStorageAcrossRestart` is its own setup too, against the in-cluster server through the instance's tunnel, so it must pass three times (#596), and at setup it also creates a notificationConfig the later runs require present, then absent (#701). `TestCloudSQLAcrossRestart` reads a row `TestCloudSQLRestartSetup` writes alone just before `stop` (#701), and `TestFirestoreAcrossRestart` the documents and named database `TestFirestoreRestartSetup` does (#1636). |
| `TestGenerateContentThroughTheOfficialSDK`, `TestStreamGenerateContentThroughTheOfficialSDK`, `TestGenerationNeverUsesApplicationDefaultCredentials`, `TestStreamGenerateContentThroughThePredictionClient` | Local AI needs a 2.59 GB model download and minutes of CPU inference. The decision is that it does not run in per-PR CI. The Local AI and Vertex AI generation rows come from runs on a developer machine, dated in [generation.md](generation.md) (2026-09-21) and [local-ai.md](local-ai.md). They and the Functions and source-build rows backed by the tests below (`TestFunctionsFrameworkBuiltWithBuildpacks`, `TestFunctionsRebuildReusesLayers`, `TestFunctionsBuildBrokenModulePathFails` and the six language tests) are the only Verified rows whose evidence is not re-run on every merge. |
| `TestFunctionsFrameworkBuiltWithBuildpacks` | It pulls Google's builder and run images and runs two Buildpacks builds, which take minutes, so it is too slow for every merge while runners are the bottleneck; it is in no CI shard and does not run on merges. It runs only with `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_FUNCTIONS=1` against an instance whose cluster nodes are amd64 (the builder's only platform), and needs `pack` and Docker. It runs on demand in [`functions.yml`](../.github/workflows/functions.yml) (Functions build, `workflow_dispatch` only), on an amd64 runner with the run shard's instance and the pinned `pack`, and fails if any selected test skips. **Dated run: passed on 2026-09-27, [run 36357529139](https://github.com/cloudburrow/cloudburrow/actions/runs/36357529139) of `functions.yml` on main, `ubuntu-latest` amd64 runner, pack 0.40.9** (136s; it built `Hello` (`http`) in 58s and `Event` (`cloudevent`) in 39s). That run is the evidence for the Verified Functions Framework and source-build rows; the workflow is dispatch-only, so nothing re-runs it on merge. |
| `TestFunctionsRebuildReusesLayers`, `TestFunctionsBuildBrokenModulePathFails` | Same reason: they pull Google's builder and run Buildpacks builds (the first builds the fixture twice), which take minutes; they are in no CI shard and do not run on merges. `functions.yml` runs them on demand with the test above. They run only with `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_FUNCTIONS=1` and need `pack` and Docker, but no cluster: they build into a local registry and run nothing. **Dated run: both passed on 2026-09-27, macOS/arm64 Docker Desktop, emulated amd64 builder, pack 0.40.9** (first build 1m48s, rebuild 1m32s reusing 6 layers; the broken-module test 50s). **Both passed again on 2026-09-27, [run 36357529139](https://github.com/cloudburrow/cloudburrow/actions/runs/36357529139) of `functions.yml` on main, `ubuntu-latest` amd64 runner, pack 0.40.9**, natively (the rebuild test 74s: first build 38s, rebuild 35s reusing 6 layers; the broken-module test 17s). Those two runs are the evidence for the Verified cache-reuse and failed-build rows; the workflow is dispatch-only, so nothing re-runs them on merge. |
| `TestFunctionsNodejsBuiltWithBuildpacks`, `TestFunctionsPythonBuiltWithBuildpacks`, `TestFunctionsJavaBuiltWithBuildpacks`, `TestFunctionsRubyBuiltWithBuildpacks`, `TestFunctionsPHPBuiltWithBuildpacks`, `TestFunctionsDotnetBuiltWithBuildpacks` | Same reason as `TestFunctionsFrameworkBuiltWithBuildpacks` (#1303, #1319): each builds its fixture (`testdata/function-nodejs`, `-python`, `-java`, `-ruby`, `-php`, `-dotnet`) twice, one image per signature, with the pinned Google builder, which pulls the builder, run images and the language runtime, and deploys both images through the official Cloud Run v2 client, so it needs `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_FUNCTIONS=1`, `pack`, Docker and amd64 cluster nodes. They are in no CI shard and do not run on merges; `functions.yml` runs them on demand with the others. A PHP function is built with Google's PHP functions builder, which `internal/buildpacks` picks for it: the general builder has no PHP Functions Framework buildpack (#1319). **Dated run: all six passed on 2026-10-15, [run 38805202491](https://github.com/cloudburrow/cloudburrow/actions/runs/38805202491) of `functions.yml` on `fix/1319-php-function`, `ubuntu-24.04` amd64 runner, pack 0.40.9** (with the four tests above: ten passed). That run is the evidence for the Verified Node.js, Python, Java, Ruby, PHP and .NET functions rows; the workflow is dispatch-only, so nothing re-runs them on merge. |

#### Retried once

CI retries seven tests once, and no others (#566). When `go test` fails in a compat shard or in
the restart probe and every test it names as failed is on this list, those tests are re-run once,
by name, with the same environment, and the run fails if a retry fails too. A failure of any
other test fails at once, and so does a package-level failure that names no test (#675). A pass
on the second attempt counts as a pass, so the rows that cite these tests say that their evidence
tolerates one retry. Every retry is a `::warning::` annotation on the run page and a line of the
job summary with its outcome (#704).

| Retried test | Where CI runs it | Evidence for |
|---|---|---|
| `TestHostEndpointSurvivesABackendRestart` | Compat shard | Advertised host port after a pod restart |
| `TestMemorystoreAcrossRestart` | Restart probe | Memorystore durability |
| `TestDatastoreAcrossRestart` | Restart probe | Datastore keeps its data in persistent mode |
| `TestDatastoreSurvivesAPodRestart` | Compat shard | Datastore keeps its data in persistent mode |
| `TestFirestoreSurvivesAPodRestart` | Compat shard | Firestore keeps its documents in persistent mode (#1615) |
| `TestFirestoreAfterTheEmulatorIsKilled` | Compat shard | Firestore keeps its documents across an emulator crash (#1615) |
| `TestSpannerStateDoesNotSurviveARestart` | Compat shard | Spanner state does not survive a restart |

**Removal rule.** An entry is taken off the list once 20 consecutive CI runs on `main` have
passed with no retry of it, counted from the annotations. A test is added only together with a
row in this table: `TestRetryAllowListMatchesTheDocs` (`test/repo`) fails when this table and the
allow-list in `.github/scripts/retry-flaky.sh` differ.

## Native Kubernetes portability

Tested by #29, independently of any GCP API. A cluster that answers GCP calls is not
automatically a cluster your manifests run on, so this is never inferred from the sections
below. CI runs `test/k8s` on every merge, and fails if any of it skips (#596).

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `kubectl apply` of ordinary manifests | **Verified** | `test/k8s`: Namespace, ConfigMap, Secret, multi-replica Deployment and Service applied directly, with `readyReplicas` asserted. Tests: `TestOrdinaryManifestsApply`. |
| Helm chart install | **Verified** | `TestHelmChartInstalls` installs a chart and asserts the release reports `deployed`. |
| Custom resources and operators | **Verified** | `TestCustomResourceDefinition` establishes a CRD and reads back a custom resource — the operator pattern. |
| PersistentVolumeClaims | **Verified** | `TestPersistentVolumeClaimBindsAndPersists` writes from one pod and reads from **another**, which is what proves the volume persisted rather than the data living in one container. |
| Jobs | **Verified** | Used by the PVC test; `batch/v1` Jobs run to completion. Tests: `TestPersistentVolumeClaimBindsAndPersists`. |
| **Unmodified GKE manifests** | **Not promised** | Endpoint configuration and local overlays legitimately differ. No universal claim is made, and nothing here tests a GKE-specific API. |

## REST system parameters (#1954)

Google's standard system parameters (<https://docs.cloud.google.com/apis/docs/system-parameters>) are implemented once, in `internal/sysparams`. The shared transcoder (`internal/transport/rest`) applies them to every transcoded API (Cloud KMS, Cloud Run, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Logging, Eventarc, Vertex AI, Cloud Build, Cloud Functions, Resource Manager, Memorystore, Kubernetes Engine and the rest). It checks a mask against the method's response message, through the discovery overlay where there is one. The hand-written JSON fronts get them from `sysparams.Wrap`: Secret Manager, Resource Manager's hand-written routes, Cloud SQL Admin, Backup and DR, API Keys, Service Usage, Vertex AI's JSON routes, the Compute Engine API (whose errors already carry `errors[]`), the Cloud Storage companion APIs (Batch Operations, Insights, Transfer), the Bigtable admin, Pub/Sub and emulator fronts, and BigQuery. Cloud Storage's JSON API formats its own answers with the same parser and pruner. Every gRPC server built by `internal/grpchttp` applies `x-goog-fieldmask`.

| Parameter | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `fields`, `$fields`, `X-Goog-FieldMask` | **Verified** | The documented partial-response grammar: `a,b`; `a/b`; `a(b,c)`, nested to any depth; `*`; and the FieldMask form `a.b`. A selection under an array applies to each element (`items(id,name)`). Lists and long-running operations are pruned like any other response; an Any's `@type` is kept, and any selection inside an Any is accepted. The query wins over the header. A malformed mask, or one naming a field the response does not have (on transcoded APIs and over gRPC), is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT `Invalid field selection <path>`, Google's documented answer (<https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/how-tos/performance#partial-response>). The hand-written fronts have no response schema, so they refuse only malformed masks and drop names they do not know. Tests: `TestSystemParametersKMS`, `TestSystemParametersSecretManager`, `TestSystemParametersCloudRun`, `TestSystemParametersStorage`, `TestSystemParametersBigQuery` (the discovery clients' `.Fields(...)`, raw HTTP), and the unit tests `TestParse`, `TestPrune`, `TestValidateAndPruneProto` and `TestSystemParameters`. |
| `x-goog-fieldmask` (gRPC metadata) | **Verified** | Prunes a unary answer and each message of a stream, on a clone, so the server never sees its own message pruned. A bad mask is INVALID_ARGUMENT, as over REST. The raw-codec proxies to the emulators (Pub/Sub, Bigtable, Firestore, Datastore, Spanner) pass their gRPC answers through unpruned, because they never decode them. Tests: `TestSystemParametersKMS` and `TestSystemParametersSecretManager` (official gRPC clients), `TestInterceptors`. |
| `alt=json`, `alt=proto` | **Verified** | `alt=proto` on a transcoded method returns the binary response message, pruned to the mask, as `application/x-protobuf`. An error under `alt=proto` is the binary `google.rpc.Status` with the HTTP status; Google's error body for `alt=proto` is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-19: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/apis/docs/system-parameters>). `$alt=json;enum-encoding=int` writes enums as numbers. Any other value is 400. Tests: `TestSystemParametersKMS` (decoded with `kmspb.KeyRing`), `TestSystemParameters`. |
| `alt=media`, `alt=sse` | **Partial** | `alt=media` is served where a method has media: Cloud Storage downloads. No transcoded method has media or a JSON stream, so on those methods both values are 501 UNIMPLEMENTED. Hand-written fronts pass both values through to their own handlers (Vertex AI's `streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`). |
| `prettyPrint`, `$prettyPrint` | **Verified** | `true` indents and `false` compacts. Without the parameter, Google indents; CloudBurrow writes the handler's own formatting, which is the same JSON (compact for transcoded APIs, indented for Cloud Storage). Values other than `true`, `false`, `1` and `0` are 400. Tests: `TestSystemParametersKMS` and `TestSystemParametersStorage` (`prettyPrint=false`), `TestSystemParameters` and `TestWrap` (`true`). |
| `$.xgafv` | **Verified** | `2` (the default) is the AIP-193 envelope `{"error":{"code","message","status","details"}}`. `1` adds the legacy `errors[]` list of `{message, domain: "global", reason}`. The exact v1 shape is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-19: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/apis/docs/system-parameters>, which says only that 1 is for the client libraries). Cloud Storage's and BigQuery's errors already carry `errors[]`. Any other value is 400. Tests: `TestSystemParametersKMS`, `TestSystemParameters`, `TestWrap`. |
| `callback`, `$callback` (JSONP) | **Verified** | The answer, success or error, becomes `// API callback\n<name>(<json>);` as `text/javascript`. A name that is not a JavaScript identifier path is 400. Tests: `TestSystemParametersKMS`, `TestSystemParametersStorage`. |
| `$outputDefaults` | **Verified** | On transcoded APIs, writes fields at their defaults. Tests: `TestSystemParameters`. |
| `quotaUser`, `userIp`, `key`, `$key`, `$userProject`, `access_token`, `oauth_token`, `$unique`, `uploadType`, `upload_protocol` | **Verified** | Accepted and ignored, since CloudBurrow meters, bills and caches nothing. Credentials are read from the `Authorization` header. Tests: `TestSystemParametersKMS` (quotaUser, userIp), `TestQueryBinding`. |

## Cloud Storage — JSON API v1

**Backing component:** CloudBurrow's own server (`internal/service/storage`, #485), built to
Google's documentation and the storage v1 discovery document, which it embeds: every method of
that document is either served or answers **501 `notImplemented` naming it**. It is the only
Cloud Storage backend (#519). `up` runs it as one Deployment, from an image built locally from
the binary embedded in the CLI (#514); `cloudburrow storage-server` runs it with no cluster.
Contract: Cloud Storage JSON API v1, and the XML API subset below.
Client endpoint override: `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST` (Go, Python; see architecture §4.2). The Node
client needs `apiEndpoint` instead (see [Node.js client libraries](#nodejs-client-libraries)).

The per-method status is generated from the server's own method table in
[docs/coverage/storage.md](coverage/storage.md): a method is **Verified** when an official-SDK
or real-tool compat test annotated for it passes, **Implemented** when it is served but no such
test covers it, and **Unimplemented** when it answers 501. `TestCoverageMatchesCompatibility`
fails if a row below disagrees with that report. The official Go client retries every 5xx, 501
included, until its deadline, so an unimplemented method costs a client its timeout rather than
failing at once.

### Control plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `buckets.insert`, `buckets.get`, `buckets.delete` | **Verified** | `TestStorageBucketLifecycle`. A non-empty bucket delete is 409 (`TestStorageNonEmptyBucketDelete`; UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/status-codes>) for the JSON API). |
| `buckets.list` | **Verified** | `TestStorageBucketsList`; buckets are scoped by project. |
| `buckets.patch` | **Verified** | `TestStorageBucketPatchKeepsOmittedFields`, `TestBucketUpdateChangesMetadata`, `TestStorageBucketMetagenerationPreconditions`: a JSON merge patch, with omitted fields kept (#374). |
| `buckets.update` | **Verified** | A full replace: `TestStorageBucketsUpdateReplaces`, through Google's generated JSON API client (`google.golang.org/api/storage/v1`), since the Go client's `Update` is a patch. Labels and versioning the request omits are cleared, the location is kept, and a stale `ifMetagenerationMatch` is 412 (#691). |
| `buckets.lockRetentionPolicy` | **Verified** | `TestStorageLockRetentionPolicy`, `TestStorageLockRetentionPolicyTwice` (a repeat lock is refused, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-lock>); see Retention and holds). |
| `buckets.restore` | **Verified** | `TestStorageBucketsRestore`, through the generated JSON API client: the bucket returns by generation with its soft-deleted objects restorable; a live bucket of the same name is 409 and a generation that is not soft-deleted is 404 (both UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/buckets/restore>) against Google; #691). |
| `buckets.getStorageLayout` | **Verified** | `TestGcloudStorageParallelCompositeUpload`: gcloud reads it before a parallel composite upload. `rapidCacheInfo` (discovery revision 20261107): `cacheType` of the bucket's first Rapid Cache, by zone, that is not disabled, absent when it has none (unit `TestRapidCachesAndManagedFolderConfig`; which type a bucket with caches of both types reports is UNVERIFIED, docs re-read 2026-11-18). |
| `buckets.getIamPolicy`, `buckets.setIamPolicy`, `buckets.testIamPermissions` | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestStorageBucketIAMRoundTrip`, `TestStorageBucketIAMStaleEtag`, under [ADR-0006](adr/0006-iam-policy-surface.md) as amended by #504: a policy round-trips with its etag and version, and nothing is enforced. **IAM Conditions** (#1745, `TestStorageBucketIAMConditions`, the official client's `IAM().V3()` handle): a conditional binding is stored on a bucket with uniform bucket-level access (version 3, a version 1 read rendering `ROLE_withcond_HASH`) and refused 400 on one without it, as Google requires; uniform bucket-level access cannot then be disabled (refusal texts are CloudBurrow's, Google publishes none). From the console's Permissions tab: `TestConsolePermissionsOnABucket` (#793). |
| `projects.hmacKeys.create`, `projects.hmacKeys.get`, `projects.hmacKeys.update`, `projects.hmacKeys.delete`, `projects.hmacKeys.list`, `projects.serviceAccount.get` | **Verified** | `TestStorageHMACKeyLifecycle`, `TestStorageHMACKeyLimit`, `TestGcloudStorageHMAC` (#505). A key's secret is shown once, at creation. |
| `notifications.insert`, `notifications.get`, `notifications.list`, `notifications.delete` | **Verified** | `TestNotificationConfigsCRUDThroughTheSDK`; see the notifications section. |
| `managedFolders.insert`, `managedFolders.get`, `managedFolders.list`, `managedFolders.delete` | **Verified** | `TestStorageManagedFolderLifecycle`, through Google's generated JSON API client, since the official Go client has no managed folder call (#828). A name is returned ending in `/` (one sent without it has it added, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/managed-folders>)); the page's naming rules (read 2026-10-17) are enforced, 1-1024 bytes, no CR or LF, "At most, a managed folder name can have 15 `/`s", and names "cannot start with `.well-known/acme-challenge/`" (400, #1595; the status is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/managed-folders>)); a second insert is 409, an absent one 404; list takes `prefix`, `pageSize` and `pageToken`, the parameters the discovery document gives it (it has no delimiter); delete honours `ifMetagenerationMatch` (412 when stale) and refuses a managed folder with objects or managed folders under it unless `allowNonEmpty`, which keeps the objects (409, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/managed-folders>)). A bucket needs uniform bucket-level access to hold one (400, status UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/managed-folders>)), and a bucket that holds one cannot be deleted (409, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/managed-folders>)). Managed folders persist with the bucket's metadata: `TestStorageAcrossRestart` finds one, with its policy, after a persistent restart and none after an ephemeral one. gcloud's `managedFolders.list` on `storage rm -r` is `TestGcloudStorageClearLabels`. |
| `managedFolders.getIamPolicy`, `managedFolders.setIamPolicy`, `managedFolders.testIamPermissions` | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestStorageManagedFolderIAM`: kept on the managed folder as a bucket's is on its bucket, under [ADR-0006](adr/0006-iam-policy-surface.md) as amended by #504: a policy round-trips, leaves the bucket's alone, a stale etag is 412 and conditions are refused 400 (#1745: Google does not list managed folders among the resources that accept conditional role bindings; unit-tested); no object access consults it. Viewed and edited in the console on the managed folder's page (#847, `TestConsolePermissionsOnAManagedFolder`). The same methods on the Storage Control API (`StorageControlClient.GetIamPolicy`, `SetIamPolicy`, `TestIamPermissions` with a `managedFolders` resource) are gRPC on the v2 API, which CloudBurrow does not serve. |
| `managedFolders.update` | **Verified** | Patch semantics on `rapidCacheConfig`, its only settable field (#1505): a policy sent replaces that key's, a null one removes it, a null `rapidCacheConfig` clears them all; each key is its policy's `rapidCacheId`, a Rapid Cache of the bucket that is not disabled (else 400, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/managed-folders>)), `ingestOnWrite` `enabled` or `unspecified`. Bumps the metageneration and takes `ifMetagenerationMatch` and `ifMetagenerationNotMatch`. `insert` takes `rapidCacheConfig` too. Over gRPC, StorageControl's `CreateManagedFolder`, `GetManagedFolder`, `ListManagedFolders`, `DeleteManagedFolder` and `UpdateManagedFolder` (masks `rapid_cache_config`, `rapid_cache_config.policies` and `rapid_cache_config.policies.<key>`; a path within a policy is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, as documented). Stored, no effect: there is no cache tier. gcloud has no command that sets it, and hashicorp/google 8.4.0 no `rapid_cache_config`. Console: Edit managed folder on a managed folder's row (`TestStorageEditManagedFolderThroughTheConsole`, `TestStorageEditManagedFolderThroughTheBrowser`). `TestStorageRapidCachesJSON`, `TestStorageRapidCachesControl`. |
| `objects.insert`, `objects.get`, `objects.delete` | **Verified** | `TestStorageObjectRoundTrip`. |
| `objects.list` | **Verified** | `TestStorageListWithPrefix`: prefix **and** delimiter, with the synthetic `dir/sub/` prefix. `filter` on object contexts (`TestStorageObjectContexts`, both transports, and `TestGcloudStorageObjectContexts`, `gcloud storage objects list --metadata-filter`, #1345): the grammar Google documents (listing-objects#filter-by-object-contexts), `contexts."KEY":*`, `contexts."KEY"="VALUE"` and either negated by `NOT` or a leading `-`; prefixes are exempt. AND, OR, other fields and anything malformed are 400 `invalid` / `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, since Google documents no more (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/object-contexts>) against Google: whether it accepts more, and its exact message). |
| Object contexts | **Verified** | `TestStorageObjectContexts` (official Go client, `storage.NewGRPCClient` and the JSON client) and `TestGcloudStorageObjectContexts` (`gcloud storage objects update --custom-contexts`, `--update-custom-contexts`, `--remove-custom-contexts`, `--clear-custom-contexts`) (#1345). `contexts.custom` holds key, value, `createTime` and `updateTime`, set on an upload and returned by get and list on both APIs. A patch sets the keys it names; a key set to null, or to a payload with no value (the Go client's `Delete`), is deleted; `contexts` or `contexts.custom` null or empty clears them; an update replaces them; none makes a new generation, each a new metageneration. Keys and values are 1 to 256 bytes, begin with a letter or digit and hold no `'` `"` `\` `/`; `google:` keys are reserved; each refusal is 400 `invalid`. Copy, rewrite and compose transfer the source's contexts (a compose merges its sources', a later source winning a shared key: UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/object-contexts>)), body contexts override them, and `dropContextGroups=custom` drops them; another group is 400 (the discovery document's only accepted value is `custom`). Extended data (Preview) is attached only by Google's own services, under `google:` keys a client cannot write, so no context here has any: `extendedDataTypeUrl` is never answered, and in a request body it is accepted and ignored as `createTime` and `updateTime` are (#1700). |

RSA signatures verify against a registered public key: `up` registers the ADC fixture's own (#577), so a URL signed with the credentials `cloudburrow env` exports verifies with no setup, and `storage.signingCerts` (or `storage-server --signing-cert`) adds others. An account with no registered key is verified against the certificates its email domain's source serves (`storage-server --service-account-certs DOMAIN=URL`, Google's `/service_accounts/v1/metadata/x509/EMAIL`, read on every request; a source that does not answer or an account it does not know is 403, #1786): `up` names the BigQuery front for `gcp-sa-bigquery-condel.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, whose connections' service agents sign `EXTERNAL_OBJECT_TRANSFORM`'s URLs (`TestBigQueryObjectTables`, unit `TestSignedURLCertSource`). ### What the server does

Built to Google's spec in steps (#485), one issue per feature:

#### Buckets (#490)

Are served: insert, get, list (prefix, pages of at most 1000), patch as a JSON merge patch (an omitted field stays, `null` clears it, a `null` label removes that key), update, delete, and metageneration with `ifMetagenerationMatch`/`NotMatch` (412 `conditionNotMet`; 304 for a read). Every settable field is kept, stored or refused by name with 400, never dropped with 200; see the bucket fields table below. A non-empty bucket delete is 409 (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/status-codes>) for the JSON API).

#### Objects (#491)

Media and multipart uploads (`uploadType=media`, `multipart`; a metadata-only POST is 400 `wrongUrlForUpload`), with `Content-MD5`, `x-goog-hash` and the metadata's `md5Hash`/`crc32c` verified and a mismatch refused; `ifGenerationMatch` (including 0, "only if absent") and the other three preconditions; metadata reads, `alt=media`, `/download/storage/v1/…`, and XML `GET`/`HEAD /{bucket}/{object}` with the `x-goog-*` headers; one byte range (`a-b`, `a-`, `-N`; 206, or 416 with `Content-Range: bytes */size`); and a new generation, metageneration 1, on every finalize. `TestStorageObjectRoundTrip`, `TestStorageChecksums` and `TestMultipartUploadStoresMetadataWithContent` pass against it.

#### Object metadata (#492)

Patch (merge; a `null` metadata key removes it) and update (replace), each advancing the metageneration and keeping the generation and bytes; `customTime` only moves forward and cannot be removed, as documented; A body may restate the object's `storageClass` but not change it, which only a rewrite does (#515); holds and retention follow the retention rules below. Preconditions combine with AND on the live generation unless one is named: `ifGeneration(Not)Match`, `ifMetageneration(Not)Match` (412, or 304 for a failed NotMatch on a read), `If-Match` (412) and `If-None-Match` (304 on reads), and for the XML API `x-goog-if-generation-match`, `x-goog-if-metageneration-match`, `If-Modified-Since` (304) and `If-Unmodified-Since` (412). `TestStorageGenerationPreconditions` and `TestObjectMetadataUpdate` pass against it.

#### Listing (#494)

`prefix`, `delimiter` with synthetic `prefixes` (which count toward `maxResults`), `includeTrailingDelimiter`, `startOffset`/`endOffset`, `matchGlob` (`**`, `*`, `?`, `[…]`, `[!…]`, `{a,b}`), and pages of at most 1000 in byte order. `TestStorageListWithPrefix` passes against it.

#### Resumable uploads (#493)

A session from `uploadType=resumable` (200 with `Location`; the `upload_id` is random), chunks by PUT or POST with `Content-Range: bytes a-b/TOTAL|*` (every chunk but the last a multiple of 256 KiB; persisted bytes immutable, so a re-sent range is skipped), and an incomplete chunk answered **308 with `Range: bytes=0-N`**, or, with `X-GUploader-No-308: yes` as the Go client sends it, **200 with `X-Http-Status-Code-Override: 308`**. Both handshakes are undocumented and required by the clients. `bytes */TOTAL` and `bytes */*` query the status; the final chunk verifies `x-goog-hash` and applies `X-Goog-Meta-*`; DELETE cancels with 499. A session lasts a week, then answers 410 for a week, then 404. Sessions and their chunks survive a restart in persistent mode. `TestStorageResumableUploadAndRangedRead` and `TestResumableUploadCompletes` pass against it.

#### Compose, copy, rewrite and move (#495)

Compose takes 1 to 32 sources of one storage class, with per-source `generation` and `ifGenerationMatch` and `deleteSourceObjects`; the result has **no MD5**, a CRC32C combined from the components, and `componentCount` (counting a composite's components). Copy and rewrite share the source's bytes, cross buckets and honour `ifSource*`; rewrite changes the storage class, and with `maxBytesRewrittenPerCall` (a multiple of 1 MiB) proceeds by tokens, each good for a week and once. Move renames atomically within a bucket. `destinationPredefinedAcl` is refused by name; `kmsKeyName` and `destinationKmsKeyName` choose the destination's Cloud KMS key (below), and a copy or rewrite to or from a customer-managed key re-encrypts the bytes rather than sharing them. `TestStorageCompose`, `TestStorageCopy` and `TestObjectCopyAndRewrite` pass against it; the Go client's copier sends `objects.rewrite`, so `TestStorageObjectsCopy` drives `objects.copy` through Google's generated JSON API client, and `TestStorageObjectMove` drives `objects.move` through the Go client's `ObjectHandle.Move`.

#### Customer-managed encryption keys (#1938)

**Verified** (`TestStorageCMEK`, the official Go client over the JSON API and gRPC with the official `cloud.google.com/go/kms` client; `TestStorageEncryptionEnforcement`; `TestGcloudStorageCMEK`, `gcloud storage buckets create --default-encryption-key`, `cp --encryption-key`, `objects describe`, `buckets update --clear-default-encryption-key`; `TestTerraformStorageBucketCMEK`, `google_storage_bucket` with `encryption { default_kms_key_name }`; `TestIAMEnforcementStorageCMEK` with `--iam-enforcement=on`), to <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/customer-managed-keys>, <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/using-customer-managed-keys> and <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/enforce-encryption-types>. A write takes a key from `kmsKeyName` (JSON simple, multipart and resumable uploads, and the upload metadata's `kmsKeyName`; gRPC `WriteObjectSpec.resource.kms_key`), `x-goog-encryption-kms-key-name` (XML `PUT`, resumable and multipart uploads), `destinationKmsKeyName` (copy, rewrite; `Copier.DestinationKMSKeyName`) or `kmsKeyName` (compose), else from the bucket's `encryption.defaultKmsKeyName`; a customer-supplied key wins over the bucket's default, and naming both kinds is 400. The key ring must be in the bucket's location (`us` for `US`, the region, the dual-region's code). The bytes are **really encrypted at rest**: each object gets a fresh 256-bit data key, the bytes are sealed with AES-256-GCM in 64 KiB segments, and the data key is kept only as the instance's Cloud KMS `Encrypt` returned it; a read asks Cloud KMS to `Decrypt` it. The object reports `kmsKeyName` with its version (`.../cryptoKeyVersions/N`, the key's primary when written; XML reads echo `x-goog-encryption-kms-key-name`); after a rotation new writes use the new primary and older objects keep theirs. While the object's version is disabled or destroyed its bytes cannot be read, copied, rewritten or composed (400, through JSON, XML and gRPC), and a key whose primary is not enabled cannot encrypt (400); metadata, listing and deletion still work. A JSON API listing leaves out a CMEK object's `crc32c` and `md5Hash`, as documented. A patch cannot change `kmsKeyName` ("only by rewrite"); restating it is accepted. With `--iam-enforcement=on` the project's Cloud Storage service agent (`service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gs-project-accounts.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, what `projects.serviceAccount.get` returns) must hold `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt` or `useToDecrypt` on the key, as `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` gives (the key's and key ring's policies, then the project's): without it 403 "Permission denied on Cloud KMS key …". Without the `kms` service a key is refused (400), never ignored. **Encryption enforcement:** `googleManagedEncryptionEnforcementConfig`, `customerManagedEncryptionEnforcementConfig` and `customerSuppliedEncryptionEnforcementConfig` take `restrictionMode` `NotRestricted` or `FullyRestricted` and report an output-only `effectiveTime` (stamped when the mode changes), over JSON and gRPC; an omitted config keeps its value; at least one type must stay allowed, and a bucket with a default key must allow customer-managed or customer-supplied keys; every operation that creates an object (upload, copy, rewrite, compose, move, restore) is refused with 400 when its encryption type is restricted. **What differs from Google:** intermediate resumable chunks and XML multipart parts are kept unencrypted until the upload completes, and are then removed; the ciphertext format is CloudBurrow's own. UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-19, the pages above give no codes or messages): every refusal's code and message, and the key-location check's wording.

#### Customer-supplied encryption keys (#1345)

**Verified** (`TestStorageCSEKParity`, the official Go client's `ObjectHandle.Key` over the JSON API and over gRPC). A write names a key with `x-goog-encryption-algorithm: AES256`, `x-goog-encryption-key` and `x-goog-encryption-key-sha256` (JSON simple, multipart and resumable uploads, XML `PUT`, resumable and multipart uploads); a malformed set is 400 with Google's reasons. The object records only the key's SHA-256, never the key, and its metadata has `customerEncryption` (`AES256`, `keySha256`). Reading the bytes needs the key: without it 400 `resourceIsEncryptedWithCustomerEncryptionKey`, with another 400 `customerEncryptionKeyIsIncorrect`, and a key on an unencrypted object 400 `resourceNotEncryptedWithCustomerEncryptionKey`. Metadata reads and lists without the key leave out `crc32c` and `md5Hash`. Copy and rewrite take the source's key as `x-goog-copy-source-encryption-*` and the destination's as `x-goog-encryption-*`, so a rewrite adds, rotates or removes a key; compose needs every source encrypted with its key and encrypts the result with it. The bytes are held as written (not encrypted at rest); the observable behaviour is Google's. An XML multipart upload's parts are not checked for the key.

#### Batch (#496)

`POST /batch/storage/v1` takes a `multipart/mixed` body of `application/http` parts, dispatches each through the same handler as the direct call, and answers each in order with `Content-ID: <response-…>`; an upload or a download inside a batch is refused per part, and more than 100 calls refuse the whole batch (the refusal is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/batch>)). A part's body needs no `Content-Length`: the Python client sends none, and the body is the rest of the part.

#### Object versioning (#498)

On a bucket with `versioning.enabled`, replacing or deleting the live version keeps it as a **noncurrent** version with its generation and a `timeDeleted`; noncurrent versions appear only with `versions=true` (each name's oldest first, paged within a name) or when named by `generation=`, and can be read, patched and used as a copy source. A delete that names a generation removes that version permanently. Disabling versioning stops new noncurrent versions and keeps the existing ones, `ifGenerationMatch=0` succeeds when only noncurrent versions exist, and a bucket holding only noncurrent versions is not empty (409). Versions survive a restart in persistent mode. `TestStorageVersioningKeepsNoncurrent`, `TestStorageVersioningDeleteKeepsNoncurrent`, `TestStorageVersioningDisableKeepsExisting`, `TestStorageDoesNotExistWithOnlyNoncurrent` and the restart probe `TestStorageVersioningPersistentMode` pass against it.

#### Soft delete (#499)

Every bucket has a soft delete policy, 7 days unless set (7 to 90 days, or 0 for none; `effectiveTime` moves when the retention changes). Under it, a version that leaves the bucket (deleted, overwritten, or a deleted noncurrent version) is kept **soft-deleted** with `softDeleteTime` and `hardDeleteTime`: hidden from reads and listings, listed with `softDeleted=true`, its metadata readable by generation (never its bytes), and `objects.restore` makes it live again as a new generation with metageneration 1, retiring any live version it replaces. A restore answers **412 `softDeletePolicyNotSet`** on a bucket without a policy and **412 `objectNotSoftDeleted`** for a live or noncurrent generation, as the status-codes page lists. A bucket whose only objects are soft-deleted can be deleted; it is then soft-deleted itself under its own policy, readable and listable with `softDeleted=true`, and `buckets.restore` brings it back empty, with its soft-deleted objects restorable again (a live bucket of the same name refuses the restore with 409, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/soft-delete>)). A policy change applies only to later deletions. Reads treat anything past its `hardDeleteTime` as gone, and a sweep removes it. `softDeletePolicy.hardDeletePause` (discovery revision 20261009, #1702) pauses that: while `enabled` is true the bucket's soft-deleted objects are kept past their `hardDeleteTime`, which is left as it was (soft-delete docs: they are "retained indefinitely, regardless of the retention duration"), so reads, `softDeleted=true` listings, `objects.restore` and `bulkRestore` still see them and the sweep skips them; the output `effectiveTime` is when the pause was enabled, and disabling it drops `effectiveTime` and resumes the hard delete of everything past its `hardDeleteTime`. The rules of the pause-hard-deletions page (#1715) are enforced: `buckets.insert` with the pause enabled is refused (400), and so is pausing a bucket without soft delete (412 `softDeletePolicyNotSet`, judged on the bucket before the update); the pause changes, either way, at most once every 24 hours of the server's clock, counted from its last change (412 `conditionNotMet`, naming when it can); while it holds, soft delete cannot be disabled, by a 0 retention or by removing the policy (412 `conditionNotMet`), though the retention can change, and `buckets.delete` is refused (409), so a bucket is never soft-deleted while paused. Each status and reason is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/pause-hard-deletions>, which lists none): each is coded as CloudBurrow codes its nearest refusal (a create-only field 400, the status-codes page's `softDeletePolicyNotSet` for a bucket without soft delete, a bucket-state precondition 412, a refused bucket delete 409 as for a non-empty bucket). The console's Edit bucket and Delete bucket show the API's refusal. The pause and its refusals are exercised through the generated JSON API client; the 24-hour limit and the sweep past `hardDeleteTime` are unit-tested on a fake clock. A move is a rename and leaves nothing soft-deleted (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/copying-renaming-moving-objects>)). `objects.bulkRestore` restores the matching soft-deleted objects in one done operation (#1279). `TestStorageSoftDeleteAndRestore`, `TestStorageRestoreNotSoftDeleted412`, `TestStorageRestoreWithoutPolicy412`, `TestStorageBucketDeleteIgnoresSoftDeleted`, `TestStorageBucketsRestore` and `TestStorageHardDeletePause` pass against it.

#### Retention and holds (#500)

With the status-codes page's reasons: a bucket `retentionPolicy` (1 s to 3,155,760,000 s) applies to existing and new objects, which report `retentionExpirationTime`; an object younger than the period cannot be deleted or replaced (**403 `retentionPolicyNotMet`**), though a versioned bucket may make it noncurrent, and its metadata stays editable. `lockRetentionPolicy` needs `ifMetagenerationMatch` (required in the pinned discovery document; 400 without, 412 stale) and a policy (400 `badRequest`). **A second lock of a locked policy is refused 400 `badRequest`** "The retention policy on bucket … is already locked." and changes nothing, metageneration included (#829). This is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-lock>): the lockRetentionPolicy reference, the bucket-lock and using-bucket-lock pages and the status-codes page say what a lock needs and that it is irreversible, but not what a repeat lock answers, and no observation of Google has been recorded; 400 `badRequest` is the status-codes page's reason for a lock the bucket's settings do not allow, the conservative choice over accepting it. The metageneration is checked first, so a stale one is 412 whether or not the policy is locked; a locked period can grow but not shrink or be removed (400 `badRequestException`; the discovery document says PERMISSION_DENIED, the status-codes page 400). `temporaryHold` and `eventBasedHold` block delete and replace (**403 `objectUnderActiveHold`**) but not metadata changes; releasing an event-based hold restarts the retention clock, and no `retentionExpirationTime` is given while it is held; `defaultEventBasedHold` holds each new object. Object retention `{mode, retainUntilTime}` needs a bucket created with `enableObjectRetention=true` (400 `invalid` otherwise, and with an event-based hold); removing, shortening or locking an Unlocked one needs `overrideUnlockedRetention=true` (403 `forbidden`), and a Locked one only extends. A copy, rewrite or restore does not inherit holds or retention. Holds also block a live version becoming noncurrent (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/object-holds>)). `TestStorageRetentionBlocksDelete`, `TestStorageLockRetentionPolicy`, `TestStorageLockRetentionPolicyTwice`, `TestStorageHoldsBlockDelete` and `TestStorageObjectRetentionRequiresEnabledBucket` pass against it.

#### Lifecycle (#501)

`lifecycle.rule` is validated when set, and an unknown action or condition is 400 naming it, with the old configuration kept. Actions are Delete, SetStorageClass and AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload (#508; with only `age`, `matchesPrefix` and `matchesSuffix`, as documented). Conditions are `age`, `createdBefore`, `customTimeBefore`, `daysSinceCustomTime`, `daysSinceNoncurrentTime`, `isLive`, `matchesPrefix`/`matchesSuffix` (at most 1000 across all rules), `matchesStorageClass`, `noncurrentTimeBefore`, `numNewerVersions` and `sizeAboveBytes`/`sizeBelowBytes` (at most 5 TiB). The rules run at least hourly on the server's clock, and on demand with `POST /_cloudburrow/lifecycle`. A rule's conditions combine with AND; `age` 0 is met at midnight UTC after creation, and age N N days after it. Delete takes precedence over SetStorageClass, and the cheapest target class wins; a class only moves to a cheaper one. A hold or an unmet retention period keeps Delete from taking effect, and a deleted live version becomes noncurrent or soft-deleted as any delete does. No limit on the number of rules is imposed, since none is documented. `TestStorageLifecycleConfigRoundTrip` and `TestStorageLifecycleUnknownCondition400` pass against it.

#### CORS (#502)

**CloudBurrow checks the browser's origin first** (#677, [ADR-0004](adr/0004-local-access-and-no-authentication.md)). Google can allow any origin because every call carries an OAuth token; CloudBurrow checks none, so a page on any site you have open could otherwise read and change every bucket. A request with an `Origin` header is served only when the origin is loopback (`http://` or `https://` at `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, `localhost` or `*.localhost`, any port), the server's own, or named with `up --cors-allow-origin` ([configuration.md](configuration.md#browser-access-to-cloud-storage)). Any other origin, `https://evil.example` say, gets **403 with no CORS headers**, a preflight included, however the bucket's `cors` is set. A request with no `Origin` (the SDKs, `gcloud`, `curl`) is not checked. This is a deliberate difference from Google. `TestStorageCORSRefusesForeignOrigin`, `TestStorageCORSLoopbackOriginWorks` and `TestStorageCORSAllowlistedOriginWorks` pass against it, the last two with a resumable upload started and finished from the browser's origin.

For an origin that passes, Google's behaviour applies. The bucket's `cors` (`origin`, with `*`; `method`; `responseHeader`; `maxAgeSeconds`, 3600 by default) is kept and validated. **XML endpoints** follow it: a preflight is answered from the first rule that matches its origin, its method and every requested header, with that rule's methods and max age; a preflight that matches none gets **200 with no CORS headers**, as documented; an actual request that matches gets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and the rule's `responseHeader` as `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`. **JSON endpoints** (`/storage/v1`, uploads, downloads, batch) always allow, whatever the bucket says: the Origin echoed, `DELETE, GET, HEAD, PATCH, POST, PUT`, a Max-Age of 3600, and the requested headers echoed (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/cross-origin>)). **`Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`** is sent as <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/cross-origin> documents it (read 2026-10-17, #1595): on an approved simple request, and with **404** on an `OPTIONS` whose `Access-Control-Request-Method` is empty. #677 had dropped it while every origin was served; now only an origin that passes the check gets it, and CloudBurrow reads no cookies, so it grants a page nothing more. A resumable session URI answers with the Origin that started the session, and is itself behind the origin check. `TestStorageCORSRoundTrip`, `TestStorageXMLPreflightMatches`, `TestStorageXMLPreflightMismatch200NoHeaders` and `TestStorageJSONAlwaysAllowsCORS` pass against it.

#### XML API subset (#507)

Path-style or virtual-hosted (`{bucket}.{host}` with `storage-server --host`): object `PUT` (with `x-goog-meta-*`, `Cache-Control` and the other content headers, `x-goog-storage-class`, `x-goog-if-generation-match`/`-metageneration-match` and `Content-MD5`; 200 with the ETag, `x-goog-generation` and `x-goog-hash`, no body), `GET`/`HEAD` (#491) and `DELETE` (204); bucket `GET` (a `ListBucketResult` with `prefix`, `delimiter` and its `CommonPrefixes`, `marker`, `max-keys`, `IsTruncated` and `NextMarker`) and `DELETE`; and resumable uploads, where `POST` with `x-goog-resumable: start` is **201 with the session URI**, chunks are `PUT` to it with `Content-Range` (308 while incomplete), and a `DELETE` cancels with **204**. Errors are `<Error>` documents: `NoSuchBucket`, `NoSuchKey`, `PreconditionFailed`, `BucketNotEmpty` (409), `InvalidArgument`, `InvalidRange`, `AccessDenied`. `x-goog-copy-source`, `x-goog-acl` on an object `PUT` and customer encryption headers are refused by name. Signed URLs (#509) are verified; see the data plane. `TestStorageXMLPutGetDelete`, `TestStorageXMLListBucket`, `TestStorageXMLResumable201And204`, `TestStorageXMLErrorCodes` and `TestStorageXMLHostStyle` pass against it.

**Bucket `PUT`, service `GET` and form `POST` (#1258).** The project is `x-goog-project-id`, or else the project of the HMAC key an `Authorization` header names (the interoperability default project); with neither, **400 `MissingSecurityHeader`** naming `x-goog-project-id` (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/xml-api/get-service>)). Bucket `PUT /{bucket}` with no subresource takes an optional `CreateBucketConfiguration` (`LocationConstraint`, `StorageClass`; any other element is refused by name), `x-goog-acl` as a canned ACL and `x-goog-bucket-object-lock-enabled`, and runs `buckets.insert`, so both APIs make the same bucket; 200 with no body, or 409 `BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou` (same project) or `BucketAlreadyExists`. Service `GET /` is a `ListAllMyBucketsResult` of the project's buckets with their `CreationDate` (the `Owner` ID is opaque). Form `POST /{bucket}` (`multipart/form-data`, the `file` field last) stores the file under `key`, with `${filename}` replaced, `Content-Type`, `Cache-Control`, `Content-Disposition`, `Content-Encoding`, `x-goog-meta-*` and a canned `acl`; any other field is refused rather than ignored. With a `policy`, its `expiration` is judged on the server's clock and every condition is checked: exact-match objects, `eq`, `starts-with` and `content-length-range`, and every form field must be named by one (`x-goog-signature`, `signature`, `GoogleAccessId`, `policy`, `file` and `x-ignore-*` excepted). A failed condition, or a field no condition names, is 400 `InvalidPolicyDocument` "Invalid according to Policy", the status table's "The content of the form does not meet the conditions specified in the policy document" (<https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/xml-api/reference-status>, read 2026-10-17; #1595). An expired policy is 403 `AccessDenied`, a file outside the range 400 `EntityTooLarge`/`EntityTooSmall`, a malformed policy 400 `InvalidPolicyDocument` (those UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/xml-api/reference-status>): the table has no row for an expired or malformed policy). The policy's signature is **verified as a signed URL's is**, failing closed: `x-goog-signature` with `GOOG4-RSA-SHA256` against a registered certificate or `GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256` against an ACTIVE HMAC key, or V2's `signature` with `GoogleAccessId`; a form with neither policy nor signature is served unsigned, as any unsigned request is (ADR-0004). Success is `success_action_redirect` (303 with `bucket`, `key` and `etag` added to its query), else `success_action_status` 200, 201 (a `PostResponse` document, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/xml-api/post-object-forms>)) or the default 204, each with the object's `x-goog-generation` and `x-goog-hash`. A policy from the official Go client's `GenerateSignedPostPolicyV4` uploads through it: `TestStorageXMLBucketPutAndServiceGet` and `TestStorageXMLFormPostPolicyV4` pass against it.

#### XML multipart uploads (#508)

`POST ?uploads` (an `InitiateMultipartUploadResult` in the S3 namespace the clients parse), `PUT ?partNumber=N&uploadId=` for N 1 to 10,000 (the ETag, and `x-goog-hash` the Python client validates; the same number again replaces the part), `POST ?uploadId=` with `CompleteMultipartUpload` (parts in ascending order with their ETags; every part but the last at least 5 MiB; **no MD5** on the object, as documented, and a CRC32C), `DELETE ?uploadId=` (**204**), list parts (`max-parts`, `part-number-marker`, at most 1000) and `GET /{bucket}?uploads`. **Preconditions are refused with 400 `NotImplemented`**, as the docs say they are not supported. A part out of order, a bad ETag and a part under 5 MiB that is not the last are 400 `InvalidPartOrder`, `InvalidPart` and `InvalidArgument`, the codes [post-object-complete](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/xml-api/post-object-complete) documents; the completed upload's ETag is S3's `"md5-of-md5s-N"` (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/xml-api/post-object-complete>)). An incomplete upload stays until aborted, or until a lifecycle `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` rule (age, `matchesPrefix`, `matchesSuffix`) removes it. Google's Python `transfer_manager.upload_chunks_concurrently` uploads a 20 MiB file in 5 MiB parts against it: `test_transfer_manager_xml_multipart_upload` runs in CI (#516). `TestStorageXMLMultipartAbort204`, `TestStorageXMLMultipartListParts` and `TestStorageXMLMultipartPreconditionRefused` pass against it.

#### Persistence by mode (#512; the #481 lesson)

With `--data-dir`, `storage-server --mode persistent` (the default) keeps buckets, every object version's bytes and metadata, and in-progress resumable sessions across a restart. `--mode ephemeral` deletes the store an earlier run left in that directory before serving, so nothing survives whatever is on disk: the choice is made by the mode, never by whether a store exists. CI's restart probe `TestStorageAcrossRestart` runs at setup, after a persistent restart (a bucket, a two-version object and a 256 KiB-in session: **present**; with a Pub/Sub emulator, a notificationConfig too, #701) and after an ephemeral restart on the same directory (**absent**); unit `TestStorageEphemeralClearsLeftoverStore` does the same in-process. `up` passes the instance's mode to the in-cluster server (#514), and the compat job's restart probe measures it on every merge (#596): the same `TestStorageAcrossRestart` runs against the in-cluster server through the instance's tunnel at setup, after `stop` and `up` (**present**, from the Deployment's PVC) and after `up --mode ephemeral` (**absent**; the Deployment has no volume). The session is resumed at the restarted instance's endpoint, whose port is OS-assigned and so new.

#### In the cluster (#514)

`up` runs **one** Deployment for the host and the cluster, with no notification front, no second Deployment and no Host-binding workaround (#268), because the server builds `mediaLink` from each request's Host. Its image is built at `up` from the Linux `cloudburrow-storage` binary embedded in the CLI, on a distroless base pinned by digest (`build.storageServerBase`), and `kind load`ed; nothing is published or downloaded but the base. Readiness is a real request (`GET /storage/v1/b?project=_`). A NetworkPolicy allows egress only to DNS and the Pub/Sub emulator, and object change notification channels do not widen it: the server runs with `--relay-channels`, and the CLI takes their messages through the tunnel and POSTs them on the host, to local addresses only (#1290); kind's default CNI does not enforce NetworkPolicy, so `TestStorageNoEgress` proves in-process that a whole workload resolves no name at all. Measured against a real instance: 58 builtin storage and notification compat tests passed through the tunnel, the e2e `TestAcceptanceWorkflow` passed with the worker's `STORAGE_ENDPOINT` on the single Deployment, and the CLI scrapes the server's calls into `/admin/events` and `/metrics`. Measured for #514: a pod could **not** reach the CLI's loopback-bound ports through the kind gateway, but **could** through `host.docker.internal` on Docker Desktop, admin API included (#553). **The official Go client retries every 5xx, 501 included, until its deadline**, so a method not built yet costs a client its timeout rather than failing at once. CI runs the whole compat suite against it twice: through the tunnel on an instance (the `official SDK compatibility (storage)` shard, #565), and against a standalone `cloudburrow storage-server` with the Python suite, the restart probes and a registered signing certificate (`check` job).

#### Audit logs and request activity (#1979)

**Verified** by `TestStorageDataAccessAuditLogs` and `TestStorageDataAccessAuditLogsOffByDefault` (official storage, Resource Manager and Logging clients) and `TestStorageInsightsActivityViews` (official storage, Storage Insights and BigQuery clients). The server keeps one record per request (method, bucket, object, project, status, bytes each way, processing time, request ID, host, referrer, user agent, caller IP), from which the CLI writes Cloud Storage's audit log entries to the instance's Cloud Logging, as [Google documents them](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/audit-logging): Admin Activity entries (`cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity`) always, and Data Access entries (`cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Fdata_access`) of type `ADMIN_READ`, `DATA_READ` or `DATA_WRITE` only when the IAM policy `auditConfigs` of the bucket's project, a folder above it or the organization enable that type for `storage.googleapis.com` or `allServices` (off by default, as on Google). The type follows the permission each request is checked for, so a copy or a compose writes two entries (the source's read and the destination's write); the resource is `gcs_bucket` with `project_id`, `bucket_name` and `location`; `resourceName` is `projects/_/buckets/B[/objects/O]`; an XML API or gRPC request is named by the JSON API method that serves it. No caller is authenticated (ADR-0006), so `authenticationInfo` names no principal and `exemptedMembers` exempt nothing; `request` and `response` (Google's Detailed audit logging mode) are not written. The same records fill the Storage Insights activity views (docs/storage-companions.md). The record costs the hot path an append to a bounded buffer, never a wait (about 0.3 µs and 3 allocations on a small download, `BenchmarkStorageObjectGet`); when the buffer (8,192 records, drained every 100 ms) is full a record is dropped. Entries reach Logging within about 2 seconds. A batch request's parts are one record.

#### Official clients and tools (#516, #517)

**The official Python client** (google-cloud-storage 3.14.1, #516) runs against the storage server in CI: CRUD with a resumable upload, a resume after an interrupted chunk (`recover()`'s `bytes */*` answered 308 with the `Range` held), `mediaLink` on the emulator's host, `if_generation_match=0` and a ranged download, batch, `transfer_manager` XML multipart, and a V4 signed URL. **gcloud storage** (586.0.0, #517; CI installs 593.0.0 since #1927, checksum-pinned, #694), configured by `gcloud-setup` alone, with every non-loopback request refused by a test proxy: `storage ls`, `buckets create`, `buckets update --update-labels` then `--clear-labels`, `objects update`, `hmac create/list/update/delete`, and `cp` of 200 MiB by the parallel composite path. That path reads `buckets.getStorageLayout` and composes with `deleteSourceObjects` in the request body, which deletes the components, and a download over the sliced threshold reads it back in four ranged slices. `gcloud storage rm -r` lists `managedFolders`, which is empty unless one was created. On macOS, gcloud's `gcloud-crc32c` helper under Gatekeeper quarantine hangs on any file, CloudBurrow or not; the test checks the sliced download by SHA-256 instead. **gsutil** (5.37, the one Google Cloud CLI 586.0.0 carries; 5.38 in CI's 593.0.0, which sends its built-in key on anonymous calls, accepted as Google accepts it) requires HTTPS on both APIs (`gcs_json_api.py` hard-codes `https://`; `is_secure = False` is refused), and CloudBurrow serves plain HTTP, so it works only behind a TLS front; `TestGsutilJSONAndHMACXML` supplies one. Through it, cp, ls and rm work over JSON with no credentials and over XML with HMAC-only credentials. gsutil cannot download over XML from any port but 443 or 80, whatever the server (its `_AddCustomEndpointToKey` sets the port as a string, and boto formats it with `%d`). apitools sent **no** `X-GUploader-No-308` (0 of 15 requests).

### Bucket fields

Every settable Bucket property of the discovery document (#503). *Kept* fields are stored, echoed and act as documented. *Stored, no effect* fields are stored and echoed as sent, but nothing here acts on them. *Refused* fields get 400 naming the field, never 200 and a silent drop. `TestStorageBucketFieldsNeverSilentlyDropped` checks this list against the schema.

| Field | Behaviour | Issue |
|---|---|---|
| `location`, `storageClass`, `labels` (a `null` key removes it) | Kept; the location is fixed at creation | #490, #503 |
| `versioning` | Kept | #498 |
| `softDeletePolicy` | Kept | #499 |
| `retentionPolicy`, `defaultEventBasedHold`, `objectRetention` (with `enableObjectRetention=true`) | Kept | #500 |
| `lifecycle` | Kept | #501 |
| `cors` | Kept | #502 |
| `website` | Stored, no effect: no website serving | #503 |
| `logging` | Stored, no effect: no usage logs are written | #503 |
| `encryption` (`defaultKmsKeyName`, the three enforcement configs) | Kept: new objects are encrypted with the default key and the enforcement configs are enforced (customer-managed encryption keys above) | #1938 |
| `billing` (`requesterPays`) | Stored, no effect: nothing is billed, and `userProject` is accepted and ignored | #503 |
| `iamConfiguration` (`uniformBucketLevelAccess`, `publicAccessPrevention`) | Stored. Nothing is enforced either way; uniform access refuses the ACL methods with 400 (#1233), and `uniformBucketLevelAccess.enabled` (or the legacy `bucketPolicyOnly.enabled`) is what `managedFolders.insert` requires, as Google does (`TestStorageManagedFolderLifecycle`, #828) | #503 |
| `rpo` (`DEFAULT` or `ASYNC_TURBO`) | Stored, no effect: there is no replication | #503 |
| `autoclass` | Stored, no effect: classes move only by rewrite or lifecycle | #503 |
| `customPlacementConfig` | Stored, no effect: there is one location. Set only at creation (a later change is 400 naming it, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/buckets>)); one zone with `storageClass` `RAPID` makes a Rapid storage bucket, which holds appendable objects over gRPC, and `RAPID` without exactly one zone of the bucket's location is 400 (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/rapid/rapid-bucket>); `TestGcloudStorageRapidBucket`: `gcloud storage buckets create --placement=us-central1-a --default-storage-class=RAPID`) | #503, #1443 |
| `hierarchicalNamespace` | Kept: set only at creation (a later change is 400 naming it), it needs `uniformBucketLevelAccess` and excludes `versioning` (400, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/hns-overview>)), and it enables folders (`TestStorageFoldersControl`) | #503, #1203 |
| `ipFilter` | **Enforced** for public sources (#1505): stored and returned after Google's documented checks (`mode` `Enabled` or `Disabled`, CIDR ranges that parse, at most 200 ranges and 25 VPC networks, networks named `projects/{project}/global/networks/{network}`). With `mode` `Enabled`, a request to the bucket or its objects (JSON, upload, download, XML, gRPC) from an address in none of `publicNetworkSource.allowedIpCidrRanges` is 403 (message UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/ip-filtering-overview>)). The address is the caller's: the tunnel passes it on, so a caller on this machine is its loopback address and one on the LAN its LAN address. The bucket's own metadata (GET, PATCH, PUT, DELETE of the bucket) is exempt, as for a holder of `storage.buckets.exemptFromIpFilter`, which every caller is here (IAM is not enforced), so a filter can always be fixed. `vpcNetworkSources` are stored and admit nobody, as no request arrives from a VPC network; their networks' existence is not checked. `allowAllServiceAgentAccess` is stored, no effect (no service agent calls CloudBurrow). `TestStorageIPFilterJSON`, `TestStorageIPFilterGRPC`; `TestGcloudStorageIPFilter` (`gcloud storage buckets create` and `update --ip-filter-file`, `--clear-ip-filter`, which sets the mode `Disabled`); `TestTerraformStorageBucketIPFilter` (`google_storage_bucket`'s `ip_filter`: apply, clean plan, change in place, clean plan, destroy). Console: the IP filtering group on the Configuration tab and Edit IP filtering (`TestStorageIPFilterThroughTheConsole`, `TestStorageIPFilterThroughTheBrowser`) | #1443, #1505 |
| `acl`, `defaultObjectAcl`, `predefinedAcl`, `predefinedDefaultObjectAcl` | Stored, not enforced: returned under `projection=full`; a predefined ACL overrides the body's; a body that leaves an ACL out keeps it (`TestStoragePredefinedACL`) | #1233 |

### UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/status-codes>) choices

Where no Google page states a behaviour, the server makes a choice and marks it UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/status-codes>) in the
test that pins it; the method-level codes are also listed in [docs/coverage/storage.md](coverage/storage.md). Every item below was re-read against Google's docs on 2026-10-17 (<https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/status-codes>, <https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/xml-api/reference-status>) and is still unanswered there, but for the XML multipart part order, ETag and part size codes, which are now documented (<https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/xml-api/post-object-complete>).

- `buckets.delete` of a non-empty bucket answers 409, as the XML API documents `BucketNotEmpty`; no page states the JSON API's status.
- `buckets.setIamPolicy` with a stale etag answers 412, the JSON API's precondition code.
- A live bucket of the same name refuses `buckets.restore` with 409.
- A move is a rename and leaves nothing soft-deleted; holds block a live version becoming noncurrent.
- More than 100 calls refuse a whole batch.
- The JSON API's CORS defaults beyond `Allow-Origin`, `Allow-Methods`, `Max-Age` and `Allow-Credentials`: the requested headers echoed.
- XML multipart part order, ETag and size errors are `InvalidPartOrder`, `InvalidPart` and `InvalidArgument` (400), as [post-object-complete](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/xml-api/post-object-complete) documents them (read 2026-10-17); still UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/xml-api/post-object-complete>): the completed upload's ETag is S3's `"md5-of-md5s-N"`.
- A signed URL's `X-Goog-Expires` is at most 604800 seconds, from the docs rather than a measured refusal.
- The XML API's 400 `MissingSecurityHeader` for a service request with no project, and a form `POST`'s other policy refusals (403 `AccessDenied` for an expired policy, 400 `EntityTooLarge`/`EntityTooSmall`, 400 `InvalidPolicyDocument` for a malformed one) and its 201 `PostResponse` body (#1258).

## Cloud Storage — gRPC (`google.storage.v2`)

The builtin server serves `google.storage.v2.Storage` on the **same port** as the JSON and XML
APIs, as h2c (#1321): `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST`'s host:port, which `cloudburrow env` also exports
as `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST_GRPC` for the Go client. `storage.NewGRPCClient` with
`option.WithEndpoint(host:port)` and insecure transport credentials reaches it, in the cluster
(through the tunnel) and as `cloudburrow storage-server`. Every method is answered by the JSON
API's own handler: the gRPC request becomes the JSON request that means the same thing, served
in process, so both APIs read one store and agree on generations, metagenerations,
preconditions (`FAILED_PRECONDITION` where JSON says 412), CRC32C and MD5 checks, soft delete,
holds and retention. Every write goes through a resumable session: chunks persist in whole
256 KiB units, and the object is committed, with its checksums verified, at `finish_write`.
`TestStorageGRPCBuckets`, `TestStorageGRPCObjects`, `TestStorageGRPCComposeDeletesSources`, `TestStorageGRPCACLs` and `TestStorageGRPCAppendableObjects` (official Go client v1.69.0 on its gRPC
transport, `ReadObject` and `BidiReadObject` reads, each result read back over JSON and the
other way round) passed 2026-10-15 on an instance with `--services storage` and against the
builtin `storage-server`; the #1443 tests (`TestStorageGRPCAppendableObjects`, `TestStorageGRPCSetIamPolicyUpdateMask`,
`TestGcloudStorageRapidBucket`) passed 2026-10-16 on an instance with `--services storage`. The console uses the JSON API, so the Cloud Storage pages cover what
gRPC changes; an appendable object is appended to and finalized only over gRPC, as on Google's console, and its page shows it *Not finalized* while it is open.

|---|---|---|
| `CreateBucket`, `GetBucket`, `ListBuckets`, `UpdateBucket`, `DeleteBucket` | **Verified** | `TestStorageGRPCBuckets`. `UpdateBucket` takes the `update_mask` paths `labels` (and `labels.<key>`), `versioning`, `storage_class`, `default_event_based_hold`, `retention_policy`, `soft_delete_policy`, `iam_config`, `cors`, `website`, `logging`, `billing`, `encryption`, `autoclass`, `lifecycle`, `rpo`, `acl`, `default_object_acl`, `custom_placement_config` and `*`; any other path is `UNIMPLEMENTED` naming it. `custom_placement_config` is the JSON API's `customPlacementConfig` (#1443): set on create and read back on both APIs, and fixed at creation on both, so a change under the mask is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/storage/v2/storage.proto>)), as the JSON API's 400. `ip_filter` (and its mask path) is the JSON API's `ipFilter`, stored, checked and enforced the same way (#1505, `TestStorageIPFilterGRPC`); an invalid mode is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (`TestStorageGRPCSetIamPolicyUpdateMask`). A repeat create is `ALREADY_EXISTS`. `Bucket.acl` and `default_object_acl` are the JSON API's ACLs (#1233), stored and never enforced; each entry's `entity` and `role` are sent, and the rest is read back as the JSON API returns it (#1345, `TestStorageGRPCACLs`: an ACL on create, `BucketHandle.ACL` and `DefaultObjectACL` set and delete, which the Go client does as `GetBucket` then `UpdateBucket` with the `acl` or `default_object_acl` mask, each read back through JSON, and a JSON change read back over gRPC).
