## Pub/Sub — `google.pubsub.v1`

**Backing component:** Google `cloud-pubsub-emulator` 0.8.35 (integrate).
Contract: `google/pubsub/v1/pubsub.proto`. Client endpoint override: `PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST`.

**Inherited limitations**, measured in #24:

- **State is not persisted.** A topic was `NotFound` after restart even with `--data-dir`.
  Pub/Sub is effectively memory-only, and CloudBurrow will not imply otherwise.
- **IAM methods return `Unimplemented`.** The emulator announces this at startup, and over REST
  it answered a plain-text 404. CloudBurrow's front serves them instead (#1367, the IAM row below).
- The emulator describes itself as a "fake" that "may be incomplete or differ from the real
  system."
- **A subscription keeps every message it was sent, acknowledged or not, for as long as it
  exists** (#1603, measured; [soak.md](soak.md#results)). The emulator's backlog of a
  subscription (`MessageBacklog`) never removes a message, only marks it acknowledged, so its heap
  grows with every message published: about 0.9 KB per message of the soak's (a few bytes of data
  and two attributes, on two subscriptions), and 1.5 KB per 1 KB message on one. Deleting the
  subscription frees it (`DeleteSubscription`, detaching it, or `cloudburrow reset --service
  pubsub`): after the soak deleted its topic and subscriptions the live heap fell from 109 to
  10 MiB. CloudBurrow bounds the heap (`--emulator-heap-mib`, 1024 MiB by default since #1611,
  [configuration.md](configuration.md#settings)); 512 MiB held about 350,000 such 1 KB messages, or
  550,000 of the soak's. **When the heap is full the emulator exits and its container restarts,
  empty.** Unbounded, it would instead have grown to a quarter of the cluster node's memory; bounded
  without that exit, it was measured to answer nothing at all (every `Publish` timing out) until its
  pod was deleted. A publisher that runs for hours should delete and recreate its subscriptions, or
  raise the bound.
- **CloudBurrow's front brings the definitions back after an emulator restart** (#1608,
  `internal/pubsubfront/restore.go`). It keeps every topic, subscription (its whole configuration),
  AVRO schema with its revisions and snapshot the emulator holds in its state file, read from the
  emulator after each call that changed one and before that call is answered. When the emulator's
  container restarts, from an `OutOfMemoryError` or any crash, the front holds every call (at most
  2 minutes) until it has created them all again, so no client sees an empty emulator; IAM
  policies, updated expiration policies and labels, detached subscriptions, snapshot updates and
  Protocol Buffer schemas were always the front's and need nothing. What cannot come back is the
  emulator's memory: **every message not yet acknowledged when it crashed is lost**, and a snapshot
  is taken again with no backlog. Google's at-least-once delivery redelivers an unacknowledged
  message; it does not cover an emulator that crashed. A schema's revisions are committed again
  in order, so they get new revision IDs and creation times (a topic bound to a revision range is
  bound to the new IDs). The state file is on the pod's emptyDir, as before: in either `--mode`,
  the definitions outlive a restart of the emulator's container or the front's, and go with the
  pod, as the emulator's resources always have. The front does not delete and recreate a fully
  acknowledged subscription to free its memory: it cannot see a subscription's backlog without
  leasing messages, deleting it ends every open `StreamingPull` (fatal `NOT_FOUND` to the official
  clients), a message published in between would be lost, and a `Seek` to a time before it, or a
  snapshot's backlog, would no longer replay; none of that is invisible to a client.

**CloudBurrow's front** (#873). The emulator stores a subscription's `expiration_policy` and never
acts on it, so the Pub/Sub pod runs `cloudburrow-storage pubsub-front` (`internal/pubsubfront`)
beside it, on the Service's port, from the locally built storage image; the emulator listens on
the pod's loopback alone, port 8086, which the Service does not publish and no other pod reaches
(#1114, `TestEmulatorsBehindAFrontRefuseOtherPods`). Every client goes through the front, the
host tunnel, workloads in the cluster and the storage server's notifications alike, and it passes
every call through unchanged except the ones the Subscription expiration row names, and a
`labels` update of a topic or subscription, which the emulator refuses and the front applies
(#949, the `Publisher.UpdateTopic` and `Subscriber.UpdateSubscription` rows), and it answers the
IAM methods itself, which the emulator does not serve (#1367, the IAM row). **It serves
the emulator's REST API too**, as the emulator does, on the same port: each request is gRPC when it
is HTTP/2 with an `application/grpc` content type, and REST otherwise, over HTTP/1.1 or plain-text
HTTP/2 with prior knowledge (h2c, #909), proxied to the emulator's REST API with the
same rules (checks and the 31-day default on `PUT .../subscriptions/{s}`, the retention check on
`PATCH`, and every call on `.../subscriptions/{s}` or `{s}:verb`, and a snapshot's create, as
activity), so gcloud and Terraform's google provider, which use REST, work as before
(`TestGcloudPubSub`, `TestPubSubRESTSubscriptionExpiresWhenIdle`, `TestGcloudSetupConfiguration`,
`TestTerraformSchedulerAndSubscription`). **A connection is routed by its first request**
(#950): one that does not open with the HTTP/2 preface is HTTP/1.1, served by net/http; an
HTTP/2 connection whose first request is gRPC, as every official client's is, goes to grpc-go's
own transport; any other HTTP/2 connection goes to net/http, which routes each of its requests by
its content type, gRPC through `grpc.Server.ServeHTTP`. To read the first request the front sends
an empty SETTINGS frame itself (a gRPC client waits for one) and hands the chosen server every
byte the client sent but its acknowledgement of that frame (unit `TestClassifyByTheFirstRequest`).
So an h2c REST client is served, and so is a proxy that carries REST and then gRPC on one HTTP/2
connection (unit `TestRESTOverH2CPriorKnowledge`, `TestOneHTTP2ConnectionCarriesGRPCAndREST`); a
connection gRPC opened no longer answers a later REST request on it with grpc-go's 415 (#963):
the front reads every request on such a connection as it passes to grpc-go, and the first that is
not gRPC is never given to grpc-go; the client is sent a GOAWAY (NO_ERROR) whose last stream is
the last gRPC call, which RFC 9113 lets it retry on a new connection, the calls already open run
to their end, and that client's later HTTP/2 connections (by remote address) are routed per
request by net/http. Unit `TestRESTOnAConnectionGRPCOpenedIsServed`: Go's HTTP/2 client, after two
gRPC calls on a connection, gets the REST answer, retried on a second connection, which then
carries both; `TestAMixedConnectionIsRefusedWithGoAway` checks the frames (the GOAWAY's last
stream, a WINDOW_UPDATE giving back the refused DATA's window, nothing answered on a refused
stream, and the next connection served per request). Not checked through the host tunnel, which
never sends such a connection: it keeps gRPC and h2c REST on upstream connections of their own
(unit `TestGuardKeepsGRPCAndH2CRESTApart`, `internal/netfwd`), since every tunnel connection comes
from one address and one mixed connection would move them all to per-request routing. Client
trailers (which gRPC clients do not send, and which grpc-go's transport takes as a protocol error
that closes the connection) are given to grpc-go as an empty DATA frame ending their stream, and
once the front has kept any header block from grpc-go (a refused request, client trailers), each
later block grpc-go is given is re-encoded so that grpc-go's HPACK decoder, which never saw the
kept blocks, can read it (#981). Unit `TestHPACKStaysInStepOnAMixedConnection`: on one connection,
gRPC calls that use the HPACK dynamic table, one ended by client trailers that index an entry, a
call whose headers name it, a refused REST request that indexes another, client trailers naming
that one on a call still open, and a call after the GOAWAY, retried on a new connection; every
call succeeds and the connection stays open.
`TestPubSubRESTOverH2CPriorKnowledge` drives `curl --http2-prior-knowledge` through the tunnel,
between official gRPC client calls, and a ttl Google refuses is refused 400 over it as over
HTTP/1.1. Why not ServeHTTP for everything, as #909 had it: measured with
`go test ./internal/pubsubfront -run '^$' -bench Transport -benchtime 3s -count 5` on an Apple M4
Max (Go 1.27.1), the front before a stub emulator that answers at once, medians of five runs,
ServeHTTP gave 224k published messages/s against grpc-go's transport's 513k (ten 1 KiB messages
a call, 64 callers), 1.38M streaming-pulled messages/s against 2.12M (one stream, batches of a
hundred 1 KiB messages), and a unary GetTopic round trip of 126 µs mean, 118 µs p50 and 350 µs
p99 against 99, 92 and 269 µs. The front measured as grpc-go's transport does: 520k, 2.16M, and
99, 92 and 270 µs (#950); the per-request watch #963 added is measured in its PR, within 5% of
those. **An HTTP/1.1 `Upgrade: h2c`** (`Connection: Upgrade,
HTTP2-Settings`, as `curl --http2` sends on an http:// URL) is answered 101 and the connection
served as HTTP/2 from then on, the request as its stream 1, with every later request routed by
its content type (unit `TestUpgradeToH2C`); one with a malformed `HTTP2-Settings` is answered
over HTTP/1.1 (`TestAMalformedUpgradeIsServedOverHTTP1`). **Through the host tunnel too**
(#964): the tunnel's Host check passes the upgrade request on whole, `HTTP2-Settings` included,
and the connection after the front's 101 is copied both ways, its HTTP/2 requests not checked
one by one (no browser can ask for the switch: it cannot set those headers, and speaks HTTP/2
only over TLS); a foreign Host is still refused 421, and a port that does not take the upgrade
answers over HTTP/1.1 as before (unit `TestGuardPassesAnH2CUpgrade`,
`TestGuardChecksAnH2CUpgradeAndLeavesItToThePort`). `TestPubSubRESTOverH2CUpgrade` runs `curl
--http2` through the tunnel and gets 101, then HTTP/2 200 with the topic the official gRPC client
made. The
[subscription properties page](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/subscription-properties) and
`Subscription.expiration_policy` in `google/pubsub/v1/pubsub.proto` are the rules it follows: a
subscription is active while a subscriber is "issuing operations on the subscription", "Examples of
subscriber activities include open connections, active pulls, or successful pushes", the default
ttl is 31 days, the minimum 1 day, a policy without a ttl never expires, and a ttl "must be at
least as long as the message retention duration". Neither source names a maximum, so none is
enforced. A second method on the same port, `cloudburrow.pubsub.v1.EmulatorClock/Advance`
(a `google.protobuf.Duration` in, the front's time out), moves the front's clock forward, so tests
pass a day in a moment instead of using a ttl Google refuses. It is not part of the Pub/Sub API,
and it grants nothing a caller could not already do, since the emulator has no authentication and
anyone who reaches the port can delete a subscription. Because the front runs from the storage
image, a Pub/Sub instance now needs a CLI with the embedded Linux binaries (`make build` or a
release), as Cloud Storage already did.

Since #880 the front also relays the emulator's pushes, refuses exactly-once delivery on a push or
export subscription (see the Exactly-once delivery row), and answers three more CloudBurrow
methods, for `cloudburrow state save` and `load`: `cloudburrow.pubsub.v1.SubscriptionActivity/Export`
and `/Import` read and set how long each subscription has been idle (a `google.protobuf.Struct` of
seconds by subscription name), and `cloudburrow.pubsub.v1.Projects/List` names every project a call
through the front has named (a `google.protobuf.ListValue`), since the emulator serves any project
and cannot list them. **The push relay:** the front hands the emulator, for every push
subscription, an endpoint of its own on the pod's loopback (port 8087) that carries the
subscription and the real endpoint, and puts the real endpoint back in every subscription the
emulator returns (`CreateSubscription`, `GetSubscription`, `UpdateSubscription`,
`ListSubscriptions`), so no client sees the relay's. Each push is forwarded to the real endpoint
with its method, headers and body, and the endpoint's status, headers and body are the emulator's
answer; one Google counts as a success (102, 200, 201, 202 or 204, from
[the push page](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/push)) is activity on the subscription. An
endpoint the relay cannot reach is a 502 to the emulator, which retries it as it would any failed
push.

Since #891 the front also applies an `UpdateSubscription` of `expiration_policy`, which the
emulator refuses ("Updating the expiration_policy field is currently unsupported in the Pub/Sub
Emulator"). It takes the path out of the mask the emulator sees and forwards the rest; an update of
that path alone never reaches the emulator. The new ttl is checked by the same rules as on create
(at least 1 day, and no shorter than the message retention, the new one when the same update
changes it), then kept in the front, which puts it in every subscription it returns
(`GetSubscription`, `ListSubscriptions`, `UpdateSubscription`) and enforces it in place of the
emulator's stored policy. A `CreateSubscription` or `DeleteSubscription` of the name, or the
subscription's expiry, drops it. An update that names the path with no policy is read as a
subscription created without one: Google's 31-day default (CloudBurrow's reading; the API reference
does not say). `state save` reads through the front, so it saves the updated policy, and `state load`
creates the subscription with it, which the emulator then keeps (unit
`TestPubSubStateKeepsAnUpdatedExpiration`). **The kept policies survive a restart of the front's
container alone** (#898): the front keeps them, its clock's offset, each subscription's last
activity and the projects calls have named in a file on an `emptyDir` volume of the Pub/Sub pod
(`/var/lib/pubsub-front/state.json`, `--state-file`), restored when it starts. The volume outlives
the front's container and goes with the pod, as the emulator's resources do, so a pod restart
loses both together and a front restart loses neither. A policy change, a clock advance and an
activity import are written before the call is answered; activity and projects at most a second
later, and when the front stops, so a front killed outright loses at most a second of activity.
A file that cannot be read as state is logged and replaced, and the front starts without it.
`TestPubSubFrontRestartKeepsItsState` stops the front's container alone through the node's
container runtime, the emulator's untouched, and through the official client a subscription whose
1-day ttl was updated to 2 days still reads 2 days after the restart and is gone once idle for 2
days, one untouched since before the restart is gone 25 hours on, and the clock has not gone back
(unit `TestStateSurvivesARestartOfTheFront`, `TestStateDropsADeletedSubscriptionsPolicy`,
`TestKeepStateRefusesAnUnwritablePathAndReplacesAnUnreadableFile`). The labels an update set
(#949) are kept in the same file, written before the update is answered, and dropped with the
topic or subscription (unit `TestStateKeepsLabels`). **Over REST too** (#908): a `PATCH .../subscriptions/{s}` whose `updateMask` names
`expirationPolicy` (what `gcloud pubsub subscriptions update --expiration-period` sends) is
checked the same way, the path is taken out of the mask and the subscription the emulator is sent,
a PATCH of that path alone is answered by the front, and the kept policy is in every REST read
(`PUT`, `GET`, `PATCH .../subscriptions/{s}`, `GET .../subscriptions`); a `PUT` of the name drops
it. `TestGcloudPubSubUpdateExpiration`: `--expiration-period=12h` is refused; 3d and `never` are
applied, read back by `describe`, `list`, REST `GET` and the gRPC client, and enforced (with a
1-day ttl raised to 3 days, kept 25 hours on and gone once idle for 73; never, kept), and a plain
REST PATCH of the policy with the ack deadline applies both (unit
`TestRESTPatchSetsTheExpirationPolicy`, `TestRESTUpdateChecksThePolicy`). **A mask in the URL**
(#928): Terraform's google provider sends `?updateMask=expirationPolicy,bigqueryConfig`, camelCase,
in the URL, with `bigqueryConfig` in every update. The emulator reads a URL mask as one path, commas
and all ("ack_deadline_seconds,bigquery_config is not a known Subscription field", measured), and
refuses a `bigquery_config` path whatever it sets. The front reads the URL's mask with the body's,
applies its rules to both, and sends the emulator the rest in the body, snake_case, with no URL
mask; an export config path (`bigqueryConfig`, `cloudStorageConfig`, `bigtableConfig`) that sets
nothing on a subscription with none of that export is a no-op, and is left out.
`TestTerraformPubSubPushAndExpiration`: a `google_pubsub_subscription` with
`push_config.push_endpoint` and `expiration_policy.ttl` applies through `cloudburrow terraform`,
plans clean (the provider reads the real endpoint and the ttl; its state never names the relay),
takes a change of the ttl (applied by the front, the emulator sent nothing) and of the endpoint
(sent to the emulator as the relay's), each read back by the official client and planning clean,
and destroys (unit `TestRESTPatchReadsTheMaskInTheURL`). A `labels` change is applied by the front
(#949, `TestTerraformSchedulerAndSubscription`).

**REST clients get the same** (#908). A push endpoint sent over REST, in `PUT
.../subscriptions/{s}` (`pushConfig.pushEndpoint`), in a `PATCH` whose `updateMask` names
`pushConfig`, or in `POST .../subscriptions/{s}:modifyPushConfig`, reaches the emulator as the
relay's, and the answers to `PUT`, `GET` and `PATCH .../subscriptions/{s}` and `GET
.../subscriptions` name the real one, with every other field of the JSON as the emulator sent it.
Exactly-once delivery with a push endpoint or an export is refused 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` on `PUT`,
`PATCH` and `:modifyPushConfig`, by the same checks as gRPC. Every `/v1/projects/{p}/...` path
records its project for `Projects/List`, so `cloudburrow state save` captures a project only
gcloud or Terraform used. `TestGcloudPubSubPushSubscription`: of four push subscriptions gcloud
makes with a 1-day ttl, the three given a storage-server upload endpoint by `subscriptions create
--push-endpoint`, `subscriptions update --push-endpoint` and `modify-push-config` are kept 25 hours
on with pushes at 0 and 20, and the one whose endpoint refuses its pushes is gone; `describe`,
`list` and the gRPC client read each real endpoint. `TestGcloudPubSubRefusesExactlyOnceWithPush`
and `TestPubSubRESTPushAndExactlyOnce` (plain REST, including a BigQuery export and an endpoint set
over gRPC read back over REST) assert the refusals and the reads. `TestGcloudPubSubStateSave`: a
project only gcloud used is saved, reset and loaded, and gcloud describes its subscriptions as they
were. Unit `TestRESTPushEndpointsGoToTheRelay`, `TestRESTReadsNameTheRealEndpoint`,
`TestRESTRefusesExactlyOnceWithPush`, `TestRESTProjectsAreListed`. **An answer over 4 MiB**
(#926), the most the front holds whole to rewrite, is streamed: a list of subscriptions is
rewritten one subscription at a time as it passes, and a single subscription (never that large)
is passed on as it came; it was a 503 before. An oversized answer that is not a list object ends
in a failed read, never a short answer that looks whole. `TestPubSubRESTListOverFourMiB`: 900
subscriptions with 64 labels each, made by the official client, list in one page of about 4.9 MB
with `pageSize=1000` (a plain REST GET, as no official client asks for a page that large), every one
in it and the push subscription's real endpoint named (unit `TestRESTOversizedAnswersPassThrough`,
`TestRewriteListKeepsEveryField`).

The subscription then reads back `detached: true` on `_deleted-topic_` and is still in `ListSubscriptions`; `ListTopicSubscriptions` no longer names it; `Pull` and `StreamingPull` fail `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, as documented; a message published afterwards reaches a sibling subscription and not it; `DeleteSubscription` removes it. Over REST too (`POST …:detach`, `TestRESTDetachSubscription`), and by `gcloud pubsub topics detach-subscription` (`TestGcloudPubSubDetachAndProtobufSchemas`). **Every other call on a detached subscription is answered as Google documents a detached subscription** (#1446, `internal/pubsubfront/detachedcalls.go`): it is still a subscription, it retains no backlog and it cannot be reattached. `TestPubSubDetachedSubscriptionCalls`, through the official `pubsub/v2` admin client: `UpdateSubscription` (ack deadline, labels, retry policy) and `ModifyPushConfig` change its configuration, read back by `GetSubscription` with it still detached on `_deleted-topic_`; a mask naming `topic` or an unknown field is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and one clearing `detached` `FAILED_PRECONDITION`; `Acknowledge` and `ModifyAckDeadline` succeed, as no message is outstanding (with exactly-once delivery each ack ID is reported `PERMANENT_FAILURE_INVALID_ACK_ID` in the `EXACTLY_ONCE_ACKID_FAILURE` ErrorInfo the client reads); `Seek` to a time succeeds and changes nothing; `Seek` to a snapshot of its old topic and `CreateSnapshot` of it fail `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, as both need the subscription's topic, and a seek to an absent snapshot is `NOT_FOUND`. Unit `TestUpdateSubscriptionSwitchesToBigQueryAndBack`, `TestExportSwitchIsKeptInTheStateFile`, and over REST `TestRESTPatchReadsTheMaskInTheURL`. |
| Label rules (topics and subscriptions) | **Verified** (message UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/labels>)) | CloudBurrow's front checks the labels of `CreateTopic`, `CreateSubscription`, and an `UpdateTopic` or `UpdateSubscription` whose mask names `labels`, over gRPC and REST (`PUT` and `PATCH` of `topics/{t}` and `subscriptions/{s}`), against Google's [labels requirements](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/labels) (#962): at most 64 labels; a key 1 to 63 characters, a value 0 to 63; only lowercase letters, international characters, digits, `_` and `-`; a key starting with a lowercase letter or an international character. Read as Unicode categories: lowercase is `Ll`, international a letter with no case (`Lo`), a digit `N`; characters, not bytes, are counted. A label that breaks a rule is refused **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`** (HTTP 400), the code Google's [error codes](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/reference/error-codes) give an invalid argument, before the emulator is sent anything; the message names the label and the rule, and is CloudBurrow's own: Google's message for it was not measured. The emulator checks no label at all. `TestPubSubLabelsAreHeldToGoogleRules`, through the official client and over REST: an uppercase key, a key starting with a digit, a value with a space and 65 labels are refused on create, an uppercase value and a dot in a key on update, and nothing is stored; 64 labels, 63-character keys and values, `größe=日本` and an empty value are created and read back. A topic bound to a schema refuses a message that does not conform (`TestConsolePubSubCreateOptions`, #852). The only revision cannot be deleted (`INVALID_ARGUMENT` "Cannot delete last revision. Please use DeleteSchema."), asserted by `TestConsolePubSubSchemas`. **Protocol Buffer schemas are served by CloudBurrow's Pub/Sub front** (#1406): the emulator refuses them (`UNIMPLEMENTED` "Protocol buffer support not implemented in emulator"), so the front parses the `.proto` definition itself (`internal/pubsubfront/protoschema.go`: proto2 or proto3, one top-level message, no imports, as Google documents; resolved with `protodesc`) and keeps the schema and its revisions. `TestPubSubProtobufSchemaService` drives all ten RPCs with a `PROTOCOL_BUFFER` schema through the same client: a definition with two top-level types, an import or a syntax error is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; `ValidateMessage` accepts a conforming message and refuses a non-conforming one in JSON and BINARY, and a proto2 message missing a required field; commit, revisions, rollback, delete revision and delete as for AVRO. `ListSchemas` names the front's schemas after the emulator's. A topic bound to one (`TestPubSubProtobufSchemaTopic`, JSON and BINARY) reads back its binding, and a non-conforming `Publish` is refused `INVALID_ARGUMENT` "Invalid data in message: Message failed schema validation." while a conforming one is delivered. `gcloud pubsub schemas validate-schema`, `create --type=protocol-buffer`, `describe`, `validate-message` and `delete` (`TestGcloudPubSubDetachAndProtobufSchemas`), and Terraform's `google_pubsub_schema` of type `PROTOCOL_BUFFER` with a topic bound to it (`TestTerraformPubSubProtobufSchema`), go through it too. **An `UpdateTopic` of `schema_settings` that names such a schema, or is on a topic bound to one, rebinds or clears the binding** (#1446): `TestPubSubProtobufSchemaTopic` binds the JSON topic BINARY from the latest revision on, a JSON message is then refused and a BINARY one accepted, an absent revision is `NOT_FOUND`, an empty `schema_settings` clears it (any message is then accepted) and binding it again restores the check; `gcloud pubsub topics update --schema=… --message-encoding=json` and `--clear-schema-settings` (`TestGcloudPubSubDetachAndProtobufSchemas`), and Terraform changing the `google_pubsub_topic`'s encoding in place (`TestTerraformPubSubProtobufSchema`), go through it too. The front's error messages for a refused definition or message are its own (Google's are not measured). |
| Snapshots (`Subscriber.CreateSnapshot`, `Subscriber.GetSnapshot`, `Subscriber.DeleteSnapshot`) / `Seek` | **Verified** | `TestSnapshotsAndSeekAreSupported` — create, get, seek-to-snapshot and delete. **The matrix was wrong**: a test written to confirm these were refused found they work. That test does not show replay; `TestConsolePubSubSnapshotsAndSeek` (#787) does, through the official client: after two messages are pulled and acknowledged, a Seek to a snapshot taken while the first was waiting makes the next pull receive both again, and a Seek to a time after them marks every message acknowledged. A Seek to a snapshot of another topic is refused `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. **`CreateSnapshot` does not keep labels**: a snapshot created with labels reads back with none (same test). |
| `Subscriber.ListSnapshots` | **Verified** | `TestPubSubTopicAndSnapshotListings` |
| IAM, `google.iam.v1.IAMPolicy` on topics, subscriptions, snapshots and schemas: `pubsub.projects.topics.getIamPolicy`, `pubsub.projects.topics.setIamPolicy`, `pubsub.projects.topics.testIamPermissions`, `pubsub.projects.subscriptions.getIamPolicy`, `pubsub.projects.subscriptions.setIamPolicy`, `pubsub.projects.subscriptions.testIamPermissions`, `pubsub.projects.snapshots.getIamPolicy`, `pubsub.projects.snapshots.setIamPolicy`, `pubsub.projects.snapshots.testIamPermissions`, `pubsub.projects.schemas.getIamPolicy`, `pubsub.projects.schemas.setIamPolicy`, `pubsub.projects.schemas.testIamPermissions` | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | Served by CloudBurrow's front (`internal/pubsubfront/iam.go`, #1367), over gRPC and REST (`GET` or `POST :getIamPolicy`, `POST :setIamPolicy`, `POST :testIamPermissions`), under [ADR-0006](adr/0006-iam-policy-surface.md) as amended by #1367, through the shared `internal/iampolicy`: a policy round-trips with a new etag, a stale etag is `ABORTED` (409 over REST), a condition is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming it (#1745: Pub/Sub is not among the services Google lists as allowing conditions), a version 3 policy without conditions is accepted, and a resource the emulator does not have is `NOT_FOUND` to `GetIamPolicy` and `SetIamPolicy`. `TestIamPermissions` returns, of the permissions asked, those Pub/Sub defines on that kind of resource (`pubsub.topics.publish` on a topic, not `pubsub.subscriptions.consume`): nothing is denied; on a resource that does not exist it returns none, not `NOT_FOUND`, as iam_policy.proto documents (#1595, `TestPubSubIAMHandle`, `TestPubSubIAMOnASnapshotAndASchema`). **No Pub/Sub call consults a policy.** Deleting a topic, subscription, snapshot or schema, an expiry, or creating one of the same name, drops its policy, so `/admin/reset` clears them; the policies are in the front's state file. `TestPubSubIAMHandle` (the `iam.Handle` that `topic.IAM()` and `sub.IAM()` return, and the v2 admin clients), `TestPubSubIAMOnASnapshotAndASchema`, `TestGcloudPubSubIAM` (`gcloud pubsub topics add-iam-policy-binding`, `get-iam-policy`, `remove-iam-policy-binding` and the subscription ones, egress blocked), `TestTerraformPubSubIAM` (`google_pubsub_topic_iam_*`, `google_pubsub_subscription_iam_*` and `google_pubsub_schema_iam_*`, member, binding and policy), and the console's Permissions tab on a topic's and a subscription's page (`TestConsolePermissionsOnATopicAndASubscription`). Unit: `TestIAMPolicyOnATopicAndASubscription`, `TestRESTIAMPolicy`, `TestStateKeepsIAMPolicies`. Which permissions Google answers on a resource, and its answer on a missing one, are UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/iam/v1/iam_policy.proto>). |
| `Subscriber.UpdateSnapshot` | **Verified** | `TestPubSubUpdateSnapshot` (#1406), through the official `pubsub/v2` admin client. Google's emulator refuses it (`UNIMPLEMENTED` "Method google.pubsub.v1.Subscriber/UpdateSnapshot is unimplemented"); CloudBurrow's Pub/Sub front applies it (`internal/pubsubfront/snapshots.go`), as it applies topic labels (#949): `labels` and `expire_time`, through the update mask, kept in the front and named by `GetSnapshot`, `ListSnapshots` and `UpdateSnapshot`, over gRPC and REST (`PATCH …/snapshots/{s}`). A mask naming anything else, labels Google refuses, or an `expire_time` in the past or after the snapshot's own (Google: "A newly-created snapshot expires no later than 7 days from the time of its creation") is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; the front deletes the snapshot once the kept `expire_time` passes. |

### Data plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Publisher.Publish` | **Verified** | `TestPubSubPublishAndPull`, data and attributes both asserted. |
| `Subscriber.Pull` | **Verified** | `TestPubSubPublishAndPull` |
| `Subscriber.StreamingPull` | **Verified** | `TestPubSubStreamingPull` delivers 20 distinct messages through the SDK's default `Receive` path. |
| `Acknowledge` | **Verified** | `TestPubSubPublishAndPull` |
| `ModifyAckDeadline` | **Verified** | `TestPubSubRedeliveryAfterNack` |
| Ack-deadline expiry and redelivery | **Verified** | `TestPubSubRedeliveryAfterNack`: returning the deadline redelivers the message. At-least-once, so duplicates remain possible by design. |
| Push delivery to HTTP endpoint | **Verified** | The acceptance workflow pushes to a Cloud Run service at its cluster-local address. `TestPubSubPushSubscriptionExpiresWithoutSuccessfulPushes` (#880) pushes to the builtin storage server's upload endpoint by its Service name, which stores the push envelope the test reads back. Every push passes through the front's relay (see CloudBurrow's front). |
| Ordering keys | **Verified** | `TestPubSubOrderingKeys`: order preserved within a single key. Ordering *across* keys is not claimed. |
| Dead-letter topics | **Verified** | `TestDeadLetterPolicyIsRecorded`: the policy round-trips, topic and max attempts included. `TestPubSubDeadLetterDelivery`: with `max_delivery_attempts=5`, a message nacked on each delivery is delivered with `delivery_attempt` 1 to 5, then appears on the dead-letter topic's subscription with its data and `CloudPubSubDeadLetterSourceDeliveryCount=5`, in under a second. |
| Subscription expiration | **Verified** | Enforced by CloudBurrow's front (above), not the emulator. `TestPubSubSubscriptionExpiresWhenIdle` (#873): with a 1-day ttl, a subscription nothing touches is gone from `ListSubscriptions` 25 hours after creation and `GetSubscription` answers `NOT_FOUND`; one pulled at 20 hours is kept at 25 and gone at 45; one with a streaming pull open throughout is kept at 45; one whose policy has no ttl, and one created with no policy (which reads back a 31-day ttl), are kept. Time passes through the front's clock. `TestPubSubRefusesAnExpirationGoogleRefuses`: a ttl of 12h, a 1-day ttl with the default 7-day retention, and a 2-day ttl with a 3-day retention are each refused `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and create nothing (error code UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/subscription-properties>): Google documents the rule, not the code); a 1-day ttl with a 1-day retention is created. Unit tests in `internal/pubsubfront` also cover an `UpdateSubscription` that would raise the retention above the ttl (refused) and the 31-day default expiring. **Push subscriptions** (#880): the front relays the emulator's pushes (above), so a successful push is activity. `TestPubSubPushSubscriptionExpiresWithoutSuccessfulPushes`: of two push subscriptions with a 1-day ttl, the one whose endpoint (the builtin storage server's upload endpoint, in the cluster) stores its pushes, and so answers 200, is kept 25 hours after creation with a push at 20; the one whose endpoint refuses them (404) is gone. The same holds for push subscriptions gcloud makes over REST (`TestGcloudPubSubPushSubscription`, #908). The endpoint receives the emulator's push envelope unchanged, and `GetSubscription` and `ListSubscriptions` read the real endpoint, never the relay's (unit `TestPushRelayObservesPushes`, `TestPushRelayRefusesOtherAddresses`). **Gaps:** activity is any call naming the subscription except a read of its configuration (`GetSubscription` and its REST `GET`, which are not activity since #1039: Google names "open connections, active pulls, or successful pushes") (update, pull, streaming pull, acknowledge, modify ack deadline, modify push config, seek, create snapshot), which may count more as activity than Google does; a push subscription with no messages to push has no activity but calls, as on Google; the front's clock, its activity records and its kept policies survive a restart of the front's container alone (#898, `TestPubSubFrontRestartKeepsItsState`, above), a front killed outright losing at most the last second of activity, and are lost with the pod, as the emulator's state is. **An updated policy is enforced** (#891): in `TestPubSubExpirationCanBeUpdated` a subscription created with a 1-day ttl and updated to 3 days is kept 25 hours later and gone once idle for 73, and one updated to never expire is kept (unit `TestUpdatedExpirationIsEnforced`). |
| Exactly-once delivery | **Verified** | Implemented by the emulator itself; the front passes it through. `TestPubSubExactlyOnceDelivery` (#873), through the official client on a subscription with `enable_exactly_once_delivery` and a 10s deadline: `AckWithResult` reports `AcknowledgeStatusSuccess` and the acknowledged message is not delivered again in the 15 seconds after; a message left unacknowledged is not resent before its deadline, is resent with a new ack ID after it, and `Acknowledge` with the old ack ID is refused `INVALID_ARGUMENT` whose `ErrorInfo` marks it `PERMANENT_FAILURE_INVALID_ACK_ID`, as [Google's exactly-once page](https://cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/exactly-once-delivery) describes, while the new ack ID is accepted. **With a push endpoint, refused** (#880): Google says "Push and export subscriptions don't support exactly-once delivery", and the emulator accepts the pair, so the front refuses it `INVALID_ARGUMENT` ("exactly-once delivery is supported only for pull subscriptions: push and export subscriptions don't support exactly-once delivery") on `CreateSubscription`, on an `UpdateSubscription` whose result would have both, and on `ModifyPushConfig` giving an exactly-once subscription an endpoint, changing nothing (`TestPubSubRefusesExactlyOnceWithPush`; over REST, from gcloud and plain HTTP, `TestGcloudPubSubRefusesExactlyOnceWithPush` and `TestPubSubRESTPushAndExactlyOnce`, #908; error code and message UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/exactly-once-delivery>): Google documents the rule, not the error). A BigQuery, Cloud Storage or Bigtable export with it is refused the same way (unit `TestExactlyOnceIsRefusedWithPush`). Changing it on an existing subscription: see `UpdateSubscription`. |
| BigQuery subscriptions | **Verified** | Delivered by the front (#1874, `internal/pubsubfront/exportbq.go`): it pulls the subscription's messages from the emulator, streams each into the local BigQuery table with `tabledata.insertAll` (the message ID as `insertId`) and acknowledges it once written, to [Google's BigQuery subscriptions page](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/bigquery). The `data` column (BYTES, STRING or JSON), `write_metadata` (`subscription_name`, `message_id`, `publish_time`, `attributes`), `use_table_schema`, `use_topic_schema` with Google's Avro and Protocol Buffer type mapping, and `drop_unknown_fields` are written as Google documents; `CreateSubscription` refuses a missing table `NOT_FOUND` and a table that does not fit `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; `state` reads `ACTIVE`, `NOT_FOUND` or `SCHEMA_MISMATCH` (and `PERMISSION_DENIED` when the instance serves no BigQuery); a message that cannot be written is nacked and, with a dead-letter policy, forwarded after `max_delivery_attempts` with `CloudPubSubDeadLetterSourceDeliveryErrorMessage`. `TestPubSubBigQuerySubscriptionWritesRows` through the official Pub/Sub and BigQuery clients. Each failure state is reached and recovered from, as [Google's troubleshooting page](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/bigquery-troubleshooting) describes ("the subscription eventually returns to a healthy state"), the messages kept in the backlog and not dead-lettered meanwhile ("They are not sent to a dead-letter topic"), and written once fixed: `NOT_FOUND` (table deleted, then created again) and `SCHEMA_MISMATCH` (table without its `data` column, then fixed), `TestPubSubBigQuerySubscriptionStatesRecover`; `PERMISSION_DENIED` while the BigQuery API is disabled in the subscription's project (the front's calls name it as their quota project), `TestPubSubBigQuerySubscriptionPermissionDenied`; `IN_TRANSIT_LOCATION_RESTRICTION` for a topic whose `message_storage_policy` sets `enforce_in_transit` and a dataset outside its `allowed_persistence_regions` (a multi-region is never one region), until the dataset is in an allowed region, `TestPubSubBigQuerySubscriptionInTransit`. `use_topic_schema` with `write_metadata` (a JSON `attributes` column) and `drop_unknown_fields`, and the same table refused without it, `TestPubSubBigQuerySubscriptionTopicSchemaMetadata`. From gcloud (`--bigquery-table`, `--write-metadata`), `TestGcloudPubSubExportSubscriptions`, and Terraform (`bigquery_config` with `use_table_schema`, `drop_unknown_fields`), `TestTerraformPubSubExportSubscriptions`. **Writer roles under `--iam-enforcement=on`** (#1998, `internal/pubsubfront/exportiam.go`): the subscription writes as its project's Pub/Sub service agent (`service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-pubsub.iam.gserviceaccount.com`) or its `service_account_email`, which needs `bigquery.tables.get` and `bigquery.tables.updateData` (BigQuery Data Editor) on the table, its dataset or its project, as the host's evaluator (`internal/iameval`) decides; a `service_account_email` needs the service agent's `iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken` on it and its creator's `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` (`PERMISSION_DENIED`). Without the roles `CreateSubscription` is refused with the troubleshooting page's "Service account ... is missing permissions required to write to the BigQuery table: bigquery.tables.get, bigquery.tables.updateData." (`FAILED_PRECONDITION`; the code is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-20: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/bigquery-troubleshooting>), the page quotes the text alone), and a subscription whose account loses the role reads `PERMISSION_DENIED`, its messages kept, and `ACTIVE` once it is granted again: `TestIAMEnforcementPubSubBigQueryServiceAgentRoles`, with the role on the table's own policy. Change data capture (#1999, `internal/pubsubfront/exportcdc.go`), `TestPubSubBigQuerySubscriptionChangeDataCapture`: with `use_table_schema` (JSON messages) or `use_topic_schema` (an Avro schema with the fields), a message with `_CHANGE_TYPE` `UPSERT` or `DELETE` updates, inserts or deletes the row of its primary key, ordered by `_CHANGE_SEQUENCE_NUMBER` (a lower number than a key's highest has no effect), written as Google's subscriptions write it, through the Storage Write API's `_default` stream with the pseudo-columns (row *Storage Write API: change data capture*); with neither option the message is the `data` column's value as it is; `use_topic_schema` whose schema has `_CHANGE_TYPE`, to a table without a primary key, is refused `INVALID_ARGUMENT` at creation ("the BigQuery table must have a primary key"; `SCHEMA_MISMATCH` if the key goes later); a `use_table_schema` change to such a table, a `_CHANGE_TYPE` other than `UPSERT` or `DELETE` and a malformed sequence number are not written and are dead-lettered with the reason. The exact text of Google's other create-time errors is not documented, so CloudBurrow's own is given. |
| Cloud Storage subscriptions | **Verified** | Delivered by the front (#1874, `internal/pubsubfront/exportgcs.go`), to [Google's Cloud Storage subscriptions pages](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/create-cloudstorage-subscription): batches closed by `max_messages` (at least 1000), `max_bytes` (1 KB to 10 GiB) or `max_duration` (1 to 10 minutes, 5 by default, on the front's clock, which `EmulatorClock/Advance` moves), objects named `<prefix><UTC-date-time>_<uuid><suffix>` with `filename_datetime_format`, text output (messages separated by newlines) and Avro output (`PubsubMessage`, or `PubsubMessageWithMetadata` with `write_metadata`); a missing bucket refused `NOT_FOUND` and a suffix ending in `/` or limits out of range `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. `TestPubSubCloudStorageSubscriptionWritesObjects` through the official Pub/Sub and Storage clients. `max_messages` and `max_bytes` each close a batch before `max_duration`, and an object is named exactly `<prefix><YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss+00:00>_<uuid><suffix>`, `TestPubSubCloudStorageSubscriptionBatchLimits`. `avro_config.use_topic_schema` writes the topic's Avro schema, with `write_metadata`'s `subscription_name`, `message_id`, `publish_time` and `attributes` as top-level fields of its root record (a topic without a schema, a schema that is not Avro, or, with `write_metadata`, a root that is not a record or has a field of those names, refused `INVALID_ARGUMENT`), one object per schema revision, `TestPubSubCloudStorageSubscriptionAvroTopicSchema`. `NOT_FOUND` (bucket deleted, then created again) and `IN_TRANSIT_LOCATION_RESTRICTION` (a bucket outside an `enforce_in_transit` topic's regions, until it is in one) are reached and recovered from, the messages held meanwhile not dead-lettered ("Messages also aren't sent to a dead-letter topic while the subscription is in error", [troubleshooting](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/cloudstorage-troubleshooting)) and written once fixed, `TestPubSubCloudStorageSubscriptionStatesRecover`; `PERMISSION_DENIED` is the state while the Cloud Storage API is disabled in the subscription's project, the message kept and written once it is enabled, `TestPubSubCloudStorageSubscriptionPermissionDenied`. From gcloud (`--cloud-storage-bucket`, `--cloud-storage-file-prefix`, `-file-suffix`, `-file-datetime-format`, `-max-bytes`, `-max-duration`, `-max-messages`, `-output-format=avro`, `-write-metadata`), `TestGcloudPubSubExportSubscriptions`, and Terraform (`cloud_storage_config` with `avro_config`), `TestTerraformPubSubExportSubscriptions`. **Writer roles under `--iam-enforcement=on`**, as for BigQuery subscriptions (#1998): Storage Object Creator (`storage.objects.create`) and Storage Legacy Bucket Reader (`storage.buckets.get`) on the bucket or its project, refused at create with the troubleshooting page's "Cloud Pub/Sub did not have the necessary permissions configured to access the provided bucket ... (or the bucket may not exist). Please verify that the service account ... was granted the Storage Legacy Bucket Reader and Storage Object Creator roles for the provided bucket.", `PERMISSION_DENIED` when one is removed and `ACTIVE` once it is back, `TestIAMEnforcementPubSubStorageServiceAgentRoles`; a `service_account_email` its caller lacks `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` on is refused `PERMISSION_DENIED`, then, with Service Account User, refused until the service agent has `iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken` on it and it has the bucket roles itself, `TestIAMEnforcementPubSubExportServiceAccountActAs`. |
| CMEK topics (`kms_key_name`) | **Verified** | Checked by the front against the instance's Cloud KMS (#1874, `internal/pubsubfront/cmek.go`), to [Google's encryption page](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/encryption): the key name's form (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`), the key's existence (`NOT_FOUND`), purpose `ENCRYPT_DECRYPT`, an enabled primary version (`FAILED_PRECONDITION`), and a regional key against the topic's allowed persistence regions; while the key is disabled, `Publish`, `Pull` and `StreamingPull` fail `FAILED_PRECONDITION` and export subscriptions deliver nothing. `TestPubSubCMEKTopic` through the official Pub/Sub and Cloud KMS clients, which also enables the key version again and sees `Publish` and `Pull` work again on the same topic. The emulator keeps messages in memory only, so there is nothing at rest to encrypt. |
| Schema revision creation time | **Verified** | The emulator answers Avro revisions with a `revision_create_time` in 1970; the front answers the time it first saw each revision (#1874, `internal/pubsubfront/schematime.go`). `TestPubSubAvroSchemaRevisionTime`. |
