## Cloud Tasks — `google.cloud.tasks.v2`

**Backing component:** none — implemented by CloudBurrow. No official emulator exists and no
viable community implementation was found (#24).

**It runs in the CLI process, not the cluster**, since there is no upstream workload to
deploy. Its dispatch targets are therefore addresses reachable from the host. There is **no
emulator environment variable** in any official client, so the endpoint and insecure
credentials must be passed explicitly in client options — see `test/compat/tasks_test.go`
for the exact form.
Contract: `google/cloud/tasks/v2/cloudtasks.proto`.
**No emulator environment variable exists.** Callers must set an explicit endpoint and
disable authentication in client options. This is a documented ergonomic limit.

### Control plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateQueue` | **Verified** | `TestTasksQueueLifecycle`, via the official `cloudtasks/apiv2` client. Contract defaults are returned, each `retry_config` and `rate_limits` field defaulting on its own: before #692 a queue given only `max_dispatches_per_second` had it replaced by the default. |
| `GetQueue` | **Verified** | `TestTasksQueueLifecycle`, including `NotFound` for an absent queue. |
| `ListQueues` | **Verified** | `TestTasksListQueues`; pagination covered by unit tests. A **`filter` on `state`** (`:`, `=` or `!=` `RUNNING`, `PAUSED` or `DISABLED`; Google's sample is `state: PAUSED`) is honoured (`TestTasksListQueuesFiltersByState`, #1222). Since #1255 a filter on **any Queue field** is honoured, as the reference documents (`TestTasksListQueuesFiltersOnQueueFields`): a dotted path in snake_case or lowerCamelCase (`rate_limits.max_dispatches_per_second`, `retryConfig.maxAttempts`) ending on a string, number, enum, `Duration` (`90s`) or `Timestamp` (RFC 3339, quoted), with `=`, `!=`, `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` and `:` (a case-insensitive substring on a string, `FIELD:*` for set), combined with `AND` (or a space), `OR` and `NOT` (or `-`), with parentheses; an enum takes `=`, `!=` and `:` only. A path that is no Queue field, or a value its field cannot hold, is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`** (Google's wording not measured); Cloud Logging's regular-expression operators `=~` and `!~` take an RE2 expression on a string or enum field (#1943; a bad expression is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`). The console's queue list has a filter box evaluated by the same code (`TestConsoleQueueListFilter`). |
| `retry_config.max_retry_duration` | **Verified** | Stored, returned, and **honoured**: a task is retried until both it and `max_attempts` are exhausted, measured from its first attempt, as `RetryConfig` documents (`TestTasksRefusesWhatItWouldDrop`, unit `TestMaxRetryDurationExtendsRetryingUntilBothLimitsAreReached`, #578). |
| `stackdriver_logging_config` | **Verified** | `TestTasksStackdriverLoggingConfig` (#1256), through `cloud.google.com/go/cloudtasks/apiv2` and `cloud.google.com/go/logging/logadmin`: `sampling_ratio` is kept and returned by `CreateQueue`, `GetQueue` and an `UpdateQueue` whose mask names `stackdriver_logging_config` (or `.sampling_ratio`); a mask naming it with no config clears it, and a ratio outside 0.0 to 1.0 is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**. When the instance serves Cloud Logging, that fraction of dispatch attempts (every one at 1.0, none at 0, the default) is written through the instance's own `WriteLogEntries`, as Cloud Tasks writes it (docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/logging): log `cloudtasks.googleapis.com/task_operations_log`, monitored resource `cloud_tasks_queue` with `project_id`, `location`, `queue_id` and `target_type` (`HTTP`), severity `INFO` for an `OK` attempt and `ERROR` otherwise, and a jsonPayload of `@type` `type.googleapis.com/google.cloud.tasks.logging.v1.TaskActivityLog`, `task` and `attemptResponseLog` (`attemptDuration`, `dispatchCount`, `responseCount`, `maxAttempts`, `scheduleTime`, `status` as a `google.rpc.Code` name converted from the HTTP status, `UNAVAILABLE` or `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` with no response, `targetAddress` as `METHOD URL`, `targetType`, and `retryTime` when the task will be retried); read back with `ListLogEntries`. The console sets it on Edit queue and shows it on the queue's page (`TestConsoleTasksLoggingSampling`). **What differs:** Google documents the log, the resource and the sampling, not the payload field by field: its fields are those of entries Google wrote, and their exact value formats are UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/tasks/docs/logging>). Only attempts are logged, not `CreateTask` or `DeleteTask`. Without Cloud Logging on the instance the config is kept and nothing is written. Attempts are also in the console's operations ledger and `/admin/events`. |
| `http_target` (queue-level routing) | **Verified** | `TestTasksQueueHTTPTarget` (#1282), through the official client: `CreateQueue`, `GetQueue` and `UpdateQueue` (mask `http_target`) keep and return it, and it is applied to each dispatch attempt of the queue's HTTP tasks, from the queue as it is at that attempt. `uri_override` replaces the scheme, host, port (0 clears it), path and query it names, for every task in `ALWAYS` mode (the default) and only for a task with no URL in `IF_NOT_EXISTS` mode; a task may be created with no URL on a queue whose override names a host. `http_method` replaces the task's (a `GET`, `HEAD`, `DELETE` or `OPTIONS` override drops the body), `header_overrides` replace the task's headers of the same name, and `oidc_token` / `oauth_token` replace its token, minted locally as for a task's own. The stored task keeps its own `httpRequest` (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/cloud/tasks/v2/target.proto>) that Google does not rewrite it). An empty host, a port outside 0 to 65535, a header with no key or a token with no service account is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. |
| `app_engine_routing_override` | **Verified**, *stored; delivered to `--appengine-url`* | `TestTasksAppEngineTargets` (#1447), through the official client: `UpdateQueue` (mask `app_engine_routing_override`) and `GetQueue` keep and return it, with the output-only `host` computed as Google documents it (`[instance.][version.][service.]{project}.appspot.com`; a `host` sent is ignored), and it sets the host of every App Engine task in the queue, whatever the task's own routing. `TestTerraformAppEngineTargets` applies it in `google_cloud_tasks_queue`, plans clean, changes it in place and destroys it; `TestGcloudAppEngineTargets` creates a queue with `--routing-override`. The console's **Edit queue** sets it and, with its service, version and instance emptied, clears it (`TestConsoleTasksEditQueueAppEngineRouting`), and a seed document's queue object takes it as `appEngineRoutingOverride` (`TestAppEngineSeedIsReadBackByTheOfficialClients`). With `--appengine-url` its host is the `Host` of each attempt (`TestTasksAppEngineDelivery`, #1506); see the App Engine target row. |
| `DeleteQueue` | **Verified** | Removes the queue's tasks too, so a recreated queue cannot inherit them. Tests: `TestDeleteQueueRemovesItsTasks`. |
| `UpdateQueue` | **Verified** | `TestTasksUpdateQueue` (#692), via the official client: a mask of `retry_config.max_attempts` and `rate_limits` changes those and keeps the rest (`min_backoff` stays), and `GetQueue` reads them back; `gcloud tasks queues update --max-attempts --max-concurrent-dispatches` and Terraform's in-place change of `google_cloud_tasks_queue` do the same over JSON (`TestGcloudTasks`, `TestTerraformAppliesAndDestroysThroughTheWrapper`). **Mask semantics:** a path replaces the field it names, a whole message (`retry_config`) or one field of it (`retry_config.max_attempts`); an **empty mask replaces every settable field**, as the API documents, so a field the request leaves out is cleared and then defaulted as on create. Each field defaults on its own. A path naming `name`, an output-only field (`state`, `purge_time`, `rate_limits.max_burst_size`) or no field is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the path**; `state` is changed by `PauseQueue`/`ResumeQueue` only, and a `state` in the body is ignored. The fields `CreateQueue` refuses are refused when the mask names them: `app_engine_routing_override` is **`UNIMPLEMENTED`**; `http_target` is applied (#1282, below). **A queue that does not exist is created**, as the method documents ("creates the queue if it does not exist"), with `CreateQueue`'s name rules. The dispatcher reads the stored queue on every pass and retry, so an update applies to tasks already queued: a failing task in a queue updated from 5 attempts to 2 stops at 2 (same test; unit `TestAnUpdatedRetryConfigChangesRetrying`). Queues have no etag. **Documented limits are refused** (#784), on `CreateQueue` and on an `UpdateQueue` whose mask names the field: `max_attempts` below -1 ("Must be >= -1"), `max_dispatches_per_second` above 500 and `max_concurrent_dispatches` above 5000 (the contract's "maximum allowed value"), and a negative `min_backoff`, `max_backoff`, `max_doublings` or `max_retry_duration`, each `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the field; before, a value out of range was stored or silently replaced by the default (unit `TestQueueLimitsTheContractDocumentsAreRefused`; through the console, `TestConsoleTasksEditQueueAndCreateTask`). |
| `PauseQueue` / `ResumeQueue` | **Verified** | `TestTasksPauseAndResume`. A paused queue genuinely stops dispatching. |
| `PurgeQueue` | **Verified** | `TestTasksPurgeQueue`: every task in the queue goes and no other queue's, the queue and its state stay, it takes tasks again, and `purge_time` is reported (#691). A missing queue is `NotFound`. |
| `CreateTask` | **Verified** | `TestTasksTaskLifecycle`. Name generation, method, body and headers all round-trip. |
| `GetTask` / `DeleteTask` | **Verified** | `TestTasksTaskLifecycle`. |
| `ListTasks` | **Verified** | `TestGcloudTasks`: `gcloud tasks list` over JSON (#591); also gRPC unit tests. |
| Durability | **Verified, measured** | Queues and tasks follow `--mode`: a store under the state directory in persistent mode, memory in ephemeral mode. CI's restart probe (#596): `TestTasksRestartSetup` runs alone just before `stop` and leaves a paused queue holding a task scheduled a day ahead. After `stop` and `up` in persistent mode, `TestTasksAcrossRestart` finds the queue still `PAUSED` and the task's body and `scheduleTime` unchanged; brought up again with `--mode ephemeral`, `GetQueue` is **NOT_FOUND**. |
| `GetIamPolicy`, `SetIamPolicy` on a queue | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestQueueIamPolicyIsStoredNotEnforced` (#366, [ADR-0006](adr/0006-iam-policy-surface.md)): bindings set through the official client read back with a new etag, and a stale etag is **ABORTED**. **No RPC consults a stored policy**: a binding grants and denies nothing, and dispatch is unaffected. Conditions are **INVALID_ARGUMENT** (#1745: Cloud Tasks is not among the services Google lists as allowing conditions) and audit configs **UNIMPLEMENTED**, with the field named. A version 3 policy without conditions is accepted. The policy is kept on the queue, so it goes with `DeleteQueue`, is cleared by `/admin/reset` and is captured by `state save`. From the console's Permissions tab: `TestConsolePermissionsOnAQueue` (#793). |
| `TestIamPermissions` on a queue | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | Same test: returns **every** requested permission, the literal truth when nothing is enforced. |
| JSON API (`/v2/…/queues`) | **Partial** | On the same port as gRPC, for REST clients such as Terraform (#366). Queues are hand-written routes: create, get, list, delete, pause, resume and purge, and their IAM methods (`:getIamPolicy` by GET or POST), each calling the gRPC server; on them an unknown query parameter is ignored. **`PATCH` (UpdateQueue) is transcoded** (#692), by Google's binding `PATCH /v2/{queue.name=projects/*/locations/*/queues/*}`: `updateMask` is a lowerCamelCase FieldMask converted to proto paths, the path's name wins over the body's, and an unknown query parameter is INVALID_ARGUMENT. Unknown JSON fields are refused. Unit-tested (`TestRESTQueueAndIamPolicy`, `TestRESTUpdateQueue`) and driven by Terraform and gcloud (below). |
| JSON API, tasks (`/v2/…/queues/*/tasks`) | **Verified** | Since #591, through the shared `Transcoder` by Google's own `google.api.http` bindings, with the same `GRPCServer` gRPC registers: CreateTask, ListTasks, GetTask and DeleteTask. RunTask, BatchCreateTasks, BatchDeleteTasks and the CMEK config are transcoded too (#1215). The transcoder's query policy applies to task paths and the queue `PATCH` only: `pageSize`, `pageToken` and `responseView` are fields, and an unknown parameter is INVALID_ARGUMENT, where the queue routes ignore it. The official client's REST transport drives a task's lifecycle (unit `TestRESTTasksWithTheOfficialRESTClient`, `TestRESTTaskPathsRefuseUnknownParameters`), and `TestGcloudTasks` does it with the real gcloud. JSON requests, queues and tasks, appear in `/admin/events`. |

### Data plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP target dispatch | **Verified** | `TestTasksHTTPDispatchCarriesCloudTasksHeaders`: a task created with the official client reaches a host HTTP server with its method, body and headers, and with `X-CloudTasks-QueueName`, `-TaskName`, `-TaskRetryCount` and `-TaskExecutionCount`. The names are **short IDs**, as the service sends them; full resource names were sent until #276. Non-2xx is retried, matching the real service including 4xx. **`X-CloudTasks-TaskETA`, `-TaskPreviousResponse` and `-TaskRetryReason` are not set.** |
| `oidcToken` / `oauthToken` on an HTTP task | **Verified**, *locally minted* | `TestTasksOIDCAndOAuthTokens` (#1243), with the official client: the token config is kept and returned by `CreateTask` and `GetTask`, and a local HTTP target receives `Authorization: Bearer` with the token: an ID token for the service account whose audience is the URL when none is given, signature checked against the instance's `/certs`, or an opaque access token, the scope defaulting to `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`. A token without `serviceAccountEmail` is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**. Before #1243 both were refused `UNIMPLEMENTED` (#578). **What differs from Google:** the token is minted by this instance, not by Google. An OIDC token is an RS256 JWT signed with the instance's own key (the key behind the ADC fixture and the metadata server), so it verifies against the instance's `/certs` and **never against Google's certificates**: a target that verifies it with Google's keys, as Cloud Run's front end does, rejects it, and one that skips verification or checks the claims only accepts it. Its claims are Google's: `iss` `https://accounts.google.com`, `aud` the audience or else the URL, `email` the service account, `email_verified`, a numeric `sub` and `azp` derived from the account, `iat` and a one-hour `exp`, plus a `cloudburrow` claim naming its origin. An OAuth token is opaque (`cbl_…`), as Google's are, so it carries no account or scope; no Google API would accept it, and CloudBurrow's own services accept every request anyway. **No permission is checked** (ADR-0004): the service account need not exist or be in the queue's project, and the caller need not be allowed to act as it, where Google requires `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs`. A token is minted afresh for each attempt and replaces an `Authorization` header the target's own headers set. |
| A body on a `GET`, `HEAD`, `DELETE` or `OPTIONS` task | **Verified** | **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**, as Google; same test. Tests: `TestTaskFieldsAreRefusedOrKept`. |
| `dispatch_deadline` | **Verified** | Validated (15 s to 30 min, else **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**), stored and returned by `GetTask` (same test), and **applied to each attempt**: an attempt runs under the task's deadline, or Google's default of 10 minutes, and one that runs past it is a failed attempt recorded at the deadline (unit `TestAttemptsRunUnderTheTaskDeadline`, #579). Before, every attempt was cut off at a fixed 30 s. |
| App Engine target (`appEngineHttpRequest`) | **Verified**, *delivered to a local stand-in with `--appengine-url`; else every attempt fails* | `TestTasksAppEngineTargets` (#1447), through the official client. A task is kept as sent (method, defaulting to POST; `relative_uri`, defaulting to `/` and **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`** without a leading `/`; headers; body, only for POST and PUT; `app_engine_routing`) and returned with `app_engine_routing.host`, the queue's override's when it has one, and a `dispatch_deadline` up to 24 h 15 s, as App Engine allows. **No App Engine runs on an instance, and Google documents no mapping from an App Engine service to Cloud Run.** With **`--appengine-url`** (#1506), a local HTTP server the developer runs stands in for the app, as Google documents the request an App Engine handler gets (tasks/docs/creating-appengine-handlers, `AppEngineHttpRequest`): each attempt is sent to that URL plus `relative_uri`, with the task's method, body and headers, `Host` the routing's host, `User-Agent: AppEngine-Google; (+http://code.google.com/appengine)`, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` when the task sets none, and `X-AppEngine-QueueName`, `-TaskName` (short names), `-TaskRetryCount`, `-TaskExecutionCount`, `-TaskETA` (seconds since the epoch) and, after a response, `-TaskPreviousResponse`; a task's own `X-AppEngine-*` and `X-Google-*` headers are replaced. A 2xx answer completes the task, any other is retried by `retry_config`, as for an HTTP task; every service and version reaches the same server, which tells them apart by `Host`. `-TaskRetryReason` and `-FailFast` are not sent. `TestTasksAppEngineDelivery` (with `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_APPENGINE_URL`; unit `TestAppEngineTaskDelivered`). Without the flag nothing is delivered anywhere: each attempt fails as a request to an app that does not exist, HTTP 404, recorded in `last_attempt.response_status` as **`NOT_FOUND`** with the reason and the URL it would have reached; `dispatch_count` and `response_count` count it, `first_attempt.dispatch_time` is set, the queue's `retry_config` retries it, and a task that exhausts it is deleted, as Google drops a task. Each attempt also reaches the console's attempt history and, when sampled, Cloud Logging with `targetType` `APP_ENGINE`. `TestGcloudAppEngineTargets`: `gcloud tasks create-app-engine-task` with `--relative-uri`, `--method`, `--body-content`, `--header` and `--routing`, read back with the official client and `gcloud tasks describe`. |
| `first_attempt`, `last_attempt` | **Verified** | `TestTasksAppEngineTargets` (#1447): `first_attempt` carries only `dispatch_time`, as documented, and `last_attempt` `schedule_time`, `dispatch_time`, `response_time` and `response_status` (an HTTP task's response status converted to its `google.rpc.Code`; without a response, `response_time` and `response_status` are unset, as the API says they are then meaningless). Before #1447 neither was returned. |
| Scheduled execution at `scheduleTime` | **Verified** | `TestTasksScheduleTimeIsHonoured`: a task scheduled 3s ahead is not delivered early, and is delivered within 3s of its time. The dispatcher polls every 200ms, so delivery can trail the time by that much. |
| Retry with backoff | **Verified** | `TestTasksAFailingTargetIsRetriedPerRetryConfig`: a target answering 500 is retried after `minBackoff`, then after the doubled delay capped at `maxBackoff`, and dispatch stops at `maxAttempts`. **`maxDoublings` is modelled** as the service documents it: double that many times, then grow linearly (`TestBackoffGrowsLinearlyAfterMaxDoublings`, `TestTheWorkerReschedulesOnTheLinearPhase`). Each `RetryConfig` field defaults on its own, as in the API, and `maxAttempts: -1` is unlimited. Driven by the queue's own `RetryConfig`, distinct from Pub/Sub redelivery. Exhausted tasks are dropped, as the real service does. |
| `RunTask` (forced immediate run) | **Verified** | Since #1215. Returns the task and dispatches it on the dispatcher's next pass, even on a paused queue or one at its rate limits; on failure the retry policy reschedules it, and a task that has succeeded is `NOT_FOUND`, as documented. A task already in flight finishes that attempt first, where Google may start a second. Console: Run now on a task's page (`TestTasksRunTaskDispatchesNow`, `TestConsoleTasksRunNow`). |
| `BatchCreateTasks`, `BatchDeleteTasks` | **Verified** | Since #1215. At most 100 creates, all for the parent queue, and at most 1000 deletes, else `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Non-atomic: each request succeeds or fails alone, failures are in the operation metadata's `failed_requests` by index with state `PARTIALLY_SUCCEEDED`, and when every request fails the operation's error is `ABORTED`. The operation is done when returned; a repeated `request_id` for the queue returns the first operation (`TestTasksBatchCreateAndDelete`). |
| `GetCmekConfig`, `UpdateCmekConfig` | **Verified**, stored only | Since #1215. The location's key is validated (a `cryptoKeys` name in the config's location), stored and returned; empty clears it. Nothing is encrypted with it and the key is not looked up in Cloud KMS (`TestTasksCmekConfig`). |
| Concurrent dispatch, `max_concurrent_dispatches` | **Verified** | Attempts run concurrently, across queues and within one, bounded per queue by `max_concurrent_dispatches` (default 1000); a task is never dispatched again while an attempt is out (unit `TestQueuesDispatchConcurrently`, `TestMaxConcurrentDispatchesBoundsAQueue`, #579). Before, dispatch was serial, so one slow handler held up every queue. |
| `max_dispatches_per_second` | **Verified** | **Enforced** with a token bucket per queue, refilled at the queue's rate (default 500/s) and holding up to `max_burst_size` tokens; each dispatch, first attempt or retry, takes one, and the queue's other due tasks wait for the next (#716). `TestTasksMaxDispatchesPerSecondSpacesDeliveries`: a queue created with the official client at 1/s delivers 3 tasks enqueued together at least a second apart, over at least 2 seconds (measured at the target, with 50ms allowed for loopback jitter); without enforcement they arrived microseconds apart. Unit tests on a fake clock cover the spacing, a rate below 1/s, a burst followed by the rate, an idle queue banking no more than its burst, and queues not sharing a bucket (`TestMaxDispatchesPerSecondSpacesDispatches`, `TestAFractionalRateSpacesDispatchesBeyondASecond`, `TestMaxBurstSizeBoundsABurstThenTheRateApplies`, `TestAnIdleQueueBanksNoMoreThanItsBurst`, `TestEachQueueHasItsOwnBucket`). The worker polls every 200ms, so a dispatch can trail its token by that much. Before, the rate was stored and returned but not enforced. |
| `max_burst_size` | **Verified**, CloudBurrow's own value | Output only, and enforced as the bucket's size (#716). Google picks it "based on the value of `max_dispatches_per_second`" and does not document the rule, so the value is **CloudBurrow's choice, not Google's**: one second of the rate, rounded up, at least 1 (500 at the default rate, 1 at 1/s or less). A queue on Google may report and allow a different burst. `GetQueue` returns it (`TestTasksMaxDispatchesPerSecondSpacesDeliveries`, unit `TestBurstSizeIsOneSecondOfTheRate`); before, it was returned as 0. |
| Task name reuse | **Verified** | A task name that was executed, deleted or dropped after its last attempt is **`ALREADY_EXISTS`** for an hour, Cloud Tasks' "approximately one hour", which applications use to de-duplicate enqueues (`TestTasksExecutedNamesAreTombstoned`, unit `TestTaskNamesAreTombstoned`, #579). Deleting the queue, which `/admin/reset` does, clears them. A tombstone is removed once its hour is past, whether or not its name comes back (unit `TestExpiredTombstonesAreSwept`, #1594). **Differs:** a task created without a name, which CloudBurrow names, leaves no tombstone, so re-creating that generated name at once is accepted where Cloud Tasks may refuse it; Cloud Tasks' de-duplication is for names the caller chooses, and a tombstone for every unnamed task kept the store growing for as long as tasks were made (unit `TestServerNamedTasksLeaveNoTombstone`, [soak.md](soak.md)). |
| Queue and task IDs | **Verified** | Cloud Tasks' own rules: a queue ID is letters, digits and hyphens, at most 100; a task ID adds underscores, at most 500; anything else is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`** (unit `TestCloudTasksIDRulesAndMissingQueue`). `ListTasks` on a queue that does not exist is **`NOT_FOUND`**, not an empty page (`TestTasksExecutedNamesAreTombstoned`). |

---

## Cloud Run — `google.cloud.run.v2`

**Backing component:** Knative Serving v1.23.0, behind a CloudBurrow-owned Cloud Run v2
adapter. Contract: `google/cloud/run/v2/*.proto`. Admin API is REST. No emulator environment
variable. Requires a local Kubernetes cluster; its absence is a clear capability error, not a
silent degradation.

> **Knative is not Cloud Run.** It is the closest available model. No blanket claim is made
> that it reproduces Cloud Run semantics. Revision traffic and scaling behavior are mapped and
> tested explicitly in #30; whatever is not tested there is not claimed here.
>
> The adapter **refuses configuration it cannot map**, naming the field. NFS volumes are mounted from the
> server the caller names (#1448; see "NFS volumes" below), and Cloud Storage FUSE volumes from the
> instance's own Cloud Storage (#1474; see "Cloud Storage FUSE volumes" below). Secret Manager and in-memory
> volumes, a mount's `subPath`, and the service account are mapped (#1297, #1346; see
> "Volumes and the service account" below); Cloud SQL volumes are served by the Cloud SQL
> Auth Proxy (#1346; see "Cloud SQL volumes" below). VPC access, encryption keys, binary
> authorization, `template.executionEnvironment` and `template.sessionAffinity` are **stored
> and returned, with no effect** (#1346; see "Stored settings" below). A caller who set one
> of the refused fields and had it silently dropped would believe it took effect.
>
> Secret-backed environment is **not** in that list and was listed there in error:
> `secretKeyRef` is mapped and tested — see the Secret Manager section's
> `TestCloudRunRevisionReadsASecretManagerSecret`, which also asserts the payload does not
> appear in the deployed Knative Service.

### Control plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateService` | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceLifecycle`: deploys a real container through the official SDK and returns a long-running operation. |
| `GetService` | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceLifecycle`, including `NotFound` for an absent service. |
| Stored settings (#1346) | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceStoredSettingsAndSubPath` and `TestRunJobSubPathAndStoredSettings`, the official `run/apiv2` clients: `template.vpcAccess` (connector, `networkInterfaces`, `egress`), `template.encryptionKey`, `template.executionEnvironment`, `template.sessionAffinity` (services only) and `binaryAuthorization` are accepted, the service becomes ready and the job runs, and each reads back as set on the service, its revision and the job. **Stored and returned, not acted on:** with `--services compute` the connector and network interfaces are checked first (see "Serverless VPC Access" below, #2140), and no traffic goes through them; nothing is encrypted with the key and the KMS key is not checked; there is one runtime, so gen1 and gen2 are the same; requests are not pinned to an instance; no image is checked against a policy. Each is a setting Google documents, so it is stored rather than refused; nothing here claims its effect. A worker pool and an instance still refuse VPC access and the encryption key, and an instance its execution environment. The console's deploy, job and edit forms set them (`TestConsoleRunStoredSettings`). `encryptionKeyRevocationAction` and `encryptionKeyShutdownDuration` stay refused. Unit: `TestStoredTemplateSettingsReadBack`, `TestVolumeMountSubPath`, `TestJobRefusesWhatItDoesNotMap`, `TestRunSettingsFieldsRoundTrip`. |
| Cloud SQL volumes (#1346) | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceCloudSQLVolume`, `TestRunJobCloudSQLVolume` and `TestRunServiceCloudSQLMySQLVolume`, the official `run/apiv2` clients on one instance with `--services run,storage,cloudsql,cloudsql-mysql`: a `cloudSqlInstance` volume naming `<project>:us-central1:postgres`, mounted at `/cloudsql`, gives the container a Unix socket at `/cloudsql/<connection name>/.s.PGSQL.5432`, as Cloud Run does; the revision answers `SELECT 1` over HTTP from `psql -h /cloudsql/<conn>`, and the task exits 0 only when that query returns 1. The volume reads back as set. **How:** as on Cloud Run, Google's Cloud SQL Auth Proxy runs beside the container: `gcr.io/cloud-sql-connectors/cloud-sql-proxy:2.19.0`, pinned by digest, unmodified, with `--unix-socket /cloudsql`, `--sqladmin-api-endpoint` at the Cloud SQL Admin API as pods reach it (`cloudburrow-host`), and the connection names; it takes its token from the metadata server. In a service it is a second container (and the serving container gets an explicit port 8080, which Knative requires beside a sidecar); in a job's task a Kubernetes native sidecar, so the task completes when its container exits. The proxy calls `connect.get` and `connect.generateEphemeralCert` and dials port 3307 with TLS 1.3, as against Google; `cloudburrow-host` maps 3307 to a connector listener for pods, and `connectSettings` asked from a pod names that Service's cluster IP, so a pod's volume works even while another CloudBurrow instance holds the host's 3307. A connection name that is not `project:region:instance`, or names an instance or region this instance does not serve, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (`Cloud SQL instance "…" does not exist or you do not have permission to access it`, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/connect-run>) wording); with Cloud SQL off, `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. For Cloud SQL for MySQL the socket is `/cloudsql/<conn>` itself: in `TestRunServiceCloudSQLMySQLVolume` a second container runs the MySQL 8.4 image's own `mysql -S /cloudsql/<conn>` as the `cloudburrow` user, and the service returns its `SELECT 1`. Worker pools and instances refuse the volume. **v1 and gcloud:** `TestGcloudRunDeployCloudSQL`, gcloud through the harness: `gcloud run deploy --add-cloudsql-instances` sends `run.googleapis.com/cloudsql-instances` on the revision template to the v1 (`serving.knative.dev/v1`) API, as `--log-http` shows; it is the same volume, named `cloudsql` and mounted at `/cloudsql` in every container, as Google documents the socket. The service answers `SELECT 1` through it, `services describe` shows the annotation, the official v2 client reads the `cloudsql` volume and mount (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/connect-run>) that Google's v2 shows exactly this shape), the console's edit form prefills Cloud SQL connections from it, and `--remove-cloudsql-instances` removes it. v1 reads any template's Cloud SQL volumes back as the annotation and lists no v1 volume or mount for them; a v1 replace that names the same instances keeps a v2 template's volume names and mount paths. A v1 job's execution-template annotation maps the same way, by unit test only (`TestV1JobCloudSQLAnnotation`). A `cloudsql` volume, or a mount at `/cloudsql`, beside the annotation is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. IAM database authentication is not served (docs/cloudsql.md). The console's deploy, edit and job forms take Cloud SQL connections (`TestConsoleRunCloudSQLConnections`). Unit: `TestCloudSQLVolumeRendersTheAuthProxy`, `TestCloudSQLVolumeInAJobIsANativeSidecar`, `TestCloudSQLVolumeRefusals`, `TestConnectSettingsForPods`, `TestV1CloudSQLAnnotationIsTheVolume`. |
| Volumes and the service account (#1297) | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceVolumesAndServiceAccount` and `TestRunJobMountsSecretAndMemoryVolumes`, the official `run/apiv2` clients with Secret Manager on the same instance; `TestRunV1VolumesProbesAndServiceAccount` for v1. A `secret` volume mounts a Secret Manager secret (see the Secret Manager section); an `emptyDir` volume is a Kubernetes `emptyDir`, `MEMORY` as `medium: Memory` (a tmpfs, which the job's task checks in `/proc/mounts` and writes to) with its `sizeLimit`; each container's `volumeMounts` are rendered, read-only for a secret, and one naming no declared volume, or with a relative path or `/`, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Volumes, mounts and `serviceAccount` read back as set on the service, revision, job and execution. **The service account is the one the workload is told it runs as** (#1388): `TestCloudRunWorkloadIsToldItsServiceAccount` deploys a service with `serviceAccount` set and one without, and runs a job with it set; each container reads `instance/service-accounts/default/email` through `cloud.google.com/go/compute/metadata`, takes an identity token from `google.golang.org/api/idtoken` and an access token from ADC, and reports them. The email and the identity token's `email` claim are the template's `serviceAccount`, or, when none is set, the project's Compute Engine default account `{number}-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com`, with the number every service reports; the access token is a local one (opaque, as Google's are). How: every workload reaches the one metadata server through `cloudburrow-host`, from an address that says nothing about it (the pod's traffic is translated on its way to the host), so the account rides on the name it dials. Each account has an ExternalName Service, `cloudburrow-sa-<hash>`, in the workload namespace, an alias of `cloudburrow-host`, recording the account in an annotation; the injected `GCE_METADATA_HOST` (and a Cloud SQL Auth Proxy sidecar's) names it, every client library sends that name as `Host`, and the metadata server answers as that account. `cloudburrow-host` itself, and the host's own port, still name the instance's `cloudburrow-local@…`, which `cloudburrow env` and the ADC file use. A worker pool's and an instance's pods are given their template's account the same way (unit `TestWorkerPoolPodsNameTheirAccount`). **Not acted on:** the workload still runs as the namespace's default Kubernetes ServiceAccount, the account need not exist in IAM, and no permission is checked: tokens are never verified (ADR-0004). `gcs` and `nfs` volumes: see their rows below (#1474, #1448). **A mount's `subPath`** (#1346) is Kubernetes' `subPath`: `TestRunJobSubPathAndStoredSettings` mounts one in-memory volume at `/data` and at `/sub` with `subPath: a/b`, and the task finds at `/data/a/b/x` the file it wrote through `/sub`; `TestRunServiceStoredSettingsAndSubPath` reads it back on a ready service and its Knative revision; on v1, `TestRunV1VolumesProbesAndServiceAccount` (#1576) mounts the in-memory volume a second time with `subPath: a/b`, reads it back through `run.namespaces.services.get` and finds it on the Knative Service (it was dropped from v1's read-back before #1576); an absolute `subPath`, or one with `..` or not in clean form, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. A job's `startupProbe` and `livenessProbe` stay refused, as a task serves no port. Unit: `TestVolumesAndServiceAccountRender`, `TestV1RoundTripAndRefusals`. |

Blobs, manifests and package-format files are sealed with AES-256-GCM in the repository's own directory, never in the shared plaintext store (unit-tested, `TestRepositoryCMEK`; a cross-repository mount or a remote repository's cache takes its own sealed copy). A pushed Alpine 3.13 image with zlib 1.2.11-r3 gets a `DISCOVERY` occurrence of `projects/goog-analysis/notes/PACKAGE_VULNERABILITY` (`PENDING` and `SCANNING` while the scan runs) ending `FINISHED_SUCCESS` with `continuousAnalysis: ACTIVE`, `cpe` and `lastScanTime`, `PACKAGE` occurrences of each package, and a `VULNERABILITY` occurrence of `projects/goog-vulnz/notes/CVE-2022-37434`: `CRITICAL`, CVSS v3 9.8 with its vector parts, the affected and fixed (`1.2.12-r2`) versions, `fixAvailable`, `packageType: OS`; filtered by `kind`, `resourceUrl`, `dependencyPackageName` and `has_prefix`; the summary counts it. A push to a `DISABLED` repository is not scanned. **The scan is OSV-Scanner's, not Google's scanner**: `cloudburrow prefetch --vulnerability-scanning` downloads Google's [OSV-Scanner](https://github.com/google/osv-scanner) v2.7.1 and a pinned snapshot of the OSV database (Alpine, Debian, Ubuntu, Go, Maven, npm, PyPI), checked by SHA-256 (dependencies.json `scanning`); the scan runs `--offline` with every proxy at a closed port, so nothing reaches osv.dev or any Google API; which CVEs and severities it finds are the snapshot's, so they can differ from Google's. Without the prefetch the `DISCOVERY` occurrence is `FINISHED_FAILED` with **`FAILED_PRECONDITION`** and the test skips, except where `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_OSV_REQUIRED` is set: CI's `run` shard prefetches the scanner and the Alpine snapshot before `up` (`tools/osvmirror fetch`, from a cache keyed by the pins, else the latest release's mirror, else upstream) and sets it, so there the tests scan or fail (#1917). OSV keeps a pinned generation for about a week; each release mirrors the scanner and the Alpine, Debian, Go, Maven, npm and PyPI snapshots as its assets, and prefetch tries that mirror first, so a release's prefetch keeps working after OSV drops its pins (Ubuntu, 820 MB, is not mirrored; see docs/install.md). Severity is the CVSS v3 base score's band, `effectiveSeverity` the distribution's own rating when OSV carries one. Continuous analysis: an image is rescanned when pulled after a new snapshot, `INACTIVE` after 30 days unpulled, and archived (`archiveTime`) after 90, checked hourly (unit: `TestRepositoryVulnerabilityScanning`). Each digest is scanned once; an image index is not scanned, its platform manifests are. Unit: `TestConvert`, `TestCVSS3BaseScore`, `TestPrefetchChecksAndSkips`, `TestPinsMatchDependenciesJSON`, `TestPrefetchTriesTheMirrorFirst`, `TestDefaultMirrors`, and tools/osvmirror's `TestStageFallsBackToAnEarlierRelease`, `TestFetchPrefersTheMirror`, `TestBump`. Language packages (Go, Maven, npm, PyPI) are scanned whenever the API is enabled, as Google's "Enabling this API also enables language package scanning". Licenses (#2072): each `PACKAGE` occurrence's `license.expression` is an SPDX expression, as Artifact Analysis reports licenses for OS and "supported language packages" ([view licenses and dependencies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-analysis/docs/view-licenses-dependencies), re-read 2026-11-20). An OS package's comes from its package database (OSV-Scanner's `--licenses`); offline, the scanner reads no language package's license (it asks deps.dev, which `--offline` never calls, measured on the pinned v2.7.1), so they are read from the image's own files: npm `node_modules/*/package.json` `license` (and the legacy `licenses` list, read as a choice) and the hidden lockfile; PyPI `*.dist-info/METADATA` `License-Expression`, else `License`, else unambiguous `License ::` classifiers; Maven `<licenses>` of a jar's `META-INF/maven/**/pom.xml` and of `.pom` files, through the `<parent>` chain, several read as a choice, as the POM reference says; Go module `LICENSE`/`COPYING` files in a module cache (`pkg/mod/{module}@{version}/`) or a `vendor/` directory, classified by Google's `github.com/google/licensecheck` (BSD-3-Clause). A Go binary's modules with no module cache in the image, and the standard library, have none. `TestArtifactRegistryLanguagePackageLicenses` pushes an image of npm, PyPI, Maven and Go packages and reads each license with the official grafeas client; unit: `TestAddLocalLicenses`, `TestCanonicalExpression`. UNVERIFIED (re-read 2026-11-19, the page names no `PACKAGE` occurrences): the `PACKAGE` occurrences' note name, `projects/goog-analysis/notes/PACKAGE_{type}` here. |

too few is `FAILED_PRECONDITION` naming the counts. `require_comments_resolved` refuses while a code comment conversation is unresolved or an account's latest decisive review requests changes. `required_status_checks` name triggers of the triggers file: each one's latest `pull_request` build of the head must be `SUCCESS` (`TestSecureSourceManagerPullRequestTriggers`). `require_code_owner_approval` makes the merge wait for the code owners of the base branch's CODEOWNERS files, and the push of a CODEOWNERS file that does not parse refused (#1928, `TestSecureSourceManagerCodeOwners`: the next row). `UpdateBranchRule` takes a mask (`*`, or every field when none), `validate_only` and a current `etag`; `DeleteBranchRule` takes `allow_missing`. |
| Secure Source Manager code owners (#1928): CODEOWNERS files and a branch rule's `require_code_owner_approval` | **Verified**, *owners are email addresses; no Google Groups, as Google's* | `TestSecureSourceManagerCodeOwners` with the official client over gRPC on the Run port, as three accounts (the instance's own and two service accounts whose tokens IAM Credentials mints), as Google's "Manage pull request approvals with CODEOWNERS" (Preview) describes them (<https://docs.cloud.google.com/secure-source-manager/docs/codeowners>, read 2026-11-19). **Files:** a `CODEOWNERS` file in any directory but `.securesourcemanager` covers its directory, its paths relative to it, a deeper file overriding a shallower one's matching rules; `.securesourcemanager/CODEOWNERS`, when present, is the only file read, relative to the root; only the base branch's files count (a pull request's own changes to them do not). **Syntax:** `[BRANCH_GLOB] PATH_GLOB [OWNERS...]`, fields with `@` being owners (individual email addresses, compared case-insensitively), a rule with no owners a path exclusion, a rule whose branch glob does not match the base branch ignored; gitignore-style path globs (no slash but a trailing one: any directory; a trailing slash: directories and all they hold, a directory otherwise matching only when the last part has no wildcard; `**` across slashes, mixed with other characters a `*`; case sensitive; `\` escapes `[ ] space @ * ? \ { } !`); `#` comments, whole-line or after a field; `[Section]` and `[Section][N]` (default 1, 0 optional), sections of one name merging case-insensitively across files, rules before any section one section needing one approval; within a section the last matching line wins, and every section applies. **Approvals:** with the rule on, `MergePullRequest` is `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, naming the files, owners and section, until in every section each changed file (merge base to head, renames as both names) has its count of distinct owners whose latest Approve or Request changes review approves the head commit (any commit with `allow_stale_reviews`), as the minimum reviewer and approver counts count them, so one review can satisfy both; the author cannot approve their own pull request. **Invalid lines:** a line that is not a comment, section header or rule (an owner that is not an email address, such as `@name`, three globs, a field after the owners, default owners on a section header, `!` negation, an unescaped reserved character, a non-numeric count) is ignored and a negative count read as 0; the repository's pre-receive hook (the CloudBurrow executable) refuses a push, and `MergePullRequest` a merge, that brings such a file to a branch whose rule requires code owner review, as Google's presubmit guard does. Google Groups as owners are not supported, as on Google Cloud. |

A read carries **no etag**, a deliberate deviation from the proto's "computed by the server": Terraform's `google_developer_connect_connection` and `_git_repository_link` declare `etag` optional and not computed and copy a read's into state (the link's forcing replacement), and the provider's acceptance tests plan clean against Google with none configured, so any etag a caller sends is stale. `FetchLinkableGitRepositories` lists the instance's repositories by git URL; a git repository link's `cloneUri` must be one of them (a hosted URL is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`), and its `gitProxyUri` is the same URL, as this port serves the repository (CloudBurrow's choice). A push to the linked repository runs every enabled such trigger whose branch or tag RE2 (`invertRegex` reversing it) matches the pushed ref, with the commit's tree as `/workspace` and the built-in `COMMIT_SHA`, `SHORT_SHA`, `REVISION_ID`, `REPO_NAME`, `REPO_FULL_NAME`, `REF_NAME` and `BRANCH_NAME` or `TAG_NAME`; `RunBuildTrigger` builds the head of `source.branchName`, `tagName` or `commitSha`, else the default branch. **File and CEL filters** (#1955, `TestCloudBuildSourceManagerTriggerFilters`, official `cloudbuild` client): `includedFiles`/`ignoredFiles` are matched against the push's changed files as Google's BuildTrigger reference documents them (globs with `filepath.Match` syntax extended with `**`; with neither set every push builds; files matching an `ignoredFiles` glob are dropped and a push with none left builds nothing; with `includedFiles` set one remaining file must match it): a push touching only `docs/guide.md`, `src/notes.md` and an unincluded `README` (included `src/**`, ignored `**/*.md`) builds nothing, a push touching `src/app.go` builds; the trigger's `filter` (CEL over its substitutions and the push's built-ins `BRANCH_NAME`, `TAG_NAME`, `REF_NAME`, `COMMIT_SHA`, `SHORT_SHA`, `REVISION_ID`, `REPO_NAME`, `REPO_FULL_NAME`, `TRIGGER_NAME`, `PROJECT_ID`) must be true for a push to build (`BRANCH_NAME == "release"` builds a push to `release`, not to `main`), and `!`, an unknown variable, a non-boolean filter or a malformed glob is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; A trigger's `channel` (#1947) is served: see the Eventarc Advanced and channels row below. Triggers are kept in memory. **Direct events of the other Google sources served** (#1997, `TestEventarcEventarcAndFunctionsDirectEvents`, `TestEventarcRedisDirectEvents`, with the official Eventarc, Cloud Functions and Memorystore for Redis clients, as Google's supported-events reference lists them and the google-cloudevents catalogue documents their data): `google.cloud.redis.instance.v1.created`, `updated` and `deleted` (provider `redis.googleapis.com`, with `--services memorystore`), `google.cloud.functions.function.v2.created`, `updated` and `deleted` (`cloudfunctions.googleapis.com`), and Eventarc's own `google.cloud.eventarc.trigger.v1.created`, `updated`, `deleted`, `channel.v1.created`, `updated`, `deleted` and `channelConnection.v1.created` and `deleted` (`eventarc.googleapis.com`), each optionally filtered on the resource's ID extension (`instance`, `function`, `trigger`, `channel`, `channelconnection`). Each resource kind a trigger names is read each second; a resource is reported `created` once it has settled (a Redis instance READY, a function ACTIVE or FAILED), `updated` when a settled read differs from the last, `deleted` when it is gone; the first read, when the trigger is made, is the baseline. The data is the catalogue's InstanceEventData, FunctionEventData, TriggerEventData, ChannelEventData or ChannelConnectionEventData in JSON, the resource as `payload` (none in a Redis or function deletion, as the catalogue says), delivered with the extension; `ce-source` `//SERVICE/projects/P/locations/L`, `ce-subject` `COLLECTION/ID` and the extension being an optional exact filter are UNVERIFIED (re-read 2026-11-20: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/eventarc/docs/reference/supported-events> and the catalogue's `proto/google/events/cloud/{redis,functions,eventarc}`, which do not say). **Refused `UNIMPLEMENTED` with the reason:** the Firebase providers' direct events (Firebase Alerts, Authentication, Data Connect, Realtime Database, Remote Config and Test Lab: their services are not served), Speech-to-Text's (v1 Adaptation's custom classes and phrase sets; v1's `Adaptation` service is not served), the direct events of the providers whose services this instance does not serve, and Redis's without `--services memorystore`. **Dead-letter topic** (`TestEventarcDeadLetterTopic`, as Google's "Retry events" page documents it, on the trigger's Pub/Sub subscription): with `deadLetterPolicy` (5 attempts) and a short `retryPolicy` set on the trigger's subscription with the Pub/Sub client, an event its Cloud Run destination answers 500 is delivered 5 times and lands on the dead-letter topic with its data and `CloudPubSubDeadLetterSourceDeliveryCount` 5. **gcloud and Terraform for GKE and Datastore mode** (#1997): `TestEventarcGKEDestination` also runs `gcloud eventarc triggers create --destination-gke-cluster --destination-gke-location --destination-gke-namespace --destination-gke-service --destination-gke-path`, `describe`, `update --destination-gke-path` and `delete`, and a `google_eventarc_trigger` with a `destination.gke` block (applied, planned clean, a path change in place, destroyed), each delivering to the cluster's Service; `TestGcloudAndTerraformEventarcDatastoreTriggers` makes a `google.cloud.datastore.entity.v1.written` trigger with `--event-filters` database and namespace, `--event-filters-path-pattern=entity=KIND/{id}` and `--event-data-content-type=application/protobuf`, and a `google_eventarc_trigger` with the `entity` `matching_criteria` `operator = "match-path-pattern"` and `event_data_content_type`, each receiving the create of an entity of its kind. Console: Create trigger offers these event types with a Resource ID field; `TestEventarcCreateTriggerNewFieldsThroughTheBrowser` drives the Datastore mode Namespace and Entity fields, the Resource ID, and the Google Kubernetes Engine destination's fields (a cluster that does not exist is refused with the API's reason). `match-path-pattern` is the only filter operator Google documents beyond an exact match (re-read 2026-11-19: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/eventarc/docs/path-patterns>). Without Pub/Sub, the transport, `CreateTrigger` is `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. The JSON API is served under `/eventarc/v1/` on the Run port (its trigger paths are Cloud Build's); `UpdateTrigger` also takes the mask paths `destination.cloud_run.service`, `.path` and `.region` gcloud sends. `TestGcloudEventarcTriggers`, gcloud through the harness (the `eventarc` override): `gcloud eventarc providers list`, `triggers create --destination-run-service --destination-run-region --event-filters=type=google.cloud.pubsub.topic.v1.messagePublished` (a topic Eventarc makes), `describe`, `list`, `update --destination-run-path`, `delete`, and an audit-log trigger with `--event-filters-path-pattern=resourceName=...` (its filter's operator `match-path-pattern`), `providers describe pubsub.googleapis.com` (the audit-log type, `pathPatternSupported: true`) and the refusal of one with no `methodName`. `TestTerraformEventarcTrigger`, `hashicorp/google` 8.4.0 through `cloudburrow terraform` (`eventarc_custom_endpoint`) with egress blocked: a `google_eventarc_trigger` with `matching_criteria`, `destination.cloud_run_service` (service, region, path) and `transport.pubsub.topic` is created, read back by the official client as Terraform holds it (uid, subscription), plans clean, takes new labels and a new path in place, plans clean again and is destroyed. Console: Eventarc's own Triggers page (`TestEventarcTriggersPageThroughTheBrowser`): the list, Create trigger, the trigger's page, Edit and Delete; and Cloud Run's Triggers tab (#1852): the service's triggers, Add trigger and Delete trigger, `TestCloudRunEventarcTriggersThroughTheBrowser`. `ListTriggers` and `ListProviders` take an AIP-160 `filter` (the reference's `destination:gke`) and an AIP-132 `order_by` (`name desc, trigger_id`; `TestListFiltersEventarc`, #1943). |
| Eventarc Advanced and channels (#1947): `Eventarc.CreateMessageBus`, `GetMessageBus`, `ListMessageBuses`, `UpdateMessageBus`, `DeleteMessageBus`, `ListMessageBusEnrollments`, `CreatePipeline`, `GetPipeline`, `ListPipelines`, `UpdatePipeline`, `DeletePipeline`, `CreateEnrollment`, `GetEnrollment`, `ListEnrollments`, `UpdateEnrollment`, `DeleteEnrollment`, `CreateGoogleApiSource`, `GetGoogleApiSource`, `ListGoogleApiSources`, `UpdateGoogleApiSource`, `DeleteGoogleApiSource`, `CreateChannel`, `GetChannel`, `ListChannels`, `UpdateChannel`, `DeleteChannel`, `CreateChannelConnection`, `GetChannelConnection`, `ListChannelConnections`, `DeleteChannelConnection`, `GetGoogleChannelConfig`, `UpdateGoogleChannelConfig`; `Publisher.Publish`, `PublishEvents`, `PublishChannelConnectionEvents` | **Verified**, *events delivered locally* | `TestEventarcAdvancedBusToCloudRun` and `TestEventarcChannelsToCloudRun`, with the official `cloud.google.com/go/eventarc/apiv1` and `.../eventarc/publishing/apiv1` clients over gRPC on the Run port, as Google's "Eventarc Advanced overview", "Publish events directly", "Transform received events", "Publish events from custom sources" and the v1 and Publishing REST references document them. **Message buses** take `displayName`, `labels`, `annotations`, `cryptoKeyName` (projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*, recorded) and `loggingConfig.logSeverity`; IDs are 1 to 63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen; a stale `etag` is `ABORTED`; `ListMessageBusEnrollments` names a bus's enrollments. **Pipelines** hold exactly one destination and at most one transformation (`INVALID_ARGUMENT` otherwise): an `httpEndpoint` (`https` only, or the URL of a Cloud Run service of this instance in the pipeline's location, which is reached through the cluster's ingress; `networkConfig.networkAttachment` recorded), with an optional `messageBindingTemplate` (`headers` and `body`) and `authenticationConfig.googleOidc` (an ID token for the account, audience the URI unless given); a Pub/Sub `topic` (published in the CloudEvents Pub/Sub binding: `ce-` attributes and `content-type`); or a `messageBus` of the same project (republished; a loop ends after 8 buses); or a `workflow` of the same project, which must exist (#1996: one execution per event, the CloudEvent in JSON its argument; `TestEventarcAdvancedPipelineStartsAWorkflow` and `TestPipelineToWorkflow`). `inputPayloadFormat` and each destination's `outputPayloadFormat` (only with an input format) are JSON, Avro (the schema, with Avro's JSON encoding for the CEL view) or Protobuf (the schema, parsed as a Pub/Sub schema is); data that does not decode in the input format is a persistent error and is dropped. A transformation is a CEL template over `message` (the context attributes, extensions and `data`) with Google's `setField`, `removeFields`, `merge`, `denormalize`, `toMap`, `toJsonString`, `toBase64` and `re.capture`, `re.captureN`, `re.extract`; its result is the new message (`id`, `source`, `specversion`, `type` kept when it leaves them out). `retryPolicy`: `maxAttempts` 1 to 100 (5 by default), `minRetryDelay` and `maxRetryDelay` 1 to 600 s (1 s and 60 s), exponential. **Enrollments**: a CEL `celMatch` on `message` (compiled at create, `INVALID_ARGUMENT` otherwise), the bus (in the enrollment's location, immutable) and the destination pipeline, which must exist. **Publish** takes `protoMessage` (the CloudEvent proto) or `jsonMessage` (the CloudEvents JSON format, `data` or `data_base64`); an event without `id`, `source`, `specversion` 1.0 or `type` is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Each enrollment whose match accepts it sends it to its pipeline: in the test a JSON event reaches a Cloud Run probe service transformed (`removeFields`, `setField`) in binary content mode with its extension attributes, an event the match refuses does not, and both reach a Pub/Sub topic pipeline. **Google API sources** (`destination` a bus, `projectSubscriptions`, `organizationSubscription`, `loggingConfig`) put the project's Google events on their bus: the Admin Activity audit-log entries of the calls this instance serves over gRPC, as `google.cloud.audit.log.v1.written` CloudEvents with the extensions Eventarc's triggers carry; in the test a `CreateMessageBus` call's entry reaches the service through an enrollment on its type and `methodname`. A bus, pipeline or source with a `logSeverity` other than `NONE` writes its platform log entries at or above it to the instance's Cloud Logging (resource types `eventarc.googleapis.com/MessageBus`, `/Pipeline`, `/GoogleApiSource`; the log names and payload are UNVERIFIED, re-read 2026-11-19: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/eventarc/advanced/docs/monitor> names the logs only). **Channels**: one with no `provider` is `ACTIVE` at once, for custom events; one for a provider is `PENDING` with an `activationToken` until a `ChannelConnection` with that token (a wrong one is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`) activates it; `PublishEvents` to a channel that is not `ACTIVE` is `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. A trigger on a channel filters on `type` and any attribute (exact or `match-path-pattern`), has no transport of its own, and receives `PublishEvents`' events (`events`, Any-wrapped `io.cloudevents.v1.CloudEvent`s, or `textEvents` in the JSON format) and `PublishChannelConnectionEvents`' at its destination in binary content mode, retried up to 10 times, 1 s to 60 s apart (UNVERIFIED, re-read 2026-11-19: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/eventarc/docs/retry-events> gives Google's 24 hours), unless its retry policy allows one attempt. `GetGoogleChannelConfig` and `UpdateGoogleChannelConfig` keep a location's `cryptoKeyName` and `labels`. Unit `TestBusEventFlowsThroughEnrollmentAndPipeline`, `TestPipelineAvroOutputAndRetries`, `TestPipelineToTopicAndBus`, `TestChannelEventsReachTriggers`, `TestTransformationFunctions`. Every resource is kept in memory; the List `filter` is `UNIMPLEMENTED`, `orderBy` is `name` (asc or desc). **`UNIMPLEMENTED` with the reason:** a `workflow` destination (a pipeline does not deliver to Workflows here; a trigger's `destination.workflow` does, #1986), `authenticationConfig.oauthToken` (it authenticates a call to a Google API, which this instance never makes), and `Publish`'s `avroMessage` (the CloudEvents Avro format's schema is the CloudEvents specification's, which Google's pages cite but do not give). `TestGcloudEventarcAdvanced`, gcloud through the harness (the `eventarc` and `eventarcpublishing` overrides, the latter under `/eventarcpublishing/` on the Run port): `message-buses create --logging-config`, `describe`, `list`, `list-enrollments`, `update`, `publish --json-message` and `--event-id --event-source --event-type --event-data --event-attributes`, `pipelines create --destinations=pubsub_topic= --input-payload-format-json --mediations=transformation_template= --max-retry-attempts`, `list`, `enrollments create --cel-match --message-bus --destination-pipeline`, `describe`, `google-api-sources create --destination-message-bus`, `describe`, `channels create`, `describe`, `publish`, and each `delete`; the published events matching the enrollment reach the topic transformed. `TestTerraformEventarcAdvanced`, `hashicorp/google` 8.4.0 through `cloudburrow terraform` with egress blocked: `google_eventarc_message_bus`, `google_eventarc_pipeline`, `google_eventarc_enrollment` and `google_eventarc_google_api_source` apply, read back with the official client, plan clean, take a new CEL match, labels and log severity in place, plan clean again and are destroyed. Console: Eventarc's Buses, Pipelines, Enrollments, Google API sources and Channels pages (`TestEventarcAdvancedPagesThroughTheBrowser`). |
| Cloud Build approvals: `CloudBuild.ApproveBuild`, a trigger's `approvalConfig.approvalRequired` | **Verified** | `TestCloudBuildApproveBuild` (#1449) with the official `cloudbuild` client over gRPC on the Run port, on one instance with `--services run,storage,secretmanager,pubsub` and `--cloudbuild-host-steps`: a trigger created through the JSON API with `approvalConfig: {approvalRequired: true}` reads back with it (this release of the Cloud Build protos has no `BuildTrigger.approvalConfig`, so the JSON API carries it beside the proto: it is taken out of a create or update body and written back into every trigger the JSON API returns; the Go client cannot set or see it). Each build `RunBuildTrigger` starts is `PENDING`, with `approval.state` `PENDING` and `approval.config.approvalRequired`, and does not run (no `startTime`). `ApproveBuild` `APPROVED` returns a done operation with the build, `QUEUED`, which then runs to `SUCCESS` with `approval.state` `APPROVED` and `approval.result` (`comment`, `approvalTime`); approving it again is `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. `REJECTED` ends a build `CANCELLED` with `approval.state` `REJECTED`, its operation failed `CANCELLED`; `CancelBuild` on a pending build ends it `CANCELLED` with `approval.state` `CANCELLED`. The build's timeout starts when it runs, not while it waits. A rejected build is `CANCELLED`: Google's status for one is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/securing-builds/gate-builds-on-approval>). `approverAccount` is empty: callers are not authenticated. `TestGcloudBuildsApproveAndReject`, gcloud through the harness: `gcloud builds triggers create manual --require-approval` (describe shows `approvalConfig.approvalRequired`), `run`, `gcloud alpha builds approve --location` (only alpha takes `--location`) and `gcloud beta builds reject` of a global trigger's build (reject takes no `--location` in any track; `ApproveBuild` accepts the global name `projects/{p}/builds/{id}` gcloud sends). Console: a pending build's page offers Approve, Reject (each with a comment) and Cancel, and shows the approval; Create trigger takes Require approval, and the Triggers list has an Approval column. |
| Cloud Build `options.dynamicSubstitutions`; `secretEnv` on a docker build or pack step | **Verified** | `TestCloudBuildDynamicSubstitutionsAndSecretBuildArg` (#1449) with the official `cloudbuild` client over gRPC on the Run port: with `options.dynamicSubstitutions`, a user substitution `_REPO: us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/${PROJECT_ID}/dyn` names a built-in, and `${_VER#release-}` strips a prefix in a docker build's `-t`, which the step's args read back substituted. Every bash parameter expansion Google documents is applied: `${V:offset}`, `${V:offset:length}` (a negative offset written `: -n` or `:(-n)`), `${V#glob}`, `${V##glob}`, `${V%glob}`, `${V%%glob}`, `${V/glob/rep}` and `${V//glob/rep}`, globs with `*`, `?` and `[...]` (unit-tested); user substitutions are expanded against each other until none changes; without the option the operators are left as written, as before. A docker build step's `secretEnv` (and `options.secretEnv`) gives `--build-arg TOKEN` the Secret Manager value, which the test's Dockerfile checks with `RUN test "$TOKEN" = …`: the builder passes the bare `--build-arg TOKEN` and the value in docker's environment, so it is on no command line and in no step's args. A pack step's `--env NAME` reads a secret the same way (pack's `--env NAME` takes the value from its environment; unit-tested). A bare `--build-arg NAME` or `--env NAME` that names no secret takes `options.env`'s value, else is dropped, as Docker drops an unset one; the host's environment never reaches the build. `secretEnv` on a docker push step is accepted and has nothing to read it. `env` and `volumes` on these steps stay refused (**`UNIMPLEMENTED`**): the local builder runs them, not the step's container. Console: Run build takes substitutions and Dynamic substitutions; a build's page says when they were on. |

Clones use git's file transport only (`GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file`), from the repository's own directory, so a build never fetches from another host; a submodule is cloned the same way when its URL is this instance's repository, and refused otherwise. A URL on any other host is **`FAILED_PRECONDITION`** at create, quoting Google's requirement ("A Git repository that is either a public repository or linked to Cloud Build using Developer Connect"): a local instance cannot reach it. A `destPath` outside the working directory is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; a revision the repository lacks fails the build at FETCHSOURCE. With dependencies, a triggered build's own repository is not cloned ("only those listed in dependencies are cloned"), and `{empty: true}` fetches nothing, not even the source. |
