### Data plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pull image and start container | **Verified** | Prebuilt images only. Local images are rewritten to `dev.local/` with `imagePullPolicy: Never`; untagged references are refused. An image under a `DOCKER` repository this instance's Artifact Registry holds, and not built here, is pulled from that registry by digest (#1383, `TestArtifactRegistryDockerRegistry`): its tag is resolved there, the revision names `image@digest` (so Knative resolves nothing), and each kind node's containerd reaches the registry through `/etc/containerd/certs.d/{region}-docker.pkg.dev/hosts.toml`, written at `up` for every region, whose server and mirror are the Run port at the address pods reach the host at, so a pull never falls back to Google. The service reads back the reference deployed. |
| Readiness detection | **Verified** | Reported from Knative's `Ready` condition, including the failure message. A service still reconciling is pending, not failed. Tests: `TestFromKnativeReportsRealReadiness`, `TestUnknownConditionIsPending`. |
| Request routing to container | **Verified** | The acceptance workflow delivers a Pub/Sub push to a deployed Cloud Run service, which reads and writes Cloud Storage. Tests: `TestAcceptanceWorkflow`. |
| Injected environment (endpoints, `PORT`) | **Verified** | `TestCloudRunRevisionReachesStorageAndPubSubWithNoClientOptions` (#576): a service deployed with no `env` calls `storage.NewClient(ctx)` and `pubsub.NewClient(ctx, project)` with no options, lists a bucket and publishes to a topic, and the host pulls the message. `TestCloudRunRevisionUsesInjectedMetadataADCAndServedEndpoints` (#681): a service deployed with no `env` gets credentials from `google.FindDefaultCredentials`, which finds no file and asks the metadata server at the injected `GCE_METADATA_HOST`; an official Storage client sends that local token on a bucket listing. The same revision calls KMS `Encrypt`, Scheduler `ListJobs` and Logging `WriteLogEntries` at the injected `CLOUDBURROW_KMS_ENDPOINT`, `CLOUDBURROW_SCHEDULER_ENDPOINT` and `CLOUDBURROW_LOGGING_ENDPOINT`, and the host decrypts the ciphertext, finds its job in the listing and lists the entry. Every revision and job task is given the in-cluster `*_EMULATOR_HOST` of each enabled emulator, `CLOUDBURROW_*_ENDPOINT` and `GCE_METADATA_HOST` at `cloudburrow-host` (with Cloud Run, [networking.md](networking.md#reaching-your-machine-from-a-pod)), and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` (the service's project). **Exercised from a pod, through the injected value:** `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST`, `PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GCE_METADATA_HOST`, `CLOUDBURROW_KMS_ENDPOINT`, `CLOUDBURROW_SCHEDULER_ENDPOINT`, `CLOUDBURROW_LOGGING_ENDPOINT` and `CLOUDBURROW_BIGQUERY_ENDPOINT`. `TestCloudRunRevisionGetsBigQueryRefusalsThroughTheFront` (#874, #902) calls BigQuery at the injected `CLOUDBURROW_BIGQUERY_ENDPOINT`, the emulator's Service, whose REST port is the validating front in the emulator's pod. **Injected but not exercised from a pod:** `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST`, `DATASTORE_EMULATOR_HOST`, `BIGTABLE_EMULATOR_HOST`, `SPANNER_EMULATOR_HOST` (the Spanner pod test sets its own), `CLOUDBURROW_BIGQUERY_STORAGE_ENDPOINT`, and `CLOUDBURROW_TASKS_ENDPOINT`, `CLOUDBURROW_SECRETMANAGER_ENDPOINT` and `CLOUDBURROW_RESOURCEMANAGER_ENDPOINT` (the host probe is given its addresses); no CI shard enables Cloud Run with the opt-in emulators other than BigQuery (the run shard, #874). **A variable the caller sets wins.** In the pod the injected ones follow the caller's, each in name order. The Cloud Run API (`GetService`, `ListServices`, `GetRevision`, jobs and executions) shows **only the caller's** env, as Cloud Run keeps `K_SERVICE` and `PORT` out of the resource, so a Terraform plan sees no drift; `kubectl get ksvc -o yaml` shows the injected ones. No credential is injected. `PORT` is Knative's. The caller's `env` is still mapped and ordered deterministically. |
| Logs in Cloud Logging | **Verified** (stderr severity and `instanceId` value UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/logging>)) | `TestCloudRunLogsInCloudLogging` (#1298), in CI's run shard (Logging as `RUN_LOGGING`), read back with the official `logadmin` client: while Cloud Run and Cloud Logging are both served, each line a revision's or a job task's container writes is an entry in log `run.googleapis.com/stdout` or `run.googleapis.com/stderr` (by the stream the container runtime recorded, read from the pod's log file on the kind node), with resource `cloud_run_revision` (`project_id`, `service_name`, `revision_name`, `location`, `configuration_name`) or `cloud_run_job` (`project_id`, `job_name`, `location`), the label `instanceId` (the pod's UID) and, for a task, `run.googleapis.com/execution_name`, `task_index` and `task_attempt`. A line that is a JSON object is a `jsonPayload`, its `severity`, `logging.googleapis.com/labels`, `trace`, `spanId`, `trace_sampled`, `insertId` and an RFC 3339 `time` or `timestamp` read out of it as Google's structured logging documents, `message` kept; any other line is a `textPayload` with severity DEFAULT, stderr included. The entries go through WriteLogEntries, so exclusions apply, and are read by ListLogEntries, `gcloud logging read 'resource.type="cloud_run_revision"'` (run by hand through `gcloud-setup`) and the console's Logs Explorer. Not the queue-proxy sidecar's lines; lines a pod wrote before `up` started are not written again. Units `TestRunLogTargets`, `TestRunLogEntry`, `TestRunLogFeederReadsCRIStreams`. Since #1333 `TestGcloudRunLogsRead`, through the compat harness with egress to Google blocked: the real `gcloud run services logs read` and `gcloud run jobs logs read` print the lines the service's and the job's containers wrote, and not another service's; `--log-filter=severity>=WARNING` leaves out the DEFAULT lines. Their filters (`resource.type`, `resource.labels.service_name` or `job_name`, `resource.labels.location`, `severity >= DEFAULT`) are in the grammar below. In CI's run shard where gcloud is installed, through gcloud-setup's `run` and `logging` overrides of that instance. |
| Stop and cleanup | **Verified** | Deletion refuses any Knative Service lacking `cloudburrow.dev/owned=true` (`internal/adapter/run/knative.go`): `TestRunDeleteRefusesAnUnownedKnativeService` (#1576) applies a Knative Service by hand with kubectl in the adapter's namespace, reads it with the official `ServicesClient`, and `DeleteService` is `FAILED_PRECONDITION` with the service left in the cluster. `TestOwnershipLabelsArePresent` checks that the label is stamped on what CloudBurrow makes. |
| Scale to keep an instance warm (`minInstanceCount`) | **Verified** | `TestMinScaleKeepsAnInstanceWarm`: a pod stays running with no traffic. |
| Requests per instance (`maxInstanceRequestConcurrency`) | Partial | Mapped to Knative's `containerConcurrency` and readable on the console's Configuration tab. **Not tested under load** — proving a concurrency limit needs sustained traffic. |
| Request timeout (`template.timeout`) | Partial | Mapped to Knative's `timeoutSeconds` and asserted by `TestTimeoutReachesKnative`. It was previously **dropped in silence**, so a service deployed with a ten-minute timeout got Knative's default and failed at five with nothing to explain it. The mapping is asserted; the resulting behaviour under a long request is not. |
| Resource limits (`container.resources.limits`) | Partial | CPU and memory limits reach the manifest. Whether the kubelet enforces them identically to Cloud Run is not claimed. |
| Scale to zero | **Verified** | `TestScaleToZeroHappensWithoutTraffic`, observed on Knative's own schedule. Cloud Run also scales to zero but on a different schedule; the timing is **not** claimed to match. |
| Max instances (`maxInstanceCount`) | Partial | `TestMaxScaleIsRecordedOnTheRevision` proves the annotation reaches the revision. **The cap is not tested under load** — proving a ceiling needs sustained concurrency that would make the suite slow and flaky. |
| Traffic to the latest revision | **Verified** | `TestSingleRevisionTakesAllTraffic`: 100% to the latest revision. |
| Traffic splitting across revisions | **Verified** | `TestRunTrafficSplitAndTags`: a 50/50 split over 40 requests reached both revisions (see Traffic above). The split is Knative's; the distribution is not claimed to match Cloud Run's request for request. |
| Service name validated before apply | **Verified** | An invalid name previously reached the cluster and came back as `Internal` — which says the fault is ours when it is the caller's, and buries the rule. Now `InvalidArgument` naming the rule. A cluster rejection is also classified as `InvalidArgument` rather than `Internal`, and carries the cluster's own message. Tests: `TestServiceIDIsValidatedBeforeAnythingIsApplied`, `TestClusterRejectionIsInvalidArgumentNotInternal`, `TestServiceIDRejectsBadNames`. |
| Jobs / Executions | **Verified** | Served on Kubernetes `batch/v1` Jobs (#582); see [Jobs and executions](#cloud-run-jobs-and-executions) below. Tests: `TestRunJobLifecycle`, `TestRunJobFailureAndCancel`. |
| **Service URL reachable from a browser** | **Verified** | `cloudburrow up` publishes the Knative gateway on a host port (default `9080`) and names services `<service>.<namespace>.cloudburrow.localhost`. Verified with headless Chrome and `test/k8s/ingress_test.go`. **Loopback only**, HTTP only. The mapping is fixed at cluster creation, and `up` reports when a cluster predates it rather than leaving a port that silently refuses. Tests: `TestBrowserStyleRequestReachesTheService`, `TestKnativeServiceIsNamedUnderTheLocalDomain`, `TestIngressIsLoopbackOnly`. |
| Service URL DNS resolution | Partial | `*.cloudburrow.localhost` resolves on the macOS system resolver and musl, **not** on bare glibc or **Go's pure resolver** (`CGO_ENABLED=0`), which forwards the query to the configured nameserver. The `Host`-header path needs no resolver and always works. Measured matrix in [networking.md](networking.md). |
| HTTPS to a service | **Not supported** | No certificate is issued. Publishing a port answering with a self-signed certificate would look like support for something that does not work. |

### Cloud Run: Worker pools and instances

`google.cloud.run.v2.WorkerPools` (#1300) and `google.cloud.run.v2.Instances` (#1299) are served on
the Cloud Run port, over gRPC and JSON. Both are containers that run with no request routed to them,
at a fixed count, which is an `apps/v1` Deployment with no Knative Service, route or autoscaler. The
resource is kept as protojson in a ConfigMap the adapter owns (`run-worker-pool-<scope>-<id>`,
`run-instance-<scope>-<id>`, where `<scope>` is a hash of `projects/{p}/locations/{l}`, also the
`cloudburrow.dev/run-scope` label on every object and in every selector, so two projects' or regions'
resources of one ID are two, #1399; one an older version created as `run-worker-pool-<id>` still
reads back, updates and deletes under that name), so its `etag` is the ConfigMap's `resourceVersion` and does not move when the
Deployment's status does. The pods are rendered by **the same container mapping as a revision and a
task**: image localisation, `command`, `args`, `env`, `secretKeyRef`, `resources.limits`, probes,
secret and in-memory volumes. A create, update, stop or start operation completes **once the
instances are ready** (#1348), as a service's completes once its revision is: while they come up,
a read reports `reconciling` with a `Ready` terminal condition of `CONDITION_RECONCILING`, then
`CONDITION_SUCCEEDED` once every wanted pod is available (and, for an instance, its route is
programmed). The operation fails, FAILED_PRECONDITION with the reason, when the Deployment's rollout
stalls (`CONDITION_FAILED` with the controller's message), when a pod cannot start (`ErrImagePull`,
`ImagePullBackOff`, `InvalidImageName`, `CreateContainerConfigError`, `CreateContainerError`), or
when the instances are not ready within the adapter's ready timeout (five minutes by default).

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `WorkerPools.CreateWorkerPool`, `WorkerPools.GetWorkerPool`, `WorkerPools.ListWorkerPools`, `WorkerPools.UpdateWorkerPool`, `WorkerPools.DeleteWorkerPool` | **Verified** | `TestRunWorkerPoolLifecycle`, official `run.WorkerPoolsClient`: a pool of two instances becomes ready, is read and listed (newest first). `scaling.manualInstanceCount` is the Deployment's `replicas`; unset, a pool gets **one** instance. Changing only the count keeps the revision; a changed template is a new revision named `{pool}-{generation}-{suffix}` (or `template.revision` when set), and the old one is retired. `UpdateWorkerPool` with no `update_mask` replaces the whole pool; **with one** (#1387) only the fields it names change, merged onto the stored pool as `UpdateService` merges (#1260, AIP-134): `TestRunWorkerPoolUpdateMaskAndInstanceSplits` rescales with `scaling.manual_instance_count` alone (the description and the revision are kept) and changes `template` alone (a new revision at the same count); a path names a field anywhere in the tree and replaces it whole, `*` replaces every settable field, and an output-only or unknown path is INVALID_ARGUMENT. `allow_missing` creates; a stale `etag` is ABORTED. **`instanceSplits` across revisions** (#1387), as Google documents for worker pools: each split gives the latest revision (`INSTANCE_SPLIT_ALLOCATION_TYPE_LATEST`) or a named one a percentage of `scaling.manualInstanceCount`, and they add up to 100 (otherwise INVALID_ARGUMENT, as is a split naming no revision, the same revision twice, or a revision the pool does not have). The pool's Deployment runs the latest revision's share; each other revision with a share runs as a Deployment of its own, rendered from the template its ReplicaSet recorded. A share is its percentage of the instances rounded by largest remainder, so the shares add up to the instance count, ties to the split listed first (Google does not document its rounding; UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/cloud/run/v2/worker_pool_revision_template.proto>)). The test splits four instances 50/50 between two revisions and finds two running pods of each, both revisions `Active`, `instanceSplitStatuses` as set, and the split revision's `DeleteRevision` FAILED_PRECONDITION; 100% to the latest again retires the old revision and its pods stop. The pool is ready once every revision's instances are. Unit `TestInstanceSplitsAreChecked`, `TestSplitSharesAddUpToTheInstanceCount`, `TestSplitRevisionRendersItsOwnDeployment`, `TestMergeWorkerPoolMask`. `DeleteWorkerPool` removes the Deployment, every revision and every pod. Refused as UNIMPLEMENTED with the reason: `container.ports` (a worker pool has no ingress), `customAudiences`, `binaryAuthorization`, `template.serviceMesh`, and the pod fields a service refuses (VPC access, CMEK, node selector). Cloud Storage and NFS volumes are not refused (#1474, #1448), and a worker pool mounts a Cloud Storage volume as a service does: `TestRunWorkerPoolMountsACloudStorageVolume` (#1576), whose instance reads an object the Storage client wrote and writes one it reads back, the volume read back by `GetWorkerPool`. |
| Worker pool revisions: `Revisions.GetRevision`, `ListRevisions`, `DeleteRevision` under `workerPools/{pool}` | **Verified** | `TestRunWorkerPoolLifecycle`, official `run.RevisionsClient`. Each revision is the ReplicaSet the Deployment created for its template, which records the template; a retired revision is a ReplicaSet scaled to zero, with `Active` `CONDITION_FAILED` reason `RETIRED`; a revision with a share of `instanceSplits` is `Active` (#1387). Listed newest first. Deleting the revision the pool runs, or one with a split share, is FAILED_PRECONDITION; a retired one is deleted. `service` is left empty. |
| `CreateInstance`, `GetInstance`, `ListInstances`, `StopInstance`, `StartInstance`, `DeleteInstance` | **Verified** | `TestRunInstanceLifecycle`, official `run.InstancesClient`: a standalone instance is a Deployment of one replica, becomes ready, is listed, is stopped (scaled to zero; the terminal condition says "the instance is stopped") and started again, and is deleted. Whether it is stopped is kept on the stored instance. `CreateInstance`'s operation completes once the instance is ready and its route is programmed (#1348). **An instance has a URL** (`urls`, which the proto documents as "All URLs serving traffic for this Instance"): `http://<id>.instance.<namespace>.cloudburrow.localhost`, served through the Knative gateway as a service is, by a Knative networking Ingress over a ClusterIP Service on the serving port; `TestRunInstanceLifecycle` reads the container's reply through it. The serving container is the one that declares a port, or the only one, on its port or 8080, and is given `PORT` unless it sets it, as Cloud Run's container contract does; an instance of several containers none of which declares a port has no URL. Google's URL form for an instance is not documented; the local host is CloudBurrow's (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/cloud/run/v2/instance.proto>)). `ingress` `INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL` (the value read back when unset) is mapped; any other value is UNIMPLEMENTED, as for a service; `invokerIamDisabled` is stored and returned, and no invoker IAM is enforced either way; `iapEnabled` is UNIMPLEMENTED. `showDeleted` is UNIMPLEMENTED, since a deleted instance is not kept. `etag` is checked on stop, start and delete. |
| `Instances.GetIamPolicy`, `Instances.SetIamPolicy`, `Instances.TestIamPermissions` | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestRunUpdateInstance` (#1958), the official `run.InstancesClient` over gRPC: a policy set on an instance is read back with its binding and etag, `TestIamPermissions` returns every permission asked, and a missing instance is `NOT_FOUND`. The policy is the one v1's `projects.locations.instances` IAM methods store beside the instance (row above); nothing enforces it (ADR-0006). |
| `Instances.UpdateInstance` | **Verified** | `TestRunUpdateInstance` (#1958), the official `run.InstancesClient`: `update_mask` names the fields taken from the request (a dotted path ends anywhere in the message, `*` replaces every settable field), the rest are kept, and with no mask the instance is replaced, as `UpdateWorkerPool` does (AIP-134); the change is a new `generation` whose Deployment rolls the instance's container, and the operation completes once the new pod is ready, after which its URL serves the new configuration. A stopped instance stays stopped. `validate_only` returns the instance as it would be and writes nothing; a stale `etag` is `ABORTED`; an output-only path (`uid`, `generation`, `urls`, ...) is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; a missing instance is `NOT_FOUND`, and with `allow_missing` is created. The same configuration checks as `CreateInstance` apply (unsupported fields `UNIMPLEMENTED`, naming them). Unit `TestMergeInstanceMask`. Console: the instance's **Edit** (description, image, environment variables) sends it with a mask of `description` and `containers`. |
| `SourceUpload.UploadSource` | **Verified**, *media upload; the bucket and object names are gcloud's, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-19: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.run.v2>) against Google's* | #1958. The archive is a media upload, as gcloud's generated client sends it (`run.projects.locations.sourceUploads.upload`): a `POST` to `/upload/v2/{parent}:uploadSource` with `uploadType=multipart` (the request's JSON, then the archive) or `uploadType=media` (the archive; the request's fields as query parameters), at most 262,144,000 bytes (the discovery document's `maxSize`). It is written to the instance's Cloud Storage in the regional bucket gcloud's own upload uses, `run-sources-{project}-{region}` (made on first use), at `{services,jobs,workerpools,instances}/{name}[/{containerId}]/{timestamp}-{uuid}{.zip,.tar.gz}`, as gcloud names its objects, and `cloudStorageSource` names it. `encryptionKey` must be a CryptoKey name and is stored with nothing encrypted (as a function's `kms_key_name`); naming two targets is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. A request with no media (gRPC, or the JSON path) carries no archive and is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, naming the upload path (*code UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-19: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.run.v2>)*). `TestRunUploadSource`: the official `run.SourceUploadClient` over gRPC gets that refusal; a multipart upload's object is read back with the official Storage client. `TestGcloudBetaRunDeployRunUpload` (needs Docker, as `TestGcloudRunDeploySource`): `gcloud beta run deploy --source --run-upload` uploads through it, and the build and deploy then run from that object. Unit `TestUploadSourceMedia`. |
| Two projects' resources of one ID | **Verified** for worker pools, jobs, instances and services | `TestRunNamesPerProject` (#1399, #1400), official `run.WorkerPoolsClient`, `run.JobsClient`, `run.ExecutionsClient`, `run.InstancesClient`, `run.ServicesClient` and `run.RevisionsClient`: two projects each create a worker pool, a job, an instance and a service of one ID; each reads back under its own full name with its own labels, lists only in its own project, runs its own pods (each instance and each service answers at its own URL with its own greeting), and counts only its own executions; a second create of the service in one project is ALREADY_EXISTS; deleting one project's leaves the other's ready and serving. Their Kubernetes objects are named `run-<kind>-<scope>-<id>` (bounded to 63 characters with a hash where a DNS label needs it) and selected by the `cloudburrow.dev/run-scope` label; the full resource name is the `cloudburrow.dev/cloud-run-name` annotation, which is what reads back. An execution keeps its generated ID as its batch Job's name, drawn again on a collision. **A service** (#1400) is the Knative Service `<id>-<scope>` (an ID too long for that keeps its first 48 characters and a hash of the full name, so its revisions' names fit in 63), so its URL is `http://<id>-<scope>.default.cloudburrow.localhost` and a tag's `http://<tag>-<id>-<scope>.default.cloudburrow.localhost`; Google's `https://<id>-<hash>-<region>.a.run.app` does not resolve locally. Its revisions read back as Cloud Run names them, `<id>-<generation>-<suffix>` (`x-00001-k4q`; the three-character suffix is a hash of the Knative revision's name, so it is the same on every read), in `latestReadyRevision`, `latestCreatedRevision`, `traffic`, `trafficStatuses`, `Revisions.*`, the v1 API, the console and the logs' `revision_name`, and a revision named so is found again for `GetRevision`, `DeleteRevision`, traffic and tags; Knative's own form (`x-<scope>-00001`) is not a revision ID. A service an older version created is a Knative Service named by its ID: it keeps that name, its URL and its revisions' names (`x-00001`), and is still read, updated, deleted and given IAM under them. **Gap:** a revision's container sees `K_SERVICE`, `K_CONFIGURATION` and `K_REVISION` as Knative sets them, the scoped Knative names, where Cloud Run sets the service ID and the revision ID; Knative reserves the three, so they cannot be set to Cloud Run's values. The console lists the selected project's services (and any older one that recorded no project). |

### Cloud Run: Jobs and executions

`google.cloud.run.v2.Jobs`, `google.cloud.run.v2.Executions` and `google.cloud.run.v2.Tasks` (#1223) are served on the Cloud Run port
over gRPC (#582). A job is configuration, stored as a ConfigMap the adapter owns
(`run-job-<scope>-<id>`, scoped by project and location as a worker pool is, #1399, labelled
`cloudburrow.dev/owned=true`, the job kept as protojson; one an older version created as
`run-job-<id>` still reads back, updates and deletes); each
`RunJob` creates one `batch/v1` Job, which is the execution. Its containers are rendered by
**the same code as a service's revision**: image localisation and pull policy, untagged images
refused, `command`, `args`, `workingDir`, `env`, `secretKeyRef` resolved to the Secret Manager
store's Kubernetes Secret, and `resources.limits`. They are served over JSON too, on the same port (#591): Terraform's
`google_cloud_run_v2_job` applies, updates and destroys (`TestTerraformRun`). `gcloud run jobs`
uses Cloud Run's v1 API: `create`, `list`, `describe` and `delete` are served (#1349), and `update`, `execute` and `executions` (#1379). Worker pools and standalone instances are served
on `apps/v1` Deployments (below); Builds is (#1268, above).

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateJob`, `GetJob`, `ListJobs`, `UpdateJob`, `DeleteJob` | **Verified** | `TestRunJobLifecycle`, with the official `run.JobsClient`. Each returns a long-running operation that is done at once: the job is ready when it is written. Unset task fields read back with Cloud Run's documented defaults (1 task, 3 retries, a 10-minute timeout; asserted in unit `TestJobRunsAsABatchJob`). `etag` is the ConfigMap's `resourceVersion`, and a stale one on update, delete or run is **`ABORTED`**, as for services (not measured against Google). `UpdateJob` replaces the whole job and bumps `generation`; `allow_missing` creates; `validate_only` writes nothing (unit, on create). `DeleteJob` deletes every execution of the job too. A job under another project or location is NOT_FOUND. `executionCount` counts the executions that **still exist**; Cloud Run may keep counting deleted ones. |
| `RunJob` | **Verified** | `TestRunJobLifecycle`: a two-task job runs as one batch Job with `completions: 2` and `completionMode: Indexed` (asserted on the cluster), each task printing its own `CLOUD_RUN_TASK_INDEX`. `task_count` is `completions`, `parallelism` is `parallelism` (0 runs every task at once), `max_retries` is `backoffLimitPerIndex` (retries per task, as Cloud Run counts them), and the task `timeout` is each pod's `activeDeadlineSeconds` (per attempt). `CLOUD_RUN_JOB`, `CLOUD_RUN_EXECUTION`, `CLOUD_RUN_TASK_INDEX`, `CLOUD_RUN_TASK_ATTEMPT` and `CLOUD_RUN_TASK_COUNT` are set; `CLOUD_RUN_TASK_ATTEMPT` (#1448) is the Job controller's `batch.kubernetes.io/job-index-failure-count` on the pod, the task's retries so far, 0 on its first attempt (`TestRunNFSVolumesAndCloudRunEnv` asserts all five as the task saw them). The operation's metadata is the execution from the start, and it completes when the execution does: with the execution on success, and on failure with an error carrying the failing task's message (code FAILED_PRECONDITION, not measured against Google). Overrides of `args`, `env`, `task_count` and `timeout` apply to that execution only (`TestRunJobFailureAndCancel`; unit `TestRunJobOverridesAndEtags`). `secretKeyRef` is verified by `TestRunJobReadsASecretManagerSecret`, which also asserts the batch Job carries the reference, not the payload. |
| `GetExecution`, `ListExecutions` | **Verified** | `TestRunJobLifecycle`. Read from the batch Job's status: `runningCount` is `active`, `succeededCount` is `succeeded`, `failedCount` the tasks in `failedIndexes`, `retriedCount` the other failed pods. Conditions are `Completed` and `Started`; `reconciling` is true until the execution ends. Listed newest first; a missing job is NOT_FOUND. The execution's `template` is the one it ran with, recorded on the batch Job. |
| A failed task | **Verified** | `TestRunJobFailureAndCancel`: a container that exits 3 yields `Completed` = `CONDITION_FAILED`, `executionReason` `NON_ZERO_EXIT_CODE`, and a message naming the task, the container, the exit code and **the container's own output** (the container's termination message is `FallbackToLogsOnError`, so the tail of its log is kept). A task timeout reports the pod's `DeadlineExceeded` the same way (unit `TestExecutionHelpers` only). |
| `CancelExecution` | **Verified** | `TestRunJobFailureAndCancel`: a running execution is cancelled by suspending its batch Job, which stops its pods; the operation completes when none is running, with the unfinished tasks in `cancelledCount` and `executionReason` `CANCELLED` (`CANCELLING` while pods stop). Cancelling an execution that has ended is FAILED_PRECONDITION (unit only; not measured against Google). |
| `DeleteExecution` | **Verified** | `TestRunJobLifecycle`: the batch Job and its pods are deleted, running or not. |
| `ListTasks`, `GetTask` | **Verified** | `TestRunTasksAreAnExecutionsPods` (#1223), with the official `run.TasksClient`: an execution of two tasks lists one task per index, named `{execution}-task{index}`, in index order. A task is the pods the batch controller made for its completion index, one per attempt: `retried` is the attempts after the first, `start_time` the newest attempt's container start, `completion_time` its container's finish, `scheduled_time` its pod's creation, and `last_attempt_result` the newest finished attempt's exit code, signal and status (OK, or UNKNOWN with the failing container's message, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED for a task timeout). Conditions are `Completed` and `Started`: a failed attempt with retries left keeps `Completed` pending, the last one fails it with `NON_ZERO_EXIT_CODE`, and a task the execution ended before (cancelled, or stopped by another task's failure) is `CANCELLED`. `containers`, `max_retries`, `timeout`, labels and annotations are the execution's. `log_uri` is Google's Logs Explorer link for the task's entries (Logs, `logUri`, below; #1379); the console's task page shows its pods' logs. A task beyond the count, or under another execution, is NOT_FOUND; paging is unit-tested (`TestTasksAreReadFromTheExecutionsPods`). |
| Refused fields | **Verified** | The task template's `nodeSelector`, a container's `dependsOn`, `readinessProbe`, `baseImageUri` and `sourceCode`, are refused by **the same check as a service's template**, in the same words, prefixed `template.template.`; so are `startExecutionToken`/`runExecutionToken`, `gpuZonalRedundancyDisabled`, and a job container's `ports`, `startupProbe` and `livenessProbe`, which a task has no use for. All UNIMPLEMENTED naming the field (`TestRunJobFailureAndCancel` for `nodeSelector` through the SDK; unit `TestJobRefusesWhatItDoesNotMap` for the rest). A job's Cloud Storage volumes are served since #1474 (`TestRunCloudStorageFUSEVolumes`), and NFS volumes since #1448. `vpcAccess`, `encryptionKey`, `executionEnvironment`, `binaryAuthorization` and a mount's `subPath` are stored, and `subPath` mapped (#1346; "Stored settings" above); a Cloud SQL volume is served (#1346; "Cloud SQL volumes" above). |
| `Jobs.GetIamPolicy`, `Jobs.SetIamPolicy`, `Jobs.TestIamPermissions` | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestRunJobIamPolicyIsStoredNotEnforced` (#1216), official `run.JobsClient`, with the same semantics as a service's (above): a policy round-trips with its etag, a stale etag is ABORTED, conditional bindings follow the service's (#1745), and the job's own `etag` is unchanged. `RunJob` does not read it: the test runs the job under a policy that grants `run.jobs.run` to no one. Kept in its own ConfigMap owned by the job's, so it goes with `DeleteJob`. Unit `TestJobIamPolicyIsStoredNotEnforced`. From the console's Permissions tab: `TestConsolePermissionsOnARunServiceAndJob`. |
| `WorkerPools.GetIamPolicy`, `WorkerPools.SetIamPolicy`, `WorkerPools.TestIamPermissions` | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestRunWorkerPoolLifecycle` (#1300), official `run.WorkerPoolsClient`, with a service's and a job's semantics under ADR-0006: a policy round-trips with its etag, a stale etag is ABORTED, conditional bindings follow the service's (#1745), an empty set on a missing pool. Kept in its own ConfigMap owned by the pool's. |
| Logs, `logUri` | **Verified**, *Google's form* | `TestRunV1JobExecutionsAndTasks` (#1379), v1 `status.logUri` and v2 `log_uri`, which are the same: an execution's is Google's Cloud Logging console link, `https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/viewer?project={project}&advancedFilter=…` with the filter `resource.type="cloud_run_job"`, `resource.labels.job_name`, `resource.labels.location` and `labels."run.googleapis.com/execution_name"`, and a task's adds `labels."run.googleapis.com/task_index"`. It is not the CloudBurrow console's Logs Explorer, which takes no Cloud Logging filter; the same filter given to `gcloud logging read` reads the entries locally, which the run log feeder writes under that resource and those labels (#1298). |
| Console screen | **Verified** | `TestConsoleRunJobsCreateExecuteAndCancel` (#785): the console's Jobs page at `/run/jobs`, through this API. See the Console table. |

## Optional services

Opt-in, and **never started by default** — a developer should not pay memory for databases
they did not ask for. Enable with `--services firestore,datastore,bigtable,spanner`.

These four each wrap a **Google-published emulator**: Firestore, Datastore and Bigtable run the
emulators of the Google Cloud CLI image (`gcr.io/google.com/cloudsdktool/google-cloud-cli`,
digest-pinned), and Spanner Google's own `gcr.io/cloud-spanner-emulator/emulator` (measured
2026-10-16 for the first three, from their pods' images; Spanner's is the digest in
`internal/components/optional.go`). The database is not reimplemented, but some of what each pod
serves is CloudBurrow's own: the call front in each pod (#1288), Firestore's Admin API and
Bigtable's instance admin API (#1331), and the fifteen Bigtable RPCs the front answers itself
(#1206). The other opt-in services are **not** Google emulators: BigQuery runs a community
emulator, built from source with CloudBurrow's patches ([below](#bigquery-is-a-community-emulator);
measured: `goccy/bigquery-emulator v0.8.1-cloudburrow.2`), Cloud SQL runs PostgreSQL or MySQL
([below](#cloud-sql-is-not-an-emulator)) and Memorystore Valkey
([below](#memorystore-is-not-an-emulator)). Each of the four has an official emulator environment
variable, so an application needs no code change to use it.

| Service | Backing component | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Firestore ([every RPC](coverage/firestore.md); Admin API, [every RPC](coverage/firestoreadmin.md)) | Cloud SDK `cloud-firestore-emulator`; the Admin API is CloudBurrow's own, in the pod's call front (#1331) | **Verified** | `TestFirestoreDocumentCRUD`: document CRUD, a `>` query, and a transaction. `TestFirestoreAdminDatabases`, `TestFirestoreAdminIndexes`, `TestFirestoreAdminFields`: databases, indexes and field overrides through the official Admin client (the `FirestoreAdmin` rows below) |
| Datastore ([every RPC](coverage/datastore.md); Admin API, [every RPC](coverage/datastoreadmin.md)) | Cloud SDK `cloud-datastore-emulator`, as Firestore in Datastore mode | **Verified** | `TestDatastoreEntityCRUD`: entity CRUD, a filtered query, and a transaction. `TestDatastoreQueriesSeeAFreshWrite`: 50 queries in a row, each made right after its write, all see it. The emulator runs in Firestore-in-Datastore mode, which is strongly consistent like a Datastore database in Google Cloud today. It does not reproduce legacy Datastore's eventually consistent non-ancestor queries. Left at its default (`--consistency=0.9`), about one query in ten missed a fresh write (#371). |
| Bigtable ([every RPC](coverage/bigtable.md)) | Cloud SDK `bigtable` (`cbtemulator`); the instance admin API is CloudBurrow's own, in the pod's front (#1331) | **Verified** | `TestBigtableTableAndRows`: table and column family creation, row write, read, and a filtered scan. `TestBigtableInstancesAndClusters`, `TestBigtableAppProfilesAndInstanceIAM`: instances, clusters, app profiles and instance IAM through the official `InstanceAdminClient` (the `BigtableInstanceAdmin` rows below) |
| Spanner ([every RPC](coverage/spanner.md)) | `cloud-spanner-emulator` 1.5.58 (own image, digest-pinned) | **Verified, host and pod** | `TestSpannerSchemaAndQuery`: instance, database, DDL, write, read, SQL query. `TestSpannerReadWriteTransactionIsAtomic`: a read-modify-write transfer, and an aborted transaction leaving nothing behind. `TestSpannerDatabasesAreIsolated`. `TestSpannerFromInsideAPod`: the same client from a Job, over cluster DNS. Every RPC is classified (#1199): 64 verified through the official clients (`AddSplitPoints` a stored no-op since #1523, `FetchCacheUpdate` an empty routing cache since #1523) and 1 refused `UNIMPLEMENTED`, naming why (`InternalUpdateGraphOperation`, Google's internal API for Spanner Graph jobs). The emulator refused backups, backup schedules, IAM, instance configurations, instance and partition updates; the call front in its pod serves them (#1461, #1486, #1498). |

A **Verified** row above is for the RPCs a test exercises, not for the whole service. Each
service's generated page lists every RPC of its protos: an RPC an official-client test issues is
Verified and links that test, and every other RPC is **Unknown**, so nothing is claimed for it.
The RPCs are the ones each client method issues, read from the pinned client libraries: Firestore's
`DocumentRef.Get` is `BatchGetDocuments` and `Set` and `Delete` are `Commit`; Datastore's `Get` is
`Lookup` and `Put` and `Delete` are non-transactional `Commit`s; Bigtable's `ReadRow` is `ReadRows`
and an unconditional `Apply` is `MutateRow`; Spanner's `NewClient` creates a multiplexed session
with `CreateSession`, and a mutation-only `Apply` is `BeginTransaction` then `Commit`. A result a
test ignores (a cleanup's `DeleteTable` or `DeleteInstance`) claims nothing. Bigtable's instance
admin service is listed on its page since #1331, and waiting on an admin operation polls `google.longrunning.Operations`,
which no page lists.

The emulator does not serve PartitionQuery (it answered `UNIMPLEMENTED`); the call front in the Firestore pod answers it (`internal/queryfront`), over gRPC and REST, from the emulator's `RunQuery` over the collection group selecting `__name__` alone (at `read_time` when given): at most `partition_count` cursors, each a document reference, evenly spaced in name order, none when there are too few documents to split, paged by `page_size` and `page_token`. A query Google does not partition (not a collection group, a filter, limit, offset, cursor, or an order other than `__name__` ascending) is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. **Difference:** Google may return fewer cursors than asked, choosing its split points from its storage; this returns as many as asked whenever the group has more documents than that, so its partitions can be smaller than Google's |
| `Firestore.ExecutePipeline` | **Verified** | `TestFirestorePipelines` (#1500), through the official Go client's pipeline API (`Client.Pipeline`), on a database created with the `ENTERPRISE` edition: `collection` with `where` (`and`, `greater_than`, `equal`), `collection_group` with `sort`, `offset` and `limit`, `aggregate` (`count`, `sum`, grouped), `add_fields` (`string_concat`), `remove_fields`, `unnest` (of an `array` expression), `select` and `distinct`, and `explain_options` in `analyze` mode; on `(default)`, a Standard edition database, it is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` "ExecutePipeline requires the Database Edition to be `enterprise`.", as on Google, and a `subcollection` stage outside a subquery is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. `TestFirestorePipelinesMore` (#1523), each result checked against a value computed by hand: `let` with variable references, `literals`, `regex_find`, `regex_find_all`, `array_first_n`, `array_last_n`, `array_index_of_all`, `maximum_n`, the `array_filter` and `array_transform` (with an index) lambdas, `timestamp_trunc` (day, month, and in a time zone), `timestamp_extract` (hour, dayofweek, isoweek, isoyear), `timestamp_diff`, `geo_distance`, the `search` stage over a `geo_distance` query (with its `sort`), the `update` stage (with transformations, and without, replacing the document; `NOT_FOUND` for a document that does not exist) and the `delete` stage, each returning `documents_modified`, a write stage before another stage or in a transaction refused `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, a pipeline in a transaction (`Transaction.Execute`, the client then committing), and pipelines at a `read_time` before the documents existed, after they were created, and between two updates. `TestFirestorePipelineFunctions` (#1951), against the examples of Google's function reference (<https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/pipelines/functions/array-functions> and its string, timestamp, comparison, logical, map, arithmetic and debugging pages, read 2026-11-20): `regex_find` and `regex_find_all` with a string and with a REGEX value (`regex("two", "i")`, the client's `BSONRegex`), the whole match returned, `NULL` and `[]` when nothing matches, an invalid pattern refused; `array_first_n`, `array_last_n`, `array_index_of_all` (of `null`), `minimum_n` and `maximum_n` (nulls ignored), each refusing a negative n, and `offset` (absent out of bounds and on a non-array); `array_filter` over `[1, null, 3]` and with the row's fields in the predicate, `array_transform` with and without an index; `timestamp_trunc` (`week(friday)`, `week`, `isoweek`, `quarter`, `isoyear`, a day in `America/Los_Angeles`, a month in `GMT+06:32:43`), `timestamp_extract` (`week`, `dayofyear`, a year in `Asia/Tokyo`), `timestamp_diff` (negative, truncating, and over two thousand years in microseconds); `cmp` across types and of `NULL` with absent; `switch_on` with and without a default (an error when nothing matches); `rand`, `current_document` and `map_entries`; and, as raw functions through the generated client (`apiv1`), `error` (caught by `if_error` and `is_error`, else `INVALID_ARGUMENT` with its message) and `current_context`. The same test (#1990) checks the logical, comparison and array pages' semantics: three-valued `and`, `or`, `nor` and `xor` (`NULL` when a `NULL` or absent input leaves the result open, `and(NULL, FALSE)` `FALSE`, `or(NULL, TRUE)` `TRUE`; `where` keeps only `TRUE`), `equal(NaN, NaN)` `TRUE` and `not_equal(NaN, NaN)` `FALSE`, `NaN` in `equal_any`, `not_equal_any` and `array_contains`, `NaN` incomparable in `less_than` and `greater_than_or_equal`, the scalar `maximum` and `minimum` over their arguments (`LogicalMaximum`, `LogicalMinimum`) and over one array's elements (`ArrayMaximum`, `ArrayMinimum`), `sum` of an array (`ArraySum`: non-numbers ignored, `NaN`, `NULL` with no number, an error on integer overflow before any float), and `count_distinct` taking `1` and `1.0`, `0.0` and `-0.0`, and two `NaN`s as one value each. UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-20: <https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/pipelines/functions/logical-functions> and its comparison, array and aggregate pages say nothing): `not(NULL)` is `NULL`; a non-boolean input to the logical functions is an error; `NaN` sorts below every number in `maximum` and `minimum`; `less_than_or_equal(NaN, NaN)` is `FALSE`; a lone array argument to `maximum`/`minimum` is the array form; `sum(NULL)` is `NULL`; the `sum` aggregate of no number is `0`. The Node.js client (`@google-cloud/firestore` 9.4.1's `pipelines`, `test/compat-node/firestore-pipeline.test.mjs`) runs `array_filter`, `array_transform` (with an index) and `regex_find` on an Enterprise database. **Edition:** CloudBurrow follows Google's rule: pipelines run only on a database created with `database_edition: ENTERPRISE` (CreateDatabase accepts it since #1500, and a clone keeps its source's edition); `(default)` and every other database are Standard. The emulator does not serve pipelines: the call front in the Firestore pod answers ExecutePipeline itself (`internal/firestoreadmin/pipeline.go`), over gRPC (server streaming) and REST (`documents:executePipeline`, the responses as a JSON array). The input stage's documents are read from the emulator's own API (`ListCollectionIds` and `ListDocuments`, recursively), and every stage is evaluated in Go, in order. **Stages served:** `collection`, `collection_group`, `database`, `documents`, `where`, `select`, `add_fields`, `remove_fields`, `sort`, `limit`, `offset`, `aggregate`, `distinct`, `find_nearest` (euclidean, cosine, dot product; `limit` and `distance_field`), `sample` (documents or percent), `union`, `unnest` (`index_field`), `replace_with`, `literals` (a `__name__` reference names the document), `let`, `update` and `delete` (#1523), `search` over geographic queries, and `subcollection` in a subquery (#1613). **Subqueries** (#1613, `TestFirestorePipelineSubqueries`, on Google's own restaurants and reviews, each result as the subcollection stage's page gives it): `array(pipeline)` (the client's `ToArrayExpression`) is the subquery's results, each a map of its fields (no `__name__`), an empty array when there are none; `scalar(pipeline)` (`ToScalarExpression`) is its one result, `null` when there is none and an error when there are more, a single field elevated to its value and more fields a map, as Google's "Perform joins with subqueries" guide documents. A subquery is evaluated once for each row of the outer pipeline, in any stage's expression (`add_fields`, `select`, `where`, `sort`); its field references read its own documents, and the variables the outer pipeline bound with `let` reach it through `variable(...)`, so Google's manual form (`let` the parent's `__name__`, then a `collection_group` filtered on `parent(__name__)` equal to it) reads the same as `subcollection`, which is the documents of the named collection under the outer document: none for an outer row without a document name (after a `select`, say). `subcollection` outside a subquery, and `update` or `delete` inside one, are `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. **Storage size** (#1613): `storage_size` is a value's size by Google's "Storage size calculations" page (<https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/storage-size>): a string its UTF-8 bytes + 1, a boolean or null 1, an integer, floating-point number or timestamp 8, a geographical point 16, bytes their length, a vector 8 bytes a dimension, an array the sum of its values, a reference its document name's size (each collection and document ID's string size, + 16), absent absent; the page's `users/jeff/tasks/my_task_id` example is checked to the byte (name 44, values 9, 1, 8 and 22, and the document 147: `storage_size(__name__)` plus `storage_size(current_document())`). A map is "calculated the same way as document size", which CloudBurrow reads as its field names' string sizes, its values' sizes and 32 bytes, a map having no name (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/storage-size>): the page does not say whether a map's size takes the 32 bytes). **Reference slices** (#1613): `reference_slice(ref, offset[, length])` is the reference's (collection ID, document ID) segments sliced as `array_slice` slices an array, a negative offset counting from the end and no length meaning to the end (the client's `ReferenceSliceToEnd`); Google's examples on `a/1/b/2/c/3` (`1, 2` is `b/2/c/3`, `0, 2` is `a/1/b/2`) are checked; its third, `-2, 2` as `c/3`, contradicts its own "just like `array_slice(...)`", by which it is `b/2/c/3`, and CloudBurrow follows the rule (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/pipelines/functions/reference-functions>)). **Write stages:** `update` and `delete` must be last, after none of `aggregate`, `distinct`, `unnest`, `find_nearest`, `union` or `search`, and not in a transaction, as Google documents; they write through the emulator's `BatchWrite`, at most 500 documents a batch, each document atomically on its own and none across documents, stopping at the first failure (partial success is possible, as on Google). `update` replaces each document with the row, after its transformations, with the precondition that it exists; a document met twice is written twice, and `delete` deletes a repeat once. The result is one document, `documents_modified`. In explain mode `explain` they write nothing. **Search:** the `search` stage must follow the input stage; its `query`, `sort`, `add_fields`, `offset`, `limit` and `retrieval_depth` are served, results newest first unless sorted, as Google documents; `geo_distance` is in meters, the haversine distance on a sphere of S2's 6371010 m radius (Google names no Earth model), and needs no geospatial index here; it is served only inside the `search` stage (its `query`, `sort` and `add_fields`), as the client documents ("This Expression can only be used within a Search stage"), and is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` anywhere else (#1951). Full-text search (`document_matches`, `score`, a string query) is `UNIMPLEMENTED`: Google's text search reference defines neither its tokenization nor its score, so no equivalent can be built from it. **Functions served:** logic (`and`, `or`, `xor`, `nor`, `not`, `conditional`), comparison (`equal`, `not_equal`, `less_than`, `less_than_or_equal`, `greater_than`, `greater_than_or_equal`, `equal_any`, `not_equal_any`), existence and types (`exists`, `is_absent`, `is_null`, `is_nan`, `is_error`, `if_error`, `if_absent`, `if_null`, `coalesce`, `type`, `is_type`), arithmetic (`add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `divide`, `mod`, `pow`, `log`, `abs`, `ceil`, `floor`, `round`, `trunc`, `sqrt`, `exp`, `ln`, `log10`), strings (`char_length`, `byte_length`, `to_lower`, `to_upper`, `trim`, `ltrim`, `rtrim`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `string_contains`, `string_concat`, `string_reverse`, `string_index_of`, `string_replace_all`, `string_replace_one`, `string_repeat`, `split`, `substring`, `like`, `regex_contains`, `regex_match`, `concat`, `reverse`, `length`, `join`), arrays (`array`, `array_contains`, `array_contains_any`, `array_contains_all`, `array_length`, `array_reverse`, `array_concat`, `array_get`, `array_first`, `array_last`, `array_index_of`, `array_slice`, `array_first_n`, `array_last_n`, `array_index_of_all`, `minimum_n`, `maximum_n`, `offset`, `logical_minimum`, `logical_maximum`), lambdas (`array_filter`, `array_transform`, with an index parameter; a predicate that is neither boolean nor null is an error), regular expressions (`regex_find`, `regex_find_all`, `regex_contains`, `regex_match`, RE2, the pattern a string or a REGEX value with the options `i`, `m` and `s`; `regex_find` is the whole first match, as the reference says "the first substring in value that matches"), general (`cmp` across types in the sort order, absent as null; `switch_on`, an error when no condition is true and there is no default; `rand`; `current_document`; `current_context`, the row's fields; `error`, an expression error with its message; `map_entries`, the entries in key order (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-20: <https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/pipelines/functions/map-functions>): Google states no order, and its example lists `foo` before `bar`, an order a map value does not keep)), geography (`geo_distance`), maps (`map`, `map_get`, `get_field`, `map_merge`, `map_set`, `map_remove`, `map_keys`, `map_values`), documents (`document_id`, `collection_id`, `parent`, `reference_slice`), `storage_size`, the subqueries `array` and `scalar`, timestamps (`current_timestamp`, `timestamp_add`, `timestamp_subtract`, `timestamp_to_unix_seconds`/`_millis`/`_micros`, `unix_seconds_to_timestamp`/`_millis_`/`_micros_`, `timestamp_trunc` and `timestamp_extract` with every granularity and part Google lists (and `isoweek` for `timestamp_trunc`, which Google's Go client sends) and an optional IANA time zone or offset from GMT, UTC by default, `timestamp_diff` in whole units, truncated toward zero and exact over the whole timestamp range; an offset `GMT+hh[:mm[:ss]]` is read with the POSIX sign, west of Greenwich, as the tz database's `Etc/GMT+N` zones are, which is what Google's one example (2026-01-24 20:00 UTC truncated to the month in `GMT+06:32:43` is 2026-01-01 06:32:43 UTC) gives (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-20: <https://firebase.google.com/docs/firestore/pipelines/functions/timestamp-functions>): the page states no sign convention, and two of its other examples contradict its own rules)), vectors (`cosine_distance`, `euclidean_distance`, `dot_product`, `vector_length`), and the aggregates `count` (of all or of a field), `count_if`, `count_distinct`, `sum`, `average`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `first`, `last`, `array_agg` and `array_agg_distinct`. **Refused, naming it:** a stage or function Google documents that is not served is `UNIMPLEMENTED` (full-text search's `score` and `document_matches`), and a name Google does not know `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (`minimum_n` and `maximum_n` are array functions, not aggregates: Google's aggregate reference lists neither). **Consistency:** a pipeline in a `transaction` reads the documents in the emulator's transaction (its `ListDocuments`, which locks what it reads), and the client commits it there; `new_transaction` begins one in the emulator and returns its ID in the first response; at a `read_time`, the documents are read as they were then, the emulator keeping each document's versions (#1523). `index_mode` is accepted and changes nothing (no index is used). Results carry `__name__`, create and update time while they are still documents, and none after `select`, `aggregate` or `distinct`, as Google documents; each response has the `execution_time`, and the last the explain stats when asked. **Differences:** the explain stats' text (and `output_format: json`) is CloudBurrow's own: the plan's stages and, in `analyze` mode, the results returned, the duration and each stage's output count, not Google's planner output; an expression error (a type error, say) drops the row in `where` and fails the pipeline `INVALID_ARGUMENT` elsewhere; the error messages are CloudBurrow's (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/firestore/native/docs/pipeline/overview>)) but for the edition refusal; a pipeline reads the whole input before evaluating it, as fits an emulator's data. |
| `FirestoreAdmin.ListDatabases`, `FirestoreAdmin.GetDatabase`, `FirestoreAdmin.CreateDatabase`, `FirestoreAdmin.UpdateDatabase`, `FirestoreAdmin.DeleteDatabase` | **Verified** | `TestFirestoreAdminDatabases` (#1331), through the official `firestore/apiv1/admin` client. The Firestore Admin API is not the emulator's, which serves the documents API alone and answered every admin call 404: the call front in the Firestore pod serves it itself (`internal/firestoreadmin`), over gRPC and over REST on the same port, keeping its state in memory as the emulator keeps its documents, and passes every other call to the emulator. `(default)` is described for every project (`FIRESTORE_NATIVE`, location `nam5`, `PESSIMISTIC` concurrency, Standard edition, point-in-time recovery and delete protection off, a one-hour version retention) until it is deleted. CreateDatabase makes a named Native mode database: the emulator serves any database ID it is sent, each with its own documents (measured), so the created database is the emulator's database of that ID, and the official client writes and reads a document in it. A taken ID is `ALREADY_EXISTS`, an ID outside Google's rule (4 to 63 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens) and a missing location `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; Datastore mode (#1880) and customer-managed keys (#1881) are served, in the two rows below; the Enterprise edition is accepted (#1500), and its databases run pipelines and keep user credentials (the rows below). UpdateDatabase changes concurrency mode, point-in-time recovery (enabled, the version retention is seven days), App Engine integration and delete protection; DeleteDatabase is `FAILED_PRECONDITION` while delete protection is on, and otherwise deletes the database's documents through the emulator's reset endpoint, after which the client's read is `NOT_FOUND`. Every create, update and delete returns a done long-running operation with Google's metadata type, which `google.longrunning.Operations` (Get, List, Delete, Cancel) serves. **Differences:** a project's documents can be written to a database ID that was never created, which Google would refuse; the location is stored, not served from. |
| `FirestoreAdmin.CreateDatabase`, `FirestoreAdmin.GetDatabase`, `FirestoreAdmin.ListDatabases`, `FirestoreAdmin.DeleteDatabase` of a Datastore mode database (`type: DATASTORE_MODE`) | **Verified** (refusal messages UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-19: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/datastore/docs/manage-databases>, which quotes none)) | `TestFirestoreDatastoreModeDatabases` (#1880), through the official `firestore/apiv1/admin`, `datastore` and `firestore` clients, and `TestGcloudFirestoreDatastoreModeAndKMSKey` (`gcloud firestore databases create --type=datastore-mode`). The Admin API, in the Firestore pod's call front, records the database (Standard edition alone: an Enterprise edition one is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`), and Get and List report its type. Its entities are the Datastore emulator's, in the Datastore pod: that pod's call front asks the Firestore front's Admin API, over the cluster, whether the Datastore API serves the database a call names (kept a second), and the official Datastore client's `NewClientWithDatabase` writes and reads it, in a namespace too, apart from `(default)`. Each named database's entities are apart from every other's in queries too (#1885, `TestDatastoreNamedDatabasesKeepTheirEntitiesApart`, two Datastore mode databases holding the same kind and keys): kind, kindless, filtered, offset, limited and cursor queries, in a namespace too, `COUNT` and `SUM`, GQL queries and GQL counts, `__kind__` and `__namespace__`, and transactions see the named database alone, and `(default)` neither. The emulator's lookups keep a key's database but its query indexes do not (a query in one named database returned another's entities, measured), so the Datastore front keeps each named database in an emulator project of its own, rewriting every partition ID a call names on its way to the emulator and back, over gRPC and REST (JSON and protobuf). The Firestore client on it is `FAILED_PRECONDITION` "The Cloud Firestore API is not available for Firestore in Datastore Mode database projects/p/databases/d.", and the Datastore client on a named Native mode database `FAILED_PRECONDITION` "The Cloud Datastore API is not available for Firestore in Native mode database …". DeleteDatabase has the Datastore front delete every entity of the database, in every namespace. **Differences:** a database the Admin API has no record of is still served by both APIs, as the emulators serve any database ID (#1550); the Datastore API serves every project's `(default)`, which the Admin API describes as Native mode, as the Datastore emulator always has; the exports, imports, backups, restores and clones of a Datastore mode database answer `UNIMPLEMENTED` (they copy documents, and its entities are the Datastore emulator's). |

The database reports the version in use as `active_key_version`, with a rotated key's new primary added once it is. | `BigtableInstanceAdmin.CreateInstance`, `BigtableInstanceAdmin.GetInstance`, `BigtableInstanceAdmin.ListInstances`, `BigtableInstanceAdmin.UpdateInstance`, `BigtableInstanceAdmin.PartialUpdateInstance`, `BigtableInstanceAdmin.DeleteInstance`, `BigtableInstanceAdmin.CreateCluster`, `BigtableInstanceAdmin.GetCluster`, `BigtableInstanceAdmin.ListClusters`, `BigtableInstanceAdmin.UpdateCluster`, `BigtableInstanceAdmin.PartialUpdateCluster`, `BigtableInstanceAdmin.DeleteCluster` | **Verified** | `TestBigtableInstancesAndClusters` (#1331), through the official `bigtable.InstanceAdminClient` at `BIGTABLE_EMULATOR_HOST`. The emulator registers `BigtableInstanceAdmin` and answers every method of it `UNIMPLEMENTED`, so the Bigtable pod's front (`internal/bigtablefront`) serves it itself, keeping its state in memory as the emulator keeps its tables. An instance is created `READY` (`PRODUCTION` when no type is given) with its clusters `READY`, SSD by default; a taken ID is `ALREADY_EXISTS`, an ID outside Google's rule (6 to 33 characters, a lowercase letter first) or a display name outside 4 to 30 characters `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, a production cluster with neither nodes nor autoscaling `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. CreateInstance, PartialUpdateInstance, CreateCluster, UpdateCluster and PartialUpdateCluster return a done long-running operation with Google's metadata type, which `google.longrunning.Operations` (Get, List, Delete, Cancel, Wait) serves; UpdateCluster changes the node count alone, PartialUpdateCluster the node count and autoscaling. The last cluster of an instance, or one an app profile routes to, cannot be deleted (`FAILED_PRECONDITION`). `ListClusters` takes `instances/-`. **Tables and instances:** the emulator scopes tables by their full name, so a created instance is a real namespace for the table admin and data clients, and **DeleteInstance deletes its tables** (`TestBigtableInstanceDeletesItsTables`). **Difference:** an instance that was never created is still served, as the emulator always has: tables and rows under any instance name work, where Google answers `NOT_FOUND`. Refusing them would break every client written against the emulator, which never creates an instance (cbt, the SDKs' emulator mode, Terraform's `google_bigtable_table` alone, CloudBurrow's console). Nodes, zones, storage types and autoscaling are stored, not acted on: the emulator is one process. |

By hand through the generated stub: the configuration (`INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a malformed instance name), the handshake and parameters, a `MutateRow` and a `ReadRow` vRPC, a read on a write session `PERMISSION_DENIED`, a session not begun with `OpenSession` `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The first session call on each table and view warms its pool and is retried once if v1.58.0's client loses its own cold-pool wake-up (`bigtable: no sessions available`, raised before the vRPC is sent; fixed upstream after v1.58.0 by googleapis/google-cloud-go#20832). Google documents it as retrieving "a cache update for a given database", to "warm up the client cache by fetching key recipes and server information" for location-aware routing, streamed "because the response can be too large to fit into a single CacheUpdate message" (`google/spanner/v1/spanner.proto`). The test: one update with a non-zero ID and nothing to cache, the same ID again, `NOT_FOUND` for a missing database, `INVALID_ARGUMENT` for a malformed name. | `DatabaseAdmin.UpdateDatabase` | **Verified** | `TestSpannerDatabaseDropProtection` (#1461), through the official database admin client: `enable_drop_protection` is set and the operation is done, GetDatabase reads it back, DropDatabase and DeleteInstance (of the instance holding it) are `FAILED_PRECONDITION` while it is on, as Google refuses them, another field (`encryption_config`) is `UNIMPLEMENTED` naming why, and the database drops once it is off; `TestTerraformSpannerInstanceAndDatabase` sets and clears a `google_spanner_database`'s `enable_drop_protection` in place. The emulator refuses UpdateDatabase; the call front in the Spanner pod answers it over gRPC and REST, keeps the flag in memory, lays it over GetDatabase and ListDatabases, and enforces it on DropDatabase and DeleteInstance. The messages are CloudBurrow's (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/prevent-database-deletion>)) |

Clearing `edition` or `default_backup_schedule_type` is no change, and clearing `autoscaling_config` beside a node count, as gcloud does, returns to manual scaling; setting them is the editions row's (#1949); `config` is MoveInstance's. | Editions, default backup schedules, incremental backups and the managed autoscaler (#1949): `InstanceAdmin.CreateInstance`, `InstanceAdmin.UpdateInstance`, `InstanceAdmin.GetInstance` (`edition`, `default_backup_schedule_type`, `autoscaling_config`), `DatabaseAdmin.CreateDatabase`, `DatabaseAdmin.ListBackupSchedules`, `DatabaseAdmin.CreateBackupSchedule`, `DatabaseAdmin.GetBackupSchedule` (`incremental_backup_spec`), `DatabaseAdmin.UpdateDatabaseDdl` | **Verified** | `TestSpannerEditionsAutoscalingAndSchedules` (official instance and database admin clients), `TestGcloudSpannerEditions` (`gcloud spanner instances create --edition --default-backup-schedule-type --autoscaling-*`, `instances update --edition`, `backup-schedules create --backup-type=incremental-backup`), `TestTerraformSpannerInstanceEdition` (`google_spanner_instance` `edition`, `default_backup_schedule_type`, `autoscaling_config`, applied, updated and planned clean), `TestSpannerEditionsThroughThePage` (the console's Create instance, the instance's page and Create backup schedule). As <https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/editions-overview>, <https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/backup> and <https://docs.cloud.google.com/spanner/docs/managed-autoscaler> (read 2026-11-19) document them, the call front keeps an instance's edition, default backup schedule type and autoscaling configuration beside the emulator's instance (persisted with its other changes). An instance created with no edition gets the lowest its configuration allows: `STANDARD` for a regional one, `ENTERPRISE_PLUS` for a multi-region one (an explicit lower edition there is `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, as is `STANDARD` with a custom configuration's read-only replicas); an instance from before #1949 reports `EDITION_UNSPECIFIED` and is gated as Standard.
