`@@row_count` after DML, run directly or by `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, read by a query, a `SET`, a condition or another `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, is the DML statement's `numDmlAffectedRows` (BigQuery: "If used in a multi-statement query and the previous statement is DML, specifies the number of rows modified, inserted, or deleted"), NULL before any DML and after a statement of another kind (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/system-variables>)), and (#1459) in a script with a `TEMP` table or function too, run as its session's text (`TestBigQueryStatementsInTempScripts`), as the emulator alone does not know it (measured: "Unrecognized name: @@row_count"); `INTO` of a query of more than one row ("an error is thrown if you attempt to return more than one row") and `INTO` a number of variables other than the query's columns (they are "assigned by position") are 400 `invalidQuery` (a failed job for `jobs.insert`), and the statements after do not run; an `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, `BEGIN … END`, `CASE`, `IF`, `LOOP`, `REPEAT`, `WHILE` or `CALL` inside one is 400 `invalidQuery`, as BigQuery documents each "restricted from being executed dynamically as a nested element" (the wording of these errors UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/procedural-language>)). In a script with a `TEMP` table or function, the front puts the statement in the script's text, as follows. Formerly **Verified** for a string literal, or a script variable set to one by its `DECLARE`'s `DEFAULT` or a `SET` (a `CONCAT` or `||` of string literals and such variables counts as one, #1037, unit only), with `USING` literals, script variables or query parameters, named or positional, and `INTO` one or several variables of a query (#1037: run as `SET v = IF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (query)) > 1, ERROR(…), (query))`, as the emulator's scalar subquery of two rows gives the first (measured); several variables as one such `SET` per variable, each taking its column of the same row by position, `(SELECT AS STRUCT * FROM (query))[OFFSET(i)]`, since the emulator does not run `SET (a, b) = …` (measured: a parse error); read back: `'SELECT 41 + 1' INTO x` sets 42, a variable's query with `USING` is read, `'SELECT 5, "five"' INTO a, b` sets 5 and `five`, named columns too; a query of two rows fails the script at the statement when a later statement gives the script's answer (a query, DML or DDL: the front puts a `CREATE TEMP TABLE _cloudburrow_into_n AS SELECT IF(…, ERROR(…), 0)` before the `SET`s, which the emulator runs at once, measured, and the statement after is not run); with no such later statement (the guard would become the script's answer), the front counts the query's rows first, with the probe it uses for computed SQL, and when there are several puts `SELECT ERROR(…)` in the statement's place, so the script fails there, after the statements before it; otherwise the statement is run as before and the answer is unchanged (read back: `DECLARE x INT64; SELECT 7 AS v; EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT 1' INTO x` answers 7, and `… INTO x` of two rows with no later statement fails, with and without an earlier query; #1037); when that count cannot be faithful (the probe's rules below) it is 501; no rows set every variable NULL, as BigQuery documents ("If the query returns zero rows, all variables in the `INTO` clause are set to NULL"), read back for one and two variables; a backticked variable that need not be quoted is set as the same name unquoted, read back for `` INTO `a` ``; a number of variables other than the query's columns, when its text gives them, is 400, as the columns are assigned by position, #1037); SQL **computed** by any other expression (`FORMAT`, `CAST`, a variable set by a query, #1037) is evaluated first: the front runs the statements before it and then `SELECT (<expression>)` on the emulator, as a script of its own with its variables renamed (the emulator keeps a script's variables after it, #956), and runs the string it gives; `DECLARE` and `SET` are run again, queries, DML and DDL are left out, and a `BEGIN … END` block is run as its statements (the emulator does not run a block sent as one, measured), so computed SQL also works in a `BEGIN … END` block and after DML and DDL, provided neither the expression nor a `DECLARE` or `SET` after the DML or DDL reads a table (`FROM`); read back: `FORMAT` in a block, after a block, and after `CREATE TEMP TABLE`; read back: `FORMAT('SELECT %d AS v', 1)`, `CONCAT('SELECT ', CAST(4 AS STRING))`, a variable whose `DEFAULT` is `(SELECT 'SELECT 1')`, `FORMAT` of a variable a `SET` changed, with `USING` and with `INTO` of the same variable, and a computed `CREATE TABLE`, which is made; the evaluation is a job of the front's own, which `jobs.list` does not list (checked on a local instance through jobs.query and query jobs: only the client's job is listed); SQL that is NULL or not a STRING, and an expression whose evaluation fails, are 400 `invalidQuery`, BigQuery's wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/procedural-language>); SQL computed with `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` or `RAND`, or from a table after DML, a `USING` value that is an expression, and a statement that names a script variable BigQuery hides from it, are carried out in their turn, as BigQuery does (#1037, below); **Not implemented** (501) for what BigQuery does not document (`INTO` of a statement other than a query) and the rest | `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediateForms`, `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediateErrors` and `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediateChildJobs` (#1037: a test per form, the documented errors, the child jobs and `@@row_count`), `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediate` (#1011) and `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediateInTurn` (#1037), official Go client, through `jobs.query` and query jobs, on one instance with `--services bigquery,storage`. Measured first against the pinned emulator: every `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` was answered done and ran nothing: `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT 1 AS a'` returned no rows and no schema, `'CREATE TABLE ds.t (x INT64)'` made no table (a query job ended `DONE` with no error), and `'CREATE FUNCTION …'`, alone, in `BEGIN … END` and from a `DECLARE`d variable, made no function. BigQuery runs the statement ([EXECUTE IMMEDIATE](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/procedural-language#execute_immediate)). Now the front replaces each one it can carry out with its statement before the query is sent, each query parameter (`@name`, `?`) with its `USING` value in parentheses, and then checks and runs the query as any other (`jobs.get` shows the client's text). Read back: `SELECT 1 AS a` returns 1, `'SELECT @a + 1' USING 1 AS a` returns 2, `'SELECT ? * 10, ?' USING 4, 'four'` returns 40 and `four`, a variable's statement and a `USING` variable are read; `CREATE TABLE` makes the table, and `CREATE FUNCTION` alone, in `BEGIN … END` and from a variable set by `SET` makes the function, which is then called. **501** `notImplemented`, before anything of the query runs (a `CREATE TABLE` before it is not made): what BigQuery does not document, `INTO` of a statement that is not a query (SELECT or WITH; BigQuery: "If this returns a value, the `INTO` clause must contain values of the same type"), also in a script the front runs in its turn (there after the statements before it ran, which are kept; #1037); `INTO` a backticked name that must be quoted (the emulator does not run a `SET` of one, measured, and the front's own run of a script does not read such a variable); and a statement of several statements, which BigQuery's documentation does not give it. A script with a `TEMP` table or function is run as its session's text since #1459, so what the front carries out in its turn (below) is carried out there too (`TestBigQueryStatementsInTempScripts`). **Carried out in its turn** (#1037): an `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` the front cannot put in the script's text is run, as BigQuery runs it, by the front's own run of the script, a statement at a time, as a script with control flow is (row `DDL in a script's blocks, and control-flow blocks`): its SQL is evaluated when the statements before it have run, its `USING` values each once, and its statement is sent as a request of its own, with only the `USING` values bound. That is: computed SQL that cannot be evaluated first faithfully (in or after a block with an `EXCEPTION` handler, after a `CALL`, `RAISE`, transaction or other `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, after DML or DDL when the expression or a later `DECLARE` or `SET` reads a table, a probe that fails after DML or DDL it left out, or a function whose value changes from one run to the next, `RAND`, `GENERATE_UUID`, `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` and the other `CURRENT_` functions, `SESSION_USER`, `TABLESAMPLE`, a function of a dataset, or a system variable `@@` in it or before it); a `USING` value that is an expression (`1 + 1`, `n * 2`, `RAND()`), which BigQuery binds as a value ("These identifiers function similarly to query parameters"); and a statement that names one of the script's variables other than as an alias, a field, a parameter or a function: BigQuery hides them from it ("all other local variables and query parameters aren't exposed"), and the statement sent alone does not see them either, so the name reads the statement's own column or alias of that name, or fails (`Unrecognized name`), 400, and the statements after it do not run. Read back in `TestBigQueryExecuteImmediateInTurn`: `FORMAT('SELECT %T', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()) INTO t` after a query sets a timestamp of the statement's time, not after the next statement's; `CREATE TABLE t …; INSERT t VALUES (1), (2); EXECUTE IMMEDIATE (SELECT FORMAT('SELECT %d', COUNT(*)) FROM t)` answers 2; `'SELECT @a, @a * 2' USING 1 + 1 AS a` answers 2 and 4, `USING n * 2` reads the variable, `'SELECT @r = @r, @r < 1' USING RAND() AS r` answers true (one value), `INTO y USING 40 + 1 AS v` sets 42; with `x` declared, `'SELECT x FROM UNNEST([5]) AS x'` answers 5 and `'SELECT x'` fails 400 (a failed job `invalidQuery` for `jobs.insert`) and the `CREATE TABLE` after it is not made. A parameter with no `USING` value, a count of positional values that differs, and named and positional mixed are **400** `invalidQuery` (a failed job for `jobs.insert`), BigQuery's wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/procedural-language>). The console's Read-write editor runs an `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE FORMAT(…) USING …` that makes a table (`TestBigQueryEditorRunsExecuteImmediate`, browser, #1037). Units `TestExecuteImmediateRunsInTurn`, `TestExecuteImmediateIsExpanded`, `TestExecuteImmediateOfAConstant`, `TestExecuteImmediateHidesVariables`, `TestExecuteImmediateEvaluated`, `TestExecuteImmediateQuotedInto`, `TestExecuteImmediateEvaluatedInBlocks`, `TestExecuteImmediateIntoCountsRows`. |
| Schema updates: `tables.patch` and `tables.update` (`Table.Update`) | **Verified** for new top-level columns at the end (NULLABLE or REPEATED, of any type the emulator makes, `RECORD` included), fields added at the end of a `RECORD` or a `REPEATED RECORD` at any depth (#1036), a schema given in another order (the table keeps its own), a mode relaxed from `REQUIRED` to `NULLABLE`, and descriptions; **400** for what BigQuery refuses, and since #1111 **412** "Precondition Failed" for a new column or field given before one the table has; **Not implemented** (501) for a renamed column and a view's columns | `TestBigQueryTableUpdateAddsColumns` (#1010, #1013, #1036), the official Go client's `Table.Update` (`tables.patch`) and the generated client's `Tables.Update` (`tables.update`, google.golang.org/api/bigquery/v2). Measured first against the pinned emulator: both answered 200 and `tables.get` read the new columns, but the emulator changed only the table's metadata (its `tablesPatchHandler` and `tablesUpdateHandler` call `metadata.Table.Patch`/`Replace`), never its engine's columns: `INSERT INTO ds.t (f, g)` failed 400 "Column g is not present in table", `SELECT h` failed "Unrecognized name: h", and every later `tabledata.insertAll`, with or without the new column, failed **500** "Column … is not present", which the Go client retries until its deadline (#1013). In BigQuery an added column is added to the table, NULL (or empty) in its rows ([Add a column](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas#add_columns)). Now the front, before it sends the request on, makes the table again when its schema adds columns: its rows are copied to a scratch table made with the new schema (in `_cloudburrow_query_results`, deleted later while the instance is idle, #1091), the table is deleted and made again with the new schema and its description, labels, expiration, partitioning and clustering (through `tables.insert`, so a `FLOAT` column is `FLOAT64`, #1000), the rows are copied back, and its creation time is set back; then the request is sent on. Read back through the Go client: a table with a `REQUIRED` `INTEGER` and a `FLOAT` column and two rows, after `Table.Update` adding a `STRING`, a `REPEATED STRING` and a `RECORD` and relaxing the first to `NULLABLE`, reads the new schema, keeps its description, labels and creation time, and its two rows read the new columns NULL (the `REPEATED` one empty); it then takes `Inserter.Put` with all the columns, with the old ones only and with none of the old ones (a NULL `id`), a DML `INSERT` of the new ones (a query job), and a CSV load with the new `STRING` column, and `Table.Read` and a `SELECT` of the new column read every row; `Tables.Update` adding an `INTEGER` then takes an `UPDATE … SET` of it. **400** `invalid`, the table unchanged ("Provided Schema does not match Table p:ds.t. Field id is missing in new schema", "… Field id has changed type from INTEGER to STRING", "… Field id has changed mode from NULLABLE to REQUIRED", "… Cannot add required fields to an existing schema. (field: req)"; BigQuery refuses each, its wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas>)). **Fields added to a `RECORD`** (#1036): BigQuery adds a nested field through the same methods, at the end of its `RECORD` ("New columns and nested fields are always added at the end of the table or field", [Add a nested column to a RECORD column](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas#add_a_nested_column_to_a_record_column)). The front makes the table again as above, and copies each row with every `RECORD` rebuilt by name in the new schema's order, the new fields NULL (a `REPEATED` one empty), a NULL `RECORD` NULL and a `REPEATED RECORD`'s elements in their order (`IF(r IS NULL, NULL, STRUCT(r.x AS x, …, CAST(NULL AS T) AS y))`, `ARRAY(SELECT STRUCT(…) FROM UNNEST(rr) … ORDER BY offset)`; measured first: read back every row as it was, the new fields NULL). Read back: after `Table.Update` adding a `RECORD` `n` to the `RECORD` `r` and a new `REPEATED RECORD` `rr`, a DML `INSERT` of both, and a second `Table.Update`, given with its first two columns swapped, adding `r.n.w` (`BYTES`, two levels down), `r.q` (`REPEATED STRING`) and `rr.v` (`NUMERIC`, in the `REPEATED RECORD`), the table reads the new schema in its own order, every earlier row reads as it did (id, f, g, tags, whether `r` is NULL, `r.x`, h), the new fields read NULL or empty and `rr`'s elements in order, and the table takes an `INSERT` of `b'\xff\x00'`, `['q1']` and `NUMERIC '1.25'` into them, which read back so. **A schema in another order** is sent in the table's order, the new columns and fields after its own: "Modifying schema order after table creation doesn't have an effect on column or nested field order" (same page, Add columns). **412**, nothing changed (#1111): a new column or field given before one the table has, at the top level or in a `RECORD` at any depth. BigQuery refuses it: "It isn't possible to add columns in the middle of a table schema … If you attempt to add new columns elsewhere in the array, the following error is returned: BigQuery error in update operation: Precondition Failed" ([Add columns](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas#add_columns)). The bq tool prints the message of BigQuery's REST error there, so the front answers that message, `Precondition Failed`, with the status it names, HTTP 412 (`FAILED_PRECONDITION`), and reason `conditionNotMet`, the reason of BigQuery's other 412s; the status and the reason are UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas>) for this case, as BigQuery documents only the bq text. It is checked after the 400s (a `REQUIRED` column added first is still 400) and before the 501s. Read back through the Go client: `Table.Update` with a new `STRING` column first, one between the table's first and second columns, and a new field before a `RECORD`'s own each fail `googleapi.Error` 412 `conditionNotMet`, and the table reads its schema and rows as before. The console's Edit table adds fields only after the table's own, so it never sends one. **501** `notImplemented`, nothing changed: a column's name in another case, and a view's columns other than descriptions. The emulator's engine keeps no `NOT NULL`, so a mode and a description are metadata alone and are sent as they are. A `tables.update` with no schema is sent as it is. A `tables.patch` that also gives labels or a description is then carried out as the next row says, the table read once for both (#1054). Units `TestSchemaUpdates`, `TestSchemaChange`, `TestAlterTableAdviceIsTrue`, `TestConvertColumns`. |
| Column default values (`defaultValueExpression`, `CREATE TABLE … DEFAULT`, `ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT` / `DROP DEFAULT`) | **Verified** for top-level columns; **Refused** (400, as BigQuery refuses it: "You cannot add a new column with a default value to an existing table") `ADD COLUMN … DEFAULT` and a `tables.patch` that adds a column with a default, wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/default-values>); a STRUCT's field's default (a `defaultValueExpression` below the top level in `tables.insert`, `tables.patch` or `tables.update`, and `ALTER COLUMN s.x SET DEFAULT`), as "you must set the default value for the entire `STRUCT` field. You cannot set the default value for a subset of the fields", a STRUCT column's own default kept and applied (#1456, `TestBigQueryNestedDefaultsAndTruncateDataDefaults`); **Verified** (#1456) a `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` query job whose result lacks a top-level column with a default writes the default ("If the query omits a column with a default value, the default value is assigned"), the table's schema kept; **Not supported**: `UPDATE … SET c = DEFAULT`, which the engine refuses ("DEFAULT is supported only in an INSERT's VALUES") | `TestBigQueryColumnDefaults` (#1340), official Go client and Storage Write client, each default read back through `Table.Metadata` and each row through a query, as [default-values](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/default-values) documents them: a default given by `tables.insert`, `CREATE TABLE … DEFAULT` (through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`), `tables.patch` (`Table.Update`) and `ALTER COLUMN SET DEFAULT` reads back as the column's `defaultValueExpression` as written; it is applied by a DML `INSERT` that leaves the column out or gives `DEFAULT`, `VALUES` and `INSERT … SELECT`, by `tabledata.insertAll` for a row without the column, by a JSON load whose records lack it, and by the Storage Write API's default stream when the stream's schema lacks the field; a `NULL` given (DML, `insertAll`, a load's `null`, a Storage Write field in the stream's schema left unset, unless the append's missing-value interpretation is `DEFAULT_VALUE`, #1391) stays `NULL`. `SET DEFAULT` and `tables.patch` change only future inserts, the rows the table has kept as they are; `DROP DEFAULT` and `SET DEFAULT NULL` clear the default. Measured first through the front (2026-10-15): the emulator made the engine's table without a `tables.insert` column's default (an `INSERT` read NULL), applied no default to `insertAll` or a load, and read no `defaultValueExpression` back for a `CREATE TABLE` column; engine patches bigquery-emulator 0014 and googlesqlite 0027 (third_party/bigquery-emulator/PROVENANCE.md) apply them, and since the emulator's `tables.patch` changes only metadata, a change of a default makes the table again with its rows (`internal/bigqueryfront/columndefaults.go`). Units `TestParseAlter`, `TestDefaultChange`. |
| GoogleSQL type names in a schema (`INT64`, `BOOL`, `FLOAT64`, `STRUCT`, `DECIMAL`, `BIGDECIMAL`) | **Verified** for `tables.insert`, a load job's schema and `tables.patch` | `TestBigQueryGoogleSQLTypeNamesReadBack` (#1034), official Go client. BigQuery's reference lists each field type by its legacy name with the GoogleSQL name as an accepted alias: "INTEGER (or INT64)", "FLOAT (or FLOAT64)", "BOOLEAN (or BOOL)", "RECORD (or STRUCT)" ([TableFieldSchema.type](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/tables#TableFieldSchema.FIELDS.type)); the Go client says "The API will accept alias names for the types based on the Standard SQL type names" (its `fieldAliases`, with `DECIMAL` and `BIGDECIMAL` for `NUMERIC` and `BIGNUMERIC`) and reads only the legacy names back (`Table.Read` fails "unrecognized type: INT64" on any other). Measured first against the pinned emulator: `tables.insert` of fields typed `INT64` and `BOOL` read back `INT64` and `BOOL`, and `Table.Read` failed "unrecognized type: INT64"; a table made by `CREATE TABLE … (n INT64, b BOOL, f FLOAT64, r STRUCT<x INT64>)`, and a query's result schema, read back `INTEGER`, `BOOLEAN`, `FLOAT` and `RECORD`. Now the front sends every alias in the schema of `tables.insert`, `tables.update`, `tables.patch` and a load job (at any depth) by its legacy name; the engine's types are the same (a `FLOAT` field is then made `FLOAT64` as in the `FLOAT` row above). Read back through the Go client: a table made with `INT64`, `BOOL`, `FLOAT64`, `DECIMAL` and a `STRUCT` of an `INT64` reads `INTEGER`, `BOOLEAN`, `FLOAT`, `NUMERIC` and `RECORD` of an `INTEGER`, and its row through `Table.Read`; so does a JSON load with that schema, and a column added as `INT64` through `Table.Update` reads `INTEGER`. That BigQuery's own `tables.get` of a field made as `INT64` reads `INTEGER` is **UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/tables>)** here: it is inferred from the official client, which could not read the table otherwise, and from the emulator's own DDL. Units `TestGoogleSQLTypeNamesAreSentAsLegacyNames`, `TestFloatColumnsAreMadeFloat64`, `TestSchemaUpdates`. |
| A view's table names without a dataset (`tables.insert`, `tables.update`, `tables.patch` of a view) | **Verified**: refused 400 | `TestBigQueryViewsNameTheirTablesWithADataset` (#1035), official Go client. BigQuery: "A reference inside of a view must be qualified with a dataset. The default dataset doesn't affect a view body." ([Views, limitations](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/views)). Measured first against the pinned emulator, with `one.t` made first and `two.t` after: a view `two.v` made through `Table.Create` with `ViewQuery` `SELECT * FROM t` was made and read `one.t`'s rows, through `Table.Read` and a query. Now a view's (or materialized view's) GoogleSQL query that names a table without a dataset, where a query reads or writes one (as in *Tables of one ID in two datasets*: not a CTE's name), is **400** `invalid` "Table \"t\" must be qualified with a dataset (e.g. dataset.table). A view's query is not read in any default dataset, not even the view's own.", and nothing is made (BigQuery's wording for a view is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/views>)); one naming `dataset.t` reads that table. A legacy SQL view is not read. **A `CREATE VIEW` statement's query** (and `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW`'s) is held to the same rule whatever the query's default dataset (#1049, `TestBigQueryCreateViewNamesItsTablesWithADataset`, official Go client, through `jobs.query` and as a query job): since #1015 the front had sent its table names in the default dataset, so `CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT * FROM t` with `two` the default dataset made a view of `two.t`. Now, in the query's first statement, it is **400** `invalid` with the message above (a query job fails so), for `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` too (before its 501), and nothing is made; in a later statement of a script the name is sent in a dataset that does not exist, so the script runs the statements before it and fails there, as for a query with no default dataset. The view's own name is in the default dataset, and `CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT * FROM one.t` with `two` the default makes `two.v` reading `one.t`. What BigQuery answers such a statement was **not measured** (no live GCP); the refusal follows the reference quoted above, and its wording is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/views>). Units `TestViewsNameTheirTablesWithADataset`, `TestTableNamesAreQualified`. |
| Table functions: `CREATE [OR REPLACE] [TEMP] TABLE FUNCTION`, `routines.insert` of a `TABLE_VALUED_FUNCTION`, calls, `DROP TABLE FUNCTION` | **Verified** | `TestBigQueryTableFunctions` (#1061), official Go client, through `jobs.query` and query jobs: a table function made by `CREATE TABLE FUNCTION` (two arguments, two columns), by a query job, and by `Routine.Create` of a `TABLE_VALUED_FUNCTION` is called with its arguments (`SELECT * FROM ds.tf(1, 'a')`, with an alias and a `WHERE`, and under `SUM`); each still answers after 40 queries of 50,000 rows each and a `CREATE TABLE` and `DROP TABLE` every tenth (which rebuild the engine's catalog), run between its creation and its call; `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE FUNCTION` replaces it, through both, and the new one survives 40 more; `DROP TABLE FUNCTION` drops one (a call is then "not found"), `IF EXISTS` of one that is gone does nothing and without it fails; one made again after a drop has its new body; a `TEMP` table function is called in its script; and the dataset outlives it all. Duplicates, `IF NOT EXISTS` and a failed `CREATE OR REPLACE` are `TestBigQueryCreateFunctionOfAnExistingFunction` (row above), a failed script `TestBigQueryFailedScriptFunctionsAndDropSchema`, `DROP SCHEMA … CASCADE` `TestBigQueryDropSchemaCascadeDropsTableFunctions`. **Why it needed CloudBurrow's build:** in the pinned v0.8.1, goccy/googlesqlite v0.3.1's `tvfHandleForSpec` (`internal/catalog.go` line 2651) kept only the `*TableValuedFunction` embedded in the `*FixedOutputSchemaTVF` go-googlesql's `NewFixedOutputSchemaTVF` returned, while go-googlesql's finalizer that deletes the C++ object is on the outer handle, so a garbage collection freed a table function its catalog still used (#1043); and its analyzer refused `DROP TABLE FUNCTION`. The front answered every table function 501 (#1043) until the patches (third_party/bigquery-emulator, googlesqlite 0002 and 0003). Measured against v0.8.1's image: on the emulator alone, `CREATE TABLE FUNCTION`, 30 queries of 50,000 rows and a call exited it (SIGSEGV, exit code 2); and `TestBigQueryTableFunctions`, run against it on an instance, failed at the first check after the queries ("wasm trap: runtime error: index out of range", "interface conversion"), and the emulator then crashed and restarted with the dataset lost. So the front serves the three (internal/bigqueryfront/routinedefs.go): it keeps each function's definition, from the Routine `routines.insert` answered or read from the `CREATE FUNCTION` statement's own text (type, language, arguments with `ANY TYPE`, `ARRAY`, `STRUCT` and `RANGE` types, return type or `RETURNS TABLE<…>`, description, body as written: a SQL function's expression without its parentheses, a table function's query, a JavaScript function's code), beside the function names it already kept for `DROP SCHEMA` and in the same state file; `DROP FUNCTION` forgets it. A routine is listed and read only while the engine still has the function (called with no arguments). Read back: `routines.list` gives `plus`, `rows` and `viarest` (made by `CREATE FUNCTION`, `CREATE TABLE FUNCTION` and `Routine.Create`), with BigQuery's list fields only (no body, unless `readMask` asks); `routines.get` gives `plus`'s type, language, two arguments, `STRING` return type and body `CONCAT(label, CAST(x + 1 AS STRING))`, `rows`'s `TABLE_VALUED_FUNCTION`, body `SELECT n * 2 AS y` and return table column `y`, and `viarest`'s body and `INT64` return type; a routine that does not exist is 404 for get and delete; `routines.delete` drops a function and a table function (204), after which get is 404 and a call "not found"; `DROP FUNCTION` of one `routines.delete` dropped fails, and `routines.delete` of one `DROP FUNCTION` dropped is 404. **`routines.update`** (#1238, `TestBigQueryRoutineUpdate`, `Routine.Update`): the emulator has none, so the front drops the function in the engine and sends the new definition on as a `routines.insert`, keeping the creation time and giving a new etag; a definition the engine refuses puts the old one back. A body with no `routineType` or `definitionBody` (such as `Routine.Update` given only a body, which `routines.update` does not take as partial) is 400 `invalid` before anything is dropped: the emulator answered 500 "invalid routine type", which the Go client retried to its deadline (wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/error-messages>)). The new body, description and return type read back and a query calls the new body; a stale `If-Match` etag is 412 `conditionNotMet` (wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/error-messages>)) and changes nothing; a body `routineReference` naming another routine is 400. From the console: Edit routine on a routine's page (`TestBigQueryEditRoutine`). Units `TestRoutineFromDDL`, `TestRoutinesListGetDelete`, `TestRoutinesUpdate`. Since #1562 (`TestBigQueryTempScriptsUndropAndAlterSchema`): in a script with a TEMP table or function too, run a statement at a time in the script's session (a TEMP function of the rows of the dataset it brought back); inside a transaction, which BigQuery documents takes only queries, DML and DDL of temporary entities, it fails the script 400 in its turn (an exception handler sees it; wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/transactions>)); and a dry run answers `statementType` `UNDROP_SCHEMA` alone and `SCRIPT` in a script, nothing undeleted (whether BigQuery's dry run looks the dataset up is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create>)). **Not implemented** (501): `UNDROP SCHEMA` of another project's dataset; `TestBigQueryDatasetUpdatesAreSaved` (an undelete of a dataset never deleted). Measured first: `datasets.undelete` and `UNDROP SCHEMA` were 501 (#1200 measured the emulator's own: 400 "Table ID is required"; the engine failed `UNDROP SCHEMA` 400, a syntax error), and a copy of a deleted `table@time` failed `notFound`: the emulator drops a table's rows and its change history (#1418, googlesqlite patch 0036) with it, and every table of a dataset it deletes the same way. Now, before a table is deleted by any of those paths, the front copies its change table (each change of the last seven days, with its row, order and time) into a table of its own dataset, `_cloudburrow_dropped` (left out of `datasets.list`; the engine records no history of it), and keeps the table's resource and the deletion time in `dropped.json` on its state directory (`internal/bigqueryfront/dropped.go`); a view keeps its resource, with the client's text of its query. As https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/restore-deleted-tables documents, a copy job of `dataset.table@<milliseconds since the epoch>`, or `@-<milliseconds before now>`, writes the table as it was then: the last change of each row at or before the time, when not a DELETE (as `FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF` reads a table, *Time travel* row), with the deleted table's schema; of a table that exists, it reads the table's own history (`table@time` of a live table), and a time before the window or the table's creation (of a live or a deleted table) fails 400 "Invalid time travel timestamp N for table P:D.T@N. Cannot read before M", bq cp's message on [restore-deleted-tables](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/restore-deleted-tables) (read 2026-10-17; #1595, `TestBigQueryUndeleteAndRestore`); a time after the deletion fails 400 "Invalid snapshot time … the table did not exist at that time" (wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/datasets/undelete>)). As https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/restore-deleted-datasets documents, `datasets.undelete` and `UNDROP SCHEMA [IF NOT EXISTS] dataset` restore the latest deletion of the dataset (or the one of the request's `deletionTime`): the dataset with its description, labels and options as `datasets.get` gave them, and each table and view it held, with its description, schema, partitioning and clustering and the rows it had; `datasets.undelete` answers the dataset. A dataset that exists fails 409 `duplicate` "Already Exists" (`UNDROP SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS` does nothing), and one with no deletion kept fails 404 `notFound` (both wordings UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/restore-deleted-datasets>)). A restored table keeps its change history (#1483, `internal/bigqueryfront/droppedkeep.go`): the kept changes are carried into its new change table as a rebuild carries them (*Change history* row), each row still there ended at the deletion, so `FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF` a time before the deletion reads the rows of then, nothing between the deletion and the restore, and `APPENDS` and `CHANGES` give the rows as changed when they were. A deletion keeps, and an undelete puts back (#1483), a materialized view (made again from its query, as `tables.insert` makes one), a table snapshot (its rows and `snapshotDefinition`), the settings the front keeps of a table (`enable_change_history`, `privacy_policy`), its IAM policy and its row access policies. A dataset deletion keeps, and an undelete puts back (#1483, `TestBigQueryUndeleteKeepsRoutinesAndModels`, `internal/bigqueryfront/droppedroutines.go`), the dataset's routines and BigQuery ML models: each SQL function and table function (made by `CREATE FUNCTION` or `routines.insert`) is made again through the emulator's `routines.insert` with the resource it had, its `creationTime` among them, and each stored procedure and model (#1465) comes back as it was, so `routines.list`, `routines.get`, `models.list`, `models.get`, a call, `CALL` and `ML.PREDICT` give what they gave before the deletion; while the dataset is deleted its functions cannot be called (the emulator's `datasets.delete` leaves them in its engine, so the front drops them, as `DROP SCHEMA` does), and `DROP SCHEMA … RESTRICT` of a dataset with a model fails 400 `resourceInUse`, as `datasets.delete` without `deleteContents` does. Measured first: after `datasets.delete` with `deleteContents` a function still ran and `datasets.undelete` failed 404 (#1465's handling of the models took the request before the deletion was kept). Kept since #1522 (`TestBigQueryUndeleteKeepsExternalTables`, `TestBigQueryUndeleteKeepsRoutinesTheFrontDidNotSee`): an external table, as its definition (its resource with `externalDataConfiguration`; BigQuery keeps none of its data, which is its source's), made again through `tables.insert`, which reads the source as it is then; a copy of `table@TIME` of a deleted one fails `invalid`, as of a live one; and a function `routines.insert` made before the front started, which the front never saw, read at the deletion from the emulator, which keeps each Routine `routines.insert` makes (bigquery-emulator patch 0053; before, its `routines.get` and `routines.list` were stubs); the test makes it through the official Go client sent past the front, to the pod's emulator port. **Partial**: an ingestion-time partitioned table is restored without its rows' `_PARTITIONTIME`; a table whose change table was made before googlesqlite patch 0041 is kept as its rows were at the deletion, which an undelete restores and a copy at an earlier time refuses 501. **Expiry**: a kept deletion expires when the dataset's window has passed since it, by the front's clock (which the admin's `clock:advance` moves, `TestBigQueryUndeleteAndRestore`: a dataset of a 48-hour window, 49 hours on, is not found); the front looks for expired deletions whenever it keeps, restores or reads one, and deletes their copies. BigQuery's fail-safe period after the window, recoverable only by Cloud Customer Care, has nothing here. **Storage cost**: each deleted table is copied once with every change of its last seven days (every row written in them, and a copy of each row deleted or updated), so it costs about its change table's size, and its copy lives until the window ends, in the engine's database (persistent mode keeps it). `datasets.patch`, `datasets.update` and `projects.getServiceAccount` are carried out since #1205 (the row above). The other `rowAccessPolicies` methods are carried out since #1218 (the next row). The IAM methods of tables, routines and row access policies, 501 under #1218, are stored since #1231 (the next row but one). |
| Row-level security: `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.insert`, `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.list`, `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.get`, `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.update`, `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.delete`, `bigquery.rowAccessPolicies.batchDelete`; `CREATE [OR REPLACE] ROW ACCESS POLICY [IF NOT EXISTS] … ON t [GRANT TO (…)] FILTER USING (…)`, `DROP ROW ACCESS POLICY [IF EXISTS] … ON t`, `DROP ALL ROW ACCESS POLICIES ON t` | **Verified**, filtering for **one fixed caller**; **Not implemented** (501) for every read the front cannot filter | `TestBigQueryRowAccessPolicies` (#1218), the generated client (`RowAccessPolicies.*`) and the official Go client (queries, `Table.ExtractorTo`, `Table.CopierFrom`, `Table.Read` through the Storage Read client). Measured first: the emulator has no row-level security and answered every method 500 (#1200). The front keeps the policies (in its state directory, so a restart of the front does not unfilter a table; an emulator restart drops them) and applies them: each read of a table with policies in a GoogleSQL query's `FROM` clause (`FROM`, `JOIN`, a comma, `MERGE … USING`, in subqueries and CTEs too) is sent as `(SELECT * FROM t WHERE (filter) OR (filter) …)`, with the filters of the policies granted to the caller, or `WHERE FALSE` when none is: a table with policies and none for the caller reads no rows, as [BigQuery documents](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/row-level-security-intro). Read back: someone else's policy alone read no rows; the caller's `region = 'eu'` read the two EU rows; adding an `allUsers` policy `amount > 6` read the union; dropping them read all four. A policy's filter is checked by a query of the table that reads no rows (a filter naming no column is 400). A table's policies go with it: they are dropped when the table is deleted or made again (`CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE`, a changed `creationTime`). **The caller.** CloudBurrow authenticates nobody ([ADR-0004](adr/0004-local-access-and-no-authentication.md)) and cannot tell who sent a query, so **every caller is taken to be the one identity it gives out**: the service account of its credentials and metadata server, `cloudburrow-local@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (`cloudburrow env`'s project). A policy grants the caller when it names `serviceAccount:` that account, `allAuthenticatedUsers` or `allUsers`; `user:`, `group:`, `domain:` and other service accounts never match here, so their rows are not returned to anyone; `SESSION_USER()` in a filter is that account. A test cannot show two callers reading different rows, and none claims to. **501, nothing read:** `tabledata.list`, an extract job, a copy job and a Storage Read session of a table with policies; `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE` and `TRUNCATE TABLE` of one; a time travel (`FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF`) or wildcard read of one; a view (or materialized view) whose query reads one; a table function, and a legacy SQL query, in a project with policies; a row access policy statement in a script with other statements, and a policy on another project's table. `INSERT` into a table with policies is carried out. A scalar SQL function whose body reads a table is not looked into (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/using-row-level-security-with-features>) that BigQuery filters it). Unit `TestFilterQuery`, `TestParseRowPolicyDDL`, `TestCallerIdentityIsTheCredentialsAccount`. |

A `TEMP` table is gone when its script ends, so it cannot be checked after the script as other tables are (the row above), and the emulator has no sessions. The front instead runs the statements before it and then `SELECT * FROM (query) LIMIT 0` as a script of its own, whose result's columns are the table's (measured: such a script returned its last query's columns, `b!` and a STRUCT's `c?` included), with the variables renamed as above: a name the rules refuse is **400 `invalidQuery`** and the script is not run; names BigQuery takes run (8 read back from a `TEMP` table made from another and a variable). That runs the statements before it twice, so only when none of them changes data (a query, `DECLARE`, `SET`, `TEMP` tables and DML on them); after one that does, it was **501**, and since #1459 the script runs as its session's text and each `CREATE TEMP TABLE` is carried out in its turn (`TestBigQueryTempScriptsInTurn`). If the columns cannot be read so, the script is run: its failure is the answer, and if it does not fail the query is failed 501, saying that the script ran. Unit `TestTempTableColumnsAreChecked`. |

INFORMATION_SCHEMA: BigQuery documents no model view (checked 2026-10-16 against the [INFORMATION_SCHEMA view list](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/information-schema-intro), #1481), so none is built. Console: a dataset's page lists its models, and a model's page shows its features and weights, its centroids (KMEANS), confusion matrix (LOGISTIC_REG), principal components (PCA) recommendations and factors (MATRIX_FACTORIZATION), feature importance (BOOSTED_TREE_*, RANDOM_FOREST_*), forecast and candidate models (ARIMA_PLUS), or global explanation (a model trained with `enable_global_explain`) (#1504: `TestBigQueryModelPageResults`), training iterations and evaluation, with Edit model and Delete model; the preprocessing functions run in the query editor as any query does. #1548, DNNs (`internal/bigqueryfront/modeldnn.go`): `DNN_REGRESSOR`, `DNN_CLASSIFIER` and `AUTOENCODER` are trained by the front as a feed-forward network of `hidden_units` layers, with the documented options and defaults (`optimizer` `ADAM`, `ADAGRAD`, `RMSPROP`, `SGD`; `learn_rate` 0.001; `activation_fn` `RELU`, `RELU6`, `ELU`, `SELU`, `SIGMOID`, `TANH`; `batch_size` 32 or the rows when fewer; `dropout` 0; `l1_reg` and `l2_reg` only with `ADAGRAD`, `FTRL` or `SGD`; `max_iterations` 20 passes; `early_stop` with `min_rel_progress` 0.01; `hidden_units` by default one layer of min(128, rows / (10 · (inputs + outputs))) units), on the auto-preprocessed rows; **UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create-dnn-models>)**, Keras's defaults where BigQuery documents none: Glorot uniform initial weights from a fixed seed (1548, so a network is the same each run but not Google's), each pass's rows shuffled by it, ADAM's betas 0.9 and 0.999, epsilon 1e-7, the mean squared error or mean log loss, inverted dropout, an iteration's loss the training rows' after the pass. `ML.PREDICT` is SQL of the network; `ML.EVALUATE`, `ML.TRAINING_INFO`, `ML.CONFUSION_MATRIX`, `ML.ROC_CURVE` and `ML.FEATURE_INFO` serve it; an `AUTOENCODER`'s `ML.PREDICT` gives the middle hidden layer as `latent_col_<n>`, INT64 as BigQuery documents it ("an INT64 value that represents the dimensions of the latent space"), the unit's value CAST to INT64, so rounded to the nearest integer, halfway away from zero (how BigQuery makes a unit's value an INT64 is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-predict>)), and `labelColumns` gives them as INT64, then the input columns, and `ML.EVALUATE` and `ML.RECONSTRUCTION_LOSS` the mean absolute, squared and squared log errors of the preprocessed columns' reconstruction (which columns BigQuery measures is undocumented). Since #1562 (`TestBigQueryMLDNNOptions1562`, and one step of each checked by hand in `TestDNNOptionsOneStepByHand`): `optimizer` `FTRL` (TensorFlow's FtrlOptimizer, which BigQuery's page links, at its defaults: learning_rate_power -0.5, initial accumulator 0.1), `activation_fn` `CRELU` (a hidden layer's output [RELU(a), RELU(-a)], twice its units wide, as `tf.nn.crelu`), `class_weights` ("a weight must be present for every class label", 400 else) and `auto_class_weights` (total_input_rows / (input_rows_for_class_n · number_of_unique_classes), as documented), each row's loss weighted by its label's weight, and an `AUTOENCODER`'s `l1_reg_activation` (an L1 penalty on the latent layer's activations, the middle of `hidden_units`); **UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create-dnn-models>)** that Google's optimizer, weighting and regularization are these. `enable_global_explain`, `ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT` and `ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN` of a DNN are 400 since #1562, as are `ML.WEIGHTS` and `ML.FEATURE_IMPORTANCE` of one: BigQuery's [explainability table](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/xai-overview) and its [end-to-end journeys](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/e2e-journey) list no explanation for a DNN or a wide-and-deep model, and neither page's option list has `enable_global_explain` (re-read 2026-11-17; they no longer document integrated gradients). Wide-and-deep (#1562, [its page](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create-wnd-models), read 2026-11-17): `DNN_LINEAR_COMBINED_REGRESSOR` and `DNN_LINEAR_COMBINED_CLASSIFIER` are a DNN as above plus a linear part, "All columns referenced by the query_statement are used as input features", so each encoded column goes to both, and the output (a value, or a logit) is the sum of the two, trained jointly on the one loss, as the [wide-and-deep paper](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/2988450.2988454) the page links does; `optimizer` and `learn_rate` take one value for both parts or an ARRAY of STRUCT values a part (`[STRUCT('dnn', 'ADAGRAD'), STRUCT('linear', 'SGD')]`; a value a part on any other model type is 400), defaults `[STRUCT('dnn', 'ADAM'), STRUCT('linear', 'FTRL')]` and 0.001 for both; the page's other options as a DNN's, and no `category_encoding_method` or `enable_global_explain` (400). UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-create-wnd-models>): the linear part's weights and bias start at 0, as TensorFlow's linear model's; `l1_reg` and `l2_reg` are 400 unless both parts' optimizers are ADAGRAD, FTRL or SGD ("You can only use this option when OPTIMIZER is set to" one of them), and regularize both parts' weights; `models.get` reports the DNN part's `optimizer` and `learnRate`, as `TrainingOptions` has one of each. `TestBigQueryMLWideAndDeep` (official Go client): a regressor of `hidden_units` [2], `TANH`, `SGD` and `learn_rate` 0.1, one pass, against the model computed by hand (`ML.PREDICT`, `ML.EVALUATE`, `ML.TRAINING_INFO`, `models.get`), classifiers at the default optimizers and at a value a part whose `ML.PREDICT` gives `ML.EVALUATE`'s log loss and accuracy, and the 400s; unit tests check one step of each part against central differences and FTRL's step from zero in closed form (`TestWideDeepOneStepByHand`, `TestParseWideDeepOptions`). `TestBigQueryMLDNN` (official Go client): a `DNN_REGRESSOR` of `hidden_units` [2], `TANH`, `SGD`, `learn_rate` 0.1, one pass, checked against the network computed by hand from the seeded initial weights and one gradient step (`ML.PREDICT` of two rows, `ML.EVALUATE` with and without an input, `ML.TRAINING_INFO`, the training options in `models.get`), and unit tests check the forward pass of a hand-computed network and one SGD step against central differences; a `DNN_CLASSIFIER`'s `ML.PREDICT` probabilities give `ML.EVALUATE`'s log loss and accuracy; an `AUTOENCODER`'s `ML.RECONSTRUCTION_LOSS` rows average to its `ML.EVALUATE`. #1548, preprocessing: `ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(x, num_buckets)` and `ML.ROBUST_SCALER(x [, quantile_range [, with_median [, with_quantile_range]]])` `OVER ()` or `OVER (PARTITION BY ...)`, and `ML.NGRAMS(tokens, range [, separator])`, in a query and in a `TRANSFORM` (whose quantiles are learned over the training rows and kept): BigQuery's quantiles are approximate, CloudBurrow's exact (`PERCENTILE_DISC`), which give BigQuery's documented examples (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-preprocessing-functions>) beyond them). `TestBigQueryMLQuantilePreprocess`: BigQuery's three examples exactly; a `TRANSFORM` of `ML.ROBUST_SCALER` (median 4, quartiles 2 and 7 of x 0..9, read back by `ML.FEATURE_INFO`, x = 100 predicting 100) and of `ML.QUANTILE_BUCKETIZE(x, 2)` (the buckets' means 1.5 and 6.5). #1548, the vocabulary functions `ML.LABEL_ENCODER(x [, top_k [, frequency_threshold]])`, `ML.ONE_HOT_ENCODER(x [, drop [, top_k [, frequency_threshold]]])`, `ML.MULTI_HOT_ENCODER(array [, top_k [, frequency_threshold]])`, `ML.BAG_OF_WORDS(tokens [, top_k [, frequency_threshold]])` and `ML.TF_IDF(tokens [, top_k [, frequency_threshold]])` `OVER ()` or `OVER (PARTITION BY ...)` (`internal/bigqueryfront/modelvocab.go`): the vocabulary is the window's top_k (32,000) categories in at least frequency_threshold (5) rows, the most frequent first and ties alphabetical, indexed alphabetically from 1, 0 for NULL and the unknown; `drop => 'most_frequent'` gives the most frequent category the value 0.0; TF-IDF is count / document size × ln(1 + documents / (1 + the term's documents)), the unknown term's inverse document frequency the mean of the vocabulary's (which gives BigQuery's example). In a query each call is written as SQL functions (`_cbml1_*`, made in the project's hidden results dataset) of the window's `ARRAY_AGG`; in a `TRANSFORM` the vocabulary, the dropped category and the inverse document frequencies are learned over the training rows and kept as constants. CloudBurrow trains on scalar features only, so a `TRANSFORM` feature of an `ARRAY<STRUCT>` output is 501 from the trainer (read an element, `[OFFSET(0)].index`, say). UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-bag-of-words>): the defaults of `ML.BAG_OF_WORDS` and `ML.TF_IDF` (BigQuery documents none; the encoders' are used), and the output of a NULL array (an empty array). `TestBigQueryMLVocabularyPreprocess`: BigQuery's examples of all five exactly (TF-IDF to 1e-12), the defaults over `PARTITION BY`, and a `TRANSFORM` of `ML.LABEL_ENCODER` and of `ML.ONE_HOT_ENCODER(c, 'none', 1, 1)` whose vocabularies are kept at prediction. |
| BQML remote models (`CREATE MODEL … REMOTE WITH CONNECTION … OPTIONS(ENDPOINT = …)`, `ML.GENERATE_TEXT`, `ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING`) | **Verified** (measured 2026-11-17, #1760) | A remote model's calls go to the instance's **own local Vertex AI endpoint**, never to Google: `up` publishes it to the cluster through cloudburrow-host and gives the BigQuery front its address (`--vertexai`), pinning an OS-assigned local AI port first; generation runs on the local LiteRT-LM runtime (`--local-ai-model`) and embeddings on the local embedding model (`--local-ai-embeddings`, the onnx build). `CREATE MODEL` checks the connection: it must exist (`Not found: Connection …`, 404), be a `CLOUD_RESOURCE` connection, and be in the dataset's location (`Dataset location … differs from connection location …`); `REMOTE WITH CONNECTION DEFAULT` (#1765, Verified 2026-11-17) is the project's `region-REGION.default_cloud_resource_connection_id` (ALTER PROJECT SET OPTIONS) in the dataset's region, else `__default_cloudresource_connection__`, which BigQuery makes when it is missing (a `CLOUD_RESOURCE` connection in the dataset's region) if the caller holds `bigquery.connections.create` on the project (else 403 naming it), and whose service account it grants `roles/aiplatform.user` on the project when it lacks it and the caller holds `resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy`, as [default connections](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/default-connections) documents (`TestBigQueryMLRemoteDefaultConnection`, same clients, passed 2026-11-17 against `gemma-4-e2b-it-community`: "Paris"; UNVERIFIED (re-read 2026-11-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/default-connections>, which quotes no error text): the 403's wording); `REMOTE_SERVICE_TYPE` is its own row (#1773); any other option 400, and a remote model takes no `AS` query. `ENDPOINT` is a model name or a Vertex AI URL or resource name, whose model segment alone is kept (the URL is never dialled); the local endpoint resolves it by its own rule, so a `gemini-*` endpoint answers only through an explicitly configured `--local-ai-alias` and otherwise its `NOT_FOUND` is the row's status, never a substitution. `models.get` answers `remoteModelInfo` (`endpoint`, `connection` as `projects/{number}/locations/{location}/connections/{id}`) and no `modelType`. `ML.GENERATE_TEXT(MODEL m, {TABLE t | (query)} [, STRUCT(…)])` reads the input's `prompt` STRING column and answers, with the input's columns, `ml_generate_text_result` (the `generateContent` response as JSON) and `ml_generate_text_status`, or with `flatten_json_output` `ml_generate_text_llm_result` (the first candidate's text), `ml_generate_text_rai_result`, `ml_generate_text_grounding_result` and `ml_generate_text_status`; a NULL prompt is not sent (its results are NULL), and a failed call is that row's status with NULL results, as in BigQuery. `request_type` is accepted; the generation options are **applied** (#1797, `TestBigQueryMLRemoteGenerationOptions`, measured 2026-11-18: `max_output_tokens` 8 answered "## The Enduring Majesty of the Sea" where 256 ran on; `temperature` 0 answers identically twice; `stop_sequences` ['5'] ended a count at "1,2,3,4,"), sent as the request's `generationConfig` with BigQuery's documented ranges (`max_output_tokens` [1,8192], `temperature` and `top_p` [0.0,1.0], `top_k` [1,40] and refused for a Gemini endpoint, which BigQuery documents none for; out of range is 400) and its Gemini defaults when unset (1024 output tokens, temperature 0, top_p 0.95); `safety_settings`, `generation_config` and `model_params` are 501 (docs/generation.md), and `ground_with_google_search` is 501 because it searches Google. `ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING` reads the `content` STRING column and answers `ml_generate_embedding_result` (ARRAY<FLOAT64>), `ml_generate_embedding_statistics` (JSON, `token_count` and `truncated`) and `ml_generate_embedding_status`, with `task_type` and `output_dimensionality` passed to `:predict`. A generative model's `ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING`, an embedding model's `ML.GENERATE_TEXT` and any other ML function of a remote model are 400. **Connection permissions (#1765, Verified 2026-11-17):** as BigQuery documents them (the CREATE MODEL remote model page: "grant the Agent Platform User role to the connection's service account"; [default connections](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/default-connections): BigQuery Connection User for `bigquery.connections.use`), `CREATE MODEL … REMOTE` and every query of a remote model need the caller to hold `bigquery.connections.use` on the connection, through an unconditioned binding on the connection's own policy (Connection API `setIamPolicy`) or on the project's (Resource Manager), of a role that includes it in Google's predefined-role catalogue (`internal/iamroles`: `roles/bigquery.connectionUser`, `connectionAdmin`, `admin`, `studioAdmin`, …) or `roles/owner`/`roles/editor`; without it the job fails **403 `accessDenied`** `Access Denied: Connection projects/{number}/locations/{location}/connections/{id}: Permission bigquery.connections.use denied on connection … (or it may not exist).` And the connection's service account (`bqcx-…@gcp-sa-bigquery-condel.iam.gserviceaccount.com`) must hold a role with `aiplatform.endpoints.predict` (`roles/aiplatform.user`) on the model's project, or the job fails 400 naming the account and the Vertex AI User role. Both are checked before any row is sent to the local endpoint. The caller is the one identity the BigQuery front takes every caller to be (`cloudburrow-local@{project}.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, as row access policies take it); conditional bindings, custom roles, folders and the organization grant nothing here; without Resource Manager the check is 501 (ADR-0006, amended by #1765). Opus (#1799, `internal/speech/opus.go`) is decoded at 48 kHz with the pure-Go `github.com/darui3018823/opus` decoder (BSD 2-Clause) EmbedContent already uses for MP4 Opus tracks, as libopus decodes it: Ogg (RFC 7845) through its `oggopus` reader, chained streams one after another, the OpusHead's output gain applied, the pre-skip and the final granule's end trimming dropped; WebM (Matroska's `A_OPUS` mapping) through a demuxer written here, which reads Segments and Clusters of unknown size (live recordings), SimpleBlocks and BlockGroups, Xiph, fixed and EBML lacing, `CodecDelay` as the pre-skip and `DiscardPadding` as the end trimming; channel mapping families 0 and 1 (mono to 7.1; 2 and 3, ambisonics, 501), resampled to 16 kHz. `TestBigQueryMLTranscribe`'s Opus copies of the WAV (`internal/speech/testdata/jfk.opus`, mono Ogg, and `jfk-stereo.webm`, stereo WebM with an unknown-size Segment and Cluster and a final `DiscardPadding`, both encoded from `jfk.wav` by unit `TestOpus` with the same module's encoder) answer the sentence, billed 11 s; unit `TestOpus` decodes each to the WAV's length within 2 samples and correlation at least 0.9 to its waveform, and `TestMKVLacing` the three lacings. `transcript_normalization` (#1799) rewrites each final transcript as the reference's `TranscriptNormalization` documents it (read 2026-11-20): its entries in order, each replacing every occurrence of `search` with `replace`, case-insensitively unless `case_sensitive`, so an earlier entry can keep a later one from matching; at most 100 entries and 100 characters a `search` or `replace`, an empty `search` 400 (`TestBigQueryMLTranscribe`: `COUNTRY` → `nation` replaces both of JFK's "country", a later `your country` entry then matches nothing, and an empty `search` is refused; unit `TestNormalize`). UNVERIFIED (re-read 2026-11-20: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.recognizers#TranscriptNormalization>, which does not say): whether a `search` matches inside a word (here it does) and whether `words[]` are rewritten (here they are not). FLAC (#1799) is a FLAC file's frames decoded by the pure-Go RFC 9639 decoder EmbedContent uses for MP4 FLAC tracks (`internal/embedding/flac.go`'s `DecodeFLACFile`, any bit depth from 4 to 32, frame CRCs not checked), resampled to 16 kHz (its first channel, #1799); `TestBigQueryMLTranscribe`'s FLAC copy of the WAV answers the same words, and unit `TestDecodeFLACIsLossless` decodes it to exactly the WAV's samples; `max_alternatives` (one alternative is returned, which the reference allows) and `enable_automatic_punctuation` (Whisper punctuates regardless) are accepted. Refused before anything is read: no `recognition_config` on a model with no recognizer (400), other models, `diarization_config` and a non-zero `denoiser_config.snr_threshold` (501), and several `language_codes` (400: only `long`, `short` and `telephony` take them, as the Speech-to-Text row says); `profanity_filter`, `enable_spoken_punctuation` and `enable_spoken_emojis` rewrite each transcript (#1799, `TestBigQueryMLTranscribe`'s spoken clip, measured 2026-11-20: "s\*\*\*", "!" and 👍; the `Speech.Recognize` row has how); `multi_channel_mode` `SEPARATE_RECOGNITION_PER_CHANNEL` (#1799) decodes each channel of a WAV, headerless, FLAC or Opus file apart (`speech.DecodeChannelsMax`) and transcribes each on its own, as the reference's `MultiChannelMode` says, each result carrying its 1-based `channel_tag`, ordered by end then channel, `total_billed_duration` counting every channel (`TestBigQueryMLTranscribe`: a stereo WAV of JFK left and the adaptation sample right answers JFK's sentence on channel 1 only and "station" on channel 2 only, billed 22 s; unit `TestDecodeChannels`, `TestParsePerChannel`); MP3 and AAC, whose decoders mix to mono, are 501 with it, as is `StreamingRecognize` with it; without it only the first channel of a WAV, headerless, FLAC or Opus file is transcribed, as the reference's default mode says (`TestDecodeChannels`), while MP3 and AAC are averaged, their decoders mixing to mono. UNVERIFIED (re-read 2026-11-20: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.recognizers#MultiChannelMode>, which does not say): the results' order across channels and the billing of each channel; `adaptation` is applied as the Speech-to-Text `Speech.Recognize` row describes (not run through ML.TRANSCRIBE here). AMR and AMR-WB files are decoded as the `Speech.Recognize` row says (#1799; not run through ML.TRANSCRIBE here). A row's error is its status: an Ogg or WebM file that is not Opus or is malformed (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`), data in no detectable audio format (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`), audio over 30 minutes (`INVALID_ARGUMENT: The audio file cannot be processed in time.`, the page's text), MP3 and AAC over 180 seconds (501: CloudBurrow's decoders stop there). Only the page's locations (`asia-southeast1`, `europe-west4`, `us-central1`, `US`, `EU`). UNVERIFIED (re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-transcribe>, whose sample output is truncated, and <https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.recognizers/recognize>): `ml_transcribe_result`'s shape beyond the sample (snake_case keys and Durations as `{"seconds", "nanos"}` objects, as the sample's `total_billed_duration` is), the space joining `transcripts`, one result for each Whisper segment, `total_billed_duration` rounded up to a second, lower-case `language_code`, the texts of the refusals. `TestBigQueryMLTranscribe` (official `cloud.google.com/go/bigquery`, `storage`, `bigquery/connection/apiv1`, `speech/apiv2` and the generated `bigquery/v2` clients) passed 2026-11-19 on darwin/arm64 against a local instance, and again 2026-11-20 with the Opus files, `transcript_normalization` and the per-channel stereo WAV; unit `TestTranscribe`, `TestDecode`, `TestOpus`, `TestMKVLacing`, `TestNormalize`, `TestDecodeChannels`, `TestParsePerChannel`, `TestDecodeFLACIsLossless`, `TestDecodeFLACStereo24`, `TestDecodeFLACRefuses`, `TestParse`, `TestRecognize`, `TestRecognizeRefusals`, `TestRecognitionConfigText`, `TestSnakeResult`, `TestG711`, `TestParseRemoteModel`, `TestSpeechRecognizers`. |

| BigQuery `AI.AGG`, the aggregate generative AI function (`bigquery.jobs.query`) | **Verified** (measured 2026-11-18, #1777) | As <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/bigqueryml-syntax-ai-agg> documents it (read 2026-11-18): `AI.AGG([DISTINCT] INPUT, INSTRUCTION [, connection_id => …] [, endpoint => …] [, max_error_ratio => …] [, output_schema => …])` answers one value per `GROUP BY` group (one for the whole input without one): a STRING, or with `output_schema` a STRUCT of the schema's fields (the `aischema.go` grammar, constrained by the runtime's JSON-schema decoding as for `AI.GENERATE`). INPUT is a STRING or a STRUCT of STRING and ARRAY<STRING> fields; INSTRUCTION a STRING literal or, "as either a string or query parameter", a query parameter, named (`@instruction`) or positional (`?`) (#1810, Verified 2026-11-18): the front reads its value from the request's parameters (it must be a non-NULL `STRING`, else 400), names positional parameters (`cbai_p1`, …) so the probes and the answered query, which move the calls' `?` around, keep their order, and sends the engine only the parameters each query it runs references, as the engine refuses one a query does not name (`expected 0 arguments, got 1`: the answered query no longer holds the instruction's); the job (`jobs.get`) shows the client's own query and parameters. Any other non-literal INSTRUCTION is 501. The front (`internal/bigqueryfront/aiagg.go`) evaluates it before the engine runs the query, block by block, the deepest first: a probe of the call's block (its select list, so `GROUP BY 1` and aliases keep their meaning, and its FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY and WINDOW clauses; HAVING, QUALIFY, ORDER BY and LIMIT left out so every group is answered) reads each group's inputs as `ARRAY_AGG([DISTINCT] TO_JSON_STRING(INPUT) ORDER BY …)` with its `FARM_FINGERPRINT`; each group is answered on the instance's **local** Vertex AI endpoint, never Google, by the documented multi-level aggregation ("batches the input, aggregates each batch, and aggregates the batch results", skipped when the group fits one call): a batch is as many rows as fit the local model's context, which is **4,096 tokens** for `gemma-4-e2b-it-community` (measured 2026-11-18: `Input token ids are too long. Exceeding the maximum number of tokens allowed: 5312 >= 4096` for a 13,134-byte prompt; batches are sized at 2 bytes a token, below the measured 2.47), and the batches' answers are combined the same way until one call holds them; the answers go back into the query as `CASE FARM_FINGERPRINT(…) WHEN … THEN … END`, evaluated in the call's own group, so it works in the select list, HAVING and ORDER BY (in WHERE, GROUP BY or FROM it is 400 `Aggregate function AI.AGG not allowed in …`). Endpoint, permissions and `connection_id` as the scalar AI functions (the caller's Vertex AI User role, else the connection's checks; the default endpoint `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` answers only through a `--local-ai-alias`). A failed call drops its rows from the answer (partial results, as documented) and counts them as failed; the query fails with BigQuery's `Query failed because AI functions exceeded their allowed error ratio` when the failed rows' ratio exceeds `max_error_ratio` (default 1.0, [0.0, 1.0] else 400) or when every row failed. A search with the index probes the `fraction_lists_to_search` nearest lists of each query vector (10% by default, at least one) and ranks only their rows, so results are approximate as BigQuery's are (every list probed gives brute force's); `use_brute_force` skips it and is exact; the index's `distance_type` is the search's default; a base query's WHERE on stored columns pre-filters, on others post-filters (fewer than `top_k` rows can come back). Refused 400: a second index of a table, the same name again without `IF NOT EXISTS` or `OR REPLACE` (409), both clauses, a missing `index_type`, `ivf_options` with TREE_AH and `tree_ah_options` with IVF, `num_lists` over 5,000, `leaf_node_embedding_count` under 500, a column of another type, arrays of different lengths or with NULL elements, a TREE_AH array under 2 dimensions, an unknown or RANGE stored column, a non-STRING lexical column; DROP and REBUILD of another index name 404, `IF EXISTS` skipping. `ALTER VECTOR INDEX … REBUILD` retrains at once and fills `last_index_alteration_info`. **Hybrid search**: `VECTOR_SEARCH`'s single form with `lexical_search_columns` and `lexical_search_query_value`, and `AI.SEARCH` `mode => 'HYBRID'` (or `AUTO`) over a hybrid index (a vector index with `lexical_search_columns`; `HYBRID` without one is 400), rank every row semantically and by BM25 of the query's terms in the lexical columns, fused by reciprocal rank fusion (k 60), `distance` 1 minus the fused score: the page's example's distances have exactly that form; a batch hybrid search is 400 ("Hybrid search doesn't support batch queries"). **Rerank**: `rerank => TRUE` reorders `options.reranker.num_candidates` candidates (top_k × 5 by default; refused under top_k) by `rerank_score` (0 to 1), rows with a NULL or empty text left out; BigQuery calls the Discovery Engine ranking API, whose models are not published, so the score here is the local embedding model's cosine similarity of the query (RETRIEVAL_QUERY) and the candidate (RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT), mapped to 0 to 1, never Google. **Not supported**: `PARTITION BY` of a TreeAH index (Preview) and a dry run of the statements, 501 named; a vector index statement inside a script, 501; the BACKGROUND reservation REBUILD needs in BigQuery. An ObjectRef is `STRUCT<uri STRING, version STRING, authorizer STRING, details JSON>`. `OBJ.MAKE_REF(uri [, authorizer] [, version => …] [, details => …])`, `OBJ.MAKE_REF(objectref_json)` and `OBJ.MAKE_REF(objectref, authorizer)` build one (the format alone is checked; `region.connection` is written `project.region.connection`). `OBJ.FETCH_METADATA` of a ref or an ARRAY fills `version` (the generation) and `details.gcs_metadata` (content_type, md5_hash, size, updated) from the instance's Cloud Storage; a ref that cannot be read still succeeds, its `details` `{"errors": [{code, message, source: "OBJ.FETCH_METADATA"}]}`. `OBJ.GET_ACCESS_URL(ref, 'r' \| 'rw' [, INTERVAL])` is the ObjectRefRuntime JSON (`obj_ref`, `access_urls.read_url`, `write_url` with `rw`, `expiry_time`), or `objectref` and `errors` as the page shows; the duration is 30 minutes to 6 hours (6 hours by default). `OBJ.GET_READ_URL(ref)` is `STRUCT<url, status>`, a 45-minute read URL. The URLs are V4 signed URLs of the instance's Cloud Storage, signed as the authorizer connection's service agent at the instance's BigQuery clock, which Cloud Storage verifies (a GET for read_url, a PUT for write_url; tampered or expired, 403). Delegated access needs the caller's `bigquery.objectRefs.read` (`.write` for `rw`) on the connection, BigQuery ObjectRef Reader / Admin, and the connection's service account `storage.objects.get` (`storage.objects.create` for `rw`) on the project or bucket; without them the documented "Connection credential for … cannot be used" or a 403 naming the permission is the ref's error. The URL functions need delegated access. An object table's `ref` column is an ObjectRef. The AI functions take ObjectRefs where Google documents them: `AI.GENERATE` (and `AI.GENERATE_BOOL/INT/DOUBLE`, `AI.IF`, `AI.SCORE`, `AI.CLASSIFY`) prompt STRUCT fields of ObjectRef or ARRAY<ObjectRef> (or an ObjectRefRuntime JSON); `ML.GENERATE_TEXT` / `AI.GENERATE_TEXT` over a STRUCT prompt column, or `TABLE object_table` with `PROMPT`; `ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING` / `AI.GENERATE_EMBEDDING` over an ObjectRef content column or an object table. Each object's access is checked as above, then it is sent to the local Vertex AI endpoint as a `fileData` part (generateContent, or the embedder's `:embedContent`), which reads it from the instance's Cloud Storage; a modality the local model cannot read (the local generator reads images; the community EmbeddingGemma embeds text only, EmbeddingGemma 2 images, audio, video and PDF) is the row's status, naming why. Nothing reaches Google.
