| The SQL engine failing after many queries | **Fixed** for the 2 GiB panic (#1061); the mitigation below is kept for any other failure of the engine | #989. **Since #1061** CloudBurrow builds the emulator with go-googlesql patched to address WebAssembly memory with unsigned offsets (third_party/bigquery-emulator, go-googlesql patch 0001): its test `TestInvokeAboveTwoGiB` fills the engine's heap below 2 GiB and makes a call whose buffers lie above it, which panicked "slice bounds out of range [-2110640288:]" without the patch and passes with it. `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh --jobs 150` on an instance of CloudBurrow's build (with the rest of #1061 and the fronts of main at the time) ran 150 query jobs and 30 `CREATE TABLE`/`DROP TABLE` pairs with no restart, the emulator container at 754 MiB at the end (281 MiB at the start), so the soak no longer reaches 2 GiB and the patched path past it is measured by the patch's test alone. **Growth through DDL** (#1057): every `DROP` of a table, view or function rebuilds every catalog, and each project's and dataset's sub-catalog registered the whole builtin function set again; CloudBurrow's build carries upstream's open goccy/googlesqlite#80 (googlesqlite patch 0006), which builds those sub-catalogs bare. Measured on an instance with 10 datasets of a table each, `bigquery-engine-soak.sh` from PR #1093, 40 operations: `--phase ddl` (CREATE and DROP TABLE) 4342 MiB before the patch, 231 MiB with it (0.50 s and 0.12 s an operation); `--phase orreplace` (CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE … AS SELECT) 11147 MiB and a 500 at the 25th before, 341 MiB and all 40 with it. The BigQuery compat suite (but `TestBigQueryJobsAcrossAnEmulatorRestart`, which restarts the emulator) on one fresh emulator took it from 62 to 2462 MiB before, and from 60 to 1372 MiB with it: less, not gone. What follows is the pinned emulator, as measured before #1061. The pinned emulator's SQL engine, goccy/go-googlesql v0.3.0 (a WebAssembly module translated to Go), lets its memory grow to 4 GiB but addresses it with signed 32-bit offsets (`(*Module).invoke`, `googlesql.go:614`, `624`), so once that memory passes 2 GiB every call panics "slice bounds out of range [-2147…:]": in a request, which the emulator answers 400 or 500 "googlesqlite: panic …" (from then on to every request, `SELECT 1` and `datasets.list` alike), or in a finalizer, which kills the process. The memory grows with each query job that returns rows (the emulator kept each result in a dataset of its own, and the engine builds a catalog of every builtin function for each) and each `DROP TABLE` (which rebuilds every dataset's catalog). The engine's objects are freed by Go finalizers, which run only when the emulator's Go heap is collected, and the engine's memory is one large `[]byte` in that heap, so a collection waits for the heap to double past it: freed engine memory is reused late, and the memory does not shrink. Measured with `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh`: the emulator container went from 455 MiB to 3840 MiB in 40 query jobs and 8 `CREATE TABLE`/`DROP TABLE` pairs, and the 60th job's `DROP TABLE` was answered the panic; one run of the BigQuery compat suite left it at 2692 MiB. go-googlesql v0.4.0 is the same. Upstream: the growth per query is goccy/bigquery-emulator#512 and #313, with a fix in review, goccy/googlesqlite#80; no upstream issue names the signed offsets. **Mitigation:** the front watches the emulator's error answers for that panic (`engineGuard`); at the first it answers that request **501** `notImplemented` naming this, sends the emulator nothing more, and fails the engine's liveness path (`/cloudburrow/bigquery-engine-live` on the front's port), so the emulator is restarted; every request until its port has closed and opened again is answered **503** `backendError` with `Retry-After: 1` (the official clients retry a 503), and then requests pass. Measured before #1091: the soak's panic was answered 501, the container's liveness probe failed, and 14 s later the emulator had restarted (restart count 1) and `SELECT 1` answered 200. **Restarts without Kubernetes' back-off (#1091):** Kubernetes restarted the emulator's container (for the probe, or when the process crashed, #1058), and the kubelet waits longer before each restart of a container that keeps failing (`CrashLoopBackOff`: 10 s, doubled at each restart up to 5 minutes, and reset only after the container has run 10 minutes). On one instance the BigQuery compat suite run four times in a row (#1057, below) reached "back-off 5m0s restarting failed container=bigquery" after the seventh restart, and in two of four series its fourth run failed most tests with 502 "the BigQuery emulator did not answer: dial tcp 127.0.0.1:9051: connect: connection refused" (545 s and 562 s). Now the emulator's container runs `cloudburrow-storage supervise` (`internal/supervisor`), which an init container copies in from the front's image (`install-self`), and which runs the image's entrypoint (`/bin/bigquery-emulator`) as its child: when the child ends, for any reason (the panic in a finalizer, a SIGSEGV, an out-of-memory kill of it), it starts it again within at most 1 s (100 ms, doubled while it keeps ending within 2 s of its start); it gets the front's liveness path every 0.5 s from 1 s after each start and kills the child (SIGKILL) after two 503s in a row, and restarts it the same way; no answer from the front (the front restarting) is not a failure. The container never restarts, so the back-off never applies, and it has no liveness probe. While the emulator's port refuses connections the front answers 503 with `Retry-After` too, not 502. `POST /cloudburrow/bigquery-restart-emulator` on the front's port restarts the emulator as the panic does (answered 202), for tests, soaks, or an instance grown slow (it empties the emulator). Measured on an instance of my own: `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh --phase restart --jobs 10` (a restart, then `datasets.list` until 200) took 1.0–2.6 s each, answering 503 then 200, with the container's restart count 0 and its memory at 78 MiB throughout (the first build, which waited 5 s after a start before checking, took 2.0 s and then 5.9–6.3 s); killing the emulator's process (`kill -9`) three times, it answered 503 and was back in 0.2 s each; the BigQuery compat suite passed, with `TestBigQueryEmulatorRestartsPromptly`'s eight restarts in a row back in 1.0–2.7 s. The suite run four times in a row on that emulator: 305 s, all passed; then 605 s, 610 s and 607 s, each stopped by the 10-minute limit (one test failed "context deadline exceeded" in the third, two in the fourth), with no restart of the emulator, no "connection refused" and no 502 in any of them: nothing failed the engine or crashed the process (table functions, whose SIGSEGV restarted it before, were 501 then, #1052; they are served since, the table functions row, `TestBigQueryTableFunctions`), so the emulator was never emptied and the growth through DDL below made it slower with each run (#1103). Units `TestCrashesRestartPromptly` (ten starts of a child that crashes, each within the delay), `TestLivenessFailuresRestartPromptly` (eight restarts in a row through the liveness path, none while it answers 200 or does not answer), `TestRestartEmulatorPath`, `TestProxyAnswersARefusedPort503`; the manifest in `TestBigQueryManifestPutsTheFrontOnTheServicePort`. **Growth per query job, fixed (#1017):** the front names a query job's destination table itself, so the emulator writes every result to one dataset (next row) and a job no longer adds a catalog. Measured with the soak script on one instance, from a fresh emulator: 60 query jobs and 12 `CREATE TABLE`/`DROP TABLE` pairs took the container from 62 MiB to 4301 MiB in 23.7 s before, and from 66 MiB to 701 MiB in 7.8 s after; 400 jobs and 80 pairs held it at 799–802 MiB from the 100th job on (100 s). Tried and measured worse: deleting each job's result dataset right after the job (64 → 1964 MiB in 60 jobs: every deletion is a `DROP TABLE`, which rebuilds the catalogs), and deleting the results of all but the last 20 jobs from the one dataset (3272 MiB at 100 jobs, 300 jobs in 110 s); so the results are kept, as the emulator kept its per-job datasets, until it restarts. Collecting the emulator's heap sooner (`GOGC=10`) held the soak at 200–205 MiB, but the compat suite's `TestBigQueryCreateFunctionOfAnExistingFunction` then failed in each of four runs ("wasm trap: interface conversion: interface {} is nil", "index out of range", a SIGSEGV that killed the process), so it is not set. **Records across a restart, fixed (#1016):** next row but one. **Growth through DDL, loads and scripts, measured (#1057):** it is the catalog rebuild, whatever the statement. Read in the engine (googlesqlite v0.3.1, `internal/catalog.go`, `stmt_action.go`): it builds a catalog with every builtin function (`newSimpleCatalog`) for the root, one for each project, and four for each dataset that holds a table (the dataset under the root and under its project, and each one's `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`: `addTableSpecRecursiveImpl`, `aliasInfoSchemaTable`), and builds them all again at each `DeleteTableSpec`, `DeleteFunctionSpec` and `DeleteTVFSpec` (`resetCatalog`): a `DROP TABLE`, `DROP VIEW` or `DROP FUNCTION` of one that exists, `tables.delete`, each table of a `datasets.delete` with `deleteContents`, and the end of a script that made a TEMP table or function (`Cleanup`); a load, `CREATE TABLE`, the engine's `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` and a `DROP … IF EXISTS` of one that is not there rebuild nothing. So the cost of each rebuild grows with the datasets that hold tables. Measured with `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh --phase <p> --jobs 20 --datasets 10` (each phase from a new emulator, first 10 datasets of one table, about 240 MiB), the container after 20 operations: a `CREATE`/`DROP TABLE` pair 2,247 MiB (10 s); a dataset made and deleted with its table 2,249 MiB; a CSV load with a schema and its `tables.delete` 2,242 MiB; a failed script given to jobs.query 2,248 MiB; `CREATE`/`DROP FUNCTION` 2,197 MiB; `MERGE` from a subquery 2,262 MiB (11 s); a copy job with WRITE_TRUNCATE 4,357 MiB (18 s); `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE … AS SELECT` 4,349 MiB (19 s); `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` of one that exists 4,243 MiB (16 s); a script with a TEMP table 4,218 MiB; a load with autodetect of a FLOAT column (#1000) and its `tables.delete`: the engine failed at the 15th (4,473 MiB); 20 query jobs 902 MiB. **The front's share, cut:** the front's own scratch tables (the copy with WRITE_TRUNCATE, the FLOAT load, `MERGE` from a subquery, `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE`, and since #1091 a Parquet load the front carries out and a schema update that adds columns) and the scratch function of `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` are made in `_cloudburrow_query_results` (next row) rather than the client's dataset, and the front's deletion of each is answered at once and carried out later, with the expired results, while the instance is idle; an error naming one names the client's dataset. Measured the same way after: `MERGE` from a subquery 428 MiB (2 s); `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` 2,249 MiB (10 s); the copy 3,683 MiB (12 s); `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` 3,555 MiB (11 s); the FLOAT load failed at the 20th; a `CREATE`/`DROP TABLE` pair unchanged (2,245 MiB). The Parquet load and the schema update, measured the same way (each phase from an emulator just restarted, twice each), before and after: a Parquet load with `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` of a table that exists (`--phase parquet`) 2,270 MiB (11–19 s) and 447–449 MiB (3–4 s); `tables.patch` adding a column (`--phase schemaupdate`, which also deletes and makes the table again) 4,365 MiB (21–22 s) and 3,528–3,531 MiB (11–12 s). Units `TestScratchTablesInResultsDataset`, `TestScratchFunctionDroppedLater`, `TestUnscratch`; the copy, FLOAT, `MERGE`, `CREATE OR REPLACE` compat tests unchanged. The rest is the clients' own drops (a compat test's cleanup deletes its dataset table by table), which the front cannot leave out without changing their results; it takes an engine whose catalogs do not each hold every builtin (goccy/googlesqlite#80, not released). The BigQuery compat suite run four times on one emulator (`-run BigQuery`, 10-minute limit; each run's time, the container's memory after it and the emulator's restarts so far), in two series on the front before this and two after (two builds that differ only in the cap of the next row, which the suite does not reach): before, 204 s, 1545 MiB, 1; 321 s, 1332 MiB, 2; 381 s, 1480 MiB, 3; 294 s, 2451 MiB, 4; and 214 s, 2476 MiB, 1; 250 s, 2471 MiB, 3; 283 s, 2444 MiB, 5; 545 s, 1311 MiB, 7; after, 169 s, 2453 MiB, 1; 182 s, 2455 MiB, 3; 289 s, 2438 MiB, 5; 562 s, 1604 MiB, 7; and 226 s, 2456 MiB, 1; 271 s, 2447 MiB, 3; 332 s, 2454 MiB, 5; 445 s, 2437 MiB, 6: no change beyond the series' spread, the suite's drops being its tests' own. In two series (one before, one after) the fourth run failed most tests "connection refused": after seven restarts Kubernetes' back-off kept the emulator down for minutes (#1091, fixed above). **What is left:** the restart loses every dataset, table and job, as the crash did (Persistence row); a finalizer can still kill the emulator before any request sees the panic, which the supervisor restarts at once (#1091); a request in flight when the emulator ends is answered 502 (it was sent before the port closed); and the growth through DDL: the BigQuery compat suite is mostly DDL, loads and scripts, and its tests run one at a time from a fresh emulator took the container from 87 MiB to 2427 MiB by its 20th test (the most at `TestBigQueryFailedScriptLeavesTheCatalogInStep`, +840 MiB, and the `CREATE FUNCTION` and `DROP SCHEMA` tests), where it stayed for the other 44. The suite run four times in a row on one emulator (`-run BigQuery`, 10-minute limit; each run's time, the container's memory after it, the emulator's restarts so far, and a `jobs.list` of 200 jobs with `projection=full` after it): before #1017, 218 s, 2872 MiB, 0, 7.4 s; 239 s, 2694 MiB, 1, 5.9 s; 250 s, 2698 MiB, 2, 6.1 s; 270 s, 2721 MiB, 3, 5.8 s; after, 194 s, 2449 MiB, 0, 7.7 s; 606 s (the limit), 4425 MiB, 0, 22.3 s; 275 s, 2830 MiB, 1, 4.9 s; 202 s, 2919 MiB, 2, 5.3 s. Every restart came during `TestBigQueryCreateFunctionOfAnExistingFunction`'s table function, which then failed, before and after alike (after, the emulator's log names a SIGSEGV in the engine, exit code 2); that test passes on a fresh emulator. After a restart, `TestBigQueryDropSchema` failed once (409 for a function it was making), and passed alone. So a long-lived instance that runs much DDL still gets slow and fails; restart it (`cloudburrow stop`, `up`). Follow-ups: the crash #1058; the restart back-off #1091, fixed; the copy with WRITE_TRUNCATE #1092, closed, see *Copy jobs*. Soak: `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh`. Units `TestEngineGuard`, `TestEngineGuardWithoutWatch`, `TestEngineGuardPassesLargeErrors`, `TestBigQueryManifestPutsTheFrontOnTheServicePort`; compat `TestBigQueryEmulatorRestartsPromptly` (#1091), official Go client. |
| Console screen | **Verified** | `TestConsoleBigQueryDatasetsSchemaAndQuery` (#698): datasets, tables, schema, a preview and the query editor, read-only by default; `TestConsoleBigQueryDatasetTableAndRowWrites` (#854): create and delete datasets and tables, with a schema, and insert rows, through the official Go client; `TestConsoleBigQueryLoadExportAndJobHistory` (#993): loads from and exports to Cloud Storage, and Job history; `TestConsoleBigQueryLoadFromAFile` (#999): Load from a file uploaded from the browser; `TestConsoleBigQueryJobPageShowsDMLRows` (#1041): a query job's statement type and DML row counts on its page; `TestConsoleBigQueryReadWriteEditorRunsDDLAndScripts` (#994): the editor's opt-in Read-write mode, through `jobs.query`: `CREATE SCHEMA`, `CREATE TABLE … AS SELECT`, `CREATE VIEW`, `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE`, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, a script with `DECLARE`, and `DROP TABLE`, each read back with the official Go client; `TestConsoleBigQueryReadWriteEditorRunsDML` (#1024, #1567): a DML statement of its own, answered with the rows it changed, an `UPDATE … FROM` a subquery, and DML inside a script and a `BEGIN` block, answered with each DML statement's rows from the script's child jobs (the DML row); `TestConsoleBigQueryEditTableViewsAndInsertOptions` (#994, #1025): flexible field names, a view from Create table, Edit table's description and labels (removing a label and clearing the description included), and Insert rows with `skipInvalidRows` and `ignoreUnknownValues`. See the Console table. |
| Query results: the destination table of a query job that names none | **Verified** | `TestBigQueryQueryResultsInOneHiddenDataset` (#1017), official Go client (`Query.Run`, `Job.Config`, `Job.Read`, `Table.Read`, `Client.Datasets` with and without `ListHidden`). BigQuery writes such a result to a temporary table in an anonymous, hidden dataset, which the job names ([docs](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/writing-results#temporary_and_permanent_tables)); the front has the emulator write it to a table named after the job in one hidden dataset, `_cloudburrow_query_results` (a name beginning with `_` is hidden, and `datasets.list` leaves it out unless `all=true`), which it makes when a project first needs it and again if it is deleted. The job's `configuration.query.destinationTable` names it, `jobs.getQueryResults` of every job and `tabledata.list` of its table read the rows back, and no dataset is named after a job. Only a query that is one `SELECT` (or `WITH`, or a parenthesised query) is given one; a DDL or DML statement, a script and a dry run are sent as they were (unit `TestQueryResultsInOneDataset`, `TestDatasetsListHidesResults`, `TestIsLoneQuery`). **Expired as BigQuery expires them (#1059):** BigQuery keeps such a table up to about 24 hours, best-effort, and "may be invalidated sooner" ([docs](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/cached-results)); the front deletes a result table once it is 24 hours old, or, oldest first, once there are more than 200, in batches of 20 while the instance is idle (no client request for 30 s; the liveness probe does not count), a batch stopping at the first request that comes in, and without waiting for idle time only past 300 (1,000 before #1655). A job whose table was deleted is answered 404 `notFound` "Not found: Table …" at `jobs.getQueryResults`, and by the emulator 404 `notFound` at `tabledata.list` of the table, as BigQuery answers a table that does not exist ([errors](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/error-messages)); `jobs.get` still names the destination; a later job's result still reads (`TestBigQueryExpiredQueryResultsAreNotFound`, official Go client: `Job.Read`, `Job.Config`, `Table.Read`, deleting one job's table through the front's `POST /cloudburrow/bigquery-expire-query-results?job=<id>`, which also takes `?keep=N`, for a test or to free the engine; units `TestResultsExpireAfterADay`, `TestResultsExpireOverTheCap`, `TestExpireResultsPath`, `TestLivenessProbeIsIdle`). Measured first: after `tables.delete` of a job's result table, the emulator answered `jobs.getQueryResults` of the job with its rows. The front forgets its tables when the emulator restarts (they are gone with it). **Adopted after a restart of the front (#1660):** the list of tables is kept in memory, so a front that restarted while the emulator went on never deleted the tables made before it (measured: 318 tables in the dataset after one run of the BigQuery compat and console tests, whose restart tests end the front three times, of which the front knew 96); now, when it starts, it lists each project's results dataset once and adopts the jobs' tables there with their `creationTime` (not its scratch tables nor its JOBS table), which the age, count and size rules then cover (units `TestResultsAdoptedAfterARestart`, `TestResultsAdoptFails`; `internal/bigqueryfront/resultsadopt.go`). **Bounded by rows and bytes (#1662):** the emulator keeps the tables in a SQLite file that never gives space back, and the JOBS_BY_ORGANIZATION results of `TestBigQueryInformationSchemaJobs` (about 9,000 rows each, two a run) filled it to 1 GB in 23 minutes under the count caps alone; so the front reads each table's `numRows` once (`tables.get`, in the background; the engine answers `numBytes` 0, so the bytes are `numRows` times the row's width by its schema, BigQuery's data type sizes with a STRING, BYTES or JSON value counted as 32), and deletes the oldest past 250,000 rows or 64 MiB in all while idle, and past 1,000,000 rows or 256 MiB while busy too, the newest table always kept (the constants `resultsMaxRows`, `resultsMaxBytes`, `resultsHardRows` and `resultsHardBytes` in `internal/bigqueryfront/resultsexpiry.go`; unit `TestResultsBoundedByRowsAndBytes`). With bigquery-emulator patch 0085 the file also gives back what a deletion frees (`auto_vacuum=FULL`). Measured (`--services bigquery,storage,kms`, arm64, Docker Desktop, 2026-11-17) after `TestBigQueryInformationSchemaJobsAtScale` (5,000 jobs), with 100 query jobs in a row, each a `SELECT *` of the region's `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS` (about 5,100 rows): before, the file grew by about 16 MB a job, to 1.40 GB in 137 s; after, it reached 605 MB in 119 s, and 481 MB once the idle front had cut the tables to 7. Most of that was the emulator's own JSON copy of each result, up to 256 MiB (bigquery-emulator patch 0002). **No second copy (#1662):** the front sends each job it gives a table with the header `X-Cloudburrow-Result-In-Table` (never a client's), and with bigquery-emulator patch 0086 the emulator keeps that job's schema, `totalRows` and statistics without its rows, and answers `jobs.getQueryResults` from the table (in the table's order, as `tabledata.list` reads it), paged as before; a result that a `SELECT *` of the table would not give back keeps its copy: one with a column named with a leading underscore, as a pseudo-column is (`SELECT *` leaves out `_PARTITIONTIME`; measured: `TestBigQueryIngestionPartitionHistory` and `TestBigQueryPastIngestionTimeCopies` failed "schema length does not match row length" without this), and one with a FLOAT64 -0, which a table holds as 0. The answers are the same: the patch's `TestResultReadFromItsTable` compares `jobs.getQueryResults` through eleven pagings and formats, and `jobs.get`, of seven queries (every scalar type, arrays, structs, a range, NaN and infinities, 250 rows, no rows, a -0, columns named `_PARTITIONTIME` and `_PARTITIONDATE`) inserted with and without the header (unit `TestResultsReadFromTheTable`). Once the table is deleted, the emulator too answers 404 `notFound` "Not found: Table …". Measured the same way (5,000 jobs, then 100 such query jobs, 2026-11-17): the file stayed between 84 and 183 MB, 136 MB after the 100th job in 109 s (605 MB before), and 53 MB a minute after the last, once the idle front had cut the tables (481 MB before). A front restarted on that instance adopted the 7 tables. Why a cap and idle time: every deletion is a `DROP TABLE`, which rebuilds the engine's catalogs (previous row), and costs more the more tables the engine has, not more memory: measured with `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh` on an emulator with only the soak's dataset, 50 deletions took 25 s with 300 result tables (container 398 → 789 MiB) and 195 s with 1,000 (622 → 627 MiB), a `CREATE TABLE`/`DROP TABLE` pair 0.8 s with 300 and 5.2 s with 1,000; deleting past a cap of 400 while busy made 600 query jobs (a pair every 5) take 454 s rather than 308 s with all kept; with this, 600 such jobs took 267 s, the idle front then deleted 400 in 481 s with the memory flat at 1,472 MiB, and a pair went from 2.7 s to 1.8 s. Why 300 since #1655: every request the emulator answers reads its project's every table, result tables among them (bigquery-emulator patch 0080), so a busy instance's requests got slower with each result table up to the cap, and a `DROP TABLE` costs far less since googlesqlite patch 0062. Measured in `TestBigQueryInformationSchemaJobs -count=200` after the `TestBigQuery*` suite and 6,000 more jobs (`--services bigquery,storage,kms`, arm64, Docker Desktop, 2026-10-19): with the cap at 1,000 a run took 5.0 s with 380 result tables and 7.5–10 s past 610, a sixth of the emulator's CPU in that read and a quarter in collection, and 52 result tables were deleted in 7.1 s with 700 held while the loop ran. **Differs:** the dataset and table names are not BigQuery's random ones; a busy instance may hold up to 300. Measured first: the emulator made a dataset named after each job, which `datasets.list` listed. |
| The emulator's jobs: what each request reads, and how long a query's result rows are kept | **Verified** that each request's time no longer grows with the jobs the emulator keeps, and that `jobs.getQueryResults` of recent jobs reads their rows; **Differs** in how long a result is kept | CloudBurrow's build, bigquery-emulator patch 0002 (#1086). **Measured first**, on the pinned v0.8.1 and on #1061's build: every request, whatever it was, read the project with every job the emulator had run, each job's metadata and its whole result decoded from JSON, and each new job wrote the project's list of jobs again, so each request got slower with each job kept. On the emulator alone (an Apple silicon Mac), `SELECT 1` through `jobs.query` took 0.006 s fresh, 0.14 s after 20 queries of 50,000 rows and 0.27 s after 40, and `datasets.list` the same; 0.37 s after 1,000 queries of 10 rows and 1.43 s after 2,000. Through an instance, `scripts/bigquery-engine-soak.sh --phase rows --rows 50000 --max-probe 1` timed `SELECT 1` at 0.034 s, 0.43 s after 50 such queries and 1.05 s after 100, where it stopped, the container at 1,378 MiB. **Now** a project is read with no jobs, a job when a request names it (its metadata alone), its result only by `jobs.getQueryResults`, and the order `jobs.list` gives them is kept in a table of its own. The same soak: `SELECT 1` 0.034 s before and 0.067 s after 300 queries of 50,000 rows (`datasets.list` 0.023 s and 0.049 s), then 0.033 s and 0.038 s across 3,000 more of 10 rows (`datasets.list` 0.023 s throughout), the container at 925 MiB; on the emulator alone, 0.005 s after 40 queries of 50,000 rows, and 0.009 s after 3,000 of 10. `jobs.getQueryResults`, `jobs.get`, `jobs.list` and `jobs.delete` of recent jobs are the compat suite's (104 `BigQuery` tests run against this build through the official Go client: 92 passed, 10 skipped for a service the instance did not run; `TestBigQueryWriteTruncateDataReplacesTheRows` failed, as it does against #1061's build, and `TestBigQueryStorageReadInAvroOnAHyphenatedProject` needs a project with a hyphen, which that instance's had not). **Differs:** BigQuery keeps a query's result, its temporary table, "up to 24 hours" and best-effort ([docs](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/writing-results#temporary_and_permanent_tables)); the emulator keeps a job's result rows up to 24 hours and while the results it keeps come to at most 256 MiB of JSON, the oldest dropped first when the next job's result is kept, so a result may outlive 24 hours on an idle emulator until then. `jobs.getQueryResults` of a job whose result was dropped is 404 `notFound`, and the job itself is kept, for `jobs.get` and `jobs.list`, as long as the emulator runs; a query job whose result table the front keeps (row above) meets the front's rule first, and since #1662 keeps no rows here at all: the emulator reads them from that table (bigquery-emulator patch 0086). Units, in the patch: `TestFindProjectReadsNoJobResults` (fails without it), `TestResultsExpire`, `TestJobsKeepTheirOrder`, `TestJobOrderMigrates`. |
| Jobs across a restart of the emulator | **Verified** | `TestBigQueryJobsAcrossAnEmulatorRestart` (#1016), official Go client: a load the front failed, the emulator's container restarted alone through the node's container runtime, then a load of the same job ID on the new emulator is done, not failed, in `jobs.get` and `jobs.list`, listed once. The front holds a connection open to the emulator's port and redials it (every 10 s, under the 15 s the emulator gives a connection to send a request's headers); the process ending closes it, and the front then drops the failures it gave, the client's texts of jobs it changed, configurations, times, its own jobs, the functions it saw made and the client's texts of views, once when the process ends and once when it is back (units `TestEmulatorWatch`, `TestEmulatorWatchNotBeforeFirstUp`, `TestFrontDropsJobsAtRestart`). Measured first (the unit, without the watch): the new job was answered with the old one's failure and times. Resumable upload sessions are kept: they hold the client's data, and their load is answered by the emptied emulator. |
| Dataset and table IDs, field names | **Verified** | CloudBurrow's front (`internal/bigqueryfront`, #861) checks BigQuery's documented rules before the emulator, which checks none (measured: it created `d-1` and `t!`). A dataset ID is letters, digits and underscores, at most 1,024 characters (`TestBigQueryRefusesInvalidDatasetID`: a hyphen is 400). A table ID is Unicode letters, marks, numbers, connectors, dashes and spaces, at most 1,024 UTF-8 bytes (`TestBigQueryRefusesInvalidTableID`: `t!` is 400, `étudiant-01 x` is created). A field name follows BigQuery's **flexible column names**, at most 300 characters and none of the reserved prefixes (`_TABLE_`, `_PARTITION` and the rest): `TestBigQueryRefusesInvalidFieldName` has `a!` refused with 400, and **a space accepted**, as BigQuery now accepts it, and the column written and read back. Two fields at one level whose names differ only in case are a 400 (`TestBigQueryDuplicateColumnIs400`; the emulator's was a 500); an unknown type or mode, and a RECORD with no fields, are 400 too (unit `TestTableIDsAndSchemas`). The same schema checks apply to `tables.update` and `tables.patch`. |
| Duplicate dataset | **Verified** | `TestBigQueryDuplicateDatasetIs409`: a second dataset of one ID is 409 `duplicate`, "Already Exists". The emulator answered 500 "already created", which the Go client retried until its deadline; the front looks the dataset up first. A duplicate table is 409 from the emulator itself, as in BigQuery. Deleting a dataset that still has tables is a 400 `resourceInUse` without `deleteContents`, as in BigQuery (measured, #854). |
| Duplicate job ID (a retried `jobs.insert`) | **Verified** | `TestBigQueryInsertOfAnExistingJobIs409` (#1622), official Go client: a query job and a DML job run under a job ID of the client's, then `Query.Run` of the same ID again is **409 `duplicate`**, "Already Exists: Job project:LOCATION.id", the job read by its ID (`JobFromID`) is the first one, DONE, with its query, and the `INSERT` sent twice made one row. The Go client retries a `jobs.insert` with a jobReference after a transient failure (a 5xx, `backendError`, `internalError`, a reset connection), when the first attempt may have made the job. BigQuery answers such an insert 409 `duplicate` ("This error returns when trying to create a job, dataset, or table that already exists", [error messages](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/error-messages)); the message's wording is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/error-messages>). Measured first: the emulator ran the query again and then failed 400 `jobInternalError` "failed to add job: job … is already created" (a DML statement ran a second time before the rollback). Before anything else the front looks up a client's job ID that it has answered an insert of (its own jobs, else the emulator's `jobs.get`; a new ID costs no request), and the emulator's patch 0076 answers an insert that reaches it the same way (two inserts of one ID at once, an ID from before the front restarted, a load's upload). A failed job inserted again stays failed, as in BigQuery (before, a retried insert that succeeded replaced the failure). The pinned Go client (v1.85.0) does not read the job on a 409: its `Query.Run` returns the 409 error, and a caller reads the job with `JobFromID`. Unit `TestInsertOfAnExistingJobIs409` (front and engine). |
| Streamed rows checked against the schema | **Verified** | Before a row reaches the emulator, the front reads the table's schema and checks every value: a missing or null REQUIRED value (`TestBigQueryInsertRefusesMissingRequiredValue`), a field the table does not have, an array for a non-REPEATED field and the reverse, a NULL array element, a non-object RECORD, and a value that does not convert to its type (`TestBigQueryInsertRefusesWrongTypeValue`: `"x"` in NUMERIC, which the emulator stored as 0, and `"abc"` in INTEGER, which it answered with 500). INTEGER, FLOAT, NUMERIC (and its range), BIGNUMERIC, BOOLEAN, BYTES (base64), DATE, TIME, DATETIME, TIMESTAMP (the canonical formats, or epoch seconds), JSON text, and GEOGRAPHY as a string are checked (unit `TestInsertAllChecksEachValue`). **A table stays readable after a refused row**: `TestBigQueryTableReadableAfterRefusedRepeatedValue` sends `["q"]` for a REPEATED INTEGER, which the emulator had stored and then failed every read with "failed to scan rows"; now the row is an `insertErrors` entry and `Table.Read` returns the one valid row. Each failure is an `insertErrors` entry with reason `invalid` and the field as `location`; the messages are CloudBurrow's own, not BigQuery's text. **Not checked:** a GEOGRAPHY's geometry, INTERVAL and RANGE text, and fractional seconds past six digits (accepted, as BigQuery documents six). |
| `insertAll` `skipInvalidRows` | **Verified** | Without it, a batch with an invalid row inserts nothing and every row is reported, `invalid` or `stopped` (`TestBigQueryInsertAllWithoutSkipInvalidRowsInsertsNothing`); the emulator had inserted the good rows. With it, the valid rows are inserted and only the invalid ones reported, at their own index (`TestBigQueryInsertAllSkipInvalidRows`). |
| `insertAll` `ignoreUnknownValues` | **Verified** | `TestBigQueryInsertAllIgnoreUnknownValues`: a field the table does not have makes the row invalid, and with the flag the field is dropped and the row inserted. |
| RECORD inside a REPEATED RECORD, and REPEATED RECORD inside a RECORD | **Verified**: created, streamed, loaded, written by DML and read back | `TestBigQueryNestedRecordsInRepeatedRecordsReadBack` (#881, #900), official Go client: both schemas are created through `tables.insert` as BigQuery creates them, and rows written by `tabledata.insertAll` (a value in the nested RECORD, and one with `null` or `[]` there), a DML `INSERT` and five one-row JSON load jobs, one after another, are read back with their values through `tabledata.list` and a `SELECT` after each load. Against the pinned v0.8.1 a streamed value there left every later read failing 500 "failed to scan rows: failed to convert struct from array" (measured, #874), and a load into a RECORD inside a REPEATED RECORD did so in 5 of 60 one-row loads ("failed to convert struct from string"), so the front answered both 501; the fault was the SQL engine's ([googlesqlite](https://github.com/goccy/googlesqlite)), which did not reshape a STRUCT under an ARRAY from the form the emulator binds it in. CloudBurrow's build carries its maintainer's open fix, [goccy/googlesqlite#76](https://github.com/goccy/googlesqlite/pull/76), unchanged (#1061), and the 501s are gone (units `TestInsertAllSendsNestedRecordsOn`, `TestJobsCheckTheTablesTheyMake`). RECORDs nested with none REPEATED, a REPEATED RECORD of scalars and REPEATED scalars in a RECORD are streamed, loaded and read back. The Storage Write API is not checked. |
| Tables made by jobs: DDL, load, copy, query destination | **Verified**, names only | `TestBigQueryJobsAreHeldToTheNamingRules` (#881), official Go client. The emulator ran `` CREATE TABLE ds.`t!` ``, a column `` `a!` `` and `` CREATE SCHEMA `bad-name` ``, and loaded rows into a table `t!` (measured); the front now answers each with 400 and nothing is made, while a table `ok table-1` with a column `first name` is created and a load into `loaded-1` writes its row. **`jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`:** a `CREATE [OR REPLACE] [TEMP] TABLE` or `CREATE SCHEMA` statement is read with a lexer, and its table ID, each column of its column list, each field of a `STRUCT` column type and the dataset ID of `CREATE SCHEMA` are held to the rules in the next rows, 400 `invalidQuery`; a load, copy or query job's `destinationTable` is held to the table ID rule and a load's `schema` to the schema rules, 400 `invalid`, including a load from a local file, whose multipart upload is checked by its first part only (unit `TestDDLNames`, `TestJobsCheckTheTablesTheyMake`, `TestLoadUploadIsCheckedByItsFirstPart`). A column named twice is refused by the emulator's own analyser, 400 (measured). `ALTER TABLE`, the columns of `CREATE TABLE … AS SELECT`, the DDL inside a script's blocks and loads with `autodetect` are the next rows (#901). **Not checked:** a statement in a string (`EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`), and `CREATE VIEW`. The refusals are at insertion, as `tables.insert`'s are; BigQuery reports some query errors on the job instead, and the messages are CloudBurrow's own. |

The engine's `TableFieldSchema` (google.golang.org/api v0.279.0) has no such field, so the front keeps each top-level column's tags in the table's settings and puts them in the `tables.get`, `tables.insert` and `tables.patch` answers (`internal/bigqueryfront/governancetags.go`). INFORMATION_SCHEMA documents no column for them. | `tables.patch`: labels, description, and schema changes BigQuery refuses | **Verified** for labels and the description; a schema that drops a column, changes a column's type or mode, or adds a `REQUIRED` column is **400**; adding columns is the *Schema updates* row (#1010) | `TestBigQueryTablePatchLabelsAndDescription`, `TestBigQueryTablePatchRefusesSchemaChanges` (#1009), official Go client (`Table.Update`, which sends `tables.patch`). Measured first against the pinned emulator: a label deleted with `DeleteLabel` (sent as `null`) read back as `""`, a patch of some labels dropped the others (it replaces the map), an empty description was ignored, and it took a schema that dropped or retyped columns and one that added a `REQUIRED` column. BigQuery's patch merges the labels, a `null` one removed ([Deleting a table label](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/deleting-labels#table)), clears a description given empty, and refuses those schemas, "Provided Schema does not match Table" ([Modifying table schemas](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas)). The front carries out a patch that gives labels or a description as the emulator's `tables.update` of the whole table with the patch applied (labels merged, `null` ones removed, an empty description cleared; every label deleted leaves none), and checks a patch's or update's schema against the table's first: a column left out, retyped or changed in mode (other than `REQUIRED` to `NULLABLE`), or a `REQUIRED` column added (at any depth), is **400 `invalid`** and the table is unchanged. This and the *Schema updates* row are one path (#1054): the table is read once, the schema checked against it (the 400s first, then the 501s of that row), columns added, and then a patch's labels and description applied, so one `Table.Update` can add a column and change the labels. The console's Edit table sends `Table.Update` too (the row *`bigquery.tables.patch` (`Table.Update`) from the console's Edit table*). Units `TestPatchTableMergesLabels`, `TestSchemaChange`, `TestSchemaUpdates`. |

Measured against the pinned emulator: it made `` CREATE VIEW ds.`v!` `` and a view whose query gave a column `` `x!` `` or a `STRUCT` field `` `y?` ``, and `tables.insert` made a view with a column `` `w!` ``. The view ID is held to the table ID rule, and the columns its query gives, read by running the query alone as for `CREATE TABLE … AS SELECT`, to the column rules: **400 `invalidQuery`** (`invalid` through `tables.insert`), and nothing is made. A view with names BigQuery takes is made and read. `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW` of an existing view failed 400 "table is already created" and left the view unreadable ("no such column", measured); the front deletes the view and sends the statement, once its query has run alone, so it **replaces** the view as BigQuery does (the new column reads back). **A view's column list** (`CREATE VIEW v (c, d) AS …`, #1240): the emulator answered 400 "CREATE VIEW with explicit column list is not supported" (measured). BigQuery names the view's columns by the list, in order, whatever the query calls them ([CREATE VIEW](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language#create_view_statement): "view_column_name_list … may be aliases to the column names in the underlying SQL query"), keeps the query as written and sets `view.useExplicitColumnNames` ([ViewDefinition](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/tables#ViewDefinition)). A query that is one such statement is now sent on as the `CREATE VIEW` it amounts to: the query is run alone (`LIMIT 0`) for its columns, and when their names are distinct and none is the engine's `$colN` for an unnamed column, the view's query is ``SELECT `_cloudburrow_q`.`a` AS `c`, … FROM (query) AS `_cloudburrow_q` ``; otherwise, as such a column cannot be named from outside the query, it is a typed empty row of the listed names `UNION ALL` the query (measured: read back the query's rows under the listed names). `OR REPLACE`, `IF NOT EXISTS` and `OPTIONS(...)` are kept (the emulator keeps none of a `CREATE VIEW`'s `OPTIONS`, with or without a list; the front sets them, #1251, the DDL `OPTIONS` row). Read back through the Go client, through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`: a view of named, unnamed (`a + 0`, `UPPER(b)`) and twice-named (`z`, `z`) columns has the listed names and the query's types in `tables.get`'s schema, its query as written, `useExplicitColumnNames` true (generated client), its rows by the listed names, and `jobs.get` shows the client's text; the console's Read-write editor runs one too. **400 `invalidQuery`**, nothing made: a list longer or shorter than the query's columns ("The number of columns in the column list (1) does not match the number of columns in the query (2)"; BigQuery refuses it, its wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job>)), a listed name BigQuery refuses for a column, a name listed twice (in any case), and a query that cannot run (the engine's message). **A column's `OPTIONS` in the list, and a list inside a script** (#1323): the emulator keeps no column description from DDL (measured). A listed column's `OPTIONS(description = '…')`, the one column option BigQuery takes for a view, is now set once the view is made: its schema is read, the listed columns given their descriptions, and written back with the emulator's `tables.update`, which keeps them; read back through the Go client (`Table.Metadata`'s `Schema[i].Description`), alone through `jobs.insert` and in a script through `jobs.query`. A column list inside a multi-statement script is carried out by the front's run of the script, a statement at a time, each `CREATE VIEW` with a list then carried out alone as above: read back through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`, the listed names in the schema, the view's rows by them, and the script's later statements read the view. The listed names are checked with the script's other statements before anything runs: a name listed twice is **400 `invalidQuery`** and an earlier `CREATE TABLE` of the script makes nothing. **A column list in a script with a `TEMP` table or function, and in a dry run** (#1335, `TestBigQueryViewColumnListInATempScriptAndADryRun`, official Go client through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`, the generated client for a dry run through `jobs.query`): a `TEMP` table lasts only for the request that made it, so such a script is not split but sent as one text, each `CREATE VIEW` with a list in it put there as the `CREATE VIEW` it amounts to (above). When the view's query cannot run alone, as when it reads a table the script makes before it, its columns are an empty row of the listed names of untyped `NULL`s `UNION ALL` the query, which takes the query's types (measured on the pinned image: `INTEGER`, `STRING`, a `REPEATED FLOAT` and a `RECORD` with its field); the engine then reports, when the script reaches the statement, a query that cannot run or of another number of columns. Once the script is done each such view gets its columns' descriptions and keeps its query as written. Read back: the listed names and the query's types, a listed column's description, `ViewQuery` as written, the rows by the listed names, and the script's last statement reads the view; also for a view of a table the script made. A name listed twice is **400 `invalidQuery`** before anything runs. A dry run of a lone such statement runs and makes nothing: the view's dataset must exist (**404 `notFound`** "Not found: Dataset project:ds"), the query and the list are checked as for the statement (**400 `invalidQuery`**), and the answer has `statistics.query.statementType` `CREATE_VIEW` (the emulator's own dry run of a `CREATE VIEW` answered `SELECT`, measured), `totalBytesProcessed` 0 and no schema or rows, the statement giving no result (BigQuery's dry run of a `CREATE VIEW` was not measured: the statement type is the reference's, the rest UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language>)). **409 `duplicate`** (#1456, `TestBigQueryCreateOfAnExistingName`, official Go client through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`, a dry run through `Query.DryRun` and the generated client's `jobs.query`): a `CREATE TABLE` or `CREATE VIEW`, with or without a column list, without `OR REPLACE` or `IF NOT EXISTS`, of a name a table or view has, and its dry run, as a dry run gives "the same error it would if it wasn't a dry run" ([JobConfiguration.dryRun](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfiguration)) and the [error table](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/error-messages) gives `duplicate` 409 "when trying to create a job, dataset, or table that already exists"; the message is `tables.insert`'s, "Already Exists: Table p:ds.v" (that DDL gives the same text is UNVERIFIED, docs re-read 2026-11-17); nothing is changed. Measured first: each was 400 `jobInternalError` with the engine's text ("sqlite3: SQL logic error: table `p_ds_t` already exists"), the dry run with a column list 501. **#1416**: "Column options for a view have the same syntax and requirements as for a table, but with a different list" ([view_column_option_list](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language#view_column_option_list)), `description` alone, so another option (`rounding_mode`, say) is **400** `invalidQuery`, nothing made (501 before; the wording CloudBurrow's, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language>)). A description that is a constant expression ("a constant expression containing only literals, query parameters, and scalar functions") is evaluated by the engine before the view is made and read back (`CONCAT('the ', 'id')`, `UPPER(…)`); one with a subquery or a function the reference bars (`REPEAT`, …) is **400**. A script with a column list in a dry run is put in the text it amounts to, each query's columns read with a dry run of it alone, and given to the emulator's dry run as a script without a list is: it is answered as that script would be, and nothing is made; a list of another length is **400** `invalidQuery` (read through `Query.DryRun`). An `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` whose text is a `CREATE VIEW` with a column list, in a script with a `TEMP` table, is put in the script's text and carried out as above: read back, the listed names, a listed column's description, and the script's last statement reading the view with the `TEMP` table, through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`. No upstream issue found. The front keeps the client's text of each view a query makes, with the emulator's, and `tables.get` answers with the client's while the emulator's is unchanged (a view replaced or dropped since, by any means, reads as the emulator has it); `CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS` of an existing view keeps the old text. The texts are in the front's memory (the last 1,000): after the front restarts, such a view reads back rewritten again. `tables.list` gives no view's query, as in BigQuery. | `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` of an existing table | **Verified** for a statement on its own, and (#1459) inside a script of several statements, which the front then carries out a statement at a time, each a child job (row `Statements beside a TEMP table`) | `TestBigQueryExceptionHandlersRaiseAndCreateOrReplace` (#918), `TestBigQueryStatementsLaterInAScript` (#1459), official Go client, through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`. The emulator failed it with 400 "duplicate: table … is already created" and kept the old table (measured); on a table that does not exist it creates it. The front carries it out: it runs the statement into a scratch table first (in `_cloudburrow_query_results`, deleted later, since #1057), and **if that fails the answer is its error and the table is kept** (a replacement from a missing table left the table as it was); then it deletes the table, sends the statement with its query replaced by `SELECT * FROM` the scratch table, and deletes the scratch table. So a query that reads the table itself works (`CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t AS SELECT a + 10 AS a FROM t` read back 21 and 22, twice), a column list replaces the schema, and no other table is left in the dataset. The job the emulator records shows the rewritten query; `jobs.insert`'s answer and `jobs.get` show the client's (#939). Inside a script of several statements an existing table was **501**, and since #1459 the statement is carried out in its turn (`TestBigQueryStatementsLaterInAScript`). `CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE` of a temp table the script made fails in the emulator and was 501 (#936); since #1459 it runs (`TestBigQueryReplacingATempTableIs501`, which now expects it to, and `TestBigQueryStatementsInTempScripts`). The table is deleted even when the new schema is the old one (#1092, closed): an unchanged-schema `DELETE` and `INSERT` would spare the engine's catalog rebuild, but BigQuery's documentation does not say whether the replaced table keeps its creation time, description, labels or expiration when the statement's `OPTIONS` do not set them: `OR REPLACE` "Replaces any table with the same name if it exists", and the example says a table that exists "is overwritten with an empty table" ([CREATE TABLE](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language#create_table_statement)); a replaced table's row access policies and policy tags are dropped ([row-level-security-intro](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/row-level-security-intro), [column-level-security-intro](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/column-level-security-intro)), where `TRUNCATE TABLE` keeps them, so a replacement is not a truncation; and the previous contents stay readable through time travel ([time-travel](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/time-travel)). Unit `TestCreateOrReplaceExistingTable`. |

BigQuery: "If any table exists with the same name, the `CREATE` statement has no effect", and the same for a view ([DDL](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-definition-language)). The emulator failed every form on an existing table or view (measured): 400 "SQL logic error: table … already exists" for `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS … AS SELECT`, and 400 "table is already created" for one with a column list, for `CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS`, and for either on a name the other kind holds; a script with one failed as a whole. So the statement succeeds and the table or view keeps its schema and rows (`t` and `v` still read `[[1]]`), a script with one runs its later statements, and one that does not exist is created. The job the emulator records shows that `DROP` as its query, as for `CREATE OR REPLACE` (#939). After a `DROP` of the same table or its dataset earlier in the script the statement is sent as it is: the emulator creates the table if the `DROP` removed it, and fails the script if not. **Not covered:** a `TEMP` table, which cannot be looked up from outside its script. `CREATE SCHEMA` of an existing dataset is the next row (#946). Measured first: the emulator ran it as done, through both, and made **no dataset**: `datasets.get` of it answered 404 and a `CREATE TABLE` in it failed "dataset … is not found"; its `datasets.insert` does make one and keeps a `description`, `friendlyName`, `labels` and `location`. In a script, `CREATE SCHEMA d; CREATE TABLE d.t …; INSERT …` runs and the table holds the row, and so does one that starts `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS d CASCADE` of a dataset that is not there (sent as a statement that does nothing); a script with a `TEMP` table or function that fails leaves no dataset (the front deletes it, as the emulator keeps nothing of a failed script); since #1459 one with none is carried out a statement at a time and keeps the dataset its `CREATE SCHEMA` made before the failing statement, as BigQuery keeps what the statements before it did (`TestBigQueryCreateSchemaMakesTheDataset`, read back). A new table in a dataset with a default collation, made by `tables.insert` or a lone `CREATE TABLE`, takes it as its `defaultCollation` unless it names one, and its top-level STRING columns take the table's unless they name one, as the [collation concepts](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/collation-concepts) describe (since #1508 a `CREATE TABLE` gets the dataset's as its own `DEFAULT COLLATE` before it runs, and the engine compares the columns by it: see the collation row below); `INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS.collation_name` reads `und:ci` for them. Units `TestCreateSchemaMakesTheDataset`, `TestCreateSchemaNotCarriedOut`, `TestCreateSchemaUndoneWhenTheQueryFails`. |
