Measured first (#1201): the emulator answered `CREATE PROCEDURE` in a dataset that does not exist done, and a `CALL` of a procedure that inserts a row done with no rows and inserted none; its `routines.get` knows no procedure. So the front keeps procedures itself (`internal/bigqueryfront/procedures.go`), beside the functions in its state file, so they survive a restart of its container (unit `TestProceduresOutliveAFrontRestart`; the emulator's restart empties them, as its datasets go), and runs each script with a procedure statement through its interpreter (row above). `CREATE PROCEDURE` needs the dataset (404 `notFound`) and fails 409 `duplicate` for a routine that exists unless `OR REPLACE` or `IF NOT EXISTS`; `DROP PROCEDURE` of none is 404 unless `IF EXISTS`; `DROP SCHEMA` (`RESTRICT`) of a dataset holding one fails `resourceInUse` and `CASCADE` drops it. `CALL` runs the body with the arguments bound in a scope of its own: an `IN` argument is the caller's expression cast to its type, `OUT` and `INOUT` ones must be the caller's variables and are written back when the procedure ends or `RETURN`s; the procedure sees none of its caller's variables; its last statement's rows are the script's answer when it is last. "The maximum depth of procedure calls is 50 frames" ([procedural language](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/procedural-language)): a deeper `CALL` fails, and a handler catches it. An error in a procedure reaches the caller's `EXCEPTION` handler with `@@error.stack_trace` holding the procedure's frame first (`location` `project.dataset.procedure:line:column`, `filename` NULL) and `@@error.formatted_stack_trace` `At project.dataset.procedure[line:column]` then `At [line:column]`, the reference's forms. Read back: two `CALL`s of a procedure that inserts a row made two rows; `OUT`/`INOUT` values, a `RETURN` part way, a deeper call caught; `routines.list` and `routines.get` show `PROCEDURE`, `SQL`, arguments with mode and type, the description and the `BEGIN … END` body; `routines.delete` and `DROP PROCEDURE` drop it. **Not checked against BigQuery:** the line and column inside a procedure (counted here from its `BEGIN`), and the error messages for an unknown procedure, a wrong argument count, an `OUT` argument that is not a variable and the depth limit. The console's Routines section and routine page show procedures (`TestBigQueryRoutinesSectionAndPage`). Units `TestProcedureParse`, `TestProcedureStackTrace`. |
| Multi-statement transactions: `BEGIN TRANSACTION`, `COMMIT TRANSACTION`, `ROLLBACK TRANSACTION` in a script | **Verified** (#1201) in any script, through `jobs.query` and query jobs, for a transaction whose statements are queries, DML (`SELECT`, `INSERT`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `MERGE`, `TRUNCATE TABLE`), `CREATE TEMP TABLE` and `DROP TABLE` of a `TEMP` table it made, with `DECLARE`, `SET`, control-flow blocks, `BEGIN … EXCEPTION` blocks, `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE` and `CALL` of a procedure inside it, its `BEGIN` and its `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` in any blocks: a statement sees the transaction's earlier writes, `COMMIT` keeps them, `ROLLBACK`, an error with no handler and the end of the query before `COMMIT` discard them, an error goes to an `EXCEPTION` handler with the transaction still open, where `COMMIT` keeps what its statements before the error did and `ROLLBACK` discards it, an error handled inside the transaction leaves it going on, and a nested `BEGIN TRANSACTION` fails the query. BigQuery's own example on the transactions page (a `TEMP` table, `DELETE`, `MERGE` from the `TEMP` table, `DROP TABLE`, `COMMIT`, a handler that rolls back) runs, both ways. **Not implemented** (501): DDL other than the above, a `TEMP` function, and `CREATE` or `DROP PROCEDURE` inside a transaction, and a transaction inside a procedure (nothing run); and, when they run, an expression the script evaluates (a `DECLARE`'s `DEFAULT`, a `SET`, a condition, a `FOR`'s query, `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE … INTO`) that reads a table after the transaction changed data or made a `TEMP` table, a statement after the transaction that names a `TEMP` table it made and did not drop, a statement inside it that names a `TEMP` table it dropped, a `CREATE TEMP TABLE` of a name made before, a transaction statement run by `EXECUTE IMMEDIATE`, and a `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` with no transaction open (undocumented) | `TestBigQueryScriptTransactions` and `TestBigQueryScriptTransactionsMore`, official Go client, through `jobs.query` (`Query.Read`) and `jobs.insert` (`Query.Run`), on one instance with `--services bigquery,storage`. BigQuery: [multi-statement transactions](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/transactions). Measured first against the pinned emulator: it treats `BEGIN TRANSACTION` and `COMMIT TRANSACTION` as statements that do nothing, refuses `ROLLBACK TRANSACTION` ("Statement not supported: RollbackStatement"), and reads the rows of a script's last statement only: `BEGIN TRANSACTION; INSERT …; SELECT 1/0; COMMIT TRANSACTION` succeeded and kept the row. Through `jobs.query` it runs a request in one SQLite transaction, rolled back whole when the request fails (#935); a `TEMP` table lasts for its request, and it cannot drop one inside a script (#936). So the front keeps the transaction itself (`internal/bigqueryfront/transactions.go`), from the `BEGIN TRANSACTION` the script runs to the `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` it runs, while its interpreter carries out variables and blocks as elsewhere: each statement that changes data, makes a `TEMP` table or reads a table is first run as a probe, a request of the transaction's earlier such statements, the statement (a query as a scalar subquery reading every column of every row) and a statement that fails, so the emulator rolls it all back; a probe that fails with another error is the statement's failure. `DROP TABLE` of its `TEMP` table is kept by the front alone. At `COMMIT` the kept statements are sent as one request, which the emulator applies atomically, all or none; at `ROLLBACK` nothing is sent. The rows of a query inside the transaction that reads a table are not the script's answer. Not as in BigQuery: the DML is applied at `COMMIT` against the tables as they are then, a serial order of the transaction among other requests; BigQuery reads a snapshot from the transaction's first statement and cancels a conflicting transaction. An error's position (`[at line:column]`) in the emulator's message points into the front's request. |
| Loads with `autodetect` and no schema | **Verified** for CSV and for `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` (#1324); **Not implemented** (501) for a JSON column whose values mix types BigQuery does not document detecting, and for `columnNameCharacterMap` `V1` or `V2` when a detected name cannot be renamed by replacing characters (a `V1` name that starts with a digit, a reserved or too long name, two names the same once replaced); a Parquet name refused only for a period the map keeps is 400 (#1547: "Periods are not replaced by underscores in Parquet file column names when a column name character map is used", [Specifying a schema](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/schemas), and a period is not a column name's character; UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/schemas>) that the load then fails, `TestBigQueryParquetColumnNameCharacterMap`); a load of another format under any map is 400 (#1336) | `TestBigQueryAutodetectLoadNames` (#901), `TestBigQueryColumnNameCharacterMap` (#1326), `TestBigQueryColumnNameCharacterMapFormats` (#1336), `TestBigQueryParquetColumnNameCharacterMap` (#1373), official Go client, a load from a local file. The emulator names the columns of a CSV from its first row whatever they hold: a header `a b!,c` made a column `a b!` (measured). BigQuery's rule is the load's `columnNameCharacterMap`: `STRICT`, the default, "reject[s] invalid column names"; `V1` and `V2` normalize them ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)). The front does not read the data, so it checks the table the load made, after the emulator ran it: under `STRICT` a name the column rules refuse **fails the job as BigQuery fails it**: the job is `DONE` with an `invalid` `errorResult`, which `Job.Wait`'s status and a later `jobs.get` (`Job.Status`) report, and the table is deleted, as BigQuery creates a load's table only when it succeeds. Under `V1` (the classic rule) or `V2`, whose renaming the emulator ignores (measured: `a!` kept under `V2`), the front **renames the detected columns** (#1326), as BigQuery does: unsupported characters "are replaced with underscores" ([load statements, `column_name_character_map`](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/load-statements)), so each character the map's rule does not take (letters, digits and `_` for `V1`; the flexible rule's for `V2`) becomes `_`, and the table is made again with the new names, its rows copied through a scratch table. Read back through the Go client (`Loader.ColumnNameCharacterMap`, a CSV load from a local file): under `V2` a header `first name,a!,n` gives `first name`, `a_`, `n`, under `V1` `first_name`, `a_`, `n`; the types are kept, `jobs.get` reports the job done, and the rows read back by the new names through a query and `tabledata.list`. A name still refused once replaced (`1a` under `V1`, whose rule for a leading digit BigQuery does not document: "Invalid column names will be normalized"), and two names the same once replaced (`a!`, `a?`), stay **501** and the table is deleted (unit `TestColumnNameCharacterMap`). Since #1336 (`TestBigQueryColumnNameCharacterMapFormats`, official Go client, uploads): the map is refused for a format other than CSV and Parquet, as BigQuery documents ("Character map supported for column names in CSV/Parquet loads ... Using this option with unsupporting load formats will result in an error", [JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)): a `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` load that gives `V1`, `V2` or `STRICT` is 400 `invalid` (wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job>)) and nothing is loaded; and a Parquet file's column names are held to it: a name the rules refuse (`!`) is 400 `invalid` under `STRICT` or no map ("Load jobs with unsupported characters in column names fail with an error message"), and under `V1` or `V2` is renamed (`_`); a name the rules take loads under any map (unit `TestCharMapFormat`, `TestParquetCharMapNames`). Since #1373 (`TestBigQueryParquetColumnNameCharacterMap`, official Go client, an upload of a file written by Arrow's Go Parquet writer) a Parquet load under `V1` or `V2` **renames the file's columns** as the documentation says, unsupported characters "(except periods in Parquet file column names) are replaced with underscores", at every depth: the front renames each name as it reads the file's schema and carries the load out itself, each value going to its renamed column. Columns `first name`, `a!` and a RECORD `rec?` with a field `in ner!` read back through `Table.Metadata` as `first_name`, `a_`, `rec_` and `in_ner_` under `V1`, and `first name`, `a_`, `rec_` and `in ner_` under `V2`, the types kept, `jobs.get` reporting the job done, and the rows read back by the new names through a query and `tabledata.list`. As for a CSV, names the same once replaced (`a!`, `a?`) and a name still refused once replaced (`x.y`, its period kept, which no rule takes; `1a` under `V1`) stay **501**, with no table (unit `TestParquetNamesUnderCharMap`). A RECORD's field with a flexible name made no table in the emulator, which wrote it unquoted in its engine's `CREATE TABLE` (measured: "Syntax error: Expected \">\" but got keyword IN"); engine patch bigquery-emulator 0019 quotes it. A header BigQuery takes, `first name,n`, loads its row. A `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` load with `autodetect` into a new table, which the emulator answers 500 "nil pointer dereference" (measured), has its schema **detected by the front** as [schema auto-detection](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/schema-detect) documents it (#1324, `TestBigQueryJSONAutodetectLoad`, official Go client, from a local file and from Cloud Storage, the schema read back with `Table.Metadata` and the rows with a query): from the first 500 records of the first file, a JSON boolean is `BOOLEAN`, an integer `INTEGER`, another number `FLOAT`, and a string `BOOLEAN`, `INTEGER`, `FLOAT`, `DATE`, `TIME` or `TIMESTAMP` when it holds one ("BigQuery converts strings into Boolean, numeric, or date/time types when possible"), `STRING` otherwise; an object a `RECORD`, an array a `REPEATED` column, every other column `NULLABLE`, and a column only ever null `STRING`. `INTEGER` with `FLOAT` is `FLOAT`, and strings of which some hold no other type `STRING`; any other mix, an array of arrays, an object only ever empty, an integer outside INT64 and a date or time in a form other than `YYYY-MM-DD`, `HH:MM:SS[.SSSSSS]` and `YYYY-MM-DD[ T]HH:MM[:SS[.SSSSSS]]` with an optional offset, `Z` or `UTC` are **501**. The detected names are held to `columnNameCharacterMap` as a CSV's are (a refused name under `STRICT` is 400 `invalid`, with no table). The load is then sent with the detected schema; a detected `TIMESTAMP` value is written in RFC 3339 UTC, the one form the emulator reads in every case (measured: it failed `2020-01-02T03:04Z`). A field first seen after the sample is outside the detected schema, which is the load's schema, so its record is bad unless `ignoreUnknownValues` is set, as the JSON loads row below says (#1339, `TestBigQueryLoadFieldsOutsideTheSchema`: a field first seen in record 501 fails the load, and loads under `ignoreUnknownValues` with the schema of the first 500) (unit `TestDetectJSONSchema`). A load into an existing table keeps that table's schema (measured) and is not checked; with no `skipLeadingRows` it is **501** (#945, the CSV loads row below) (unit `TestAutodetectedNamesAreHeldToTheCharacterMap`). The header, a resumable upload, a load from Cloud Storage and `jobs.list` are in the next rows (#919). Since #1547 (`TestBigQueryAutodetectDialect`, official Go client, uploads): a CSV with `autodetect` is detected from data read by its own `quote`, `fieldDelimiter` and `encoding` as the load reads it (a `'` quote, ISO-8859-1 with `;`, UTF-16LE with a byte-order mark, UTF-32BE), the names and types read back with `Table.Metadata` and the rows with a query; and a header the front detects (`skipLeadingRows` 2) is renamed under `V1` / `V2` as above (`first name,a!` gives `first_name`, `a_` under `V1`, `first name`, `a_` under `V2`), while `1a` under `V1` stays **501** with no table (unit `TestDetectCSVDialect`). The console's load forms send `columnNameCharacterMap` (unit `TestBigQueryLoadFormCharacterMap`). |
| CSV header detection with `autodetect` | **Verified** for a header BigQuery detects, one it does not, and `skipLeadingRows` unset, 1 or N (#1457); **Not implemented** (501) for a sample the front cannot read (below) | `TestBigQueryCSVAutodetectHeaderRows` (#1457) and `TestBigQueryAutodetectHeaderAndResumableLoads` (#919), official Go client. **Since #1457** a load with `autodetect`, no schema and a new table whose header BigQuery would not detect, or with a `skipLeadingRows` other than 1, has its schema detected by the front, as BigQuery documents it: "skipLeadingRows unspecified - Autodetect tries to detect headers in the first row. If they are not detected, the row is read as data ... skipLeadingRows is 0 - Instructs autodetect that there are no headers ... skipLeadingRows = N > 0 - Autodetect skips N-1 rows and tries to detect headers in row N. If headers are not detected, row N is just skipped" ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)); a header is not detected when "all of the data fields are strings", and then BigQuery "assigns generic column names such as `string_field_1`" ([schema detection](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/schema-detect#csv_header)). The columns are then named `<type>_field_<position from 0>`, the type as GoogleSQL names it in lower case (`string`, `int64`, `double`, `bool`, `date`, `time`, `datetime`, `timestamp`; only `string_field_` is documented, the others UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/schema-detect>)), the types detected from the first 500 records as for the formats row below, and the load sent with that schema. Read back with `Table.Metadata` and a query: `a,b / x,y` loads both rows into `string_field_0`, `string_field_1`; `1,x / 2,y` into `int64_field_0`, `string_field_1`; with `skipLeadingRows` 3, `title / note / name,n / bob,3` makes `name STRING, n INTEGER` and loads `bob,3`; with 2, `junk / 1,x / 2,y` skips row 2, which is no header, and loads `2,y`; with 1, `a,b / x,y` loads `x,y` into generic columns. 0, which the Go client cannot send, unit only (`TestDetectCSVHeader`). A header both read the same way is still the emulator's, as below. **501**: records of different widths, a mix of types BigQuery does not document, a delimiter of more than one character, a `quote` or an `encoding` of its own, and a load from Cloud Storage with no Cloud Storage for the front to read the sample from (#944). Before #1457: The emulator takes a CSV's first row as the header whatever it holds (measured: `a,b / c,d` gave columns `a` and `b`, `1,2 / 3,4` columns `1` and `2`) and ignores `skipLeadingRows`. BigQuery takes the first row as the header only "if the first line contains only strings, and the other lines contain other data types" ([schema detection](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/schema-detect#csv_header)); otherwise it loads it as data. The front still reads both halves of that rule from the table the load made when it did not detect the schema itself (the first row is the column names; the other rows' types are the columns'), and a load BigQuery would read otherwise is then **501**, the table deleted (a sample it could not read, above). `first name,n / bob,3` loads its row. Until #1457 every such load, and `skipLeadingRows` other than 1, was 501. Units `TestCSVHeaderDetection`, `TestDetectCSVHeader`. |
| Loads with no `sourceFormat` | **Verified** as CSV | Every load in `TestBigQueryAutodetectHeaderAndResumableLoads` sets none, as the Go client sends none for CSV unless told. BigQuery's default is CSV; the emulator has none (measured: 400 "not support sourceFormat: " with a schema, and 500 "nil pointer dereference" with `autodetect`, which the Go client retries until its deadline). The front sets `sourceFormat` `CSV` in the job, in `jobs.insert`'s body or a multipart upload's first part, whose data is sent as it came (unit `TestLoadWithoutSourceFormatIsCSV`). |
| CSV loads with a schema, or into an existing table | **Verified** for a load from the client (multipart and resumable uploads) and from Cloud Storage (#944) | `TestBigQueryCSVLoadWithSchemaLoadsEveryRow` (#931) and `TestBigQueryCSVLoadFromCloudStorage` (#944), official Go client. BigQuery reads every row as data unless told otherwise: `skipLeadingRows` "The default value is 0" ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)), and each value goes to the column at its position. The emulator ignores `skipLeadingRows` and always takes the first row as a header (measured, and in its source): a file of three rows with a schema and no header **loaded two, the first lost with no error**, and a file of one row loaded none; `skipLeadingRows` 2 failed the load; and a first row whose values are the columns' names maps the columns by name. The front drops the rows BigQuery skips and puts a header of its own before the rest, the columns' names in order (the load's schema, or the table's when the load gives none), which the emulator takes as the header; the data is streamed, not held in memory. So three rows load three, one loads one, `skipLeadingRows` 1 skips a header `b,a` and still loads by position, `skipLeadingRows` 2 skips a title and a quoted value over two lines, a load into an existing table with no load schema loads every row, and a resumable upload of over 768 KiB loads every row, its first included. **From Cloud Storage (#944):** the emulator reads a `gs://` load's objects itself, so the front reads them instead, from the instance's own Cloud Storage (the in-cluster server the front is started with, `--storage`, never `storage.googleapis.com`), and sends them to the emulator as a multipart upload of the same job without its `sourceUris`, through the same path: each file's leading rows are skipped, the files are loaded as one job in the order of their URIs, and a URI with one `*` wildcard reads every object it matches, in name order, as the emulator's own reader does. So a file of three rows and no header loads three, `skipLeadingRows` 1 skips a header `b,a` and loads by position, `parts/*.csv` with a header in each loads every data row of the two `.csv` objects and not the `.txt`, and two URIs into an existing table load six rows. An object that does not exist, a bucket that does not, or a wildcard that matches nothing is **404 `notFound`** from `jobs.insert` and makes no table (BigQuery fails the job "Not found: URI" instead); so is Cloud Storage that does not answer. With `autodetect` and columns given, `skipLeadingRows` says how many rows are not data (BigQuery: "0 - … no headers", "N > 0 - Autodetect skips N-1 rows and tries to detect headers in row N"); unset, BigQuery decides from the data whether the first row is a header, which the emulator always drops (measured), so that is **501** (the Go client cannot send 0). A load with `autodetect` and no columns, into a new table, keeps its header for the emulator, and a later file's first row is dropped. Unit `TestCSVLoadWithColumnsLoadsEveryRow`, `TestCSVLoadFromCloudStorage`, `TestCSVLoadFromCloudStorageIsRead`, `TestSkipRecords`. |
| CSV loads: `fieldDelimiter`, `quote`, `allowJaggedRows`, `nullMarker` | **Verified** for a one-character ASCII delimiter or quote (or none), any one ISO-8859-1 character in ISO-8859-1 data, a quote of several characters (its first byte), a delimiter of several characters (its first byte), a delimiter or quote outside ASCII in UTF-8 data, and an empty value with a `nullMarker` in a `STRING` column (#1457); **Not implemented** (501) for a quote outside ISO-8859-1, and a delimiter of several bytes or outside ASCII in UTF-16 or UTF-32 data | `TestBigQueryCSVDelimiterAndQuoteBytes` (#1457), official Go client (`ReaderSource.Encoding` `ISO_8859_1`, `FieldDelimiter` `þ`, `Quote` `«`, and `Quote` `'x`): BigQuery's `fieldDelimiter` "is interpreted as a single byte. For files encoded in ISO-8859-1, any single character can be used as a separator", and its `quote` is converted "to ISO-8859-1 encoding, and then [BigQuery] uses the first byte of the encoded string to split the data in its raw, binary state"; "BigQuery decodes the data after the raw, binary data has been split" ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)). So the front splits ISO-8859-1 data on those bytes and decodes each value after: `1þ«caféþx«` / `2þé` reads back `1, caféþx` and `2, é`, and `1,'a,b'` with quote `'x` reads back `1, a,b`. **Since #1457's second part** (`TestBigQueryCSVDelimiterAndQuoteBytes`, `FieldDelimiter` `||`, `þ` and `Quote` `«` in UTF-8 data; `TestBigQueryCSVEmptyStringWithNullMarker`): the two pages disagree on a delimiter outside ASCII in UTF-8 data (the CSV loading page: BigQuery "will interpret it correctly"), and the front follows the API reference, `fieldDelimiter`: "The separator is interpreted as a single byte. ... UTF-8 characters encoded with multiple bytes (i.e. U+0080 and above) will have only the first byte used for separating fields. The remaining bytes will be treated as a part of the field", which the CSV page's own "if you use a multibyte character as a delimiter, some of the bytes will be interpreted incorrectly as part of the field value" agrees with. So a delimiter is one byte: of several characters (`||`), its first; in UTF-8 data, the first byte of its UTF-8 form, a value left with bytes that are not UTF-8 having each read as U+FFFD, as "If BigQuery can't convert a character other than the ASCII 0 character, BigQuery converts the character to the standard Unicode replacement character" (`encoding`): `1þx` with `þ` reads back `1, �x`. A quote is its ISO-8859-1 byte in UTF-8 data too: `1,«x,y«` written with the raw byte 0xAB reads back `1, x,y`. An empty value under a `nullMarker` loads into a `STRING` or `BYTES` column as an empty string (the front sends it as a mark the emulator's patch 0038 loads as one; a load whose data holds that mark is 501): `1,` / `2,\N` reads back `""` and NULL. **501**: a quote whose first character is outside ISO-8859-1 (the reference converts it to ISO-8859-1 and documents no character without a byte there), a delimiter outside ISO-8859-1 in ISO-8859-1 data, and a delimiter of several bytes or outside ASCII in UTF-16 or UTF-32 data, none of which the reference describes; with `autodetect` and no schema, a delimiter of several characters (the autodetect row). `TestBigQueryCSVLoadOptions` (#945), official Go client (`ReaderSource.FieldDelimiter`, `Quote`/`ForceZeroQuote`, `AllowJaggedRows`, `NullMarker`), from the client and from Cloud Storage. Measured first: the emulator reads a load's data with Go's `encoding/csv` defaults: a tab- or pipe-delimited file, a file quoted with `'` and a short row with `allowJaggedRows` failed 400 "wrong number of fields"; with `quote` `""` it loaded `"x"` as `x`; with `nullMarker` `\N` it loaded the text `\N`; it loads every empty value as NULL. The front reads the data by the load's options as it passes and writes it on as the CSV the emulator reads: a tab (`\t` too) or pipe delimiter, `'` quotes with `''` inside, no quoting, short rows filled with NULLs, and `\N` loaded as NULL all read back as BigQuery documents ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)); a short row without `allowJaggedRows` still fails. With a `nullMarker`, BigQuery loads an empty value into a `STRING` or `BYTES` column as an empty string (since #1457, above), and into another column refuses it: **400 `invalid`**; a quote that is not closed, or data after a closing quote, is 400 `invalid`. These fail the load while its data passes, before the emulator loads anything, and `jobs.get` reports the job failed (unit `TestCSVDialectFailureReadsBackFailed`). A delimiter or quote the front does not read (above) is **501** before anything is sent. **Not covered:** whether BigQuery reads a quoted `"\N"` as the marker (the front does not). The other CSV options are in the next row (#952). Unit `TestCSVDialect`. |
| `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` loads: a field outside the schema, `ignoreUnknownValues`, `maxBadRecords` | **Verified** (#1339), and, with `maxBadRecords`, a record whose value its column's type refuses as a bad record (#1457); a field outside the schema whose value is null under `ignoreUnknownValues` (#1457); **Not implemented** (501) for such a null field without `ignoreUnknownValues`, and for a load with `maxBadRecords` that the emulator still fails on a value the front passes | `TestBigQueryLoadFieldsOutsideTheSchema`, official Go client, a load from a local file and from Cloud Storage. BigQuery's `ignoreUnknownValues`: "If false, records with extra columns are treated as bad records, and if there are too many bad records, an invalid error is returned in the job result ... JSON: Named values that don't match any column names" ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)). The emulator drops such a field and loads the record (measured: `{"i":13,"zz":1}` loaded into a table without `zz`). So the front reads every JSON load whose columns it knows (the table's, the load's schema, which may add to them, or the one it detected) and holds each record to them, names matched without case, at any depth of a `RECORD` and in each element of a `REPEATED` one: a record with a field outside them **fails the load** (400 `invalid`, "No such field: zz" or "No such field: r.y", nothing loaded); with `ignoreUnknownValues` it loads without the field; with `maxBadRecords` 1 it is left out, listed in the job's `status.errors`, and the other records load. A null field outside the schema, at the top or in a `REPEATED` `RECORD`, loads without it under `ignoreUnknownValues` ("If true, the extra values are ignored", #1457, read back with a query, from a file and from Cloud Storage); without `ignoreUnknownValues` it is **501**, nothing loaded, as the reference does not say whether BigQuery counts a null as an extra value. With `maxBadRecords`, since #1457 (`TestBigQueryLoadBadValuesUnderMaxBadRecords`, official Go client, a CSV and a JSON upload, the rows read back with a query and the job's `status.errors` counted), a record is bad, left out and listed, when a top-level value is one its column's type refuses by the JSON loading page's "Data types": a BOOL other than "1 or 0, true or false, t or f, yes or no, or y or n (all case insensitive)" (each of which is written as a JSON boolean for the emulator, which reads fewer), a DATE not "in the format YYYY-MM-DD", a TIME not "HH:MM:SS[.SSSSSS]", a REPEATED field that is not an array or holds a null ("The array itself cannot contain null values"), an object or array for a column that is neither, or an INTEGER, FLOAT, NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC value that is no number; "Number of errors allowed" is "the maximum number of rows containing errors that can be ignored". A load the emulator still fails on a value the front passed (an INTEGER written as a fraction, a DATETIME or TIMESTAMP it does not read) is **501**, as for CSV: the record may be one BigQuery would leave out. A `JSON` column holds a field whose values mix types (#1457, `TestBigQueryJSONLoadMixedTypesIntoJSONColumn`, the JSON loading page's example: "address" a STRING, a STRUCT or an ARRAY "is loaded into a column with type JSON that allows it to hold the mixed types"): the front writes each such value as its JSON text, which the emulator reads (measured before: it read a string value as JSON text and failed `"123 First Avenue"`, 400); `JSON_TYPE` reads back `string`, `object`, `array` and `number` (unit `TestJSONColumnValues`). A CSV record with more values than columns follows the same rule (the CSV loads row below, `TestBigQueryLoadFieldsOutsideTheSchema` from a file and from Cloud Storage). A load from Cloud Storage with no Cloud Storage given to the front (`--storage`) is read by the emulator, which drops the field (unit `TestJSONLoadUnknownFields`). |

Measured first, with a header row the emulator takes as one: it loaded a quoted newline whatever `allowQuotedNewlines` said; under `encoding` ISO-8859-1 it stored the byte 0xE9 as U+FFFD; with `maxBadRecords` 1 it failed a load with one bad value (400 "strconv.ParseInt") or one row too wide (400 "wrong number of fields"), and failed the wide row the same way with `ignoreUnknownValues`; it loaded the values of `nullMarkers` as text; it stored `\x00` and `\x01` as they were whatever `preserveAsciiControlCharacters` said; it stored a TIMESTAMP with no zone as UTC whatever `timeZone` said, and failed a DATE in `dateFormat` `MM/DD/YYYY` (#1325 above); it stored NULL in a REQUIRED column given an empty value; it matched a header's names to the columns by name. The front reads each record by BigQuery's rules as the data passes ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)): a quoted newline loads with `allowQuotedNewlines` and is **400 `invalid`** without it; ISO-8859-1 data reads back as `café`; a record that is too short (without `allowJaggedRows`), too wide (without `ignoreUnknownValues`, which drops the trailing values) or leaves a REQUIRED column without a value is bad, up to `maxBadRecords` of them are left out and one more is **400 `invalid`**; each value of `nullMarkers` loads as NULL; a control character loads with `preserveAsciiControlCharacters`; with `sourceColumnMatch` `NAME` and `skipLeadingRows` 1, each value goes to the column its header names. BigQuery reads a Parquet file's schema from the file ("the table schema is automatically retrieved from the self-describing source data", [Parquet loads](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data-cloud-storage-parquet)). Measured first: the emulator reads a Parquet file's columns only from the job's schema and each row's values by those names, checking nothing (its source: `uploadContentHandler`, `load.Schema.Fields`): with no schema a load was 500 "nil pointer dereference"; given the table's, into `(a INT64)` a file `(a INT64, b STRING)` dropped `b`, into `(z STRING)` it loaded three rows of NULL, into `(a STRING, b STRING)` it loaded `a` as text, and a file's `A` and `B` loaded NULL into `a` and `b`; it loaded TIME(MILLIS) 01:02:03.004 as 00:12:06.004, TIME(MICROS) 01:02:03.004567 as 01:02:07.567, TIMESTAMP(MILLIS) in 2024 as January 1970, BYTES 0xFF as EF BF BD, and refused INT96 ("failed to convert … to time.Time"); against the image directly, given BigQuery's schema for each shape, a LIST read without list inference failed "failed to convert struct from string", with list inference a NULL list read back NULL and a NULL element was kept, and a MAP left the emulator hung, answering nothing until it was restarted. Its JSON load is no way round it: BYTES given as base64 loaded the base64 text (`/w==` read back `2f773d3d`). So the front reads the file's schema from its footer (`parquetfooter.go`) before anything is sent, and holds it to BigQuery's rules. A load the emulator carries out as BigQuery does (flat columns of BOOLEAN, INT32 with no annotation, INT(8, 16, 32, signed or not), DATE, INT64 with no annotation, TIMESTAMP(MICROS) and BYTE_ARRAY STRING, into a new table, appended by exact names, or replacing a table of the file's schema) is sent to it with the schema to read the file by. Any other is **the front's own job** (`parquetload.go`, as a copy job is): it reads the rows with Apache Arrow's Parquet reader for Go (`github.com/apache/arrow/go/v15/parquet/file`, already in the module graph through the BigQuery client; tested with uncompressed, SNAPPY and ZSTD files, dictionary pages, version 2 data pages and several row groups), puts nested rows back together from their definition and repetition levels, writes each as a GoogleSQL literal of the table's row type, and inserts them with DML into a scratch table and then the table (measured: the emulator stores DML values of every type here exactly, RECORD inside REPEATED RECORD included); the job reports `inputFiles`, `inputFileBytes`, `outputRows` and `badRecords` 0, and `jobs.get` reads it back with the client's configuration (the source format PARQUET). **Types** by the page's "Type conversions" table, each read back as written with a row of NULLs: BOOLEAN; INT32 with no annotation, INT(8, 16, 32, signed or not) and DATE; INT64 with no annotation and TIMESTAMP(MICROS); FLOAT and DOUBLE (FLOAT64, ±Inf); BYTE_ARRAY STRING (`é☃` included); converted by the front: TIME(MILLIS), TIME(MICROS), TIMESTAMP(MILLIS), INT96 (nanoseconds of the day and Julian day), BYTE_ARRAY and FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY BYTES, unsigned INT64 up to 9,223,372,036,854,775,807 (above it the job fails `invalid`, as the page says), DECIMAL as INT32, INT64, FIXED_LEN_BYTE_ARRAY and 256-bit into NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC by `decimalTargetTypes` ("In the order of NUMERIC, BIGNUMERIC, and STRING, a type is picked if it is in the specified list and if it supports the precision and the scale", default `["NUMERIC"]`; a value beyond the widest type's range fails the job `invalid`), and ENUM as BYTES or, with `enumAsString`, STRING. **Nested and repeated**: "Nested groups are converted into STRUCT types", so a group is a RECORD and, without list inference, a LIST or MAP a RECORD holding a REPEATED RECORD (`l RECORD (list REPEATED RECORD (element))`, `m RECORD (key_value REPEATED RECORD (key, value))`); with `parquetOptions.enableListInference` a LIST in the standard form is `repeated <element-type>`, a NULL list read back empty, and so is one in Parquet's backward-compatible forms (a repeated primitive, a repeated group of several fields or named `array` or `<name>_tuple`, pyarrow's `item`; #1069, unit `TestParquetListElement` only, not yet run against files from those writers); with `mapTargetType` `ARRAY_OF_STRUCT` a MAP is a REPEATED RECORD of key and value. **Into a new table** the table takes the file's schema, a REQUIRED column REQUIRED. **Appending**, columns match by name without regard to case at every depth ("Column names from Parquet files are treated as case-insensitive"), and a table column the file lacks is left NULL (as [LOAD DATA](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/load-statements) documents for a self-describing file; not measured against BigQuery). **Schema changes** ([Modifying table schemas](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas)): `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION` adds the file's new NULLABLE columns at the end, and a field it adds inside a RECORD (REPEATED included) at the end of that RECORD ("New columns and nested fields are always added at the end of the table or field"; #1068, unit `TestParquetAddsNestedFields` only, not yet run against an instance), NULL in the table's rows; the emulator adds no engine column through `tables.patch` (#1010) or `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` (measured: success, then "Column c is not present"), so the table is made again with the new schema, keeping its description, labels, partitioning and clustering (its creation time is new); `ALLOW_FIELD_RELAXATION` sets the column NULLABLE (`tables.patch`: the engine does not hold a REQUIRED column to it, measured); `WRITE_TRUNCATE` with a file whose schema is not the table's makes the table again with the file's schema ("overwrites the data, removes the constraints and uses the schema from the load job"); `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` keeps the table's schema and replaces its rows. The rows go to a scratch table first (in `_cloudburrow_query_results`, deleted later while the instance is idle, #1091, as the front's other scratch tables, #1057), so a load that fails leaves the table as it was, or, if it fails after the table was made again, names the scratch table holding the rows. **400** `invalid`, nothing loaded and the table unchanged: a file column the table lacks ("Cannot add fields", at any depth), a column of another type ("has changed type"), a NULLABLE file column into a REQUIRED one without `ALLOW_FIELD_RELAXATION` ("has changed mode"), a REQUIRED table column the file lacks, data that is not a Parquet file, files of one load from Cloud Storage whose columns differ only in mode, an unknown `writeDisposition` or `mapTargetType`. The messages follow BigQuery's form but were not measured against it. **400** `invalid`, nothing loaded, since #1457: a column type the page's table does not list (TIMESTAMP(NANOS), TIME(NANOS), JSON, UUID and any other), as "Other combinations of Parquet types and converted types are not supported" (`TestBigQueryParquetLoadNaNAndUnlistedTypes`, `TestBigQueryParquetLoadColumns`, `TestBigQueryParquetLoadTypes`; wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/loading-data-cloud-storage-parquet>)). A NaN loads since #1457, written as `IEEE_DIVIDE(0, 0)`, which the engine CloudBurrow builds keeps (googlesqlite 0004, #1066): read back NaN, `IS_NAN` true (`TestBigQueryParquetLoadNaNAndUnlistedTypes`). **501** `notImplemented`, nothing loaded: an INT96 with a part of a microsecond, and a DECIMAL that NUMERIC or BIGNUMERIC would have to round (the page does not say whether BigQuery truncates or rounds); DECIMAL to STRING (the page does not say how it is written); a STRING or ENUM-as-STRING value that is not UTF-8; with list inference a NULL element, a LIST of lists, and a LIST in neither the standard form nor a backward-compatible one; `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION` of a REQUIRED column ("allow adding a nullable field"); a STRING column into GEOGRAPHY; a file whose schema is not its `referenceFileSchemaUri`'s (the row below); files of one load whose schemas differ otherwise (BigQuery takes the alphabetically last file's); another project's table; a view; a job schema that is not the file's; a dry run of a load the front carries out. Units `TestParquetFooterSchema`, `TestParquetFooterRefusesOtherData`, `FuzzParquetFooter`, `TestParquetLoadColumns`, `TestParquetUploadIsSentWhole`, `TestParquetLoadFromCloudStorage`, `TestParquetLoadsTheFrontCarriesOut`, `TestParquetLoadValuesRefused`, `TestParquetLoadFailuresLeaveTheTable`, `TestParquetLoadFromCloudStorageTheFrontCarriesOut`, `TestParquetLiterals`. |
| Avro and Parquet loads: `referenceFileSchemaUri` (#1457) | **Verified** for data files whose schema is the reference file's, from Cloud Storage (two URIs, a wildcard, the reference among the source URIs or not); **404** `notFound` for a reference file that does not exist; **Not implemented** (501) for a data file whose schema differs from the reference file's, a reference URI with a wildcard, and with no Cloud Storage given to the front | `TestBigQueryLoadReferenceFileSchema` (#1457), official Go client (`GCSReference` with `SourceFormat` Avro and Parquet, `LoadConfig.ReferenceFileSchemaURI`), the fixtures written in the test by goavro and Arrow's Parquet writer to the instance's Cloud Storage, the table's schema read with `Table.Metadata` and its rows with a query. BigQuery: "The user can provide a reference file with the reader schema. This file is only loaded if it is part of source URIs, but is not loaded otherwise" ([JobConfigurationLoad](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationLoad)); the Avro and Parquet loading pages: "To provide a table schema ... set the `referenceFileSchemaUri` property ... to the URL of the reference file". So the table takes the reference file's schema, by the same conversions as a data file's, and the reference file's rows load only when a source URI names it. Read back: a load of two data files holds their rows, not the reference file's; one whose source URIs name the reference file holds its row too. A data file whose schema is not the reference file's is 501: BigQuery reads it by the reference as its reader schema, and does not document how a file's columns are resolved to another schema's; nothing is loaded and no table is made. Measured first: each load was 501 ("referenceFileSchemaUri, which CloudBurrow does not read"). |
| `BYTES` values written by a JSON load, a CSV load and a streamed row (`tabledata.insertAll`) | **Verified**, any bytes, at the top level, in a `RECORD` and in a `REPEATED` column, from an upload and from Cloud Storage | `TestBigQueryBytesValuesAreWrittenAsTheirBytes` (#1065, #1075), official Go client (`ReaderSource`, `GCSReference`, `Inserter.Put` of a `[]byte`). BigQuery reads a JSON, CSV or streamed `BYTES` value as base64. Measured first through the front, on the pinned emulator: `/w==` (0xff) loaded by `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` and by CSV, and `[]byte{0xff}` put with `Inserter.Put`, each read back `TO_HEX` `2f773d3d`, the base64 text, with no error: the emulator bound each value to its engine as the string it read (`AddTableData`), and the engine stores a string as its bytes. #1074 had the front send the decoded bytes as a string, which could carry only UTF-8 text (501 for the rest). The emulator CloudBurrow builds decodes the base64 itself (#1061, bigquery-emulator patch 0001, which also hands a JSON load's nested fields to it), so every value reads back as its bytes: `YQBi`, `4piD`, `YWJj`, `DQo=`, `AA==` and `/w==` read back `610062`, `e29883`, `616263`, `0d0a`, `00` and `ff`, at the top level, in a `RECORD` and in a `REPEATED` column, by a JSON upload and load from Cloud Storage, a CSV upload (a carriage return included) and load from Cloud Storage, and `Inserter.Put` (`a\x00b`, `0xff`). The front still reads the records of a JSON or CSV load into a `BYTES` column, and a streamed row, to refuse a value that is not base64 as BigQuery does and to send one in the URL-safe alphabet, which BigQuery reads too, in the standard one the emulator decodes; a JSON load from Cloud Storage is read by it and sent as one upload when it has Cloud Storage, and sent on as it came when it has none. **400** `invalid`: a JSON value that is not base64 (nothing is loaded), and a line of a JSON load that is not one JSON object; a streamed value that is not base64 makes its row invalid. Units `TestJSONLoadChecksBytes`, `TestJSONLoadRefusesWhatItCannotWrite`, `TestJSONLoadFromCloudStorageIsRead`, `TestCSVLoadChecksBytes`, `TestInsertAllChecksBytes`, and the patch's `TestDecodeBytesValues`. |
| `FLOAT64` NaN, ±Infinity and -0 | **Verified** for NaN, written by every path and computed, and for ±Infinity; **Not supported** for -0 | `TestBigQueryNaNIsWrittenAndReadBack` (#1066), official Go client (`ReaderSource`, `GCSReference`, `Query.Parameters`) and, for `tabledata.insertAll`, the generated client (the Go client cannot marshal a NaN or an infinity). BigQuery's `FLOAT64` "includes NaN". Measured first through the front, on the pinned emulator: its engine keeps `FLOAT64` values as SQLite REALs and SQLite makes a NaN NULL, both when it is bound and when a function returns one, so a NaN from a JSON load, a CSV load, a query parameter and `IEEE_DIVIDE(0, 0)` each read back NULL (`IS_NAN` NULL), even `SELECT IEEE_DIVIDE(0, 0)`, and `CAST('NaN' AS FLOAT64)` was refused, 400 "failed to format query"; #1074 had the front answer 501 for the NaNs it could see. The engine CloudBurrow builds keeps a NaN (#1061, googlesqlite patch 0004, whose `TestNaNIsKept` covers `CAST('NaN' AS FLOAT64)`, a NaN parameter, arithmetic, `SUM` and `COUNTIF(IS_NAN(f))`), and the front sends each write on: a NaN in a `FLOAT64` column (top level, `RECORD`, `REPEATED`) of a JSON load (upload and Cloud Storage) and a CSV load (`NaN`, `nan`; upload and Cloud Storage), a streamed row, a query parameter of an `INSERT`, and `IEEE_DIVIDE(0, 0)` in an `INSERT`, each reads back `IS_NAN` true, and `SELECT @p` of a NaN parameter and `SELECT IEEE_DIVIDE(0, 0)` read NaN. **Not supported**: -0 reads back 0 through each write (its sign is lost, #1076; `CAST(x AS STRING)` of a `CREATE TABLE AS SELECT -0.0` reads `-0`), and is not refused, as BigQuery's handling of it is not documented; an infinity inside a `RECORD` or an `ARRAY`, from a JSON load or computed by a statement (`INSERT … SELECT [CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64)]`), which the pinned engine refused, 400 "json: unsupported value" (#1077), is written and read back since #1061 (`TestBigQueryInfinityInsideCompositeValues`; googlesqlite patch 0004). **±Infinity** from a JSON load (`"Infinity"`, `"-Infinity"`), a CSV load (`inf`, `-inf`), `tabledata.insertAll` and a query parameter reads back `IS_INF` with its sign. Units `TestNaNQueryParameters`, `TestJSONLoadChecksBytes`, `TestCSVLoadChecksBytes`, `TestInsertAllChecksBytes`. |
| `writeDisposition` `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` of a load, and a query job's `writeDisposition` | **Verified** for JSON and CSV loads, from an upload and from Cloud Storage (Parquet: row above), and for a query job's `WRITE_TRUNCATE`, `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` (with the result's columns in another order, missing a NULLABLE column, into `REQUIRED` columns and fields, #1083), `WRITE_EMPTY` and `WRITE_APPEND`; **Not implemented** (501) for a query job's `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` whose result column has another type or `REPEATED` mode than the table's, that leaves out a column with a default value, or whose `schemaUpdateOptions` would relax a column or add a field inside a RECORD (#1110); `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION` adds the result's new top-level columns at the end of the table, NULLABLE (#1110, unit `TestQueryJobWriteDispositions` only) | `TestBigQueryWriteTruncateDataReplacesTheRows` (#1067, #1080, #1083), official Go client (`Loader.WriteDisposition`, `Query.Dst`, `Query.WriteDisposition`, `Client.JobFromID`). BigQuery: "WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA: If the table already exists, BigQuery overwrites the data, but keeps the constraints and schema of the existing table". Measured first through the front: a JSON and a CSV upload, and a JSON load of two objects from Cloud Storage, each with `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` into a table with rows, kept the rows and added the load's (the emulator knows only `WRITE_TRUNCATE` and `WRITE_EMPTY`), and the job succeeded. The emulator's `WRITE_TRUNCATE` of a table that exists deletes its rows in the same transaction as it inserts the load's, and keeps the table's schema; so the front sends `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` to it as `WRITE_TRUNCATE`, and the job reads back `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` (`jobs.insert`, `jobs.get`) with `outputRows` the rows loaded. Read back: after each of a JSON upload, a CSV upload, a JSON load of two objects and a CSV load from Cloud Storage, the table holds only the load's rows, with its schema and description; into a table that does not exist the load makes it. A query job with a destination table: the emulator appends the result whatever `writeDisposition` says (measured: `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA`, `WRITE_TRUNCATE` and `WRITE_EMPTY` each appended to a table with rows; 501 from #1067), so since #1080 the front carries them out into a table that exists ([JobConfigurationQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationQuery), `querywrite.go`). **`WRITE_EMPTY`** (the default) into a table with rows fails the job, reason `duplicate`, "Already Exists: Table project:dataset.table", and runs nothing ("If the table already exists and contains data, a 'duplicate' error is returned in the job result"); read back: the table unchanged. **`WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA`** and **`WRITE_TRUNCATE`** run the query into a scratch table of the dataset first (so a query that reads the table reads it as it was, and one that fails leaves it: read back after `SELECT ERROR('no')`), then replace the table's rows with the result's in one script, `DELETE` and `INSERT … SELECT`, which the emulator runs in one transaction (measured: a failed script given to `jobs.query` left the rows), when the result's columns are the table's, or the job is `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA`; read back: `SELECT id + 1, … FROM t UNION ALL SELECT 20, 'u'` into `t` replaced its rows with those two, and the table kept its schema and description. **`WRITE_TRUNCATE`** with other columns "uses the schema from the query result": the table is made again with the result's schema, keeping its description, labels, expiration, partitioning and clustering and not its constraints (as a Parquet load's `WRITE_TRUNCATE`), and the result copied in; read back: `SELECT 1.5 AS z, [1, 2] AS arr` made the table `(z FLOAT, arr REPEATED INTEGER)` with its description. Those are two steps (the emulator adds no column through `tables.patch`, #1010): should the copy fail, the job fails `backendError` naming the scratch table that holds the result. `jobs.insert` and `jobs.get` show the client's destination and `writeDisposition`; the job's rows are read through `jobs.getQueryResults`, which the emulator answers from the job (measured: read back after the scratch table was deleted); no scratch table is left. **`WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` keeps the table's schema** (#1083), and the result is written into it as BigQuery writes a query's result into a table it appends to: [`schemaUpdateOptions`](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/Job#JobConfigurationQuery.FIELDS.schema_update_options) are "supported … when writeDisposition is WRITE_APPEND; when writeDisposition is WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA", and BigQuery's samples of such an append ([Add columns in a query append job](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/managing-table-schemas#add_columns_in_a_query_append_job), and relaxing a column in one) write `SELECT "Timmy" as full_name, 85 as age, "Blue" as favorite_color` into a table of `full_name` and `age`, both `REQUIRED`, with `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION`, and `SELECT "Beyonce" as full_name` into it with `ALLOW_FIELD_RELAXATION`, which makes `age` NULLABLE for the row that has none: a result's columns are the table's by name, a result column is written into a `REQUIRED` one, a column the result does not have is NULL only when it is NULLABLE, and a result column the table does not have needs `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION`. So the front writes each of the table's columns from the result's of its name, at any depth, a `RECORD` rebuilt by name in the table's order, and a column the result does not have NULL (a `REPEATED` one empty); the engine has no `NOT NULL`, so the front first counts the result's rows with NULL where the table has a `REQUIRED` column or field. Read back: `SELECT 'r' AS s, 41 AS id` into `(id, s)` wrote `41, r`; `SELECT 'only s' AS s` wrote `NULL, only s`; `SELECT 'a1' AS a, 1 AS b, STRUCT(9 AS y, 'k' AS x) AS r` into `(a REQUIRED, b, r RECORD<x REQUIRED, y>)` wrote `a1, 1, k, 9` and kept the schema. **The job fails**, reason `invalid`, the table unchanged: a result column the table does not have (`SELECT 1.5 AS z`), a NULL for a `REQUIRED` column or field (`CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS a`, `STRUCT(CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS x, …)`), and a `REQUIRED` column the result does not have (`SELECT 3 AS b`); BigQuery's wording of these errors is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/writing-results>). **501** `notImplemented`, nothing run: a result column of another type (`SELECT 1.5 AS id` into an `INTEGER` column: whether BigQuery coerces is not documented) or `REPEATED` mode, a missing column that has a default value (whether BigQuery writes its default is not documented), and `schemaUpdateOptions` `ALLOW_FIELD_RELAXATION` into a table with a `REQUIRED` column, or `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION` of a field inside a RECORD, which CloudBurrow does not carry out for a query job; `ALLOW_FIELD_ADDITION` of a top-level column is carried out, the table made again with the column at its end, NULLABLE, keeping its other properties and constraints (the emulator adds no engine column through `tables.patch`, #1010); either destination when it is a view, or when the query is not one `SELECT`. A dry run, `WRITE_APPEND` and a destination that does not exist are sent on. A load of several objects from Cloud Storage is one transaction since #1079 (row "A load of several objects from Cloud Storage"). Units `TestWriteTruncateDataIsSentAsWriteTruncate`, `TestQueryDestinationWriteDispositions`, `TestQueryJobWriteDispositions`, `TestConvertColumns`, `TestNullViolations`. |
| ±Infinity inside a `RECORD` or `ARRAY` value, and `FLOAT64` ±Infinity as the REST API reads it | **Verified** for a `RECORD`, a `REPEATED RECORD` and a `REPEATED` column written by a JSON load (upload and Cloud Storage) and a streamed row, and for the text of ±Infinity in the rows of `tabledata.list`, `jobs.query` and `jobs.getQueryResults`, and, since #1061, for an infinity inside a `STRUCT` or `ARRAY` that a statement computes; **Not supported** for one a query parameter carries | `TestBigQueryInfinityInRecordsAndArrays` (#1077) and `TestBigQueryInfinityInsideCompositeValues` (#1061), official Go client (`ReaderSource`, `GCSReference`, `Query.Read`) and, for `tabledata.insertAll`, `tabledata.list`, `jobs.query` and `jobs.getQueryResults`, the generated client, whose rows are the wire's text. Measured first through the front, on the pinned emulator: a `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` load of `{"r":{"g":"-Infinity"}}` (or `"Infinity"`) into a `RECORD` with a `FLOAT64` field failed 400 "json: unsupported value: -Inf": the engine keeps a `STRUCT` or `ARRAY` value as JSON (googlesqlite, `valueLayoutFromValue` through `json.Marshal`), which has no infinity. The same value streamed was stored and read back, because the emulator hands a streamed `RECORD` to its engine as a list of one-field objects in the schema's order (`types.go`, `normalizeData`), whose values the engine keeps as their text, and a load's as the object it read; a load of `{"r":[{"g":"Infinity"}]}`, that list, was stored and read back `+Inf` (measured). So the front sends a JSON load's `RECORD` value that holds ±Infinity, at any depth, in that form, and every other value as it was; read back: `r.g` `-Infinity`, `rr` `[1.5, Infinity]`, `a` `[-Infinity, 2]`, and a `RECORD` of a `FLOAT64` and a `STRING` from Cloud Storage. **Reading**: BigQuery writes a `FLOAT64` ±Infinity in a row as `"Infinity"` and `"-Infinity"`; the emulator wrote Go's `"+Inf"` and `"-Inf"` (measured, at the top level, in a `RECORD` and in a `REPEATED` column), which the Go client reads (its `strconv`), but which are not BigQuery's text. The front writes them as BigQuery does in the rows of `tabledata.list`, `jobs.query` and `jobs.getQueryResults`, by the schema: a `STRING` value `"+Inf"` reads back as it was (same test). **In a statement**: `STRUCT(CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64))` and `[CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64)]` failed 400 on the pinned engine ("failed to format query … strconv.ParseFloat", and "json: unsupported value"); CloudBurrow's build parses the literal and keeps an infinity inside a composite (googlesqlite patch 0004), so `SELECT` and `INSERT … SELECT` of an `ARRAY` with `CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64)`, a NaN and a `STRUCT` with `IEEE_DIVIDE(-1, 0)` read back (`TestBigQueryInfinityInsideCompositeValues`). **Not supported**, 400 from the engine, nothing written: an `ARRAY<FLOAT64>` query parameter holding an infinity in an `INSERT` ("Value has type ARRAY<STRING>", measured on the pinned emulator; not re-measured on CloudBurrow's build). Units `TestInfinityRecords`, `TestJSONLoadSendsInfinityRecordsAsAList`, `TestInfinityRows`. |
| `BYTES` query parameters, `STRUCT` query parameters, and `RANGE` query parameters | **Verified** for a `BYTES` and an `ARRAY<BYTES>` parameter, named or positional, through `jobs.query` and `jobs.insert`, and since #1082 for a `STRUCT` parameter and an `ARRAY` of them, with `BYTES` fields at any depth, and since #1111 for a `RANGE<DATE>`, `RANGE<DATETIME>` or `RANGE<TIMESTAMP>` parameter, named or positional, at the top level, in an `ARRAY` or inside a `STRUCT`, with `UNBOUNDED` bounds (`TestBigQueryRangeParameters`: measured first, the emulator read a top-level `RANGE<DATE>` parameter as a NULL INTEGER; the front sends it built as `RANGE(start, end)` of its bounds, sent as `STRUCT` leaves are, both bounds `UNBOUNDED` as `RANGE<T> '[UNBOUNDED, UNBOUNDED)'` since the emulator refuses `RANGE(NULL, NULL)`, a NULL one a typed NULL; read back as sent, with `RANGE_CONTAINS`, `RANGE_START` and `RANGE_END`), and since #1101 for reading a whole `STRUCT` with a `TIMESTAMP` field | `TestBigQueryBytesParameters` (#1078), official Go client (`Query.Parameters` with a `[]byte` and a `[][]byte`, `Client.JobFromID`). BigQuery takes a `BYTES` parameter's value as base64 and types the parameter `BYTES`. Measured first through the front, on the pinned emulator: `INSERT INTO ds.t (id, b) VALUES (1, @p)` with `@p` the bytes `ff 00 61` failed 400 "Value has type STRING which cannot be inserted into column b, which has type BYTES", `TO_HEX(@p)` failed "No matching signature … STRING", an `ARRAY<BYTES>` read back as its base64 texts, and `@p.x` of a `STRUCT` with a `BYTES` field failed "Cannot access field x on a value with type STRING": the emulator hands its engine the value as a string (its source, `queryParameterValueToGoValue`), which the engine types `STRING`. `FROM_BASE64` of the same text as a `STRING` parameter read back `ff0061` (measured). **Since #1816** the front sends `BYTES` and `STRUCT` parameters, and `ARRAY`s of them, as the client sent them: the engine binds each as a value of its declared type, a `STRUCT`'s fields in their order (googlesqlite patches 0097 and 0099, bigquery-emulator 0098 and 0100), reads standard and URL-safe base64, and refuses a value that is not base64, 400; only a parameter with a `RANGE` in it is still built in the query as described here. Until then the front sent a `BYTES` parameter as a `STRING` of its standard base64 and each reference to it as `FROM_BASE64(@p)`, and an `ARRAY<BYTES>` as an `ARRAY<STRING>` referred to as the array of its elements' bytes in order (NULL when it is NULL); positional parameters are sent as named ones (`@cloudburrow_p1` …), so that one can be referred to twice. The references are found by the front's lexer, so a string literal or comment is not changed. Read back: `SELECT @p` returns the bytes `ff 00 61` exactly, `TO_HEX(@p)` `ff0061`, `'@p'` the text `@p`, a positional `?` and a NULL the same, an `INSERT` of `@p` and of an `ARRAY<BYTES>` stores `ff0061`, `WHERE b = @p` finds it, and `jobs.get` shows the client's text and parameters. A value that is not base64 is **400** `invalidQuery`. **`STRUCT` parameters** (#1082): the emulator types a `STRUCT` parameter, and an `ARRAY` of them, as one `STRING`, the JSON of its value, whatever its fields (measured: `SELECT @p` of a `STRUCT<X STRING, Y INT64>` read back the `STRING` `{"X":"/wBh","Y":"2"}`, and `@p.X` failed "Cannot access field X on a value with type STRING"), while its engine types a `STRUCT` built in the query as it is (measured: `STRUCT<X BYTES, Y INT64>(FROM_BASE64(@a), @b)`, `ARRAY<STRUCT<…>>[…]`, `CAST(NULL AS STRUCT<…>)`, nested, read back and inserted into a `RECORD` so). So the front sends such a parameter as that expression, each reference to it replaced by it: each scalar of its value a parameter of its own (`@cloudburrow_s1_1` …), in a typed `STRUCT<…>(…)` or `ARRAY<…>[…]` in the value's order, a NULL `STRUCT` or field a typed NULL, an `ARRAY` given no values empty; a scalar is sent as its own type where the emulator types a scalar parameter so (`INT64`, `FLOAT64`, `BOOL`, `STRING`, `TIMESTAMP`, measured), `BYTES` in `FROM_BASE64`, `NUMERIC`, `BIGNUMERIC`, `DATE`, `DATETIME`, `TIME` and `INTERVAL` (which the emulator types `STRING`, a `DATETIME` `TIMESTAMP`, measured) as a `CAST` of their text, `GEOGRAPHY` in `ST_GEOGFROMTEXT` and `JSON` in `PARSE_JSON`. Read back through the Go client: a `STRUCT` of `BYTES` (`ff 00 61`), `STRING`, `FLOAT64` 0.1, `BOOL`, `DATE`, `DATETIME`, `TIME`, `TIMESTAMP`, `NUMERIC` 123.45, a nested `STRUCT` with `BYTES` and the `INT64` 9007199254740993, an `ARRAY` of `STRUCT`s and an `ARRAY<BYTES>` reads each field back exactly (`@p.X`, `TO_HEX(@p.X)`, `@p.I.Z`, `@p.A[OFFSET(1)].Z` …), `SELECT @p` of a `STRUCT` of `BYTES`, `STRING`, a nested `STRUCT` and an `ARRAY` of them reads the whole `RECORD`; an `ARRAY` of `STRUCT`s, positional `STRUCT`s and a NULL one (`@p IS NULL`) read back; an `INSERT` of a `STRUCT` and an `ARRAY` of them into a `RECORD` and a `REPEATED RECORD` with `BYTES` fields stores `ff0061` and the rest in order, and `jobs.get` shows the client's text and parameters; a `BYTES` field that is not base64 is **400**. **501**, naming it, nothing run: a type the front does not know inside a `STRUCT`, or a `RANGE` of another element type. **A whole `STRUCT` with a `TIMESTAMP` field** reads back since #1101, which gave every nested `TIMESTAMP` in the form the client asks for: measured 2026-10-16 through the Go client, `SELECT @p` of a `STRUCT<TS TIMESTAMP, N INT64>`, named and positional, and of an `ARRAY` of them, read back `2020-01-02 03:04:05 UTC` and the `INT64`, as `@p.TS` does; `TestBigQueryBytesParameters` reads a whole `STRUCT` with a `TIMESTAMP` field beside its `BYTES`, nested `STRUCT` and `ARRAY` fields. Before #1101 it failed in the Go client, as any `TIMESTAMP` inside a `RECORD` read back as the engine's text. The other scalar types at the top level are the emulator's (#1108). **Not covered**: a Go client `[]byte{}` is sent with no value, which the emulator reads as NULL, as the Go client does not send an empty base64 text. Units `TestRangeParameters`, `TestRangeParameterJobShowsTheClients`; engine units `TestTypedNullArrayStructParameters` (googlesqlite and bigquery-emulator). |

Fixed in the engine CloudBurrow builds (googlesqlite patch 0011, next row); the front no longer rewrites these calls (it sent each as `IF(arg IS NULL …, NULL, call)` since #1109). Read back through `jobs.query` and a query job: `ARRAY_TO_STRING` of a NULL array, delimiter or `null_text`, with `SAFE.`, nested in `ARRAY_REVERSE` and of a NULL parameter, reads NULL; `ARRAY_REVERSE` and `ARRAY_CONCAT` of a NULL array and `NET.IPV4_TO_INT64`, `NET.IP_TO_STRING`, `NET.REG_DOMAIN` of a NULL are NULL; `ARRAY_TO_STRING(['a', NULL, 'b'], '-')` reads `a-b`, with `'n'` `a-n-b`, of an `ARRAY_AGG` subquery `a+b`. **An emulator 500 to a query**: the emulator answers 500 only for a panic (a query it cannot run is 400, its source), so the front answers a 500 the emulator gave a query (`jobs.query`, or `jobs.insert` of a query job) **400** `invalidQuery` with the emulator's text, which the client does not retry. A 500 to anything else the front sends first (a `datasets.insert`) is left as it is. Units `TestNoRetry`. |

Returns TRUE if value_set contains a value equal to search_value. Returns NULL if the equality comparison between search_value and any value in value_set produces NULL. Returns FALSE." ([operators](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/operators)). Found by calling each of the engine's functions with a NULL argument (in its own module, googlesqlite v0.3.1): a panic (the emulator's 500) for the step of `GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY` and `GENERATE_TIMESTAMP_ARRAY`, `MAKE_INTERVAL`, `INTERVAL <NULL> DAY`, `ST_BUFFER`, `ST_BUFFERWITHTOLERANCE`, `ST_INTERSECTSBOX`, `NULLIF(x, NULL)`, `JSON_OBJECT`'s key and `JSON_SET`'s path and value, beside the previous row's; an error for `ST_DISTANCE`, `ST_HAUSDORFFDWITHIN`, `JUSTIFY_DAYS`, `JUSTIFY_HOURS`, `JUSTIFY_INTERVAL` and `JSON_TYPE`; FALSE for `NULL IN UNNEST([1, 2])`, `1 IN UNNEST([2, NULL])` and `1 IN (2, NULL)`. Fixed in the engine (googlesqlite patch 0011: one guard where every scalar function is called returns NULL for a NULL argument of those functions, and returns any function's panic as an error naming it; `JSON_OBJECT`, `JSON_SET`, `NULLIF`, `IN` and `IN UNNEST` fixed where they are). Read back: each of those calls with a NULL reads NULL, promptly; `ARRAY_LENGTH(GENERATE_DATE_ARRAY('2020-01-01', '2020-01-03'))` 3, `MAKE_INTERVAL(hour => 10)` `0-0 0 10:0:0`, `ST_INTERSECTSBOX(p, 0, 0, 10, 10)` true, `NULLIF(1, NULL)` 1, `1 IN UNNEST([NULL, 1])` true, `NULL IN UNNEST([])` false, `JSON_SET(JSON '{"a":1}', '$.a', NULL)` `{"a":null}`; `JSON_OBJECT(CAST(NULL AS STRING), 1)` fails 400 "JSON_OBJECT: a key is NULL". |
| `=`, `<` and the other comparisons of `INTERVAL`s; a negative `INTERVAL` of less than an hour; `INTERVAL n MILLISECOND` and `MICROSECOND` | **Verified** | `TestBigQueryIntervalComparison` (#1120, #1126), official Go client (`Query.Parameters` with a `*bigquery.IntervalValue`). In BigQuery "Values of the same comparable data type can be compared to each other. All data types are supported except for: GEOGRAPHY JSON ARRAY" ([comparable data types](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types#comparable_data_types)); the page does not say how two intervals compare, and GoogleSQL's own implementation compares their length, a month counting 30 days and a day 24 hours ([interval_value.h](https://github.com/google/googlesql/blob/master/googlesql/public/interval_value.h), `GetAsMicros` and the comparison operators). The canonical format is `[sign]Y-M [sign]D [sign]H:M:S[.F]`, and `INTERVAL` takes `MILLISECOND` and `MICROSECOND` ([interval type](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types#interval_type)). Measured first through the front: `SELECT INTERVAL 1 DAY = INTERVAL 1 DAY` failed 400 "unsupported eq operator for interval value", and so did `WHERE v = @p`; read in the engine: `INTERVAL -1 SECOND` was written `0-0 0 0:0:1` (and stored so, positive), and `INTERVAL 1500 MILLISECOND` failed "unexpected interval part". Fixed in the engine (googlesqlite patches 0009 and 0010). Read back: `INTERVAL 1 DAY = INTERVAL 1 DAY`, `INTERVAL 1 MONTH = INTERVAL 30 DAY`, `INTERVAL 1 DAY = INTERVAL 24 HOUR`, `INTERVAL 1 DAY < INTERVAL 25 HOUR`, `INTERVAL -1 SECOND < INTERVAL 0 SECOND` true; `CAST(INTERVAL -1 SECOND AS STRING)` `0-0 0 -0:0:1`, `INTERVAL -1 MONTH` `-0-1 0 0:0:0`, `INTERVAL 1500 MILLISECOND` `0-0 0 0:0:1.5`; a table's `WHERE v = @p` of `@p` 1 day finds `INTERVAL 1 DAY` and `INTERVAL 24 HOUR`, `v > @p` `INTERVAL 2 DAY`, `v < INTERVAL 0 SECOND` the stored `INTERVAL -1 SECOND`. `ORDER BY`, `MIN` and `MAX` of an `INTERVAL` order it by its length, through googlesqlite patch 0010's `IntervalValue` comparison (#1138): read back, `ORDER BY v, id` of the four rows `-1 SECOND`, `1 DAY`, `24 HOUR`, `2 DAY` (the two of one length tied), `ORDER BY v DESC` the reverse, and `MIN` and `MAX` `0-0 0 -0:0:1` and `0-0 2 0:0:0` (#1567). |
| `INTERVAL` arithmetic: `+` and `-` of two `INTERVAL`s, `*` and `/` by an `INT64`, unary `-`; `DATE`, `DATETIME` and `TIMESTAMP` `+`/`-` `INTERVAL`, and the difference of two as an `INTERVAL`; `JUSTIFY_DAYS`, `JUSTIFY_HOURS`, `JUSTIFY_INTERVAL`, `MAKE_INTERVAL`, `EXTRACT` from an `INTERVAL` | **Verified** (#1437) | `TestBigQueryIntervalArithmetic`, official Go client, through `jobs.query` and a query job, results cast to `STRING` and, for a table column with a `*bigquery.IntervalValue` parameter, read as the client's `IntervalValue`. As BigQuery documents them ([interval arithmetic operators](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/operators#interval_arithmetic_operators), [interval functions](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/interval_functions), [datetime subtraction](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/operators#datetime_subtraction)), and as GoogleSQL implements them ([interval_value.cc](https://github.com/google/googlesql/blob/master/googlesql/public/interval_value.cc)): an interval is months, days and a time part, each with its own sign and range, and arithmetic works part by part (`INTERVAL 1 DAY - INTERVAL 2 HOUR` is `0-0 1 -2:0:0`, `3 * INTERVAL '1-1 1 1:1:1.5' YEAR TO SECOND` `3-3 3 3:3:4.500`); `/` carries the months' remainder into days at 30 a month and the days' into the time part at 24 hours, truncated to microseconds (`INTERVAL 10 MONTH / 3` is `0-3 10 0:0:0`, `INTERVAL 1 DAY / 7` `0-0 0 3:25:42.857142`); a date or time plus an interval adds the months first, a day past the month's end being its last (`DATE '2021-01-31' + INTERVAL 1 MONTH` is `2021-02-28 00:00:00`, a `DATETIME`), then the days, then the time part; `DATE - DATE` is the days between (`0-0 396 0:0:0`), `DATETIME - DATETIME` and `TIMESTAMP - TIMESTAMP` the time between in the time part (`0-0 0 36:34:56.789`); the `JUSTIFY_` functions carry 30 days into a month and 24 hours into a day and make the parts' signs agree (`JUSTIFY_DAYS(INTERVAL -65 DAY)` `-0-2 -5 0:0:0`, `JUSTIFY_INTERVAL(INTERVAL '29 49:00:00' DAY TO SECOND)` `0-1 1 1:0:0`); `MAKE_INTERVAL` and `EXTRACT` work on the canonical interval (`EXTRACT(MINUTE FROM MAKE_INTERVAL(minute => 72))` is 12). **Errors** (400): a part out of `INTERVAL`'s range (`INTERVAL 10000 YEAR + INTERVAL 1 MONTH`: "Interval field months '120001' is out of range -120000 to 120000", `MAKE_INTERVAL(year => 10001)`), "Interval overflow during multiplication", "Interval division by zero", a date or time out of its range (`DATE '9999-12-31' + INTERVAL 1 DAY`). **Measured first through the front:** `INTERVAL 1 DAY + INTERVAL 2 HOUR` failed 400 "unsupported add operator for interval value", as did `-`, `*`, `/` and unary minus, and `DATE '2021-01-31' + INTERVAL 1 MONTH` was `2021-03-03`. Fixed in the engine (googlesqlite patch 0035; engine test `TestIntervalArithmetic`). **What differs:** UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/data-types>) against BigQuery: the wording of the range errors (GoogleSQL's). `SUM` and `AVG` of `INTERVAL`s are not covered here. |

| A load of several objects from Cloud Storage | **Verified** all or nothing for JSON, CSV and Parquet loads, with `WRITE_TRUNCATE` and `WRITE_APPEND`; **404** `notFound` with no Cloud Storage given to the front (#1457) | `TestBigQueryLoadOfSeveralObjectsIsOneJob` (#1079), official Go client (`GCSReference` with a wildcard and with two URIs, `Loader.WriteDisposition`). BigQuery's load is one job: it loads every object or none. Measured first through the front, on the pinned emulator: the emulator reads a load from Cloud Storage itself one object at a time, each in a transaction of its own, giving only the first the job's `writeDisposition` (its source, `importFromGCS`), so a `NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON` load of two objects whose second failed left the table with the first object's rows, its own gone under `WRITE_TRUNCATE` and `WRITE_TRUNCATE_DATA` and kept under `WRITE_APPEND`; a CSV load with columns, read by the front since #944, left the table as it was. Now the front reads every JSON and CSV load from Cloud Storage itself (its `--storage`, the instance's Cloud Storage) and sends the objects to the emulator as one upload, which it loads in one transaction; a Parquet load the front carries out itself, its rows in a scratch table first. Read back: after JSON (with a schema, without one, two URIs), CSV and Parquet loads whose second object fails, with `WRITE_TRUNCATE` and with `WRITE_APPEND`, the table holds its row as before; loads of two good objects load every row. A CSV load with no schema and no autodetect into a table that does not exist is **400** `invalid`, "No schema specified on job or table" (measured before: the emulator answered 500 "nil pointer dereference", which the Go client retried until its deadline). An `AVRO` or `ORC` load is refused by the emulator before anything is written (400 "not support sourceFormat", measured). Since #1457 a load of several objects (more than one URI, or a wildcard) with no Cloud Storage given to the front is **404** `notFound`, "Not found: URI gs://…", as BigQuery answers a URI that names no object, and as an instance whose Cloud Storage is not enabled answers (its front's `--storage` does not resolve); nothing is loaded, and one of a single object is sent on (before: 501). Units `TestCloudStorageLoadReportsCounts`, `TestCSVLoadFromCloudStorage`. |

The emulator does not serve the protocol: it answered the first request with a `Location` of its own listen address, `http://0.0.0.0:9051/…`, which the Go client retried until it gave up (measured), and it takes a chunk only by `PUT`, where the Go client sends `POST` (from its source). Upstream: [goccy/bigquery-emulator#160](https://github.com/goccy/bigquery-emulator/issues/160) (closed) and [#393](https://github.com/goccy/bigquery-emulator/pull/393) (closed unmerged). The front serves the upload itself: it keeps the job and the chunks, in a file in its container, answers each chunk but the last 308 with its `Range` (or 200 with `X-Http-Status-Code-Override: 308`, as the Go client asks), and on the last sends the job and the data to the emulator as one multipart upload through the same checks as any load. The first request is checked for the table ID and schema; an unfinished upload is dropped after 24 hours. Unit `TestResumableUploads`. |

Measured against the pinned emulator over REST: its `jobs.list` gave each job only `jobReference`, `kind`, `statistics` and `status`, whatever the projection, so `Job.Config()` of a listed job was nil; BigQuery's `full` projection "Includes all job data" (the enum's description in the API's discovery document; [jobs.list](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/jobs/list)). The front keeps each job's configuration from the emulator's answer to `jobs.insert`, and reads a job it has not seen (a `jobs.query`'s, whose answer has none, or one made before the front started) once with `jobs.get`; the last 5,000 are kept, and an older one is read again. A query job's and a `jobs.query` script's text read back as the client wrote them (#939). Without `projection=full` no configuration is given, as BigQuery's `minimal` "Does not include the job configuration". | `jobs.list`: order, `maxResults` and `pageToken`, `stateFilter`, `minCreationTime`, `maxCreationTime`, `parentJobId`, `allUsers` | **Verified** | `TestBigQueryJobListPagesAndFilters` (#972), official Go client (`Client.Jobs` with `State`, `MinCreationTime`, `MaxCreationTime`, `ParentJobID`, `AllUsers`, and `iterator.NewPager` pages of two). Measured first against the pinned emulator over REST: `maxResults=2` listed nine jobs, oldest first, with no `nextPageToken`; its handler (`jobsListHandler`) reads none of the request's parameters. BigQuery's list "is sorted in reverse chronological order, by job creation time", pages by `maxResults` and `pageToken`, and filters by `stateFilter`, `minCreationTime` and `maxCreationTime` ("after or at", "before or at", in milliseconds) and `parentJobId` ("If set, show only child jobs of the specified parent. Otherwise, show all top-level jobs") ([jobs.list](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/jobs/list)). The front does each over the whole list, after its own jobs and the job times (#971) are in it: newest first (jobs of one millisecond, newest made first); a page token names the page's last job, so a job made between pages does not move the next page; a job with a `parentJobId` is listed only under it (a script's child jobs, #1353, the row *A script's child jobs*). The queries the front runs itself for its checks (reading a `CREATE TABLE … AS SELECT`'s columns, the resync statements of #955, and the rest) are left out: they are no client's jobs. Since #1555 each is named as the front's on the engine, its job ID beginning `_cloudburrow_` (bigquery-emulator patch 0057 reads the prefix from the front's request), so it stays out after a restart of the front and however many there are, of INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS and its variants and the console's Job history too, and `jobs.get`, `jobs.getQueryResults`, `jobs.cancel` and `jobs.delete` of one are 404, as for a job BigQuery does not have; before, the front remembered the last 5,000 in memory, and a restarted front listed every earlier one (measured in the BigQuery suite: 1,306 jobs before a restart, 3,684 after). A client's `jobs.insert` of a job ID beginning `_cloudburrow_` is 400 `invalid`: BigQuery reserves no job ID, but this prefix is CloudBurrow's (`TestBigQueryFrontsOwnJobsStayUnlisted`, official Go client, through a DELETE, an UPDATE, `CHANGES` and `APPENDS`, a dropped table kept for undelete and the region views, before and after a restart of the front; unit `TestTheFrontsOwnJobsStayUnlistedAfterARestart`). `allUsers` lists the same jobs: the emulator has one user, so every job is the caller's. A bad `pageToken`, `stateFilter` or creation time is 400 `invalid`. Since #1564 the engine leaves out the jobs outside `minCreationTime` and `maxCreationTime` before the front reads the list (bigquery-emulator patch 0060; a job with no time in milliseconds is left to the front), so a list of the last minute's jobs no longer carries every job to the front. Unit `TestJobListPagesAndFilters`. |
