BigQuery keeps a job's `errorResult`. The front notes the failure in each `jobs.insert` answer, an `errorResult` or a 400 or 404 (not a 409, which is about an ID another job holds), and `jobs.get`, `jobs.getQueryResults` and `jobs.list` report it; a job that succeeds still reads back succeeded. The failures are kept in the front's memory, the last 1,000; the emulator keeps no state across a restart either. `jobs.query`, which answers a failure with an error and lists no job for it, is unchanged. | Where the checks run | **Verified** from the host, from Cloud Run, and from a pod without Cloud Run | The front runs **in the emulator's pod** (#902), a second container from the locally built storage image (`cloudburrow-storage bigquery-front`, the image the in-cluster Cloud Storage server runs, so enabling BigQuery builds it too), and serves the `bigquery` Service's REST port, 9050; the emulator listens on 9051, which the Service does not publish. Every client reaches the emulator through it: the host's tunnel, which the SDKs, `bq` and the console use through `CLOUDBURROW_BIGQUERY_ENDPOINT`, and any pod that dials `bigquery.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:9050`, the address `env --format kubernetes` prints and Cloud Run revisions and job tasks are given, with or without Cloud Run; that traffic stays in the cluster, so it does not depend on pods reaching the host (#575). `TestAPodDialingTheBigQueryServiceGetsTheFrontWithoutCloudRun`, on an instance without Cloud Run (emulators shard): a one-off pod running the official Go client at that address gets 409 for a dataset that exists, 400 for a hyphenated dataset ID and for a column named twice, and an `invalid` insertErrors entry for a row missing its REQUIRED value, none of them stored, and port 9060 answers; the Service selects the pod, which runs the front. `TestCloudRunRevisionGetsBigQueryRefusalsThroughTheFront` and `TestCloudRunRevisionDialingTheBigQueryServiceGetsTheFront` (run shard): a revision at the injected endpoint, and one that dials the Service itself, get the same four refusals. Until #902 the front was in the host tunnel's guard, and with Cloud Run the Service was routed to it through `cloudburrow-host` (#874, #881); neither is needed now, and nothing BigQuery's is published to pods through the host. The front serves the Storage Read API's port (gRPC, 9060) too since #1032, and the emulator's moves to 9061, which the Service does not publish either (row *Storage Read API of a table whose ID another dataset has*; unit `TestBigQueryManifestPutsTheFrontOnTheServicePort`). **The emulator's own ports refuse every other pod** (#1114): it listens on its pod's loopback alone (`--host=127.0.0.1`), and Kubernetes asks its container's readiness of the front, which dials 9051 and 9061 on loopback (`/cloudburrow/backend-ready`, `internal/frontready`). `TestEmulatorsBehindAFrontRefuseOtherPods`: from another pod, 9051 and 9061 at the BigQuery pod's IP refuse the connection, and 9050 and 9060 accept it. Measured first with the emulator on `0.0.0.0` (its default): from another pod, `CreateReadSession` of a table in a project the instance does not have, sent to 9061, which the front refuses `NOT_FOUND`, crashed the emulator, and every dataset was gone. DML is not checked. |
| Dry run statement type | **Not reliable** | Measured (#698), over REST: a dry run reports `statementType` `SELECT` for a `DELETE` and for a `CREATE TABLE` alike, so it cannot tell a read from a write. |
| Queries through `jobs.insert` | **Leave a dataset behind** | Measured (#698), over REST: each inserted query job creates a dataset named after its job ID to hold the result, and it is listed with the user's own. `jobs.query`, which the Go client's `Query.Read` sends when nothing forces a job, leaves none (`TestConsoleBigQueryDatasetsSchemaAndQuery` checks the dataset list is unchanged after a console query). |
| Creation and modification times of datasets, tables, views and routines | **Verified** (#1310) | `TestBigQueryResourceTimesInMilliseconds`, official Go client: `DatasetMetadata`, `TableMetadata` (a table, after `Table.Update` too, and a view) and `RoutineMetadata` `CreationTime` and `LastModifiedTime`, and a query job's `JobStatistics` `CreationTime`, `StartTime` and `EndTime`, are within a minute of now. BigQuery gives them in milliseconds since the epoch ([Table](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/tables#Table), [Dataset](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/rest/v2/datasets#Dataset)). Measured first (#698, #1310): the emulator wrote a table's and a job's in seconds (`tables.get` answered `"creationTime":"1792085781"`), which the client read as January 1970, and gave a dataset neither. bigquery-emulator patch 0013 gives them in milliseconds and has `datasets.insert` set a dataset's; a table saved in seconds by an earlier engine keeps them. A model's `creationTime` and `lastModifiedTime` are given in milliseconds by the front's models methods (`internal/bigqueryfront/models.go`, the models row), not checked against the clock here. The console shows no times. |
| Emulator environment variable | **None exists** | No official client reads one. `cloudburrow env` exports `CLOUDBURROW_BIGQUERY_ENDPOINT`, which code passes to `option.WithEndpoint`, and `CLOUDSDK_API_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES_BIGQUERY`, which only bq reads, with the flags in the `bq` row; see configuration.md. |

### State snapshots

`cloudburrow state save <file>` and `state load <file>`, over `POST /admin/state/export` and
`/admin/state/import` on the loopback control port, with the instance's admin token (#553). The archive is a gzipped tar whose first entry
is a versioned `manifest.json`, naming every enabled service as captured or not, with the reason.
A service is captured **record for record from the store it keeps its state in**, so it comes back
exactly: a queue's retry configuration and state, a task's schedule and dispatch count, a disabled
secret version. This holds whichever backend the instance uses: memory, a durable file, or
Kubernetes Secrets for Secret Manager.

| Service | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud Tasks | **Verified** | `TestStateSaveResetLoadRestoresEverything` (CLI, official SDKs, CI instance) and `TestStateRoundTripsTasksSecretsAndProjects`, record-identical in ephemeral and persistent modes |
| Secret Manager | **Verified** | Same tests: every version and payload restored. In CI the backend is Kubernetes Secrets. **The archive holds secret values in plain form**: the CLI warns, and writes it `0600`. Tests: `TestStateSaveResetLoadRestoresEverything`, `TestStateRoundTripsTasksSecretsAndProjects`. |
| Project registry | **Verified** | Same tests: a project created through the console is restored. Tests: `TestStateSaveResetLoadRestoresEverything`, `TestStateRoundTripsTasksSecretsAndProjects`. |
| Cloud Scheduler | **Verified** | `TestStateRestoresSchedulerJobs` (CLI, `cloud.google.com/go/scheduler/apiv1`, CI instance): a paused job is saved, reset away and listed back with its schedule, zone, target and next run (#600). `TestStateSaveCapturesSchedulerJobs` checks the store is record-identical and a job created after the save is gone. A job whose next run passed while it was away fires once on the next tick, as after a restart. |
| Cloud Storage | **Verified** | `TestStateRestoresStorage` and `TestStateRestoresVersionsAndHolds`. The state is exported from the storage server's store directly (#511, `builtinStorageSnapshotter`), so a restore fires no notifications: every bucket with all its fields, soft-deleted buckets, every object version (live, noncurrent and soft-deleted) with its generation, metageneration, holds, retention and customTime, notification configurations and undelivered events, IAM policies, sessions and multipart uploads, and the bytes, streamed. A load verifies that every blob hashes to its content address and that every object version's CRC32C matches, before it replaces anything, in one transaction. **HMAC key secrets are excluded**, and the archive says so (`secretsExcluded`): a restored key keeps its metadata and cannot sign. `TestSnapshotRoundTripKeepsVersionsAndHolds`, `TestSnapshotExcludesHMACSecrets`, `TestSnapshotImportVerifiesBytes`, `TestBuiltinStorageSnapshotRoundTrip` (10 MiB, streamed, never held whole in memory). |
| Pub/Sub | **Verified: resources, not messages** | `TestPubSubStateSaveAndLoad` (CLI, official `pubsub/v2` clients, CI instance, #880) and unit `TestPubSubStateRoundTrip` (through the real front, against `pstest`). Google's emulator has no export, so `pubsubSnapshotter` reads through the front with the official client, for every project CloudBurrow knows and every project a call through the front has named: **every schema with every revision** in order, **every topic** as the front returns it (labels, retention, schema settings), **every subscription with every setting** (ack deadline, retention, retained acknowledged messages, filter, ordering, exactly-once, retry and dead-letter policies, expiration policy, labels, push endpoint and attributes; the real endpoint, never the relay's; the expiration policy and labels an update set, which the front keeps and the emulator refuses, #949: unit `TestPubSubStateKeepsUpdatedLabels`), **how long each subscription had been idle**, its expiration clock, and **every snapshot's name and topic**. A load clears those projects' subscriptions, snapshots, topics and schemas and creates the archive's; each subscription reads back as `ListSubscriptions` read it before the save, and one saved 30 hours into a 48-hour ttl is kept 17 hours after the load and gone 2 hours later. **Not kept:** messages (published and unacknowledged, retained after acknowledgement, or in a snapshot's backlog), ack IDs and leases: a loaded subscription starts empty. A loaded snapshot is taken again from a subscription of its topic, so it marks the moment of the load, with a new expire time. A schema revision gets a new revision ID, and a topic's schema settings are pointed at the new IDs. A subscription whose topic was deleted cannot be created again and is left out. The time between a save and a load does not count towards expiration. |
| Cloud Run | **Not captured** | Services are Knative objects in the cluster; redeploy them from their images |
| Cloud KMS | **Not captured** | Key material is not exported. Keys recreated from their definitions get new material, so ciphertext produced before a `state load` cannot be decrypted after it (`TestStateManifestSaysKMSIsNotCaptured`, #388) |
| Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) | **Verified** | `TestStateRestoresCloudSQL` (CLI, `pgx`, CI instance): a table's rows come back exactly after they were changed, and a database created since the save is gone. Saved with `pg_dump -Fc` for each application database and loaded with `pg_restore --exit-on-error`, both run **inside the server's pod** through the instance's kubeconfig (#311). Nothing is exposed beyond the existing tunnel. The archive holds the dumps and no kubeconfig or cluster credential (`TestPostgresSnapshotArchiveHoldsNoClusterCredential`, and checked on the real archive). Roles are not captured, because the server has only the one it was initialised with. `reset` does not touch PostgreSQL; a load drops and recreates every application database. |
| Cloud SQL for MySQL | **Not captured** | A real MySQL: use `mysqldump` |
| Memorystore | **Not captured** | A real Valkey, and one per created instance: use its own `BGSAVE`, or the append-only file on its volume. The created instances' records (in `<state-dir>/<name>/memorystore` in persistent mode) are not in the archive either |
| Firestore, Datastore, Bigtable, Spanner, BigQuery | **Not captured** | Emulators with no export. All but Datastore are in-memory; Datastore's store, kept on its volume in persistent mode, is not in the archive |

**Load replaces.** Loading resets each captured service to exactly the archive's contents, in one
atomic commit per service, so nothing created since the save survives. **Refused before anything
is touched:** an archive whose manifest version is unknown (`TestARefusedArchiveLoadsNothing`),
one in another format, one that is not an archive, and one holding a service this instance does
not run.

**An archive from `v0.2.0` or `v0.1.0` loads (#1605, #1807).** One `v0.2.0`, the latest release,
saved loads here, Cloud Storage, Cloud Scheduler and Pub/Sub's resources included
(`TestStateArchiveFromV020Loads`, on the archive `v0.2.0` wrote). So does one from `v0.1.0`, its Cloud
Storage included: that release wrote buckets, objects and notification configurations in the layout
of the server it ran before the builtin one (#519), and a load of that layout creates each through
the builtin server's JSON API and checks every object's CRC32C (`TestStateArchiveFromV010Loads`, on
the archive `v0.1.0` wrote). `test/upgrade` checks both against real instances. See
[install.md](install.md#upgrading) for the upgrade promise.

**From the console** (#801): the **Instance** page's **Save state** downloads the archive `state
save` writes, through the same code (`exportStateArchive`), and **Load state** uploads one through
`state load`'s (`importStateArchive`), streamed into the restore without being held in memory. It
is bounded by its own limit of 5 GiB, not the upload limit in Settings, since the archive captures
the whole instance and Save state must load back (#1250); past it the console answers 413, naming
the limit and `cloudburrow state load`, which has no limit (`TestStateLoadIsNotHeldToTheUploadLimit`,
`TestConsoleLoadsTheArchiveItSavedOverTheUploadLimit`). The
entries are byte-identical to what `state save` writes from the same instance, only the
manifest's `created` differing (`TestConsoleInstanceActsThroughTheAdminAPI`); against the CI
instance, a bucket, a secret and a queue saved, reset and loaded from the console are read back
by the official clients (`TestConsoleStateSaveResetLoadRestores`). See the Console table.

**Configuration.** Storage and Pub/Sub need nothing but `cloudburrow env`. The Python Storage
client needs the scheme in `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST`, which the Go client does not, and `env` exports
the form both accept. Firestore, Datastore, Bigtable and Spanner read their emulator variables,
which the loopback guard checks at session start; each of these tests skips where the instance
does not enable its service. Cloud KMS and BigQuery, like Cloud Tasks and Secret Manager, need an
explicit channel or endpoint. Cloud Tasks and Secret Manager need an explicit plaintext channel (see
[credentials.md](credentials.md#python-clients-for-cloud-tasks-and-secret-manager)).

**Guards.** The suite refuses to run unless `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` is the generated
fixture and default credentials resolve to it. Every connection through Python sockets must be
loopback, which covers the HTTP clients, and so must every gRPC channel target. A violation
fails the whole session even if the test that caused it caught the error. `test_guard.py` proves
both guards by running sessions that break them. gRPC connects from C, which a Python guard
cannot see, so for gRPC it is the channel target that is checked, not the socket.

the `storage` shard, Firestore in the `emulators` shard, and a shard fails if any test it runs
skips. Anything not listed is not claimed for Node.

Found by the `example: Cloud Storage` block before it passed `resumable: false`; no test pins it. Pass `resumable: false`, or a `chunkSize` |

**Configuration.** Pub/Sub and Firestore need nothing but `cloudburrow env`: the clients read
`PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST` and `FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST` and open a plaintext channel, Firestore's
with the emulator's `owner` token as its only credential. **Storage does not work
with `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST` as exported.** The Node client uses the variable verbatim as the
JSON API's base URL, so it would need `/storage/v1`. It also uses it as the upload endpoint, which
must not have that path. So unset the variable and pass its value as `apiEndpoint`, as the client's
own source advises, with google-auth-library's `PassThroughClient` as its `authClient`:
`new Storage({ apiEndpoint: 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>', authClient: new PassThroughClient() })`.
Version 9 authenticates a custom endpoint too and ignores `useAuthWithCustomEndpoint`
(googleapis/google-cloud-node#9873), so without it the client fetches a token from
`oauth2.googleapis.com`. Cloud Tasks and Secret Manager read no emulator
variable. Pass the endpoint from `CLOUDBURROW_TASKS_ENDPOINT` or
`CLOUDBURROW_SECRETMANAGER_ENDPOINT` as `apiEndpoint` and `port`, with `sslCreds:
grpc.credentials.createInsecure()` (`grpc` from `google-gax`).

**Guards.** `guard.mjs` is loaded with `--import` into every process of the run. It refuses to
start unless `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` is unset or is the generated fixture, and it checks
that application default credentials resolve to that fixture (exit 3). Every TCP connection and
every DNS lookup must be loopback. Node's gRPC (`@grpc/grpc-js`) is JavaScript and connects
through `net` like the HTTP clients do, so, unlike the Python guard, this one sees the gRPC
sockets as well as the HTTP ones. A violation makes the process exit 4, and so fails the run, even
if the test that caused it caught the error. `guard.test.mjs` proves both guards by running
sessions that break them. Each service's tests skip when `cloudburrow env` exports no variable for
that service.

### Cloud SQL is not an emulator

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A real SQL server, locally | **Verified** | PostgreSQL in the cluster, digest-pinned (17.11 by the pinned image; the version is not asserted), reached with an ordinary driver (`pgx`), which created a table and inserted rows with nothing of CloudBurrow's involved; a plain `psql` client is the same wire protocol, which no test runs. Tests: `TestCloudSQLFromTheExportedPGVariables`, `TestCloudSQLRestartSetup`. |
| Durability | **Verified, measured** | A real database, so it has a volume in persistent mode, as Datastore's emulator and Memorystore's Valkey do (and Firestore's exports, #1615); Bigtable, Spanner and BigQuery are in-memory. CI's restart probe (#701): `TestCloudSQLRestartSetup` runs alone just before `stop` and leaves a table with a row. After `stop` and `up` in persistent mode, `TestCloudSQLAcrossRestart` reads the row back; brought up again with `--mode ephemeral`, the server has no volume and the table does not exist (`42P01`). |
| Connecting from `cloudburrow env` alone | **Verified** | `TestCloudSQLFromTheExportedPGVariables` (#584): pgx, given only the `PGHOST`, `PGPORT`, `PGUSER`, `PGDATABASE` and `PGSSLMODE` that `env` exported (every other `PG*` variable cleared), and again given `CLOUDBURROW_CLOUDSQL_URL`, connects and runs `SELECT 1`. The host port is fixed at `9019` (`--port-cloudsql`, moved by `--port-base`). |
| MySQL, locally (`cloudsql-mysql`) | **Verified** | `TestCloudSQLMySQLDataPlane` (#297): MySQL 8.4.11, digest-pinned, reached with `go-sql-driver/mysql` from the host and with the `mysql` client from a pod through `cloudsql-mysql.cloudburrow.svc.cluster.local:3306`; `cloudburrow reset` drops every non-system database. A generated per-instance password, exported by `env` and never printed by `status`. |
| MySQL durability | **Verified, measured** | CI reads back a row written before `stop` after `up` in persistent mode, and finds none after `up --mode ephemeral`. Tests: `TestCloudSQLMySQLAcrossRestart`, `TestCloudSQLMySQLDataPlane`. |
| MySQL in the console | **Verified** | Cloud SQL's MySQL page (#868): databases, tables, columns and indexes, an SQL editor that reads by default and writes as the application's user in an opt-in, confirmed Read-write mode (#995), and create and drop database, through the console API and in headless Chrome. See "Cloud SQL for MySQL from the console" under Console. Tests: `TestConsoleCloudSQLMySQLSchemaAndReadOnlyQuery`, `TestConsoleCloudSQLMySQLCreateAndDropDatabase`, `TestConsoleCloudSQLMySQLReadWriteEditor`, `TestCloudSQLMySQLCreateQueryAndDropThroughThePage`. |
| The Cloud SQL Admin API: `sql.instances.list`, `sql.instances.get` | **Verified** | `TestSQLAdminInstancesDescribeTheRunningServers` (#1301), official Go client `google.golang.org/api/sqladmin/v1`, on the `sqladmin` port (`9020`, `CLOUDBURROW_SQLADMIN_ENDPOINT`; v1 under `/v1/` and v1beta4 under `/sql/v1beta4/`). Each running server is one instance in every project: `postgres` (`POSTGRES_17`) and `mysql` (`MYSQL_8_4`), `RUNNABLE`, `databaseInstalledVersion` read from the server (`MYSQL_8_4_11`), connection name `{project}:us-central1:{instance}` (CloudBurrow has no regions), and one `PRIMARY` address, `127.0.0.1`. The port is not in the resource, as it is not on Cloud SQL: it is `PGPORT` or `MYSQL_PORT`. An unknown instance is 404. Settings (tier, flags, backups) are fixed placeholders, not configuration. |
| The Cloud SQL Admin API: `sql.databases.insert`, `sql.databases.list`, `sql.databases.get`, `sql.databases.patch`, `sql.databases.update`, `sql.databases.delete` | **Verified** | `TestSQLAdminDatabasesAndUsersAreTheServers` (#1301), on both servers, and through `gcloud sql` (`TestGcloudSQL`, via `gcloud-setup`'s `sql` override) and Terraform (below): each runs `CREATE DATABASE`, `ALTER DATABASE` or `DROP DATABASE` in the server, and is read back from `pg_database` or `information_schema.SCHEMATA` with `pgx` and `go-sql-driver/mysql`; on MySQL the application's user is granted the new database, as the console does. A second insert is 409; the database the server was initialised with is refused 400. A MySQL charset and collation change lands; PostgreSQL fixes a database's encoding at creation, so a change is 501. **Not Cloud SQL's way:** an error is the HTTP answer itself, not a DONE operation carrying it. |
| The Cloud SQL Admin API: `sql.users.insert`, `sql.users.list`, `sql.users.get`, `sql.users.update`, `sql.users.delete` | **Verified** | Same test: `BUILT_IN` users (IAM users and service accounts: the IAM database authentication row, #1944). PostgreSQL: `CREATE ROLE … LOGIN CREATEDB CREATEROLE`, which connects as itself. **The password is stored but never checked**: the server trusts local connections, as it always has. MySQL: `CREATE USER 'name'@'%'` (or the host given) with every privilege, a password MySQL checks, and after `users.update` only the new one logs in; on `up`'s server `root` and `cloudburrow` cannot be deleted, and on a created instance `'root'@'%'` can (#1993: the next row). Other user types (IAM) are 501. Tests: `TestSQLAdminDatabasesAndUsersAreTheServers`. |
| Cloud SQL for MySQL without `'root'@'%'` (#1993): `sql.users.delete` of `root`, `sql.users.list`, `sql.users.get`, `sql.users.insert`, `sql.instances.export`, `sql.instances.import`, `sql.backupRuns.insert`, `sql.instances.restoreBackup`, `sql.instances.clone`, `sql.instances.restart`, `sql.instances.patch` | **Verified** | `TestCloudSQLMySQLRootDeleted`, official Go client `google.golang.org/api/sqladmin/v1` and `cloud.google.com/go/cloudsqlconn` (MySQL driver), on a `MYSQL_8_4` instance: CloudBurrow manages it through its own `cloudsqladmin` account at the loopback hosts, as Cloud SQL manages through system accounts gcloud cannot display ([users](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/users)); `users.list` lists `root@%` and the test's user and no system account; an instance whose account was dropped (one made before #1993) still answers, and has it again after `activationPolicy` `NEVER` then `ALWAYS`; `users.delete` of `'root'@'%'` succeeds, `users.get` of it is then 404, `users.delete` of `cloudsqladmin` 404 and `users.insert` of it 400; then an SQL export and its import, a backup, a change and its restore (rows and users the backup's, `root` still deleted), a clone (with the source's databases) and a restart all work. `TestCloudSQLMySQLRootDeletedReplica`: a read replica of such an instance replicates and is promoted. `TestCloudSQLIAMDatabaseAuthentication` deletes the MySQL instance's `root` before its IAM users sign in. Upgrading the primary to `POSTGRES_13`, older than its replica, is 400 with or without `includeReplicasForMajorVersionUpgrade`: the rebuild would roll the replica back, and "you can't roll back the database version of the replica" (wording UNVERIFIED, re-read 2026-11-18). |

creates databases and users through the Cloud SQL Admin API, works too, and since #1330 so does
one that creates instances or connects through the Cloud SQL Go connector, or uses backups, read
replicas and point-in-time recovery, and since #1408 high availability (`REGIONAL`, `instances.failover`);
project-level backups, final backups, the Data API (`executeSql`), `truncateLog` and upgrade pre-checks since #1462;
IAM database authentication for IAM users and service accounts does since #1944 (groups do not), and a legacy failover replica is 400 as on Cloud SQL (#1462); `pointInTimeRestore` and Backup and DR backups do with `--services backupdr` (#1433). See [cloudsql.md](cloudsql.md) and
[#121](https://github.com/cloudburrow/cloudburrow/issues/121).

### Memorystore is not an emulator

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| A real Redis-compatible server, locally | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreDataPlane` (#296), with `github.com/redis/go-redis/v9` and nothing of CloudBurrow's: SET/GET, MULTI/EXEC, PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE and Lua EVAL against the host endpoint, and GET from a pod through `memorystore.cloudburrow.svc.cluster.local:6379`. Valkey 8.1.10, digest-pinned. The host address comes from `REDIS_HOST`/`REDIS_PORT` as `cloudburrow env` exports them. |
| Durability | **Verified, measured** | CI stops and starts the persistent compat instance and `TestMemorystoreAcrossRestart` reads back a key written before the stop; brought up again in `--mode ephemeral`, the same test finds no key. This evidence tolerates one retry: `TestMemorystoreAcrossRestart` is on CI's [retry-once list](#retried-once). Persistent mode is an append-only file on a PVC, fsynced every second, so up to a second of writes can be lost on a crash; ephemeral mode writes nothing to disk. |
| The Memorystore admin API (`redis.googleapis.com`) | **Partial** | Served since #1302: see [Memorystore for Redis](#memorystore-for-redis--googlecloudredisv1). The instance `up` runs is described; instances are created, resized and deleted, each a server of its own of its `redis_version` (Redis 6.2, Redis 7.0 or Valkey 8.1), exported to and imported from Cloud Storage as RDB files, with RDB persistence (#1384), and upgraded, failed over and their maintenance rescheduled (`TestMemorystoreVersionsAndUpgrade`, `TestMemorystoreStandardTierFailover`, `TestMemorystoreLocationsOperationsMaintenance`; the Memorystore rows). |
| Console screen | **Verified** | The Memorystore page (#1302) lists the instances through the admin API's `ListInstances`, offers **Flush** (FLUSHALL, confirmed) on the instance `up` runs (`TestConsoleMemorystoreFlush`), and **Create instance**, **Edit** and **Delete** through `CreateInstance`, `UpdateInstance` and `DeleteInstance`, with the AUTH string on an instance's page (`TestConsoleMemorystoreCreateEditDelete`). Recorded in [console-parity.md](console-parity.md) §3. |
| Google-published component | **No** | Google publishes no Memorystore emulator. Valkey is the server Memorystore for Valkey runs; Memorystore for Redis runs Redis, with which Valkey is protocol-compatible. |
| Authentication | **None** on the server `up` runs; **AUTH** on a created instance with `auth_enabled` | No password on the server `up` runs, as for Cloud SQL: nothing in CloudBurrow authenticates a request, and the host endpoint is loopback only; an application that sends `AUTH` to it gets an error. An instance created with `auth_enabled` runs with `--requirepass` set to a generated string (a UUID, as Google's are), which `GetInstanceAuthString` returns; without it a client gets NOAUTH (`TestMemorystoreCreateConnectUpdateDelete`). The string is in the server's Deployment arguments in the cluster. |

An application that talks RESP works. An application that calls the Memorystore admin API can
list and describe the instance `up` runs, and create, resize and delete BASIC instances of its
own, each a real Valkey server. See [memorystore.md](memorystore.md) and
[#296](https://github.com/cloudburrow/cloudburrow/issues/296).

**Bigtable starts without the network.** Its emulator is in the pinned Cloud SDK emulators image
and is the container's command; nothing is installed when the container starts (#611, #604).

Not covered, and not claimed: Firestore
indexes and security rules, Datastore composite indexes, Spanner dialects other than
GoogleSQL, and backup/restore for any of them.

### Host endpoints survive a backend restart

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Advertised host port after a pod restart | **Verified** | `TestHostEndpointSurvivesABackendRestart` restarts the pod and requires the printed address to both accept a connection **and carry a request**; this evidence tolerates one retry, since the test is on CI's [retry-once list](#retried-once). Each tunnel binds a pod the forwarder chooses itself: the newest one that is Ready and **not being deleted**. `kubectl port-forward svc/…` could bind a pod that was terminating but still Ready during a rollout, such as `up --mode ephemeral` replacing a persistent pod, and connections through it hung (#381). |

This was broken until the restart criterion exposed it: the forwarder started `kubectl
port-forward` once and watched nothing, so a crash, an OOM kill, an eviction or a rollout left
the advertised endpoint dead for the life of the instance, while the pod was `Running`, the
service existed, and the startup banner still printed the address. Worse than a refusal: the
port still **accepted connections** and carried nothing, so a client's `connect()` succeeded
and every request timed out.

The tunnel is supervised and re-established on the **same** host port — the address has
already been printed, may be in an application's configuration, and for storage is baked into
the backend's advertised download URL, so reconnecting elsewhere would be a different kind of
broken. `Restarts()` counts re-establishments, because surviving a restart and never noticing
one are different states.

**Why it still flaked in CI (#526), measured:** `kubectl port-forward` does **not** exit when
its pod is deleted while the tunnel is idle. It keeps listening, fails the *next* connection's
stream, and exits only then. A supervisor that watched only for the process exiting therefore
kept a dead tunnel until a client tripped over it, and on a loaded runner the relaunch that
followed could bind the Service, resolving to whichever pod kubectl found, Ready or not.
Three failed CI runs showed the shape: the emulator up within a second of the restart, every
forwarder reporting its process alive, and clients timing out for minutes reading a server
preface that never came. Now the supervisor **watches the bound pod** and replaces the tunnel
within seconds of the pod going, **binds only a Ready, non-terminating pod** when it
re-establishes (never the Service), and counts a tunnel as up only once a probe connection
through it is **carried**, not merely accepted, using kubectl's own stream errors as the
signal. Each exit and re-establishment is logged, so a diagnose bundle says what the tunnel
did. In-process: `TestATunnelWhosePodIsGoneIsReplacedWithoutAClient`,
`TestRelaunchWaitsForAReadyPodInsteadOfTheService`, `TestALaunchWhoseStreamFailsIsRetried`,
against a fake kubectl.

**The builder is `linux/amd64` only.** On arm64 it runs under emulation and emits an amd64
image, which needs an amd64-capable node. CloudBurrow reports this rather than letting it
surface as a scheduling failure.

## Local AI

**Text generation works**, on a runtime CloudBurrow builds from Google's source. See
[local-ai.md](local-ai.md), including §4 — which corrects this page's previous conclusion.

**Not re-run in CI.** The model download and CPU inference are too heavy for per-PR CI, so the
Verified rows in this section and in Vertex AI generation come from runs on a developer machine:
generation on 2026-09-21, embeddings on 2026-10-15 and again on 2026-10-16 (see
[What CI does not run](#what-ci-does-not-run-and-why)).

**Two embedding routes, one served.** The official LiteRT route (Google's
`embedding_litert_lm_main` on Google's EmbeddingGemma artifacts) is blocked on the model export,
so it serves nothing. Embeddings are served from a **community** ONNX conversion on ONNX Runtime
instead. The rows below name the route each one is about.

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Model catalogue with verified provenance | **Verified** | Publisher recorded per artifact; a community conversion is never reported as Google-published. Tests: `TestProvenanceIsRecordedNotAssumed`. |
| Gated-artifact handling | **Verified** | Refused without credentials, with an actionable message. Tests: `TestGatedModelIsRefusedWithoutAToken`, `TestManagerRefusesGatedDownloads`. |
| Disk preflight, checksum verification, atomic cache, recovery | **Verified** | `internal/localai`. Tests: `TestPreflightRefusesAnImpossibleDownload`, `TestAcquireVerifiesChecksum`, `TestCorruptCacheIsDetectedAndRecoverable`. |
| **Linux generation runtime** | **Verified** | `//runtime/engine:litert_lm_main` built from source at commit `02e5030` and run **from the shipped image**: **78.43 tok/s prefill, 31.98 tok/s decode, 0.39 s to first token** over a 144-token generation, CPU backend, warm cache. No LiteRT-LM release publishes a Linux artifact; Linux is nevertheless a documented, supported build target, and the gap is packaging rather than capability. Tests: `TestRealGenerationThroughTheOfficialSDK`. |
| **Linux LiteRT embedding runtime** | **Runs; no model to run** | `//runtime/engine:embedding_litert_lm_main` builds, ships in the runtime image, loads models and initialises its engine. Every obtainable model is then rejected — see [embeddings.md](embeddings.md). |
| **Text generation** | **Verified** | On `litert-community/gemma-4-E2B-it.litertlm` (2.59 GB, ungated). Tests: `TestRealGenerationThroughTheOfficialSDK`. |
| **A Google-published runnable model** | **Not available** | Every one is `gated: manual`. The model that works is a **community** conversion and is labelled as one everywhere it appears. |
| **Embeddings on the LiteRT runtime (official artifacts)** | **Blocked on the model export, not the runtime and not access** | Embeddings are served by the community ONNX route instead (next row); this row is about the LiteRT route alone. The earlier statement — *every embedding artifact is gated* — was **wrong**: three are ungated. They fail for another reason. One ships with no tokenizer at all; rebuilt correctly with Google's own `litert-lm-builder` it reaches `Input tensor bytes must be 4 but got 2048`, as does an independent bundle from a different publisher. The conversions export a fixed `[1,512]` encoder signature and the engine requires a dynamic one. No flag bridges it. See [embeddings.md](embeddings.md). |
| **Embeddings (community ONNX int8 EmbeddingGemma)** | **Verified** (measured 2026-10-15) | Maintainer decision 2026-09-28 (#41): `embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community`, onnx-community's ONNX int8 conversion of EmbeddingGemma — **NOT an official Google artifact**, and labelled so in the API response (`modelDisplayName`, `X-CloudBurrow-Model-Provenance`), the console and the catalogue. Pinned to `onnx-community/embeddinggemma-300m-ONNX` revision `5090578d`, each file by SHA-256, licence `gemma`, fetched over HTTPS by `up -local-ai-embeddings`. Runs on ONNX Runtime only in a `-tags onnx` build; the default build answers every `:predict` 501. **Measured against the real model** (#41) on an Apple M4 Max (48 GB, macOS 27.0.1, darwin/arm64), `make onnx-compile`'s `bin/cloudburrow-onnx` with ONNX Runtime 1.29.0 (the official `onnxruntime-osx-arm64-1.29.0.tgz` release, checked by SHA-256; the version `onnxruntime_go` v1.36.0's headers name) and libtokenizers v1.27.0: `up -local-ai-embeddings` fetched and verified the pinned files; 768, 512, 256 and 128 dimensions, every value finite, each a unit vector, the smaller sizes the renormalised prefix of 768 (cosine ≥ 0.9999); task types change the vector and an unknown one is 400; a sourdough-bread query scored 0.6108 against a bread-making passage and 0.0928 against an interest-rate one. An 11-token input took 37 ms per request (median of 10, warm); the whole CLI process was 1.3 GB resident. `TestEmbeddingGemmaThroughTheOfficialSDK`, official `google.golang.org/genai` on its Vertex AI backend, run where `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_EMBEDDINGS` names such an instance's local AI endpoint. The official LiteRT artifacts remain blocked as described in [embeddings.md](embeddings.md). |

a red circle, a blue square and a green triangle are each nearest the text naming them (0.757, 0.770 and 0.783 against at most 0.636 for the others). **Audio (#1651)**: a WAV clip (integer PCM of 8 to 32 bits or float, mono or stereo, 8 to 192 kHz) is decoded, downmixed as Transformers.js's `load_audio` does (√2 · (L + R) / 2), resampled to 16 kHz (Kaiser-windowed sinc, libswresample's default filter), and prepared as the model's `Gemma4AudioFeatureExtractor` prepares it (zero-padded to 128 samples, semicausal 320-sample periodic Hann frames every 160 samples, the 512-point FFT magnitude through 128 HTK mel filters to 8 kHz, log(x + 0.001), frames not wholly in the clip masked); the audio encoder keeps every fourth frame, 25 soft tokens a second, placed between the audio markers. **Checked against Transformers.js 4.3.1** on the same ONNX files (2026-10-19, CPU): the model card's 11-second `jfk.wav` at 16 kHz mono, the same clip after `Speech:`, two copies of it, and a 44-second clip (the reference's 30-second default truncation raised) gave the same token counts and vectors (cosine 1.000000); the original 44.1 kHz stereo file, which CloudBurrow resamples and the reference was given resampled by ffmpeg, 0.999821. Measured: 279 tokens for `jfk.wav`, which scores 0.769 / 0.502 / 0.486 against the model card's speech / cats / turtle queries (the card: 0.763 / 0.504 / 0.487, q4 on WebGPU). | Output quality | **Not claimed** | The measured run answered a factual question wrongly. That is a small quantised model's quality; CloudBurrow does not present model output as correct. |
| Benchmarks | **Measured, single sample** | One run on one machine (Apple M4 Max, arm64, CPU, container). Not a benchmark, and no comparison is drawn from them. Two conditions change them substantially: a **cold** XNNPACK cache raises init from 0.31 s to 3.27 s, and a **short** answer collapses decode speed (6.89 tok/s over two tokens on the same binary) because the first token's fixed cost is averaged over the generation. |
| Pinned artifact checksums | **Absent** for the Google artifacts · **Verified** for the community ONNX embedding files | The Google artifacts are gated, so they could not be downloaded and hashed; the status reports the absence rather than implying verification. The three files of `embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community` are pinned by SHA-256 in `internal/localai/catalog.go` and verified before use: the files `up -local-ai-embeddings` fetched on 2026-10-16 hash to those pins (`shasum -a 256`). The seven of `embeddinggemma-2-onnx-community` (#1454, the audio encoder's two since #1651) hash to theirs, fetched on 2026-10-19 by hand and by the Local models page's Download. |
| Runtime distribution | **Published per release; not yet exercised by one** | Each release builds `deploy/litert-lm/Dockerfile` natively for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, pushes `ghcr.io/cloudburrow/litert-lm:<tag>`, attests the index, and records its digest in the release notes. A release CLI defaults `--local-ai-image` to that digest and pulls it on first use; a checkout build defaults to `cloudburrow/litert-lm:local` from `make litert-lm`, never pulled (#602). No release has run this job yet, so no published digest exists. Locally, the Dockerfile builds it: **6m17s measured** from a cold cache on an M4 Max with 16 CPUs, once, producing a 274 MB image. Debian 13 is the base because Abseil needs C++20 `<source_location>`, which Debian 12's default clang 14 lacks. |
| Runtime image completeness | **Verified** | The image is run, not merely built. `litert_lm_main` links `libGemmaModelConstraintProvider.so` — shipped prebuilt upstream, found via a `RUNPATH` into Bazel's output tree — so a multi-stage build that copies only the binary produces an image that builds cleanly and fails on first run. The prebuilt libraries are staged and registered with `ldconfig`. Tests: `TestRealGenerationThroughTheOfficialSDK`. |
| Catalogue artifact filenames | **Verified against the live API** | `TestCatalogArtifactsExistUpstream` (tag `upstream`) lists each repository and asserts the named file is in it, and HEADs the resolve URL for entries marked ungated. It was written after the community entry was found naming `gemma-4-E2B-it-int4.litertlm`, a filename inferred from the `google/` repositories' convention, which returns **404**. |

## Vertex AI generation (local)

A **subset** of `generateContent`, served by the runtime CloudBurrow builds. Not a Vertex
emulator and not a Gemini replica. See [generation.md](generation.md) for the exact surface.

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|

| `streamGenerateContent` (SSE) | **Verified** | 12 events over 741 ms through the SDK's own stream iterator. A unit test additionally asserts the first event arrives *while generation is still running*, so streaming cannot regress into buffering. A failure after the first event (the 200 is already sent) is a final `data:` event carrying Google's JSON mapping of `google.rpc.Status`, the same body as an error response: `{"error": {"code", "message", "status"}}` with the canonical code's name in `status` (`INTERNAL`, not Go's `Internal`; #1471); `TestStreamGenerateContentFailureEventHasCanonicalStatus` (unit). No compat test: making a real runtime fail partway through needs the model and a fault it has no way to inject. `google.golang.org/genai` v1.73.0 reads such a `data:` event as an empty response rather than an error; the body decodes into its `APIError` (`TestStreamFailureEventDecodesAsTheSDKsAPIError`). |

The arguments are constrained by LiteRT-LM's LLGuidance tool-call grammar built from the declared schemas (`parameters`, converted from Vertex's OpenAPI subset, or `parametersJsonSchema`), which also applies the mode: `AUTO` text and/or calls, `ANY` calls only (one allowed name forces it), `NONE` text only, `VALIDATED` text or calls limited to `allowedFunctionNames`. | Token accounting (`usageMetadata`) | **Verified** for generation (measured 2026-11-19, #1937) and for embeddings | Every `generateContent` response, and the final event of every stream, carries `usageMetadata`: `promptTokenCount` (the same count as `countTokens`), `candidatesTokenCount` (the tokens the engine decoded, from its own counters), `totalTokenCount`, and `promptTokensDetails` / `candidatesTokensDetails` as `TEXT` (omitted for a prompt with images, whose per-modality split the runtime does not report). A generation ended by a stop sequence is stopped before the engine counts what it decoded, so it reports the prompt's count only. Intermediate stream events carry none (UNVERIFIED, re-read 2026-11-19 in the v1beta1 protos (cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform v1.127.0): Vertex's carry a partial one). `trafficType`, `thoughtsTokenCount` and `cachedContentTokenCount` are not reported. Asserted by every #1937 compat test above and `TestStopSequenceKeepsThePromptCount`. The embedding model counts with its own tokenizer too: `EmbedContent` (gRPC and REST `:embedContent`) answers `usage_metadata.prompt_token_count` and `total_token_count`, and text-embedding `:predict` answers `statistics.token_count` (measured 2026-10-16; `TestEmbedContentThroughThePredictionClient`). |
| Prompt/output separation | **Verified** | The runtime echoes the prompt before generating, and echoes a multi-line prompt across lines, so forwarding from the marker returned the caller's own prompt as generated text. The echo is now skipped by matching rather than counting, which stays correct if a future runtime stops echoing. Covered against a simulated runtime in both directions and against the real one by `TestRealMultiLinePromptIsNotEchoedBack`. |
| Cancellation | **Verified** | A cancelled request kills the runtime container by name. Found by testing: killing the `docker run` client left the container generating, because it is a client for work in the daemon and the runtime ignores `SIGTERM`. Tests: `TestRealCancellationStopsTheRuntime`, `TestCancellationStopsGeneration`. |
| Output quality, safety, or equivalence to Gemini | **Not claimed** | No test asserts what the model says. |
| Embeddings from an official LiteRT artifact | **Blocked on the model export** | The LiteRT route serves nothing. See [embeddings.md](embeddings.md): ungated artifacts do exist, and the runtime rejects them. Embeddings are served from the community ONNX conversion (next row). |
| Text-embedding `:predict` subset | **Verified** (measured 2026-10-15) | `POST /v1` (and `/v1beta1`) `/projects/{p}/locations/{l}/publishers/google/models/embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community:predict` only: `instances[].content`, `task_type` (EmbeddingGemma's prompt prefixes), `title`; `parameters.autoTruncate`, `outputDimensionality` (768/512/256/128, truncated and renormalised). Any other model is 404, never substituted. Response `predictions[].embeddings.values` and `statistics`. Unit-tested with a fake runtime (`TestPredictServesOnlyTheCommunityIdentity`), and run against the real model through the official `google.golang.org/genai` SDK (Vertex AI backend, `Models.EmbedContent`, which sends `:predict` for a model that is not Gemini) by `TestEmbeddingGemmaThroughTheOfficialSDK` (#41; gated on `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_EMBEDDINGS`; numbers and machine in the Embeddings row above). Over gRPC, `cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform`'s `PredictionClient` reaches the same model through `Predict` (#1193) and `EmbedContent` (#1244), and REST `:embedContent` is served too; see the PredictionService table below. The genai SDK cannot send `autoTruncate: false` (its field is `omitempty`), so that refusal is unit-tested only. `embeddinggemma-2-onnx-community` (#1454), once loaded, answers the same subset with its own vectors (`TestEmbedContentEmbedsImagesThroughThePredictionClient` checks its `Predict` through the PredictionClient); `:predict` carries text only, its images go through `EmbedContent`. A **community conversion, not an official Google artifact**. Console: Agent Platform → Embeddings. |

## Vertex AI custom prediction

Google's **serving contract**, on CloudBurrow's **own runtime**. See
[prediction.md](prediction.md) for the decision and its reasoning.

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AIP_HTTP_PORT` / `AIP_HEALTH_ROUTE` / `AIP_PREDICT_ROUTE` honoured | **Verified** | `TestPredictionEndpointServesTheVertexContract` deploys with **non-default** routes and asserts the defaults return 404, so the environment is proven plumbed through rather than coincidentally matching. Names checked against `google.cloud.aiplatform.constants.prediction` 2.1.3. |
| Health route reports readiness | **Verified** | Same test. Any 2xx is healthy, as Vertex defines it; a redirect is not. Tests: `TestPredictionEndpointServesTheVertexContract`, `TestHealthyStatus`. |
| `{"instances":[...]}` → `{"predictions":[...]}` | **Verified** | Same test, decoded through `internal/prediction` types rather than string matching. Tests: `TestPredictionEndpointServesTheVertexContract`. |
| One prediction per instance enforced | **Verified** | `prediction.ValidateResponse`; a mismatched count is a 500, not a mis-attributed result. Tests: `TestValidateResponseRequiresOnePredictionPerInstance`, `TestServeCatchesABrokenPredictor`. |
| `parameters` passed to the container | **Verified** | `TestPredictionDeadlineBoundsASlowPrediction` drives the fixture's delay through it. |
| Malformed input refused | **Verified** | Empty instances, wrong instance type, unknown field and invalid JSON all return 400. Tests: `TestPredictionEndpointServesTheVertexContract`. |
| Caller deadline bounds a slow prediction | **Verified** | A 10s prediction fails a 2s caller, and the endpoint remains usable afterwards. Tests: `TestPredictionDeadlineBoundsASlowPrediction`. |
| Endpoint deletion is complete | **Verified** | `TestPredictionEndpointDeletionIsComplete`; `GetService` then returns `NotFound`. |
| Startup failure reported with the container's output | **Verified** | `TestPredictionStartupFailureIsReported`. The adapter prefers Knative's `ConfigurationsReady` message over the top-level `does not have any ready Revision`. |
| **Startup-failure latency** | **Verified** | Knative declares a revision failed only after its `progress-deadline`, and Cloud Run v2 exposes no field that shortens it; with Knative's default `600s` the failure was reported after **602s, measured** (#568). `up` sets the deadline to `240s`, Cloud Run's default startup-probe budget, on install and on an already-installed cluster (`TestKnativeInstallSetsTheRevisionProgressDeadline`, `TestAnAlreadyInstalledKnativeGetsTheProgressDeadline`). Until then the endpoint reports `PENDING`. |
| `AIP_STORAGE_URI` artifact download | **Verified** for registry models (#1940) | A Model Registry model's `artifactUri` is copied into the managed bucket `cloudburrow-vertex-models-{project}` and `AIP_STORAGE_URI` names the copy; the fixture container loads its weights from it through `STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST` (`TestModelRegistryDeploysACustomContainer`). A Cloud Run service deployed directly sets whatever it sets itself; nothing is copied for it. |
| `LocalModel.deploy_to_local_endpoint` | **Declined by design** | It runs `containers.run(detach=True)` outside the cluster — unowned by readiness, reset or delete. Execution goes through the owned runtime instead. |
| `LocalModel.build_cpr_model` | Available, not invoked | CloudBurrow accepts any image honouring the contract; it does not build one for you. |
| Vertex model registry, `Endpoint` and `DeployedModel` resources | **Verified** (#1940) | `TestModelRegistryDeploysACustomContainer`, `TestGcloudAIModelsAndEndpoints`; see [Model Registry and Endpoints](#model-registry-and-endpoints-1940). |
| Prediction through `PredictionService` | See [below](#vertex-ai-predictionservice--googlecloudaiplatformv1) | The official `aiplatform` PredictionClient reaches a deployed container as `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/endpoints/{service}` (#1193). |
| Model Garden, tuning, batch prediction | **Not supported** | Out of scope. |
| Console: Online prediction | **Verified** | Agent Platform → Online prediction lists the Cloud Run services that set an `AIP_*` variable, read through `ListServices`, and sends `{"instances","parameters"}` to one's predict route through the cluster ingress; the container's status and body are shown verbatim, its own 400s included, and the console's refusals (not a JSON array, not deployed) are kept apart from them (`TestConsoleOnlinePredictionThroughTheConsoleAPI`, `TestCloudRunPredictorAnswersOnlinePredictionInTheBrowser`). Needs the ingress published on a host port; see [playground.md](playground.md) §8. |
| **GPU / accelerators** | **Not supported** | CPU only, on every platform. NVIDIA is untested and nothing configures it. On Apple Silicon a Linux container has no Metal device, so no configuration achieves it — **NVIDIA container flags do not establish Metal acceleration**. |

The host-advertised URI is the cluster ingress address and the Knative gateway is not
published on a host port, so a host-side caller reaches an endpoint through a port-forward
with the service in the `Host` header. In-cluster callers use the cluster-local name
directly. Both are documented in [prediction.md](prediction.md#reaching-the-endpoint).

## Vertex AI PredictionService — `google.cloud.aiplatform.v1`

The local AI endpoint serves `google.cloud.aiplatform.v1.PredictionService` over **gRPC** on the
same port as its JSON routes, so `cloud.google.com/go/aiplatform`'s `PredictionClient`, which has
no REST transport, reaches it (#1193). Each method converts its request to the JSON its route
reads and calls the same function, so both protocols refuse and answer a request identically.
The endpoint starts whenever Cloud Run is enabled, with or without a local model; its address is
the `local AI:` line `up` prints. Two resource name shapes are served:
`projects/{p}/locations/{l}/endpoints/{service}`, where `{service}` is the Cloud Run service ID of
a deployed [custom prediction container](prediction.md), relayed to its `AIP_PREDICT_ROUTE`
through the cluster ingress; and `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/publishers/google/models/{model}`,
for the [embeddings](embeddings.md) and [generation](generation.md) subsets. The same endpoint
names are served as JSON at `POST /v1/{endpoint}:predict` and `:rawPredict`. A custom endpoint
whose model declares `grpcPorts`, its service's port named `h2c`, also serves the raw gRPC
methods, relayed to the container's gRPC server (#1477).

| Method | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Predict` | **Verified** | `TestPredictionClientReachesACustomEndpoint`: the official `aiplatform` v1.127.0 PredictionClient against a deployed container on non-default `AIP_*` routes; one prediction per instance (a different count is `INTERNAL`, never a mis-attributed result), `deployedModelId`, `parameters` passed through, the container's own 400 as `INVALID_ARGUMENT` in its words, an endpoint not deployed `NOT_FOUND`. On a publisher model it is the text-embedding `:predict` subset, with provenance in `modelDisplayName` and the `x-cloudburrow-model-provenance` header: `TestEmbeddingGemmaThroughThePredictionClient` (needs the model, `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_EMBEDDINGS`; not run in CI; passed 2026-10-15 on darwin/arm64 with ONNX Runtime 1.29.0, on the same instance and run as `TestEmbeddingGemmaThroughTheOfficialSDK` and the custom-endpoint test) and unit tests comparing it to the JSON route. |
| `RawPredict` | **Verified** (publisher models measured 2026-10-15) | Custom endpoints: same test; the body is relayed to the container's predict route and its answer returned as `HttpBody`. Publisher models (#1284): the model's native body, answered by the same code as its typed method, so the same subset and refusals: on `embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community` the text-embedding `:predict` body, answered as `:predict` answers it (provenance in `x-cloudburrow-model-provenance`); on the generation model the `generateContent` body, answered with a `GenerateContentResponse`. A `http_body.content_type` other than `application/json` is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming it; another model is `NOT_FOUND`, never substituted; no embedding runtime is the same 501 as `:predict`, no generation runtime the same `FAILED_PRECONDITION` as `generateContent`. Also served as JSON at `POST /v1` (and `/v1beta1`) `/{model}:rawPredict`. `TestRawPredictOnTheEmbeddingModel` and `TestRawPredictOnTheGenerationModel` (official `aiplatform` PredictionClient, gRPC; need the models, `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_EMBEDDINGS` and `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_LOCALAI`; not run in CI) passed 2026-10-15 on darwin/arm64 against `embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community` (ONNX Runtime 1.29.0) and `gemma-4-e2b-it-community` in a `make litert-lm` runtime; the REST route is unit-tested (`TestRawPredictREST`). Console: Agent Platform → Embeddings, Method RawPredict. |
| `GenerateContent` | **Verified** | The `generateContent` subset of [generation.md](generation.md), unary, from the same code as the JSON route: the same refusals (every generation option, tools, multi-turn) and no substitution. `TestStreamGenerateContentThroughThePredictionClient` (official `aiplatform` v1.127.0 PredictionClient, gRPC; needs the model, `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_LOCALAI`; not run in CI) passed 2026-10-15 on darwin/arm64 against `gemma-4-e2b-it-community` in a `make litert-lm` runtime: one candidate, `STOP`, `modelVersion` the model that ran; `temperature` `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming it; `gemini-2.0-flash` `NOT_FOUND`. Console: Vertex AI Studio (`/agent-platform/studio`) with **Stream** off (#1257). |
| `StreamGenerateContent` | **Verified** | The same subset, streamed (#1257) from the same code as the JSON `:streamGenerateContent` route: one `GenerateContentResponse` per chunk as the runtime decodes it, each naming the model, `STOP` on a final message of its own and on no other; a refusal before the first chunk is the unary call's status, word for word; a failure after one ends the stream `INTERNAL` naming it. Same test and run: 7 messages over 1.83 s, the first after 1.36 s; the same refusals as `GenerateContent`. Unit tests assert the first message arrives while generation is still running. Console: Vertex AI Studio with **Stream** on, the default. Tests: `TestStreamGenerateContentThroughThePredictionClient`, `TestGRPCStreamArrivesBeforeGenerationFinishes`, `TestGRPCStreamFailureAfterFirstChunkIsVisible`. |
| `EmbedContent` | **Verified** (text measured 2026-10-15; images, audio and `file_data` 2026-10-19; MP3, HEIC, HEIF, animated WebP, AVIF, video, PDF, MPEG-2.5, a video's audio track, VP9 and AV1 video and `document_ocr` on scanned PDFs 2026-11-17; multichannel and A-law WAV and monochrome H.265 2026-11-18; surround AAC, multichannel HE-AAC, QuickTime G.711 tracks and 3-bit IMA ADPCM 2026-11-18; 2- and 5-bit IMA ADPCM and MP3 in a WAV 2026-11-18; video frames over 8K UHD, GSM 6.10 and MPEG Layer II WAV 2026-11-18; G.726, MPEG Layer I and Layer II joint stereo WAV and arithmetic-coded and 12-bit JPEG 2026-11-18) | On `projects/{p}/locations/{l}/publishers/google/models/embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community` (text) and `embeddinggemma-2-onnx-community` (text, images and audio, #1454, #1651), from the same local model as text-embedding `:predict` (#1244); also served as JSON at `POST /v1` (and `/v1beta1`) `/{model}:embedContent`. Honoured: `content` (text parts, joined with newlines), `title`, `task_type` (EmbeddingGemma's prompt prefixes; `UNSPECIFIED` is the model's default), `output_dimensionality` (768/512/256/128, truncated and renormalised) and `auto_truncate`, each at the top level or in `embed_content_config` (both set to different values is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`). Refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the field: another size, an unknown task type, a non-text part (`content.parts[i]`), `document_ocr`, `audio_track_extraction`. Another model is `NOT_FOUND`, never substituted; a build without embeddings answers the same 501 (`UNIMPLEMENTED`) as `:predict`. Response `embedding.values`, `usage_metadata.prompt_token_count`, `truncated`; provenance in the `x-cloudburrow-model-provenance` header. `TestEmbedContentThroughThePredictionClient` (official `aiplatform` v1.127.0 PredictionClient, gRPC; needs the model, `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_EMBEDDINGS`; not run in CI) passed 2026-10-15 on darwin/arm64 with ONNX Runtime 1.29.0, its vector equal to `Predict`'s for the same input (cosine ≥ 0.9999); the REST route is unit-tested (`TestEmbedContentREST`). **Not reachable from `google.golang.org/genai`:** on its Vertex backend, `Models.EmbedContent` sends `:embedContent` only for a model whose name contains `gemini` or `maas`, and `:predict` otherwise. **Images (#1454)**, on `embeddinggemma-2-onnx-community` only, in the request shape Google documents for `gemini-embedding-2` ([Get multimodal embeddings](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/embeddings/get-multimodal-embeddings), re-read 2026-10-19, page last updated 2026-10-15): an `inline_data` part with `mime_type` `image/png` or `image/jpeg`, or (#1651) `image/webp` (lossy, lossless, with or without alpha) or `image/bmp`, or (#1724) `image/heic` or `image/heif` (HEVC-coded; the container's crop, rotation and mirror applied; an image sequence's first frame), or (#1729) `image/avif` (8 to 12 bits, alpha; crop, rotation and mirror applied; an AVIS image sequence's first frame), and an animated WebP as its first frame (Google's page says nothing of animation and documents no refusal): every type Google lists for `gemini-embedding-2` (the doc re-read 2026-11-17: "JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP, HEIC, HEIF, AVIF"), each side at most 16384 pixels, at most 6 images, alone or between text parts of one `Content`, which is embedded as **one** vector in the space of the model's text vectors (Google: "Image and text embedding vectors are in the same semantic space with the same dimensionality"); the task prefix applies when there is text, and an image-only content has none, as the model card says to pass media; `prompt_token_count` counts each image's soft tokens. **Audio (#1651)**: an `inline_data` part with `mime_type` `audio/wav` (or `audio/x-wav`, `audio/wave`, `audio/vnd.wave`) or (#1721) `audio/mpeg` (the type Google's samples send; or `audio/mp3`, `audio/mpeg3`, `audio/x-mp3`, `audio/x-mpeg`, `audio/x-mpeg-3`), alone or among text and image parts, up to 180 seconds of audio a request (Google's limit), embedded in the same vector; `prompt_token_count` counts 25 soft tokens a second. **`file_data` (#1651)**: a `gs://{bucket}/{object}` `file_uri`, the form Google's samples use, is read from this instance's Cloud Storage (up to 64 MiB) and embedded as `inline_data` of its `mime_type`, or of the object's content type when the part has none; a missing object or bucket is `NOT_FOUND` naming which, and an instance without Cloud Storage answers `FAILED_PRECONDITION` saying so; the object is read only from this instance's own storage endpoint, never Google's, and with none bound the read is refused before any request (unit `TestEmbedObjectsReadsLocalStorageOnly`). Since #1736 a 10- or 12-bit AVIF decodes up to 16384 × 16384 too (it was `UNIMPLEMENTED` over 13312 × 13312, the WebAssembly decoder's 4 GiB of memory). Refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the field: another image type, a HEIC, HEIF or AVIF that does not decode (an AV1-coded HEIF among them: "the data is not a valid image/heif image"), a file that is not of its `mime_type` (`the data is not a valid MP3 file: …`, likewise WAV), a second video, a PDF of more than 6 pages, a second PDF, a seventh image, more than 180 seconds of audio, and any image or audio on `embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community`, which embeds text only. REST bodies up to 20 MiB. **Valid media this build does not decode is `UNIMPLEMENTED` (501), not `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (#1651)**, naming what is not decoded, since Google would embed it: a video's audio track in a codec not decoded (QuickTime IMA ADPCM `ima4`...; HE-AAC, AC-3, E-AC-3 and surround Opus are decoded since #1739, FLAC, ALAC, A-law and µ-law since #1651), an AAC track of the Main or SSR profile or of 960-sample frames, HE-AACv2 parametric stereo with 34 bands, IPD/OPD or mixing procedure B, a PCM track or WAV of a sample format not decoded (multichannel Microsoft ADPCM or G.726...; GSM 6.10 and MPEG Layer II are decoded since #1651's fourth round, G.726, MPEG Layer I and Layer II joint stereo since its fifth) or a sample rate outside 8 to 192 kHz, a WAV of more than 8 channels with no channel mask naming them, a JPEG, PNG or BMP that uses a feature its decoder lacks (a lossless or hierarchical JPEG, an RLE BMP...; arithmetic-coded and 12-bit JPEG are decoded since #1651's fifth round), a video frame over 16384 × 16384 (Google documents no video frame size; its image limit is 16384 × 16384), and an `http://` or `https://` `file_uri`, which Vertex AI's `FileData` also takes: an instance fetches nothing from outside the machine. **Multichannel and G.711 WAV (#1651)**: a WAV of 3 to 8 channels, or of as many as its `WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE` channel mask names, is downmixed to mono as ffmpeg's resampler downmixes it (`-ac 1`, measured channel by channel with ffmpeg 9: the front, front-of-centre and top-front pairs at √½, the centre at 1, the back, side and back-centre channels at ½, the LFE and the other top channels dropped; stereo stays √2 · (L + R) / 2), its channels named by the mask when the mask names as many as there are and else by ffmpeg's default layout for the count (2.1, 4.0, 5.0, 5.1, 6.1, 7.1); a layout with one channel of a left/right pair and not the other, which ffmpeg refuses to downmix, is `UNIMPLEMENTED`. A video's 3- to 8-channel PCM track is downmixed the same way (it was taken as pairs of channels before). 8-bit A-law and µ-law WAV are decoded as ffmpeg's `pcm_alaw` and `pcm_mulaw` decode them (ITU-T G.711). Unit `TestDecodeMultichannelAndG711WAV` (5.1 and plain 7.1 WAV and a 5.1 PCM MOV within 6e-8 of ffmpeg 9's decode, A-law and µ-law exact), `TestWAVLayoutsAndRefusals`. **Surround AAC, multichannel HE-AAC, QuickTime G.711 and 3-bit IMA ADPCM (#1651)**: a video's AAC track of channel configuration 0 (a `program_config_element`, as ffmpeg writes 7.1(wide) and 6.1; `third_party/aac-go/pce.go`, from ISO/IEC 14496-3's PCE syntax), 7 and 11 (AudioToolbox's 7.1 and 6.1) and 12 (ffmpeg's 7.1), SBR over more than two channels (5.1 HE-AAC), a QuickTime `ulaw` or `alaw` track, and a 3-bit IMA ADPCM WAV are decoded as ffmpeg 9 decodes them and downmixed as it downmixes them: within 2.4e-7 of its downmix for AAC-LC, 1.3e-5 for 5.1 HE-AAC, G.711 and ADPCM sample for sample (unit `TestDecodeMultichannelAACTracks`, `TestDecodeG711Tracks`, `TestDecodeADPCMWAV`, `TestParseASCProgramConfig`). Multichannel Microsoft ADPCM stays `UNIMPLEMENTED`: no encoder writes it and ffmpeg 9 decodes a packet of several such blocks as one block, so there is no decode to check against. **2- and 5-bit IMA ADPCM, MP3 in a WAV and video over 8K UHD (#1651)**: 2- and 5-bit IMA ADPCM WAVs (16 samples in 4 bytes and 32 in 20 a channel, the 4-byte words interleaved as the 4- and 3-bit ones are) decode sample for sample as ffmpeg 9's `adpcm_ima_wav` does (unit `TestDecodeADPCMWAV`; fixtures from a scratch encoder, since ffmpeg writes neither), and a WAV of MP3 frames (`WAVE_FORMAT_MPEGLAYER3`) decodes whole, as ffmpeg's wav demuxer passes every frame to its decoder, within one or two 16-bit steps (`TestDecodeMP3WAV`). | `DirectPredict`, `ServerStreamingPredict`, `StreamingPredict`, `StreamDirectPredict` | **Verified** (measured 2026-10-15) | The tensor methods (#1285). Each input `Tensor` becomes the JSON instance it carries (`struct_val` an object, `list_val` a list, a typed value array a scalar when it has one element and no `shape`, else a list) and each prediction an output (a number list as a `DOUBLE` vector), with `Predict`'s code behind it. Embedding model: the text-embedding instance and parameters, one message per request with the 768-value (or smaller) vector. Generation model: exactly one input, the Model Garden text instance `{"prompt": string_val}`, answered `{"content": string_val}`: one message per decoded chunk on `ServerStreamingPredict` and `StreamingPredict`, the whole text on `DirectPredict` and `StreamDirectPredict`. Custom endpoints: relayed as `Predict`, one message. Bidirectional streams need `endpoint` on the first request; a later one may omit or repeat it, not change it. Refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the field: any other prompt-instance field (`inputs[0].struct_val.max_tokens`, …), any `parameters` on the generation model (the runtime applies no option), `tensor_val`, `bytes_val`, a tensor mixing value types. Another model is `NOT_FOUND`; no runtime is the same 501 or `FAILED_PRECONDITION` as `Predict` and `generateContent`. `TestStreamingPredictOnTheGenerationModel` and `TestStreamingPredictOnTheEmbeddingModel` (official `aiplatform` PredictionClient, gRPC; need the models; not run in CI) passed 2026-10-15 on darwin/arm64 against `gemma-4-e2b-it-community` (`make litert-lm`) and `embeddinggemma-300m-onnx-community` (ONNX Runtime 1.29.0). Console: the Playground and Embeddings screens send the same requests in JSON form. |
| `DirectRawPredict`, `StreamDirectRawPredict`, `StreamingRawPredict` | **Verified** (measured 2026-10-16) | Relayed to the gRPC server in a custom endpoint's model (#1477). A model's `containerSpec.grpcPorts` is deployed as its Cloud Run service's container port named `h2c`, which Cloud Run serves end to end over HTTP/2 cleartext (#1475); the call goes through the cluster ingress with the service's host as `:authority`. `method_name` is the gRPC method called, `/namespace.Service/Method` with or without Vertex's documented trailing slash (anything else is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`); `input` is sent as its request message and each response message returned as `output`, bytes unchanged. `DirectRawPredict` is one call (2 minutes when the caller sets no deadline: a cold start); the two streaming methods are one bidirectional stream each, live both ways: each request's input is sent as it arrives, each message the container sends is returned as it arrives, and closing the caller's side closes the container's. The first request names `endpoint` and `method_name`; a later one may omit or repeat them, and changing either is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (one stream is one call). The container's own status keeps its code and message, prefixed with the endpoint. An endpoint whose model declares no `grpcPorts` (no `h2c` port) is `FAILED_PRECONDITION` naming them; one not deployed is `NOT_FOUND`; a publisher model is `UNIMPLEMENTED` (the local models run in-process and serve no gRPC). `TestPredictionClientReachesAModelsGRPCServer` (official `aiplatform` PredictionClient, gRPC) against Kubernetes' agnhost 2.53, pinned by digest, serving `grpc.health.v1.Health`: `Check` answers `SERVING` on all three methods, an unserved method is the container's `UNIMPLEMENTED`, a malformed `method_name` `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; passed 2026-10-16 on darwin/arm64 with `--services run`. Console: Online prediction's DirectRawPredict form, on an endpoint whose model declares `grpcPorts` (`TestConsoleDirectRawPredictThroughTheConsoleAPI`). |

| `Explain` | **Verified** (Sampled Shapley, measured 2026-10-16) | On a custom endpoint (#1454): Vertex Explainable AI's Sampled Shapley method, computed as Vertex computes it for a custom container, from predictions alone: for each of `path_count` (1–50) random orderings of the features, each feature in turn moves from its baseline to the instance's value, and is credited with the change in the output; the container's predict route is called once, with every perturbed instance. Answered as `ExplainResponse`: one `Explanation` per instance, an `Attribution` per explained output (`baseline_output_value`, `instance_output_value`, `feature_attributions` keyed by feature, `output_index` for a list output), the predictions and `deployed_model_id`. A prediction must be a number or a list of numbers; `top_k` (default 1) or `output_indices` chooses the outputs. On Vertex the spec lives on the DeployedModel; a Cloud Run predictor has none, so it is `explanation_spec_override`'s: `parameters.sampled_shapley_attribution` and `metadata.inputs` (a struct instance's keys, or the one input of a non-struct instance), each with `input_baselines` (several are averaged over; a number with none is 0). No override is `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, as Vertex answers for a model deployed without a spec; integrated gradients and XRAI, and example-based explanations (`parameters.examples` or `examples_override`), are `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the custom container, as Vertex documents them only for TensorFlow models (integrated gradients and XRAI in a prebuilt TensorFlow container, examples for a model that outputs an embedding) and Sampled Shapley for "any custom-trained model (running in any inference container)" ([overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/explainable-ai/overview), #1454); a publisher model is `UNIMPLEMENTED`; a `deployed_model_id` other than the container's is `NOT_FOUND`. The orderings come from a fixed seed, so one request's attributions are reproducible. Also served as JSON at `POST /v1/{endpoint}:explain`. Unit `TestExplainSampledShapleyOnAScalarModel`, `TestExplainSampledShapleyOnAStructModel` (attributions sum to the output's change; a linear output is attributed exactly) and `TestExplainRefusals`; `TestPredictionClientReachesACustomEndpoint` (official `aiplatform` v1.127.0 PredictionClient, gRPC; the Cloud Run shard) passed 2026-10-16 on darwin/arm64 against the doubling predictor: `x` credited with all of 6 from a baseline output of 0; no override `FAILED_PRECONDITION`; integrated gradients, XRAI and `examples` each `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the custom container (re-run 2026-10-16 on darwin/arm64). The official Go client has no REST transport for `PredictionService`, so `:explain` over REST is unit-tested only. Console: Agent Platform → Online prediction's **Explain** (#1454) sends the Sampled Shapley path count and each feature's `input_baselines` as `explanation_spec_override` and shows the attributions per feature; `TestConsoleExplainMatchesThePredictionClient` (the Cloud Run shard) passed 2026-10-16 on darwin/arm64, the console's attributions, baseline and instance outputs equal to the official PredictionClient's for the same request, and a path count of 51 the same `INVALID_ARGUMENT` through both; `TestCloudRunPredictorAnswersOnlinePredictionInTheBrowser` sends it from the form in Chrome. Integrated gradients, XRAI and example-based explanations are named in the page's not-served list. |


### Model Garden: Hugging Face deployments (#1840)

`ModelGardenService.Deploy` deploys a Hugging Face model (`hugging_face_model_id`) on the same
endpoint, over gRPC and JSON (`POST /v1/projects/{p}/locations/{l}:deploy`, through the REST
transcoder of the same implementations). The serving engine is the one Google's Model Garden picks
for the model's pipeline task: **vLLM** (Apache-2.0, `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu`, its CPU build) for
text-generation, text2text-generation and image-text-to-text, and **Text Embeddings Inference**
(Apache-2.0, `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference:cpu-*`) for feature-extraction and
sentence-similarity, both pinned by digest in `dependencies.json`, with Model Garden's serving
arguments (`--max-model-len=4096` capped at the model's context, `--dtype=auto`,
`--max-num-seqs=256`, `--disable-log-stats`). The engine runs as a Docker container beside the
instance's kind cluster (`cloudburrow-<instance>-mg-<endpoint>`, published on 127.0.0.1 only), on
the downloaded files mounted read-only; no token is passed into it. `stop` removes the containers
and `up` starts them again. The TEI image is published for linux/amd64 only, so arm64 hosts run it
emulated. The test downloads about 1.3 GB of models and runs about 6.4 GB of images, so it is
opt-in (`CLOUDBURROW_TEST_HF_DEPLOY=1`) and runs in no CI shard.

### Model Registry and Endpoints (#1940)

`ModelService` and `EndpointService` keep models (with versions and aliases) and endpoints (with
deployed models and a traffic split), persisted in the instance's state directory
(`vertexai/registry.json`), over gRPC and through the REST transcoder at `/v1/...` (`gcloud ai`
reaches them through the `aiplatform` override `cloudburrow gcloud-setup` writes, Terraform
through `vertex_ai_custom_endpoint`). A deployed model is a real container: `DeployModel` creates a
Cloud Run service (`aip-dm-{deployedModelId}-{hash}`) in the instance's cluster from the version's
`containerSpec` (image, command, args, env, the one port, predict and health routes as the
startup probe), with Google's `AIP_*` variables (`AIP_HTTP_PORT`, `AIP_HEALTH_ROUTE`,
`AIP_PREDICT_ROUTE` with Google's defaults, `AIP_STORAGE_URI`, `AIP_MODE`, `AIP_MODE_VERSION`,
`AIP_MODEL_NAME`, `AIP_ENDPOINT_ID`, `AIP_DEPLOYED_MODEL_ID`, `AIP_VERSION_NAME`,
`AIP_PROJECT_NUMBER`, `AIP_MACHINE_TYPE`, `AIP_FRAMEWORK`), min and max replicas as its scaling, and
the operation completes when the container answers its health route. Predict, RawPredict and
Explain go to the deployed model the traffic split picks. Model Garden's models and endpoints
(above) share the same methods. The Python SDK's documented flow, `aiplatform.Model.upload(...)`
then `model.deploy(...)` and `endpoint.predict(...)`, runs against it over REST
(`TestPythonAIPlatformUploadAndDeploy`, google-cloud-aiplatform 2.9.0 in a container on an internal
Docker network, with the ADC fixture in the `cloudburrow.localhost` universe); it polls its
operations under `/ui/{name=projects/*/locations/*/…/operations/*}`, the first binding Google's
service config gives `GetOperation`, which is served beside `/v1` and `/v1beta1`.

**Prebuilt prediction containers.** Google's prebuilt images
([pre-built containers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/pre-built-containers),
re-read 2026-11-20) are `{us,europe,asia}-docker.pkg.dev/vertex-ai/prediction/IMAGE:latest` (and
`vertex-ai-restricted/prediction/` for the optimized TensorFlow runtime), several GB each, and this
instance never downloads them. `UploadModel` accepts any of those URIs, as Google does. Locally, such
a URI names an image of this instance's Artifact Registry: `us-docker.pkg.dev/vertex-ai/prediction/sklearn-cpu.1-6:latest`
is the image `sklearn-cpu.1-6:latest` of the `DOCKER` repository
`projects/vertex-ai/locations/us/repositories/prediction`. `DeployModel` of a model with a prebuilt
URI the local registry does not hold is **`FAILED_PRECONDITION`**, naming the repository to push it
to, before anything is started or pulled; once the image is pushed there (with `docker push`, or by
`ExportModel` of another model's image), it is deployed from the local registry, pulled through the
nodes' registry mirror (`/etc/containerd/certs.d/{location}-docker.pkg.dev`, written at `up` for
every Artifact Registry location, the `us`, `europe` and `asia` multi-regions included since #1940,
so a pull of those hosts is never sent to Google). Whatever is pushed there runs as a custom
container: it must serve the custom container contract itself (`AIP_HTTP_PORT`, the health and
predict routes, its artifacts from `AIP_STORAGE_URI`); none of Google's prebuilt servers (TensorFlow
Serving, scikit-learn, XGBoost, PyTorch) is reimplemented. The older `gcr.io/cloud-aiplatform/...`
paths are refused at `DeployModel` the same way, as this instance serves no Container Registry.
`TestModelRegistryExportsTheImageToArtifactRegistry` deploys a model whose image is
`us-docker.pkg.dev/vertex-ai/prediction/sklearn-cpu.1-6:latest`, refused, then served from the image
exported there, and Predict answers from it. A locally built `dev.local/` image is loaded into the
cluster as before; on Docker Desktop with its containerd image store, the kubelet was measured
(2026-11-20) not to see a kind-loaded image (`ErrImageNeverPull`), so the tests push the fixture to
the instance's Artifact Registry, which avoids that.
Console: Agent Platform → Model Registry and Endpoints (`TestModelRegistryAndEndpointsThroughThePages`).
