### Document AI: processors (#1799)

`google.cloud.documentai.v1.DocumentProcessorService` is served on the same endpoint, over gRPC
and JSON (the JSON through the REST transcoder of the same implementations), so the official
`cloud.google.com/go/documentai` client, gRPC or REST, reaches it with the endpoint's address;
nothing is sent to Google. It is what BigQuery ML's `ML.PROCESS_DOCUMENT` calls (the BigQuery
section's `CLOUD_AI_DOCUMENT_V1` row). Two processor types are served, in the `us` and `eu`
locations: `OCR_PROCESSOR` (Enterprise Document OCR) and `LAYOUT_PARSER_PROCESSOR`. Every page is
read with local Tesseract (`internal/ocr`, the LSTM engine Google developed; PDF pages rendered by
PDFium at 300 DPI). Processors are kept in `<state-dir>/documentai/processors.json`
(`internal/service/vertexai/documentai.go`). Processor versions (`documentaiversions.go`) and
batch processing from and to the instance's Cloud Storage (`documentaibatch.go`) are served (#1930);
field masks, output sharding, the evaluations and human review status are in `documentaioutput.go`
(#1953). `ReviewDocument` (Google's Human-in-the-Loop reviewers) and the dataset methods
(`DocumentService`) are UNIMPLEMENTED. Terraform's `google_document_ai_processor` and
`google_document_ai_processor_default_version` reach the endpoint through `cloudburrow terraform`.

### Speech-to-Text v2: recognizers (#1799)

`google.cloud.speech.v2.Speech`'s recognizers are served on the same endpoint, over gRPC and JSON
(the JSON through the REST transcoder), so the official `cloud.google.com/go/speech` v2 client,
gRPC or REST, reaches them with the endpoint's address; nothing is sent to Google. They are what a
BigQuery ML `SPEECH_RECOGNIZER` names (the BigQuery section's `ML.TRANSCRIBE` row). A recognizer
keeps its display name, annotations and `default_recognition_config`; recognizers are kept in
`<state-dir>/speech/recognizers.json` (`internal/service/vertexai/speechrecognizers.go`). The
deprecated `Recognizer.model` and `language_codes` fields are UNIMPLEMENTED; `GetConfig`,
`UpdateConfig` and the resources' customer-managed keys are served (#1950, `speechcmek.go`, below). `BatchRecognize` (`speechbatch.go`), custom
classes and phrase sets (`speechadaptation.go`, kept in `customclasses.json` and `phrasesets.json`
beside the recognizers), a `RecognitionConfig`'s `adaptation` (`speechbias.go`: phrases, `${class}`
references expanded, and boost bias whisper.cpp's decoder through a logits filter and its initial
prompt), `config_mask`, and `StreamingRecognize` (`speechstream.go`, `speechstreamv2.go`) are served
(#1930), as is v1's `google.cloud.speech.v1.Speech` (`speechv1.go`, below). The models served, all on local whisper.cpp with
OpenAI's Whisper base model rather than Google's: `chirp`, `chirp_2`, `chirp_3`, `chirp_telephony`,
`long`, `short`, `telephony` and `telephony_short`; `medical_dictation` and `medical_conversation`
are UNIMPLEMENTED.
gcloud's v2 commands (`gcloud alpha ml speech recognizers create`, `run-short`, `run-batch`, ...)
cannot reach this endpoint: gcloud 593.0.0 replaces the `speech` override with
`https://LOCATION-speech.googleapis.com/` for each call (`api_lib/ml/speech/client.py`, #1945;
[security](security.md)), so no test runs them, and `gcloud ml speech recognize` is v1's JSON,
which is not served (v1 is gRPC only, below). The console's Speech-to-Text pages (Transcriptions,
Recognizers, Custom classes, Phrase sets) drive the same API through the official client.
UNVERIFIED (re-read 2026-11-19: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.recognizers>):
`recognizer_id`'s exact rule (4 to 63 characters of `[a-z0-9-]`, starting with a letter, here), the
locations served (any), `uid` and `etag` formats, the 30-day `expire_time`, the texts of the errors.

## Speech-to-Text v1 — `google.cloud.speech.v1`

#1930.
`google.cloud.speech.v1.Speech` is served on the same endpoint over gRPC
(`internal/service/vertexai/speechv1.go`), so the official `cloud.google.com/go/speech` `apiv1`
client reaches it with the endpoint's address. A v1 `RecognitionConfig` is read as the v2 config it
maps to (the same local whisper.cpp, decoders and refusals): `ENCODING_UNSPECIFIED` reads a WAV or
FLAC header, `LINEAR16`, `MULAW`, `FLAC` and `MP3` are decoded, and `OGG_OPUS` and `WEBM_OPUS`
(#1799, the v2 decoders; `sample_rate_hertz` must be 8000, 12000, 16000, 24000 or 48000, else
`INVALID_ARGUMENT`, unit `TestSpeechV1Config`; the v1 decode itself is not run against an instance), `AMR` and `AMR_WB` (#1799, opencore-amr's decoders; `TestSpeechRecognitionFeatures1799` reads JFK's sample as v1 `AMR`) are decoded and the Speex encoding is UNIMPLEMENTED; models `default`, `latest_long`, `video` read as `long`, `phone_call` as
`telephony`, `latest_short` and `command_and_search` as `short`, the medical models UNIMPLEMENTED;
`speech_contexts` and `adaptation`'s inline phrase sets and custom classes bias the decoder as v2's
`adaptation` does, while `phrase_set_references` (v1's `Adaptation` service is not served),
`abnf_grammar`, `alternative_language_codes`, `enable_separate_recognition_per_channel`,
diarization and `transcript_normalization` are UNIMPLEMENTED; `profanity_filter`,
`enable_spoken_punctuation` and `enable_spoken_emojis` are v2's (#1799, `TestSpeechRecognitionFeatures1799`).
UNVERIFIED (re-read 2026-11-19: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.speech.v1>, which does not say): the model mapping, the texts of the errors other than Google's quoted one.

For audio longer than 1 min use LongRunningRecognize with a 'uri' parameter.". Unit `TestSpeechV1Config`. |

## Credentials, metadata and external tooling

**CloudBurrow authenticates nothing.** These exist so that tools which insist on credentials
can run offline. See [credentials.md](credentials.md).

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| IAM Credentials `generateAccessToken` for impersonation | **Verified** | `TestIAMCredentialsImpersonation` (#1747), with the official `cloud.google.com/go/iam/credentials/apiv1` client, and `TestImpersonatedTokenUsedWithACloudBurrowClient` (#303), whose `google.golang.org/api/impersonate` token drives an official Storage client through a transport that fails any request not bound for loopback, and Python's `test_impersonated_token_drives_the_storage_client`. On a service account of the IAM API (below) the call is Google's ([Service account credentials](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-creds), read 2026-11-17): the caller is the account a live access token this instance minted names (none or any other bearer is 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`); it must hold `iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken` on the account, its project, the project's folders or the organization, which Google's hierarchy makes it inherit (`TestIAMImpersonationInheritsGrants`, #1750: a grant on the folder or the organization works and stops when removed), through any role that holds it: a custom role, or any predefined role of Google's catalog (#1746), such as `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator`, `roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` or a service agent role (`roles/cloudbuild.serviceAgent`); a role without it (`roles/iam.serviceAccountViewer`) grants nothing. A deleted account's bindings match no caller, and each of `delegates` `iam.serviceAccounts.implicitDelegation` on the next, else 403 "Permission 'iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken' denied on resource (or it may not exist)." (an account that does not exist answers the same); an account minting for itself is `FAILED_PRECONDITION` "You can't create a token for the same service account that you used to authenticate the request."; a disabled account is `FAILED_PRECONDITION`; `scope` is required; `lifetime` is at most 3,600 s (`constraints/iam.allowServiceAccountCredentialLifetimeExtension` is not modelled). The token is minted for, and recorded as, the target, so Memorystore's IAM auth and Firestore with MongoDB compatibility check the target's roles. The instance's own account (`-` or the ADC fixture's email) is not an IAM service account and keeps #303's behaviour: no permission is checked. |
| IAM Credentials `generateIdToken` | **Verified** | `TestIAMCredentialsImpersonation` (#1747): needs `iam.serviceAccounts.getOpenIdToken` (Token Creator, OpenID Token Creator), as above; the JWT has the audience, the account's unique ID as `sub`, and with `includeEmail` its email; it is signed with this instance's key and verifies against the local `/certs`, never against Google's. Unit: `TestImpersonatedIDTokenVerifiesAgainstTheLocalCerts`. |
| IAM Credentials `signJwt` | **Verified** | `TestIAMCredentialsImpersonation` (#1747): needs `iam.serviceAccounts.signJwt`; signs the payload's claims with the account's system-managed key, whose ID it returns in `keyId` and the header's `kid`, and the signature verifies against that key's X.509 certificate from `GetServiceAccountKey`. An `exp` more than 12 hours ahead is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. The account's public certificates are served as Google serves them at `www.googleapis.com` (row below), and `golang.org/x/oauth2/jws` verifies a signJwt token against them (`TestIAMServiceAccountCertURLs`, #1750). As the instance's own account it signs with the instance key, unit-tested. |
| IAM Credentials `signBlob` | **Verified** | `TestIAMCredentialsImpersonation` (#1747): needs `iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob`; an RSA SHA-256 signature by the account's system-managed key, verified against its certificate. The signature is local: a signed URL made with it is accepted by the instance's Cloud Storage (`TestStorageSignedURLIAMServiceAccount`, #1787), by no Google service. As the instance's own account, `UNIMPLEMENTED`, naming the reason. |
| A service account's public certificate URLs: `/service_accounts/v1/metadata/x509/EMAIL`, `/service_accounts/v1/metadata/jwk/EMAIL`, `/robot/v1/metadata/x509/EMAIL` | **Verified** | `TestIAMServiceAccountCertURLs` (#1750), on the metadata port, with no credentials and no `Metadata-Flavor` header, as `www.googleapis.com` serves them: x509 is a JSON object of key IDs to PEM X.509 certificates, jwk a JSON Web Key Set (`RSA`, `RS256`, `sig`), each of the account's enabled, valid keys, its system-managed one (which signBlob and signJwt sign with) included, so `golang.org/x/oauth2/jws` verifies a signJwt token against either; a created key file's `client_x509_cert_url` is this instance's robot x509 URL for the account, which holds that key until it is deleted. An account that does not exist or is deleted is 404 `NOT_FOUND` (Google's body for it is not documented). Google's `raw` form is not served. |
| `cloudburrow env` shell/JSON/plain export | **Verified** | `TestEnvExportsEveryClientVariable`, `TestEnvPrintsARunningInstancesLivePorts`; an instance that is not running is refused with nothing on stdout, `TestEnvRefusesAnInstanceThatIsNotRunning` (#630). Only the running instance's services are exported, `TestEnvExportsOnlyTheServicesARunningInstanceServes` (#652). Exports the client-library variables *and* the `gcloud` endpoint overrides, because `gcloud` ignores the former. |
| ADC fixture usable by Google's auth library | **Verified** | `TestOfficialAuthLibraryUsesTheLocalFixture`: `google.FindDefaultCredentials` mints a token through the fixture. The test fails if a `ya29.` token appears, which would mean it reached Google with the developer's real credentials. |
| Token exchange stays local | **Verified** | Same test. The fixture's `token_uri`, `auth_uri` and cert URLs all point at the instance. Tests: `TestOfficialAuthLibraryUsesTheLocalFixture`, `TestADCPointsEntirelyAtTheLocalInstance`. |
| Metadata server contract (`/`, project, zone, email, token, identity, scopes, aliases) | **Verified** | `TestMetadataServerAnswersTheContract` and `internal/metadata`. |
| `Metadata-Flavor: Google` required and echoed | **Verified** | Enforced even though the tokens grant nothing: a local server accepting what a real one rejects teaches code to fail in production. Tests: `TestFlavorHeaderIsRequired`, `TestFlavorHeaderIsAlwaysSetOnResponses`. |
| ID token is a valid RS256 JWT | **Verified** | Signed with the instance key and verifiable against `/certs`. Tests: `TestIdentityTokenVerifiesAgainstThePublishedKey`, `TestJWKSPublishesTheSigningKey`. |
| **ID token verifies against Google's certificates** | **Not supported** | Google did not issue it. Tokens are structurally valid and self-consistent; signature verification against Google's public certs is **not** claimed. |
| **Token validation of any kind** | **Not supported** | No OAuth access token, ID token or assertion is ever checked for signature, expiry, audience or scope (Cloud Storage signed URLs are checked and fail closed: their row, `TestStorageSignedURLV4HMAC`). The token endpoint checks only that an assertion was *sent*, so a client silently sending none finds out. |
| **IAM, scopes, per-resource permissions** | **Not supported** | Every caller can do everything. |

The JSON API serves them as the discovery document defines them, through the transcoder's overlay of the run v2 descriptors (`rest.Overlay`): accepted, stored and returned, in the pool, in its operations, and as `update_mask` paths (`scaling.minInstanceCount`). gRPC answers as the proto defines it: the fields travel in `WorkerPoolScaling` as unknown fields under CloudBurrow's own numbers, which a client's parser skips. `TestRunWorkerPoolAutomaticScaling`, the official `google.golang.org/api/run/v2` client: a pool created `AUTOMATIC` with minimum 2, maximum 4 and CPU target 0.6 reads back as set and runs two instances; patching `scaling.minInstanceCount` to 1 keeps the revision and stops one; the gRPC client reads it. `TestTerraformRunWorkerPoolAutomaticScaling`, hashicorp/google 8.4.0 with egress blocked: `scaling_mode = "AUTOMATIC"` with `min_instance_count` / `max_instance_count` applies, plans clean, changes in place and destroys. **Limits enforced:** `cpuUtilization` between 0.1 and 0.90 inclusive, or 0.0 to disable it (as the discovery document states), otherwise INVALID_ARGUMENT; negative counts INVALID_ARGUMENT; a minimum above a set maximum INVALID_ARGUMENT (UNVERIFIED for worker pools, docs re-read 2026-11-18: Google documents no such rule for them, <https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.workerPools>). **Behaviour:** `MANUAL` (or unset) runs `manualInstanceCount`, as before; `AUTOMATIC` runs `minInstanceCount` instances, split among revisions by `instanceSplits` as the field's description says, and is given no default `manualInstanceCount`. Changing the mode or a count keeps the revision, as Google documents for manual scaling (<https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/workerpools/manual-scaling>, re-read 2026-11-18). What signal grows an `AUTOMATIC` pool, and how its CPU target is measured, Google does not document (UNVERIFIED, docs re-read 2026-11-18: the worker pool docs describe manual counts and external autoscalers only, <https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/workerpools/crema-autoscaling>); locally (#1789) an `AUTOMATIC` pool with a `cpuUtilization` is scaled by CloudBurrow's CPU driver (`internal/adapter/run/cpuscaling.go`) on metrics-server's pod CPU, measured as Cloud Run measures a service's (usage over the instance's CPUs against the target, a 10% tolerance, <https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-instance-autoscaling>): each revision's share grows toward its share of `maxInstanceCount` while CPU is above the target, and returns toward its share of `minInstanceCount` once it has been below for a minute; a pool without `cpuUtilization` stays at its minimum. `TestRunWorkerPoolCPUScaling` (official `google.golang.org/api/run/v2` client, an image built from `testdata/cpuburn`): a pool `AUTOMATIC` 1-3 at 0.5 whose instances burn their CPU grows to 3, never above, and returns to 1 after. `max_surge` and `max_unavailable` are in no discovery document and stay refused. Service-level `scaling` and revision `cpuUtilization` / `concurrencyUtilization` are #1790. Console: Deploy, Edit and Scale offer the scaling mode, the instance count, the minimum, the maximum and the CPU target (`TestConsoleRunWorkerPoolAutomaticScaling`). |
| `Service.scaling` (`scalingMode`, `minInstanceCount`, `maxInstanceCount`, `manualInstanceCount`) and `RevisionTemplate.scaling.cpuUtilization` / `concurrencyUtilization` | **Verified** | #1790 (cloud.google.com/go/run v1.25.0, which adds `RevisionScaling.cpuUtilization` and `concurrencyUtilization`). Service-level counts are divided among the revisions in the resolved traffic by percent, the first-listed revision taking what rounding leaves, and written onto each Knative Revision's `autoscaling.knative.dev/min-scale` / `max-scale`, which KPA applies in place: a scaling change creates no revision, as Google documents. Combined with revision-level values as <https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/min-instances> and `.../max-instances` say (read 2026-11-18): the highest minimum wins, the lowest maximum caps it; under `MANUAL` (<https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/manual-scaling>) a revision runs exactly its share, revision-level min/max are ignored, and a tag-only revision runs at most one instance. `concurrencyUtilization` is KPA's `target-utilization-percentage`. `TestRunServiceLevelScaling`, the official `cloud.google.com/go/run` client: a service created with service-level minimum 2, maximum 5 and `concurrencyUtilization` 0.8 reads back as set and runs two pods; a masked update to `MANUAL` 3 keeps the revision and runs three. `TestTerraformRunServiceLevelScaling` (hashicorp/google 8.4.0, egress blocked): the `scaling` block applies, plans clean and changes in place. `TestGcloudRunServiceLevelScaling`: `gcloud run deploy --min=1 --max=3` and `gcloud run services update --scaling=2`, through v1's `run.googleapis.com/minScale`, `maxScale`, `scalingMode` and `manualInstanceCount` service annotations. **Limits enforced:** `cpuUtilization` 0.1-0.90 or 0.0, `concurrencyUtilization` 0.1-0.95 or 0.0, not both 0.0 (INVALID_ARGUMENT, as the proto states); negative counts INVALID_ARGUMENT; a template minimum above its maximum INVALID_ARGUMENT; `manualInstanceCount` outside `MANUAL` INVALID_ARGUMENT (UNVERIFIED, docs re-read 2026-11-18, <https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/reference/rest/v2/projects.locations.services>). **CPU (#1800):** `cpuUtilization` (Cloud Run's 60% when unset, 0.0 off) is CloudBurrow's CPU driver (`internal/adapter/run/cpuscaling.go`) on metrics-server's pod CPU, measured as <https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/about-instance-autoscaling> describes (usage over the instance's CPUs, the container's limit or 1, against the target, with a 10% tolerance; scale-in after a minute below): its recommendation is written into the revision's `min-scale` as a floor under KPA's concurrency recommendation, within the maximum, so the larger of the two drivers wins, as Google says. `TestRunServiceCPUUtilizationScaling` (official client, an image built from `testdata/cpuburn`): a revision 1-3 at 0.5 with four CPU-burning requests in flight, far below its concurrency limit, grows to 3, never above, and returns to 1 once the load stops. **Disabled service (#1800, #1802):** `MANUAL` with `manualInstanceCount` 0, as <https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/manual-scaling> documents (re-read 2026-11-18): the serving revisions run no instance, in-flight requests finish, and "any further requests to the service URL will fail with a `Service unavailable` or `Service disabled` error": the URL answers HTTP 503 with the body `Service unavailable` (the page names no status code: 503 is UNVERIFIED, re-read 2026-11-18); "revisions that are only active due to traffic tags are not impacted": their tag URLs keep serving, at most one instance each; the revision and the `uri` are kept, and a count again serves again. Locally the service's URL is taken from Knative's route (its placeholder Service, named after the route, is labelled `networking.knative.dev/visibility: cluster-local`, which Knative applies to that traffic target only, so tag URLs keep their routes) and given its own KIngress, `<service>.unavailable`, owned by the Knative Service, whose shares for revisions with no instances go to an Envoy responder (the gateway's own image) answering 503 `Service unavailable` (`internal/adapter/run/serviceunavailable.go`). `TestRunServiceDisabledByManualZero`, `TestRunServiceDisabledAnswersUnavailable` (official client: a service with a tag-only revision, disabled, answers 503 `Service unavailable` at its URL while the tag URL keeps answering from the tagged revision; `MANUAL` 1 serves the URL again) and `TestTerraformRunServiceDisabled` (hashicorp/google 8.4.0, `scaling_mode = "MANUAL"`, `manual_instance_count = 0`). Whether a tag URL of a revision that has traffic but no instances fails too is not documented: locally it keeps serving (UNVERIFIED, re-read 2026-11-18). **A `MANUAL` split leaving a serving revision at zero (#1802):** "If the number of revisions receiving traffic exceeds the manual instance count, some of the revisions will have no instances. Traffic sent to those revisions will get the same error as if the revisions were disabled": the count is divided by percent, the first-listed revision taking what rounding leaves, so `MANUAL` 1 over 50/50 runs the first revision's one instance and the second's share of the URL's requests answers 503 `Service unavailable`. `TestRunServiceManualSplitLeavesOneAtZero` (official client: 40 requests answer about half from the first revision and half 503 `Service unavailable`, never from the second; one pod runs; `MANUAL` 2 serves both). **CPU-only scaling (#1802):** `concurrencyUtilization` 0.0 disables the concurrency driver, "to scale only by CPU" (<https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/scaling-controls>, read 2026-11-18). KPA cannot be turned off, so the revision's KPA target becomes its concurrency limit at 100% (`autoscaling.knative.dev/target` = `maxInstanceRequestConcurrency`, or Cloud Run's largest, 1000, when unset): KPA then asks only for the instances the requests in flight cannot otherwise fit into, and the CPU driver scales. `TestRunServiceCPUOnlyScaling` (official client, `testdata/cpuburn`): concurrency limit 10, 1-3 instances, `cpuUtilization` 0.5, `concurrencyUtilization` 0.0: eight requests that only wait stay on one instance (at the default 0.6 target they would need two), CPU-burning requests grow it to three, and it returns to one. Google's page says Adaptive Concurrency Tuning stays active when a driver is disabled; nothing locally limits concurrency below `maxInstanceRequestConcurrency`. **Terraform (#1802):** hashicorp/google 8.4.0's `google_cloud_run_v2_service` `template.scaling` has no `cpu_utilization` or `concurrency_utilization` (its provider schema, read 2026-11-18); 8.5.0 is the first release with both. `TestTerraformRunServiceScalingControls` (hashicorp/google 8.5.0, its own lock file `test/compat/testdata/terraform-8.5.0/.terraform.lock.hcl`, egress blocked): `cpu_utilization = 0.7` and `concurrency_utilization = 0.8` apply, read back through the official client and plan clean; `concurrency_utilization = 0` changes them in place and plans clean. **gcloud (#1802):** `gcloud beta run services update --scaling-cpu-target` and `--scaling-concurrency-target` (beta in gcloud 586.0.0, CI's, and GA as well in 593.0.0; `disabled` sends 0.0; the `run.googleapis.com/launch-stage` annotation `gcloud beta` sends on the service is v2's `launchStage`, accepted and, like `client`, not read back) write v1's `run.googleapis.com/scaling-cpu-target` and `run.googleapis.com/scaling-concurrency-target` template annotations, which map onto `template.scaling.cpuUtilization` / `concurrencyUtilization` and back. `TestGcloudRunServiceScalingControls`: both targets set, `--scaling-concurrency-target=disabled`, and both disabled refused. Console: Deploy and Edit offer service scaling and both targets (`TestCloudRunServiceScalingThroughTheForms`). |

| Terraform, other services' endpoints | **Not set** | `cloudburrow terraform` sets an endpoint only for a service with a Verified row here, and names the enabled services it left out: their resources would otherwise be sent to real Google. Cloud KMS is wired (#425): `kms_custom_endpoint` is set, and `TestTerraformKMS` applies, plans clean, updates and destroys a key ring, a key and their IAM members over the JSON API. BigQuery is wired (#1236): `big_query_custom_endpoint` is set, for the datasets, tables, views and routines and their IAM resources `TestTerraformBigQueryIAM` applies; `TestTerraformBigQueryAccess` (#1304) adds `google_bigquery_dataset_access` and `google_bigquery_row_access_policy`, and `TestTerraformBigQueryPartitionedTableAndJob` partitioned and clustered tables and `google_bigquery_job` (query jobs); other BigQuery resources (connections, reservations, data transfer, Analytics Hub) are not tested and have endpoints of their own, which are not set. Firestore is wired (#1331): `firestore_custom_endpoint` is set to the emulator's port, and the provider's token is `owner`, the emulator's admin token (any other bearer it rejects as an invalid JWT). Bigtable is wired (#1331) by `BIGTABLE_EMULATOR_HOST`, which the wrapper sets for the binary it runs: the provider's Go Bigtable clients then dial the emulator in plaintext. Spanner is wired (#1331): `spanner_custom_endpoint` is set to the emulator's REST port (`--port-spanner-rest`). Artifact Registry and Cloud Build are wired (#1304): `artifact_registry_custom_endpoint` and `cloud_build_custom_endpoint` are set to the Run port; so is Cloud Run v1's `cloud_run_custom_endpoint` (#1304), at `{{location}}-run.localhost` on loopback, as its URLs are regional (`TestTerraformCloudRunDomainMapping`); without Cloud Run, a `google_cloud_run_*`, `google_artifact_registry_*` or `google_cloudbuild_*` resource is refused as below, and `google_cloudbuildv2_*` always is. Cloud Functions v2 is wired (#1377): `cloudfunctions2_custom_endpoint` is set to the Run port, and without Cloud Run a `google_cloudfunctions2_*` resource is refused; so is Cloud Functions v1 (#1428), `cloud_functions_custom_endpoint`, whose `google_cloudfunctions_function` is the row below's. When the instance does not serve one of them (for Spanner, its REST port, as with `--port-spanner-rest 0`), `cloudburrow terraform` exits non-zero, naming the resources, for any subcommand but `init`, `fmt`, `validate`, `version`, `providers` and `get` while the module declares a `google_firestore_*`, `google_spanner_*` or `google_bigtable_*` resource or data source (`TestTerraformRefusesWhatItCannotPoint`). |

## Memorystore for Redis — `google.cloud.redis.v1`

**Built, over real servers** (#1302). `--services memorystore` serves the admin API in the CLI
process, on `--port-memorystore-admin` (default `9021`), gRPC and JSON on one port as
`redis.googleapis.com` does, with `google.longrunning.Operations` for its operations. `env`
exports `CLOUDBURROW_MEMORYSTORE_ENDPOINT`; no client library reads it, so pass it to
`option.WithEndpoint`. `gcloud-setup` writes `api_endpoint_overrides/redis` and `cloudburrow
terraform` sets `redis_custom_endpoint`. Per-method status is generated in
[coverage/memorystore.md](coverage/memorystore.md).

Two kinds of instance. The instance `up` runs is
`projects/<default project>/locations/us-central1/instances/memorystore`, described from the
server itself, never invented; it cannot be updated or deleted. Every other instance is one
`CreateInstance` made: a server of its own, a Deployment and a Service per instance with the same
settings (`components.MemorystoreServer`) and the image of its `redis_version` (Redis 6.2.24 for
`REDIS_6_X`, Redis 7.0.15 for `REDIS_7_0`, Valkey 8.1 for `REDIS_7_2`), reached from the host through its own
tunnel on an OS-assigned port, which the instance's `host` and `port` report.

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CloudRedis.ListInstances`, `CloudRedis.GetInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreAdminDescribesTheServer`, with `cloud.google.com/go/redis/apiv1` against an instance started with `--services memorystore,storage`: the instance `up` runs is listed under `locations/-` and its region, and nowhere in another project; `host:port` is the RESP endpoint (`REDIS_HOST:REDIS_PORT`), which a Redis client then reaches; `state` is READY; `redis_version` is `REDIS_7_2`, from the server's `INFO server` (Valkey 8.1 reports Redis 7.2.4); `memory_size_gb` is 1, from `CONFIG GET maxmemory` (`--maxmemory 1gb`, `--maxmemory-policy volatile-lru`, Memorystore's default policy); tier BASIC, DIRECT_PEERING, transit encryption DISABLED, `auth_enabled` false. A server that does not answer is UNAVAILABLE, not a stale READY. An unknown instance is NOT_FOUND. Created instances are listed beside it, in name order and paged. |
| `CloudRedis.CreateInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreCreateConnectUpdateDelete`: the operation completes (`op.Wait`) with a READY instance, `OperationMetadata` verb `create` and its target; go-redis at the reported host and port is refused NOAUTH without the AUTH string and works with it; `CONFIG GET` shows `memory_size_gb` as `maxmemory` and `redis_configs` as the server's config; the server `up` runs does not have its keys. `TestGcloudRedis` (gcloud 587.0.0, `redis instances create --tier=basic --size=1 --enable-auth --redis-config --labels`) and `TestTerraformRedisInstance` (hashicorp/google 8.4.0) create one too. A create that fails leaves no instance. **What is accepted:** tier BASIC, or STANDARD_HA (#1385, below), `memory_size_gb` 1 to 300, `redis_version` empty or `REDIS_7_2` (Valkey 8.1, which reports Redis 7.2.4), `REDIS_7_0` (Redis 7.0.15) or `REDIS_6_X` (Redis 6.2.24), each a digest-pinned BSD-3-Clause image (#1386, `TestMemorystoreVersionsAndUpgrade`: INFO reports each); `REDIS_3_2` (Redis 3.2.12), `REDIS_4_0` (4.0.14) and `REDIS_5_0` (5.0.14), the last release of each line the Docker official `redis` image built (#1524, `TestMemorystoreEndOfLifeVersions`: INFO reports each; a 3.2 instance upgraded to 4.0 and 5.0 keeps its keys and AUTH; a STANDARD_HA 4.0 instance replicates with `SLAVEOF`, the only name 4.0 has, and fails over keeping its keys; `TestConsoleMemorystoreEndOfLifeVersions`: the console creates a 3.2 instance and upgrades it), with what Memorystore documents for later versions only refused INVALID_ARGUMENT as it documents them (`allkeys-lfu`, `volatile-lfu`, `activedefrag` and `lfu-*` need 4.0, `stream-node-*` and read replicas 5.0), in-transit encryption on them too (#1768, below); `auth_enabled`, `display_name`, `labels`, `location_id` (default `<region>-a`) and `redis_configs` of `maxmemory-policy`, `notify-keyspace-events`, `activedefrag`, `lfu-decay-time`, `lfu-log-factor`, `stream-node-max-bytes`, `stream-node-max-entries` and `maxmemory-gb` (another is INVALID_ARGUMENT). `persistence_config` (#1384) is accepted: see RDB persistence below. **In-transit encryption** (#1413, `TestMemorystoreInTransitEncryption`, official `cloud.google.com/go/redis/apiv1` and go-redis): `transit_encryption_mode: SERVER_AUTHENTICATION` runs the server TLS-only (`--port 0 --tls-port 6378`, as Memorystore's port 6378 in the cluster; `host:port` on the host is its tunnel, as for any created instance), with a server certificate (180 days, issued again at each start) of a CA of the instance's own (ECDSA P-256, ten years, as Memorystore's), which `server_ca_certs` lists (PEM, serial, SHA-1 fingerprint, create and expire times) in `GetInstance`, `ListInstances` and the create operation's response. go-redis over TLS 1.2+ trusting that CA reaches a BASIC and a STANDARD_HA instance with the AUTH string; a plain TCP client is refused and a TLS client without the CA fails verification; a Standard tier instance's nodes replicate over TLS (`WAIT 1`). `TestGcloudRedisInTransitEncryption` (gcloud 587.0.0, `--transit-encryption-mode=server-authentication`; `describe` shows the mode and `serverCaCerts[0].cert`, which a TLS client then trusts) and `TestTerraformRedisInTransitEncryption` (hashicorp/google, `transit_encryption_mode`, the `server_ca_certs` attribute, a clean second plan) create one too. Client certificates are not asked for, as SERVER_AUTHENTICATION has none; the mode cannot be changed after create. **In-transit encryption before 6.0** (#1768, `TestMemorystoreInTransitEncryptionBefore60`, official `cloud.google.com/go/redis/apiv1` and go-redis): Redis 3.2, 4.0 and 5.0 have no TLS of their own, and Memorystore serves them in-transit encryption from an endpoint in front of the server (its documented connection limits for 4.0 and 5.0 are a proxy's); CloudBurrow does the same with `cloudburrow-storage redis-tls-front` (internal/redistlsfront, Go, in the server's pod, from the storage image): TLS 1.2 or later on port 6378 with the same instance CA and server certificate as on 6.x, clients not asked for a certificate, and the server on the pod's loopback alone. A REDIS_3_2, REDIS_4_0 and REDIS_5_0 instance each report SERVER_AUTHENTICATION and one server CA in the create operation and `GetInstance`; go-redis over TLS trusting it, with `GetInstanceAuthString`'s AUTH string, reaches the old server (`INFO` `redis_version` 3.2/4.0/5.0); a plain client is refused and a TLS client without the CA fails verification. A STANDARD_HA REDIS_5_0 instance replicates over TLS (`WAIT 1`: each replica's server replicates from a relay on its pod's loopback, which the front forwards over TLS, verifying the instance CA, to the node it names), and after `FailoverInstance` keeps its keys and replicates again. `TestGcloudRedisInTransitEncryptionBefore60` (gcloud, `redis instances create --redis-version=redis_5_0 --transit-encryption-mode=server-authentication`, the CA `describe` prints trusted by a TLS client) and `TestTerraformRedisInTransitEncryptionBefore60` (hashicorp/google 8.4.0, `redis_version = "REDIS_4_0"`, `server_ca_certs` output, a clean second plan, destroy) create one too. Memorystore's page lists no in-transit encryption connection limit for 3.2 and does not say it refuses it; CloudBurrow serves it on 3.2 as on 4.0 (UNVERIFIED, re-read 2026-11-18: docs.cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/about-in-transit-encryption names 4.0 and later only). Server CA rotation and customer-managed keys (#1463) are rows of their own below. The instance ID is checked with Google's rule (1 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter). Placement is not real: any region is accepted. |
| `CloudRedis.UpdateInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreCreateConnectUpdateDelete`: `memory_size_gb`, `display_name`, `labels` and `redis_configs` change; the size and configs are set on the running server with `CONFIG SET`, which keeps its keys, and a config removed from `redis_configs` goes back to its default; `TestGcloudRedis` (`--size --update-labels`, an `updateMask` of snake_case paths, which the JSON API accepts as Google does) and `TestTerraformRedisInstance` (in place) update one too. `persistence_config` changes the server's persistence (#1384, below). A value the server refuses is INVALID_ARGUMENT and changes nothing. `maintenance_policy` is stored and `auth_enabled` turns AUTH off, or on with a fresh AUTH string, on the running server's `requirepass` (#1386, `TestMemorystoreLocationsOperationsMaintenance`; a connection made before keeps its access). `replica_count` and `read_replicas_mode` scale a STANDARD_HA instance (#1385, below); `secondary_ip_range` is accepted and not kept. Another mask path is INVALID_ARGUMENT (not an updatable field). The instance `up` runs is FAILED_PRECONDITION (CloudBurrow's own). Memorystore may flush a BASIC instance it scales; this does not. |
| `CloudRedis.DeleteInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreCreateConnectUpdateDelete`, `TestGcloudRedis`, `TestTerraformRedisInstance`: the operation completes, the instance is NOT_FOUND and its server no longer answers; its Deployment, Service and volume are deleted. The instance `up` runs is FAILED_PRECONDITION (*code UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/cloud/redis/v1/cloud_redis.proto>)*, CloudBurrow's own): run `up` without `memorystore` to have none. |
| `GetInstanceAuthString` | **Verified** | A created instance's string is returned (`TestMemorystoreCreateConnectUpdateDelete`, `TestGcloudRedis` `get-auth-string`, Terraform's `auth_string`); an instance without AUTH has an empty one, as cloud_redis.proto documents ("If AUTH is not enabled for the instance the response will be empty"), and so has the instance `up` runs, which has AUTH off (`TestMemorystoreAdminDescribesTheServer`, #1595). |
| Persistence and reset | **Verified, measured** | A created instance follows the CloudBurrow instance's mode, as the server `up` runs does. **Persistent:** the instance's record is kept in `<state-dir>/<name>/memorystore`, its server has a volume of its own, and after `stop` and `up` it is READY again (REPAIRING while its server starts), with the same AUTH string; its keys follow its `persistence_config`, as on Memorystore (#1911): without persistence its server keeps no file and comes back empty, with RDB from the last snapshot (`TestMemorystoreRDBAcrossRestart`). `TestMemorystoreCreatedAcrossRestart`, which CI's restart probe runs with `CLOUDBURROW_TEST_MEMORYSTORE_EXPECT=present` beside `TestMemorystoreAcrossRestart`, and which was run by hand on one instance through persistent, ephemeral and persistent again (the keys came back after the ephemeral run). **Ephemeral:** records are kept in memory only, and `up` removes the servers a previous run left (their volumes are kept, as the server `up` runs keeps its own); `TestMemorystoreCreatedAcrossRestart` with `absent` after `up --mode ephemeral`. `reset` does not touch Memorystore, created instances included, and `state save` does not capture them. |
| `ExportInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreExportImport` (#1384), with `cloud.google.com/go/redis/apiv1` and `cloud.google.com/go/storage` against an instance started with `--services memorystore,storage`: the operation (verb `export`) completes once the server's `BGSAVE` has finished and its RDB file is written to `output_config.gcs_destination.uri` in this instance's Cloud Storage, an object that starts with the RDB header; `TestGcloudRedisExportImport` (`gcloud redis instances export`). The instance stays READY. A URI that is not `gs://{bucket}/{object}` is INVALID_ARGUMENT; without Cloud Storage on the instance, and on the instance `up` runs, FAILED_PRECONDITION (CloudBurrow's own). |
| `ImportInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreExportImport`: the object is read first (a missing one is NOT_FOUND); the instance is IMPORTING until the operation (verb `import`) completes, and then holds exactly the file's keys, as Memorystore documents an import overwrites: a key set since is gone, a changed one is back, and a second instance gets the first's data. The file is copied into the server's container, checked with the server's own `valkey-check-rdb`, and loaded by the server itself: a second server process of the same image serves it on a loopback port and the instance's server replicates it once, which empties its data and loads the RDB (an AOF, when it keeps one, is written again from it), then stops replicating. A file that is not an RDB the server reads, a newer RDB version among them, fails the operation INVALID_ARGUMENT and changes nothing. `TestGcloudRedisExportImport` (`gcloud redis instances import`) imports over later changes. Memorystore restarts the instance to import; this does not, and clients stay connected. |
| RDB persistence (`persistence_config`) | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreRDBPersistence` (#1384): RDB with `rdb_snapshot_period` on create and through `UpdateInstance`'s mask reads back with `rdb_snapshot_start_time` (default: now; kept by an update that leaves it out) and `rdb_next_snapshot_time` aligned to it, as Memorystore documents; the server's `CONFIG GET save` is the period with one change (`21600 1`, `3600 1`) and `appendonly` is `no`, and a snapshot is taken at once (`LASTSAVE`); DISABLED removes the save point and keeps no append-only file in either mode, so the data is lost when the server restarts, as Google documents of an instance without persistence (#1911): `TestMemorystoreDataAcrossServerRestart` restarts each server (maintenance, IMMEDIATE) with go-redis: a Basic tier instance without persistence comes back empty, with RDB ONE_HOUR with its key, and a Standard tier instance without persistence fails over to its replica and keeps it. `TestTerraformRedisInstance` applies `persistence_config` and changes its period in place. The server is started with the same save point (`components.MemorystoreServerOf`), which Valkey also honours when it stops, so in persistent mode the snapshot on the server's volume brings its data back. Valkey counts the period from its last snapshot rather than aligning it to the start time. An unknown period or mode is INVALID_ARGUMENT. |
| Maintenance policy, `CloudRedis.RescheduleMaintenance` | **Verified** on created instances, *error codes and wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/about-maintenance>, <https://docs.cloud.google.com/memorystore/docs/redis/find-and-set-maintenance-windows>, which document none)* | `TestMemorystoreLocationsOperationsMaintenance` (#1386): `maintenance_policy` on create and through `UpdateInstance`'s mask is stored and read back as Memorystore documents it, at most one weekly window (a day and a UTC start time) of one hour, with its `create_time` and `update_time`; a second window, no day or a start hour outside 0 to 23 is INVALID_ARGUMENT; with nothing scheduled `RescheduleMaintenance` is FAILED_PRECONDITION. `TestMemorystoreRescheduleMaintenance` (#1524), official Go client and `gcloud redis instances reschedule-maintenance`: an event is scheduled through CloudBurrow's control endpoint `POST /cloudburrow/v1/projects/P/locations/R/instances/I:scheduleMaintenance` (not a Memorystore API; [memorystore.md](memorystore.md#4a-maintenance-1524)); `maintenance_schedule` then has `start_time` (the first window a week away), `end_time` an hour on, `can_reschedule` and `schedule_deadline_time` a week after the original time; `IMMEDIATE` applies it at once, `NEXT_AVAILABLE_WINDOW` defers it a week, `SPECIFIC_TIME` within a week of the original time; at most twice, not past the deadline, not with less than an hour left (FAILED_PRECONDITION, INVALID_ARGUMENT for a time out of bounds). At its start a Basic tier instance is `MAINTENANCE`, unavailable while its server is replaced; a Standard tier instance fails over (`TestMemorystoreStandardTierMaintenanceFailsOver`). The console's Edit maintenance window, Schedule, Reschedule and Cancel maintenance: `TestMemorystoreMaintenanceThroughThePage`. |
| `UpgradeInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreEndOfLifeVersions` (#1524): a REDIS_3_2 instance upgraded to REDIS_4_0 and then REDIS_5_0 runs Redis 4.0.14, then 5.0.14, keeping its keys and AUTH. `TestMemorystoreVersionsAndUpgrade` (#1386): a REDIS_6_X instance upgraded to REDIS_7_0 and then REDIS_7_2 runs each version's server (INFO `redis_version` 7.0.x, then 7.2.4) and keeps its keys and AUTH: the data is snapshotted with `BGSAVE`, the server started again on the new image, and the snapshot loaded into it as an import is. The instance is UPDATING until the operation (verb `upgrade`) completes. A version not later than the instance's is INVALID_ARGUMENT (Memorystore does not downgrade); the instance `up` runs is FAILED_PRECONDITION. `TestConsoleMemorystoreUpgrade` upgrades from the console. |
| `FailoverInstance` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreStandardTierFailover` (#1385), official `cloud.google.com/go/redis/apiv1`: on a STANDARD_HA instance with read replicas, `LIMITED_DATA_LOSS` promotes a replica (`REPLICAOF NO ONE`, then `REPLICAOF` it on the other nodes and the instance's Service re-pointed); `host` and `port` are unchanged and a client there reaches the new primary (`role:master`) with the key written before, its writes reach the replicas, and `current_location_id` moves to the new primary's zone. `TestGcloudRedisFailover` (gcloud 587.0.0, `gcloud redis instances failover --data-protection-mode=force-data-loss`) and the console's Failover (`TestConsoleMemorystoreStandardTier`) fail one over too. `LIMITED_DATA_LOSS` aborts the operation FAILED_PRECONDITION when the greatest offset delta between the primary and a replica is 30 MB or more, or a replica is not replicating; `FORCE_DATA_LOSS` does not check (unit `TestLimitedDataLossRefusesALaggingReplica`: the 30 MB bound is Google's documented one, not measured). A BASIC instance is FAILED_PRECONDITION. **Automatic failover** (#1412, `TestMemorystoreAutomaticFailover`, official `cloud.google.com/go/redis/apiv1` and go-redis): after the primary node's pod is deleted (`kubectl delete pod`), the instance fails over on its own, as Memorystore documents ("a healthy replica with the least replication lag"): it is REPAIRING, then READY with `current_location_id` the replica's zone, and a client at the same `host:port` reaches the new primary with the key written before; the old primary's node comes back as its replica. The primary is checked every second (INFO replication through its tunnel) and fails over after three checks in a row in which it does not answer as a primary; Google documents no detection window. No data protection mode applies: writes the replicas had not received are lost, as Google says of asynchronous replication. No operation is recorded, as Google records none for an automated repair; `up.log` has a line. |
| Standard tier: `tier: STANDARD_HA`, `replica_count`, `read_replicas_mode`, `read_endpoint`, `read_endpoint_port`, `alternative_location_id`, `current_location_id`, `nodes` | **Verified** | `TestMemorystoreStandardTierFailover` (#1385): `READ_REPLICAS_ENABLED` with `replica_count` 2 is three Valkey servers, each a Deployment and Service, replicating asynchronously; `nodes` are `node-0` to `node-2` with zones (`node-0` in `location_id`, `node-1` in `alternative_location_id`); a key SET at `host:port` is read from a replica at `read_endpoint:read_endpoint_port`, which refuses writes (READONLY); `UpdateInstance` of `replica_count` to 3 adds a node that has the data. `TestGcloudRedisFailover` creates one with `--tier=standard` (`replica_count` 1, no read endpoint), `TestTerraformRedisStandardTier` (hashicorp/google 8.4.0) applies `tier = "STANDARD_HA"` with `read_replicas_mode` and `replica_count` 2, plans clean, and changes `replica_count` to 3 in place. Memorystore's rules are kept: `replica_count` 1 without read replicas, 1 to 5 (default 2) with them, read replicas on 5 GB or more and never disabled once enabled, none of these on BASIC (INVALID_ARGUMENT). The read endpoint spreads connections over the replicas in turn; the primary endpoint and the read endpoint are host addresses of their own, not VPC IPs. Across an automatic failover the read endpoint keeps its address and serves reads on every new connection (#1910, `TestMemorystoreAutomaticFailoverReadEndpoint`: 5 GB, two read replicas, the primary's pod deleted, six new connections in a row read the key written before). ## Cloud Scheduler — `google.cloud.scheduler.v1`

**Built, not reused** (#302). Google publishes no Cloud Scheduler emulator. It runs in the CLI
process, as Cloud Tasks does, and is opt-in: `--services scheduler`, on `--port-scheduler`
(default `9008`). `env` exports `CLOUDBURROW_SCHEDULER_ENDPOINT`. No client library reads it, so
pass it to `option.WithEndpoint`. Per-method status is generated in
[coverage/scheduler.md](coverage/scheduler.md).

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateJob`, `GetJob`, `ListJobs`, `PauseJob`, `ResumeJob`, `RunJob`, `DeleteJob` | **Verified** | `TestSchedulerHTTPAndPubSubJobs`, with `cloud.google.com/go/scheduler/apiv1` against the CI instance. |
| `RunJob` delivers at once to an HTTP target | **Verified** | The same test, against an `httptest` server. Deliveries carry `X-CloudScheduler`, `X-CloudScheduler-JobName` and `X-CloudScheduler-ScheduleTime` (an RFC 3339 time in UTC, asserted since #1567), and `User-Agent: Google-Cloud-Scheduler`. A 2xx response is success. HTTP targets are called from the host, so they must be reachable from it. Tests: `TestSchedulerHTTPAndPubSubJobs`, `TestRunJobDeliversAtOnce`. |
| Pub/Sub targets | **Verified** | The same test: the job's data and attributes reach a subscription on the local emulator, published through the official client. A job whose topic does not exist fails its attempt, as on the real service: `TestSchedulerPubSubJobToAMissingTopicFails` (#1576), after `RunJob` the official client's `GetJob` reads a last attempt time and a status that is not OK (`UNKNOWN` carrying Pub/Sub's `NOT_FOUND`; the code Google records is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/cloud/scheduler/v1/target.proto>)), and no topic is made. Tests: `TestSchedulerHTTPAndPubSubJobs`, `TestPubSubTargetPublishes`, `TestSchedulerPubSubJobToAMissingTopicFails`. |
| Cron schedules in IANA time zones | **Verified** | Unit-tested through the official client with a fake clock. Unix-cron with five fields, ranges, steps and names (`TestCronRangesStepsAndNames`, #1567: `*/15`, `9-17/2` with `MON-FRI` in America/New_York, `1 JAN`, `SUN` in Asia/Tokyo, `5,35` with `SEP,OCT THU` in Europe/London, each job's `schedule_time` read back). Zones come from Go's embedded tzdata (`time/tzdata`, imported by `internal/service/scheduler/server.go`), so they work on hosts with no zoneinfo: measured 2026-10-17 (#1576), `TestCronRangesStepsAndNames` built for linux/arm64 passes in `alpine:3.20`, which has no `/usr/share/zoneinfo` and no `/etc/localtime`; no automated test, as CI's runners all have zoneinfo. Invalid expressions and unknown zones are INVALID_ARGUMENT. Tests: `TestRunJobDeliversAtOnce`, `TestScheduleFiresPauseStopsResumeRestarts`, `TestRefusalsAndCRUD`, `TestCronRangesStepsAndNames`. |
| Paused jobs do not fire; resumed ones do | **Verified** | Unit-tested through the official client with a fake clock. Resuming restarts from the next slot; runs missed while paused are not made up. Tests: `TestScheduleFiresPauseStopsResumeRestarts`. |
| Retries | **Verified** | Unit-tested: `retry_count` retries on the Cloud Tasks backoff schedule, fed from `min_backoff_duration`, `max_backoff_duration` and `max_doublings`, and bounded by `max_retry_duration`. The last attempt's outcome is in `status` and `last_attempt_time`. Tests: `TestRetriesFollowRetryConfig`, `TestCloudTasksBackoffGrowsLinearlyAfterMaxDoublings`, `TestCloudTasksBackoffShouldRetryAfter`. |
| `UpdateJob` | **Verified** | Unit-tested, and applied by Terraform's provider (`TestTerraformSchedulerAndSubscription`) and gcloud (`TestGcloudScheduler`) over JSON. An empty mask replaces every settable field; the mask paths are `description`, `schedule`, `time_zone`, the target, `retry_config` and `attempt_deadline`. Over JSON the mask is lowerCamelCase (`timeZone`), converted by the transcoder. **Refused as the contract refuses** (#795), on `CreateJob` and `UpdateJob`, each `INVALID_ARGUMENT`: a `time_zone` of `Local` (Go's name for the host's zone, not a tz database name), a `schedule` with a `TZ=` or `CRON_TZ=` prefix (the cron parser's extension, not unix-cron, which overrode `time_zone`; one with no space after it panicked in the parser), and an `http_target.body` on a method other than POST, PUT or PATCH ("It is an error to set body on a job with an incompatible HttpMethod"). Before, each was accepted (unit `TestSchedulerRefusesWhatTheContractRefuses`). An invalid cron expression and an unknown time zone were refused already. From the console: `TestConsoleSchedulerEditJob`. |
| `ResumeJob` on an enabled job | **Verified** | Succeeds and changes nothing (#591): the Terraform provider resumes every job it creates unpaused, and `TestTerraformSchedulerAndSubscription` reads such a job back ENABLED after apply. It was FAILED_PRECONDITION here, which failed every such apply. That Google accepts it is inferred from the provider, not measured against Google. |
| `retry_config` of a job given none | **Implemented** | Not returned, though the job retries by the defaults (#591): the provider plans clean against Google for such a job, which it could not if the defaults came back, and here they did, so every plan wanted to remove them. Inferred from the provider, not measured against Google. A job given a `retry_config` returns it, with the defaults filled in. |
| JSON API (REST) | **Verified** | **One port serves gRPC and JSON** (#591), as `cloudscheduler.googleapis.com` does: the shared `Transcoder` serves Google's `google.api.http` bindings of `google.cloud.scheduler.v1`, and the Locations bindings of `cloudscheduler_v1.yaml`, with the same `GRPCServer` gRPC registers. Every CloudScheduler method is transcoded, and the Locations mixin too (#1237); a path Google does not bind 404. The query policy is KMS's: an unknown parameter is INVALID_ARGUMENT. The official client's REST transport drives a job's lifecycle (unit `TestRESTJobLifecycleWithTheOfficialRESTClient`, `TestRESTWire`). Terraform (`TestTerraformSchedulerAndSubscription`) and gcloud (`TestGcloudScheduler`) use it. JSON requests appear in `/admin/events`; fault injection and the gRPC request log are not interposed on them. |
| Terraform `google_cloud_scheduler_job` | **Verified** | `TestTerraformSchedulerAndSubscription`, with egress blocked: a Pub/Sub job applies (a create, then the provider's `:resume`), plans clean, takes a change to its description and schedule (a PATCH) and `paused = true` (a `:pause`), plans clean and is destroyed, each step read back with the official gRPC client. `TestTerraformSchedulerHTTPTarget` (#1304): a paused job with an `http_target` (POST, a header, a body and an `oidc_token`) applies, reads back, plans clean, takes a URI and audience change in place, and is destroyed. The wrapper sets `cloud_scheduler_custom_endpoint`. |
| `gcloud scheduler jobs` | **Verified where gcloud is installed** | `TestGcloudScheduler`, through `gcloud-setup`'s `cloudscheduler` override: `create http`, `create pubsub`, `list`, `describe`, `update http`, `pause`, `resume`, `run` and `delete`, read back with the official gRPC client. **Pass `--location`**: without it gcloud looks for an App Engine app's region, which is not served, and fails. |
| `Locations.ListLocations`, `GetLocation` | **Verified** | `TestSchedulerLocations` (#1237), with the official client's Locations mixin over gRPC; unit `TestLocations` and `TestRESTWire` over JSON. The list is Google's Cloud Scheduler regions plus every location that holds one of the project's jobs (any well-formed location is accepted in a job's name), paged; `GetLocation` of a listed location answers it, any other is NOT_FOUND, a malformed name INVALID_ARGUMENT, and a `filter` is the mixin's AIP-160 filter (#1943). Which fields Google sets on each Location (here `name`, `locationId`, `displayName`) is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/scheduler/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations>). From the console: the Create job form's Region is chosen from the list (`TestSchedulerCreateFormOffersListLocations`). |
| App Engine targets (`app_engine_http_target`) | **Verified**, *delivered to a local stand-in with `--appengine-url`; else every attempt fails* | `TestSchedulerAppEngineTarget` (#1447), with the official client: a job is kept as sent (method, defaulting to POST; `relative_uri`, defaulting to `/`, **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`** without a leading `/`; headers; a body only for POST and PUT; `app_engine_routing`) and returned with `app_engine_routing.host` computed as Google documents it. No App Engine runs on an instance and Google documents no mapping to Cloud Run. With **`--appengine-url`** (#1506) a local HTTP server stands in for the app: each attempt goes to that URL plus `relative_uri`, as `AppEngineHttpTarget` documents the request, with the job's method, body and headers, `Host` the routing's host, `User-Agent` `AppEngine-Google; (+http://code.google.com/appengine)` (appended to the job's own), `X-CloudScheduler: true`, `X-CloudScheduler-JobName`, `X-CloudScheduler-ScheduleTime` and `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` for a body with none; the job's `X-Google-*` and `X-AppEngine-*` headers, which "cannot be set or overridden", are dropped; a 2xx answer is `OK`, any other retried under `retry_config` (`TestSchedulerAppEngineDelivery`; unit `TestAppEngineJobDelivered`). Without it each attempt fails as a request to an app that does not exist, HTTP 404: `status` is **`NOT_FOUND`** naming the URL, `last_attempt_time` is set and `retry_config` applies. `TestGcloudAppEngineTargets`: `gcloud scheduler jobs create app-engine` with `--relative-url`, `--service`, `--version`, `--http-method` and `--message-body`. `TestTerraformAppEngineTargets`: a `google_cloud_scheduler_job` with `app_engine_http_target` applies, plans clean, changes in place and is destroyed. The console's **Edit job** is offered for such a job and changes its relative URI, method, headers, body, routing (service, version, instance) and attempt deadline through `UpdateJob` (`TestConsoleSchedulerEditAppEngineJob`), and a seed document takes `appEngineHttpTarget` (`TestAppEngineSeedIsReadBackByTheOfficialClients`). |
| OAuth and OIDC tokens on HTTP targets | **Verified**, *locally minted* | `TestSchedulerJobTokens` (#1243), with the official client: `oidc_token` and `oauth_token` are kept and returned by `CreateJob` and `GetJob`, and `RunJob` delivers to a local HTTP target with `Authorization: Bearer` and a locally minted token, the ID token's audience being the URI when none is given and its signature checked against the instance's `/certs`. A token without `service_account_email` is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**. A seed's `httpTarget` takes `oidcToken` and `oauthToken` too. Minted as for Cloud Tasks, with the same differences from Google: see Cloud Tasks, `oidcToken` / `oauthToken`. Before #1243 both were refused `UNIMPLEMENTED`. |
| Durability | **Verified, measured** | Jobs follow `--mode`: a store under the state directory in persistent mode, memory in ephemeral mode. `/admin/reset` clears them. CI's restart probe (#596): `TestSchedulerRestartSetup` runs alone just before `stop` and leaves an enabled and a paused HTTP job, each with its own schedule and time zone. After `stop` and `up` in persistent mode, `TestSchedulerAcrossRestart` reads both back with their schedule, time zone, target and state; brought up again with `--mode ephemeral`, `GetJob` is **NOT_FOUND** for both. |
| `state save` / `state load` | **Verified** | `TestStateRestoresSchedulerJobs`, with the official client against the CI instance (#600). See [state snapshots](#state-snapshots). |
| Seeding | **Verified** | `TestSchedulerSeedIsReadBackByTheOfficialClient`: a `scheduler` section in a seed document creates HTTP and Pub/Sub jobs the official client reads back field for field, and one invalid job refuses the whole document, seeding none (#600). An `appEngineHttpTarget` job is seeded too (#1447, `TestAppEngineSeedIsReadBackByTheOfficialClients`), its routing's host computed, and one whose `relativeUri` lacks the leading `/` refuses the document. |
## Cloud Logging — `google.logging.v2`

**Built, not reused** (#304). Google publishes no Logging emulator. It runs in the CLI process
and is opt-in: `--services logging`, on `--port-logging` (default `9009`). `env` exports
`CLOUDBURROW_LOGGING_ENDPOINT` for `option.WithEndpoint`. Per-method status is generated in
[coverage/logging.md](coverage/logging.md).

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `WriteLogEntries`, `ListLogEntries`, `ListLogs` | **Verified** | `TestLoggingWriteAndRead`, with `cloud.google.com/go/logging` and `logadmin` against the CI instance: structured entries are written, then read back with `logName` and `severity >= WARNING`. |
| API-written entries in the Logs Explorer | **Verified** | The same test finds them in the console's `/api/logs`, under the log's name and the project. Severities are folded onto the console's four levels: `TestConsoleFoldsLoggingSeverities` (#1576) writes one entry at each of the nine with the official client and reads `DEFAULT` and `DEBUG` as DEFAULT, `INFO` and `NOTICE` as INFO, `WARNING` as WARNING, and `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`, `ALERT` and `EMERGENCY` as ERROR. Tests: `TestLoggingWriteAndRead`, `TestConsoleFoldsLoggingSeverities`. |
| The Logging query language in filters (#2026): `ListLogEntries`, `TailLogEntries`, sinks, exclusions, log views, log-based metrics, `CopyLogEntries` and the console's Logs Explorer | **Verified** (error message wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-20: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/logging-query-language>)) | `TestLoggingQueryLanguage`, with `logadmin` and the official `ConfigClient`: `ListLogEntries` with `OR`, `NOT`, `-`, `:`, `:*`, parentheses, a value list (`severity = (WARNING OR CRITICAL)`), `jsonPayload` paths, `=~`, `SEARCH`, `log_id` and a global restriction; a sink created with `logadmin` whose `OR`/`NOT`/`:` filter routes exactly its entries to another project; an exclusion whose `OR`/`=~` filter keeps its entries out of the bucket; and malformed filters refused. `TestLoggingWriteAndRead` reads with `jsonPayload.event = "boot"` and is refused an undefined field. One parser, `internal/logfilter`, serves every filter; see the grammar below. Unit: `TestLanguage`, `TestErrors`, `TestCheckView` (internal/logfilter), `TestFilterOverLogEntries`, `TestCompileQuery`. |
| `DeleteLog` | **Verified** | Removes one log's entries. `TestGcloudLogging`: `gcloud logging logs delete` over JSON (#591). |
| The store | **Implemented** | Bounded at 20,000 entries (the oldest go first), in memory in every mode, cleared by `/admin/reset`. It keeps nothing across a restart. |
| `TailLogEntries`, `ListMonitoredResourceDescriptors` | **Verified** | Since #1215. TailLogEntries is a gRPC stream of entries written after it opens, for parent resource names (`projects/*`, and since #1395 `folders/*`, `organizations/*` and `billingAccounts/*`) and, since #1410, bucket views (`{bucket}/views/{view}`: the bucket's new entries the view's filter matches, `TestLoggingViewFiltersAndRetention`), with the ListLogEntries filter subset and `buffer_window` (default 2s, 0–60s); each response is ordered by timestamp. `suppression_info` is never set, since nothing is dropped. Over JSON (#1410), `POST /v2/entries:tail` takes one `TailLogEntriesRequest` body and streams a JSON array of `TailLogEntriesResponse`, opened at once and one element per send, until the client disconnects (unit `TestTailOverJSON`); the array framing is gRPC transcoding's for a streamed response and is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/logging/v2/logging.proto>), since no official client reads it (Go's apiv2 REST transport says TailLogEntries is not supported for REST). The console's Logs Explorer has its own live stream. ListMonitoredResourceDescriptors returns Google's `global` descriptor, the one resource type CloudBurrow emits, paged (`TestLoggingTailLogEntries`, `TestLoggingListMonitoredResourceDescriptors`). |
| Log-based metrics: `CreateLogMetric`, `GetLogMetric`, `ListLogMetrics`, `UpdateLogMetric`, `DeleteLogMetric` | **Verified** (error codes UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/logging/v2/logging_config.proto>)) | Since #1226, `MetricsServiceV2` in full. `TestLoggingLogBasedMetrics`, with the official `apiv2` `MetricsClient`: a counter with the default descriptor (DELTA, INT64, unit `1`, type `logging.googleapis.com/user/{id}`) and a distribution with a label extractor, a `REGEXP_EXTRACT` value extractor and explicit buckets are created, read back (a slash in an ID may be escaped, `nginx%2Frequests`), paged, updated (create_time kept, and UpdateLogMetric of an absent metric creates it, as the proto says), and deleted. As the proto documents: the ID is 1-100 of `A-Za-z0-9_-.,+!*',()%/`, not starting with `/`; `filter` is required (at most 20,000 characters) and `description` at most 8,000; `metric_kind` must be DELTA and `value_type` INT64 or DISTRIBUTION; a DISTRIBUTION needs `value_extractor` and valid `bucket_options` (linear, exponential or explicit) and a counter takes neither; an extractor is `EXTRACT(field)` or `REGEXP_EXTRACT(field, "regex")` with exactly one capture group; every descriptor label needs an extractor and every extractor a label; `bucket_name` must be a bucket of the metric's project; `metric_kind`, `value_type` and existing labels cannot change. Each is INVALID_ARGUMENT, a duplicate ALREADY_EXISTS and a missing metric NOT_FOUND; Google's message texts are not matched. **The filter is compiled with the ListLogEntries subset above**, so a filter outside it (`jsonPayload.x:y`, OR) is INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the term, where Google accepts it. Stored in the instance's state, so they survive a restart in persistent mode, and cleared by `/admin/reset`. |
| Log-based metric values | **Verified** through Cloud Monitoring | `TestMonitoringLogBasedMetrics` (#1939): each enabled metric is `logging.googleapis.com/user/NAME` in Cloud Monitoring (`--services monitoring`), a DELTA INT64 counter or DELTA DISTRIBUTION of one-minute points, over the entries its filter matches that were received after it was created, with its label extractors (`EXTRACT`, `REGEXP_EXTRACT` on any field of the entry's JSON form) and value extractor applied. Without Cloud Monitoring served, the console's metric page counts the stored entries its filter matches instead. Entries live in the bounded in-memory store, so values do not outlast it. See the Cloud Monitoring section. |
| Sinks: `CreateSink`, `GetSink`, `ListSinks`, `UpdateSink`, `DeleteSink` | **Verified** (error codes UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/configure_export_v2>)) | Since #1226. `TestLoggingSinks`, with the official `ConfigClient`. A project sink stores its destination, filter, description, `disabled`, embedded exclusions and `bigquery_options`. **Every destination is delivered to**: an enabled sink whose destination is `logging.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/locations/[L]/buckets/[B]` routes the entries its filter matches (less its embedded exclusions) there, readable through that bucket's views in ListLogEntries `resource_names` (#1395); a Cloud Storage bucket, Pub/Sub topic, BigQuery dataset or `logging.googleapis.com/projects/[P]` receives them as the next row says (#1404). The destination must have one of the documented forms (`storage.googleapis.com/[BUCKET]`, `bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/datasets/[D]`, `pubsub.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/topics/[T]`, `logging.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/locations/[L]/buckets/[B]`, `logging.googleapis.com/projects/[P]`), else INVALID_ARGUMENT; the ID is 1-100 letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, starting alphanumeric; the filter is compiled as above. UpdateSink changes only the `update_mask` paths, and an empty mask is `destination,filter,include_children`, as the proto documents; an output-only path is INVALID_ARGUMENT. A sink to a log bucket of its own project has no `writer_identity`, as configure_export_v2 documents ("All sinks have a writer identity except for sinks that write to a log bucket in the same Google Cloud project in which the log entries originate", #1595, `TestLoggingSinks`); on every other sink `writer_identity` is set (#1404) to the parent's Logging service agent, `serviceAccount:service-[PROJECT]@gcp-sa-logging.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (a folder's `fld-[ID]`, an organization's `org-[ID]`, a billing account's `bac-[ID]`), with the project ID where Google has the project number, as `GetSettings` names it (#1292); `logging_config.proto` documents a service agent for `unique_writer_identity` and for every non-project sink, and the identity Google returns for a project sink created without `unique_writer_identity` (an older shared one) is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/logging/v2/logging_config.proto>): the service agent is returned for it too. Nothing is enforced on it (ADR-0004): a sink delivers whatever IAM grants it has. The built-in `_Default` and `_Required` sinks are not listed. |
| Sink delivery to Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub, BigQuery and another project | **Verified** (error codes UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/troubleshoot>)) | Since #1404 and #1451, to docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/storage, /export/pubsub, /export/bigquery and /export/troubleshoot. `TestLoggingSinksDeliverToTheirDestinations`: sinks made with the official `ConfigClient` deliver entries written with the official `Client`, read back with the official Pub/Sub, BigQuery and Storage clients. **Pub/Sub** (`pubsub.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/topics/[T]`): each entry is published at once as one message, its data the LogEntry JSON and its attribute `logging.googleapis.com/timestamp` the entry's timestamp; the `compute.googleapis.com/resource_type` and `resource_id` attributes of Google's example are not set (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/pubsub>) which resources Google adds them for). **BigQuery** (`bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/[P]/datasets/[D]`): each entry is streamed (`tabledata.insertAll`, its `insertId` the row's) into a table named for its log, every character but letters, digits and `_` made `_` (`apache-access` is `apache_access`), with `_YYYYMMDD` of its UTC timestamp, or, with `bigquery_options.use_partitioned_tables`, one table partitioned by day on the `timestamp` column; the columns keep the LogEntry field names (`logName`, `resource.type`, `resource.labels.*`, `textPayload`, `jsonPayload.*`, `timestamp`, `receiveTimestamp`, `severity`, `insertId`, `httpRequest.*`, `labels.*`, `operation.*`, `trace`, `spanId`, `traceSampled`, `sourceLocation.*`, `split.*`), the names users choose are lowercased with unsupported characters made `_`, a JSON string is `STRING`, a number `FLOAT`, a bool `BOOLEAN`, an object a `RECORD` and a list `REPEATED`; a top-level `@type` of `type.googleapis.com/abc.Xyz` names the payload column `jsonpayload_abc_xyz`. `httpRequest`'s `cacheLookup`, `cacheHit` and `cacheValidatedWithOriginServer` are `BOOLEAN` and `cacheFillBytes` `INTEGER`, as its other counts are (#1451), and its `latency` is `FLOAT` seconds (#1506): Google's Log Analytics migration guide (cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/moving-to-log-analytics-for-bigquery-export-users) names `httpRequest.latency`'s sink type `FLOAT` and has it read as `latency.nanos / POW(10,9)` after the move, so every `Duration` is `FLOAT` seconds here, in `protoPayload` too (a `RequestLog`'s `latency`). **`protoPayload`** (#1451): a top-level `@type` of `type.googleapis.com/abc.Xyz` names the column `protopayload_abc_xyz`, with the types Google shortens (`google.cloud.audit.AuditLog` is `AuditLog`, so `protopayload_auditlog`; `google.cloud.bigquery.logging.v1.AuditData` `v1.bigquery`, `google.iam.admin.v1.AuditData` `v1.iam.admin`, and the rest of Google's table), and an App Engine `RequestLog`'s column is `protoPayload`; an audit log's fields keep their names (`protopayload_auditlog.methodName`, `.authenticationInfo.principalEmail`), its `request`, `response` and `metadata` are JSON strings named `requestJson`, `responseJson` and `metadataJson`, and its `serviceData` is `servicedata_<shortened type>` (`servicedata_v1_bigquery.tableInsertRequest`); other types' fields are lowercased, as Google's `@type` table shows. A proto string, enum or bytes (base64) is `STRING`, an integer `INTEGER`, a float `FLOAT`, a bool `BOOLEAN`, a `Timestamp` `TIMESTAMP`, a `Duration` `FLOAT` seconds, a message a `RECORD` (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/bigquery>): Google lists the names, not the types). The first entry makes the schema and later ones add their new fields; an entry that would change a field's type is a schema mismatch, and so is every entry of a batch whose new fields would pass BigQuery's 10,000 columns: as Google documents, those entries go to an error table in the same dataset, `export_errors_YYYYMMDD` (the entry's UTC date) or, with partitioned tables, `export_errors`, with Google's columns `logEntry` (the LogEntry JSON as a string), `schemaErrorDetail`, `sink` (the sink's resource name), `logName`, `timestamp`, `receiveTimestamp`, `severity`, `insertId`, `trace` and `resourceType`, its first row making its schema; the column types (`STRING`, `TIMESTAMP` for the times) and the `schemaErrorDetail` text (`Provided Schema does not match Table P:D.T. Field F has changed type from A to B.`) are UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/bigquery>). `TestLoggingBigQuerySinkExportErrorsAndProtoPayload`, `TestGcloudLoggingBigQuerySinkExportErrors`, `TestTerraformLoggingBigQuerySinkExportErrors`. **Not implemented** (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/bigquery>), Google does not document them; #1506 checked docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/bigquery again, which lists the `export_errors` columns without types and says only that `schemaErrorDetail` "contains the complete error message returned by BigQuery"): `Any` fields but `serviceData`, which are left out, as Google names no column for them; a `protoPayload` type the instance does not know is not exported. **Cloud Storage** (`storage.googleapis.com/[BUCKET]`): entries are batched per hour, as Google writes them, into the objects `CopyLogEntries` writes (`LOG_ID/YYYY/MM/DD/HH:00:00_HH:59:59_S0.json`, LogEntry JSON one per line, `_A0:UNIX` for an entry received in another hour than its timestamp's); an hour's batch is written once the Logging clock passes the hour it was received in, checked every 30 seconds (Google: the first entries can take 2 to 3 hours). The CloudBurrow extension `POST /cloudburrow/logging/v2/clock:advance` with `{"seconds": n}` on the Logging port (n not negative; it answers `{"time": …}`) moves the Logging clock forward, for every entry written after it too, and writes the batches due by then before it answers; the clock does not move back until the instance restarts, and batches not yet written are lost with it. **Another project** (`logging.googleapis.com/projects/[P]`): the entry goes to P's `_Default` bucket, unless one of P's exclusions matches it, read by ListLogEntries of `projects/[P]`, and through P's own sinks, once: a project destination of P's sinks is not followed again (Google's [routing overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/routing/overview) documents this one-hop limit). **Errors**: a delivery that fails (a missing topic, dataset or bucket, a service the instance does not serve, a schema mismatch) drops the entry, is shown on the sink's console page, and writes, once a day per sink and error code as Google documents, an `ERROR` entry to the sink's parent's `logging.googleapis.com/sink_error` log: resource `logging_sink` (`name`, `destination`, `project_id`), labels `activity_type_name` `LoggingSinkConfigErrorV2`, `destination`, `error_code`, `error_detail` and `sink_id`, and the text `Cloud Logging sink configuration error in [P], sink [S]: [code] ([detail])`. `topic_not_found` is Google's code; Google's troubleshooting page names no code for a missing dataset or bucket, a schema mismatch or another write failure (its other codes, `topic_region_not_allowed`, `topic_over_quota`, `table_resource_exhausted` and `bucket_changed_parent_project`, are for message storage policies, quotas and a moved bucket, which an instance does not have), so `dataset_not_found`, `bucket_not_found`, `schema_mismatch` and `write_failed` are CloudBurrow's (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/troubleshoot>): only a live sink shows the codes Google writes). A BigQuery sink's console page counts the entries written to `export_errors` (`TestConsoleSinkShowsExportErrors`). That entry is not routed by sinks. Delivery is in memory, and not across a restart. `TestGcloudLoggingSinksToEachDestination`: `gcloud logging sinks create` for each destination (`--use-partitioned-tables` for BigQuery), `describe` reading `writerIdentity`, and `gcloud logging write` arriving at the topic; `TestTerraformLoggingSinkDestinations`: below. These run in the emulators shard, beside BigQuery, as `SINK_LOGGING`, `SINK_STORAGE` and `SINK_PUBSUB`. Unit `TestSinkDelivery`, `TestTableNames`. |
| Intercepting sinks (#1521): `intercept_children` on `CreateSink`, `GetSink`, `ListSinks`, `UpdateSink` | **Verified** (error codes UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/logging/v2/logging_config.proto>)) | `TestLoggingInterceptingSinks`, with the official `ConfigClient` and `Client` over gRPC, and `TestGcloudAndTerraformInterceptingSinks`, with `gcloud logging sinks create --folder --include-children --intercept-children`, `describe` and `update --no-intercept-children`, and `google_logging_folder_sink` with `intercept_children = true` (hashicorp/google 8.4.0, egress blocked, planning clean), on one instance with `--services logging`. The field is in Google's v2 discovery document (`interceptChildren`) but not in cloud.google.com/go/logging v1.20.0's loggingpb, so it is carried beside the message: taken from a JSON body and added to every JSON answer, and over gRPC read from and answered as field 10, as a client built from the current proto sends it. As the field documents, it applies only to folder and organization sinks with `include_children` whose destination is a project (`logging.googleapis.com/projects/[PROJECT]`), else INVALID_ARGUMENT; and "any logs matched by the sink won't be included by non-_Required sinks owned by child resources": an entry it matches is routed to the destination project's _Default bucket and sinks, and kept out of its own project's _Default bucket and sinks and those of the folders below the sink's owner, while the sinks above it still route it; the farthest intercepting sink that matches applies. An update naming the field clears or sets it; `updateMask` paths are taken in snake_case, as gcloud sends them, as well as lowerCamelCase. The console's Logs Explorer, on a `_Default` bucket's `_AllLogs` view, shows the entry in the destination project's bucket only. Not served: the `_Required` sink's exemption, as `_Required` is not modelled. |

Refusals Google gives no code for are FAILED_PRECONDITION. Stored, durable in persistent mode. The key is a CryptoKey of the instance's Cloud KMS in the bucket's region (a key elsewhere is INVALID_ARGUMENT "The KMS key location must match the storage location.
