| Links (`CreateLink`, `GetLink`, `ListLinks`, `DeleteLink`) and Log Analytics' linked dataset | **Verified** for project buckets, with BigQuery on the instance, a view per log view; folder, organization and billing account buckets are **refused**, as Google documents | `TestLoggingLogAnalyticsLinkedDataset` (#1423), `TestLoggingLinkedDatasetViewsRetentionAndDeleteLog` and `TestLoggingLinkedDatasetAcrossRestarts` (#1435), official Logging `ConfigClient` and `Client` and the official BigQuery client; `TestGcloudLoggingLinks` (`gcloud logging buckets create --enable-analytics`, `gcloud logging views create`, `gcloud logging links create`, `describe`, `list`, `delete`, through the harness, egress blocked; the view gcloud made is a view of the dataset); `TestLoggingLinksSettingsAndAsyncBuckets` (#1292); units `TestLinkedDatasets`, `TestLinkedDatasetsFollowTheBucket`, `TestLinkedDatasetsRetentionByTheLoggingClock`, `TestLinkedDatasetsOutliveAFrontRestart`, `TestSettingsAndLinksOverREST`. A link is stored under a bucket with Log Analytics on (`analytics_enabled`; without it CreateLink is FAILED_PRECONDITION, as Google documents "A link can only be created for an analytics-enabled bucket", code UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/buckets>)), is ACTIVE, and **makes** the BigQuery dataset it names, `bigquery.googleapis.com/projects/{p}/datasets/{link_id with - as _}`, in the bucket's project, as [Google documents](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/analyze/query-linked-dataset) "a read-only pointer to your log bucket" whose log views are "virtual views ... named the same". The dataset has **a view per log view** of the bucket, named as it (`_AllLogs` and each view CreateView made; `tables.get` type `VIEW`; `tables.list` lists the views alone), over a table the Logging server fills (`_cloudburrow_log_entries`, left out of `tables.list`, whose `_cloudburrow_views` column lists the log views whose filter matches each row, as filter.go evaluates it): a view selects the rows of its log view inside the bucket's retention; read back: an `errors` view of `severity>=ERROR` holds the ERROR and CRITICAL entries alone. The views follow the bucket (#1435): CreateView, UpdateView of the filter and DeleteView make the dataset again with the bucket's views (read back: a view made after the link, a changed filter, a deleted view gone from `tables.list`); a log view filter CloudBurrow does not evaluate is UNIMPLEMENTED on a linked bucket (CreateLink, CreateView, UpdateView), since its view could not hold what the log view does. **Retention and DeleteLog** remove copied rows as they remove entries: a retention change, and DeleteLog of a log in the bucket, make the dataset again from what the bucket holds (read back: an entry 3 days old leaves at a 2-day retention, and DeleteLog empties the views of its log), and an entry ageing past the retention leaves every view by the view's own timestamp condition. That condition measures an entry's `timestamp` ("used to compute the log entry's age and to enforce the logs retention period", the LogEntry reference) against the Logging clock, not BigQuery's: the two `clock:advance` extensions move them apart, so a view reads the Logging clock as `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()` less the skew measured when it was made, and the dataset is made again when either clock moves (#1602; unit `TestLinkedDatasetsRetentionByTheLoggingClock`). Google keeps entries a shortened retention expired for a 7-day grace period in which "You can't query or view the expired logs" (docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/buckets); here they leave at once. The table holds every entry the bucket held at CreateLink, and every entry written to it after, streamed (`tabledata.insertAll`) in the background as `WriteLogEntries` stores it, so it is queryable once that insert is done, well under a second here (the test reads it back within its first poll; Google documents no delay, beyond "several minutes before BigQuery recognizes the dataset"). The columns are Log Analytics' schema of a log view: `timestamp`, `receive_timestamp` (TIMESTAMP), `log_name`, `log_id` (unescaped), `severity`, `severity_number` (INT64, LogSeverity's number), `insert_id`, `resource` (`type` STRING, `labels` JSON), `labels`, `json_payload`, `proto_payload` (JSON), `text_payload`, `http_request` (RECORD, `latency` FLOAT seconds), `operation`, `trace`, `span_id`, `trace_sampled`, `source_location`, `split` (column types UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/analyze/query-linked-dataset>) against a live linked dataset); read back: `JSON_VALUE(json_payload.msg)`, `JSON_VALUE(labels.env)`, `resource.type`, `text_payload`, `severity_number` 500 for ERROR. **Read-only:** the BigQuery front refuses, before anything runs, every write into a linked dataset but the Logging server's own (`internal/bigqueryfront/loglinks.go`): `datasets.patch`, `update` and `delete`, `tables.insert`, `patch`, `update` and `delete`, `tabledata.insertAll`, a load, copy or query job into it, and DML, `TRUNCATE`, `ALTER`, `CREATE` and `DROP` statements in it, 403 `accessDenied` (Google documents no error; code and wording UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/analyze/query-linked-dataset>)); read back: `tables.insert`, `tables.delete`, `datasets.patch`, `datasets.delete` 403 and `CREATE TABLE` refused. A second link of one ID, or a link whose dataset exists, is ALREADY_EXISTS; a missing one NOT_FOUND. **Refused FAILED_PRECONDITION**, naming why: CreateLink on an instance without BigQuery, and on a bucket of a project the instance's BigQuery does not serve (it serves one). **Folder, organization and billing account buckets** (#1435): Google upgrades to Log Analytics only a bucket "created at the Google Cloud project level" ([Upgrade a bucket](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/buckets)), so `analytics_enabled` on one is FAILED_PRECONDITION and so is CreateLink on one (codes UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/buckets>)); Google documents no project for such a dataset, since none can be made. **Restarts** (#1435): the links are kept in the Logging store, and every 5 seconds each link's dataset BigQuery no longer has (after an emulator restart, which loses the in-memory data, or with a new emulator) is made again with its views and filled from the bucket (read back after a restart of the emulator's container: both views hold the entry written before, and an entry written after); the front keeps the linked datasets in its state directory (`linkeddatasets.json`), so after a restart of the front's container alone the dataset is still read-only (read back: `tables.insert` 403). DeleteLink deletes the dataset (404 after). CreateLink and DeleteLink answer done Operations with a `LinkMetadata`, which `operations.get` reads back (gcloud polls it). **Differs:** the dataset is a copy kept in step, not a pointer: a view, retention or DeleteLog change makes it again (its `creationTime` changes), and for up to 5 seconds after an emulator restart the dataset is missing; the front knows a linked dataset from the Logging server's own `datasets.insert` of it (the dataset also carries the label `cloudburrow_logging_link`), so a write into any other dataset costs no extra read (unit `TestLinkedDatasetIsReadOnly`). From the console: the Linked datasets section, whose row lists the dataset's BigQuery views, one per log view (#1435), Create link and Delete link on a bucket's page, and Log Analytics in Edit bucket (`TestConsoleLoggingLinks`); a link's row opens Log Analytics: BigQuery's query editor on its dataset, with a query of `_AllLogs` filled in. |
| `CopyLogEntries` | **Verified** | Since #1394. `TestLoggingCopyLogEntries`, with the official `ConfigClient` over gRPC and the official Storage client reading the result; `TestGcloudLoggingCopy` with `gcloud logging copy`, `gcloud logging operations describe` and `list`, for a project and, since #1411, with `--folder` and `--organization`; unit `TestCopyLogEntries` and `TestCopyLogEntriesFromBillingAccount` with the REST transport. The source is any parent's bucket, `{projects|folders|organizations|billingAccounts}/X/locations/L/buckets/B` (#1411, as `gcloud logging copy --folder|--organization|--billing-account` documents). The entries of the source bucket that `filter` matches, stored when the call is made, are written to `storage.googleapis.com/BUCKET` on the instance's Cloud Storage, named as a Cloud Storage sink names its objects: `LOG_ID/YYYY/MM/DD/HH:00:00_HH:59:59_S0.json` for the UTC hour of each entry's timestamp, `_A0:UNIX.json` (UNIX the copy's start) for entries received in another hour, each holding LogEntry JSON one per line in timestamp order. A bucket holds what it is read for: a parent's `_Default` its own entries (those no exclusion kept out) and what sinks routed there, and any other bucket, an aggregated sink's destination among them, what sinks routed to it. The long-running operation `{parent}/locations/L/operations/ID`, under the source's parent (`folders/F/locations/L/operations/ID`), carries a `CopyLogEntriesMetadata` (the request, start and end time, state SCHEDULED, RUNNING, then SUCCEEDED, FAILED or CANCELLED, progress 0-100, `cancellation_requested`, `writer_identity` the parent's Logging service agent, `serviceAccount:service-{project}@gcp-sa-logging.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, or `service-fld-{n}@`, `service-org-{n}@`, `service-bac-{account}@` for the others) and a `CopyLogEntriesResponse` with the copied count. Google's copy takes at least an hour; this one is SCHEDULED for 2 seconds, then writes one object at a time. `google.longrunning.Operations` is served for copy operations (`GetOperation`, `ListOperations` with no filter or `request_type=CopyLogEntries`, `CancelOperation`, over gRPC and at `logging_v2.yaml`'s project, organization, folder and billing-account paths over JSON): a cancel before the copy finishes stops it before its next object and ends it CANCELLED with the error CANCELLED, keeping what was written, as Google documents; cancelling a finished copy is FAILED_PRECONDITION (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/routing/copy-logs>) code). A write that fails, a missing destination bucket among them, ends it FAILED with PERMISSION_DENIED "Failed to write export data", the error Google's troubleshooting names. A destination other than a Cloud Storage bucket is INVALID_ARGUMENT, a missing source bucket NOT_FOUND, and an instance without Cloud Storage FAILED_PRECONDITION. Operations are kept in memory, not across a restart. The console's log bucket page offers Copy log entries, lists the bucket's copy operations and cancels one. |

**The Logging query language** (#2026) is served in full, as its reference documents
(<https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/logging-query-language>), by one parser and
evaluator, `internal/logfilter`, for `ListLogEntries`, `TailLogEntries`, sinks, exclusions,
log views, log-based metrics, `CopyLogEntries` and the console's Logs Explorer:

```
expr       = orExpr { [ "AND" ] orExpr }      (adjacent terms are ANDed; so are lines)
orExpr     = unary { "OR" unary }             (OR binds tighter than AND)
unary      = ( "NOT" | "-" ) unary | primary  (NOT binds tightest)
primary    = "(" expr ")" | lhs op rhs | lhs ":*" | function | value
lhs        = path | cast(path, TYPE[, TIME_ZONE("zone")]) | regexp_extract(path, "re")
op         = "=" | "!=" | "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" | ":" | "=~" | "!~"
rhs        = value | "(" values joined by NOT, OR, AND ")"
function   = SEARCH([path,] "q") | log_id("id") | sample(path, f) | ip_in_net(path, "net") | source("res")
path       = segment { "." segment }          (labels."a/b", jsonPayload.x.y, protoPayload.@type)
```

- **Keywords:** `AND`, `OR` and `NOT` only in upper case; lower case they are search terms. `--` starts a comment.
- **Types:** the right side converts to the field's type, from LogEntry's schema, or from the JSON value under a payload. A failed conversion fails the comparison.
  - Strings compare ignoring case (NFKC case folding); `:` is a substring test.
  - Numbers, booleans (`true > false`), durations (`httpRequest.latency > "1s"`) and timestamps (RFC 3339 or ISO 8601; a bare date is midnight UTC) compare by value.
  - `severity` compares by level (`DEFAULT` < `DEBUG` < … < `EMERGENCY`) or by number. `NULL_VALUE` matches a null.
- **Missing and defaulted fields:** a comparison on a missing payload or label field is false, `!=` included; `NOT` inverts it. A LogEntry field the entry lacks compares as its default. `:*` tests explicit presence.
- **Field names:** repeated fields match on any element. Map and `jsonPayload` keys are case-sensitive; `protoPayload` names are not. A field LogEntry does not define is an error.
- **Global restrictions** and `SEARCH`: a bare value is searched across every field. `SEARCH` matches whole tokens, ignoring case, with `` `phrases` ``.
- **Log views** take what Google's log views docs list (#2028; <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/logs-views>): `source()`, `log_id()`, and comparisons of `resource.type`, resource labels (`resource.labels.KEY`), labels (`labels.KEY`) and App Hub labels (`apphub.application.location` and the like), with any of the operators above (`:*` too); joined by `AND` and `OR`; `NOT` on one `source()`, `log_id()` or comparison, never on a compound statement. `CreateView` and `UpdateView` refuse anything else as INVALID_ARGUMENT (`Invalid filter: …`): any other field (`severity`, `logName`, `timestamp`, payloads), `SEARCH` and the other functions, `cast()` and `regexp_extract()`, and bare text. The docs give no refusal code or message: INVALID_ARGUMENT is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-20: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/logs-views>) and the wording is ours. A view stored before #2028 whose filter falls outside the subset is UNIMPLEMENTED when read.
  - In a view, `source()` of a folder or organization also takes its descendants (#1410). Elsewhere it matches the resource's own entries.
- **Errors:** a malformed filter is INVALID_ARGUMENT. A syntax error reads `Unparseable filter: syntax error at line L, column C, token 'T'`. An undefined field, a bad regular expression, a regular expression that is not double-quoted, a bad function argument and a filter over 20,000 characters each get their own message. The wording is ours: Google documents the cases, not the messages.
- **Not served:** the Logs Explorer's custom indexes. These change speed, not results.

## Cloud KMS — `google.cloud.kms.v1`

**Built, not reused** (#309): Google publishes no Cloud KMS emulator, and each third-party one departs from Google's documented behaviour ([upstream-evaluation.md](upstream-evaluation.md#amendment-cloud-kms-is-built-not-reused-309)).
It runs in the CLI process and is opt-in: `--services kms`, on `--port-kms` (default `9018`).
`env` exports `CLOUDBURROW_KMS_ENDPOINT` for `option.WithEndpoint`. Per-method status is
generated in [coverage/kms.md](coverage/kms.md).
**One port serves gRPC and JSON** (#414), as `cloudkms.googleapis.com` does: an HTTP/2 request with an `application/grpc` content type goes to gRPC, and everything else goes to the JSON router, the shared `Transcoder` in `internal/transport/rest` (#591), which calls the same registered gRPC server. The router's paths are Google's own bindings, read from the `google.api.http` annotations of every `google.cloud.kms.v1` service plus the `cloudkms_v1.yaml` mixins (Locations, IAMPolicy, Operations). A bound path that is not transcoded yet answers **501 UNIMPLEMENTED** with an AIP-193 envelope that includes `status`, and a path Google does not bind answers 404. `:encrypt` and `:decrypt` are transcoded to the same server methods gRPC runs (#415), with protojson bodies: unknown fields are refused, CRCs are accepted as JSON strings or numbers, int64 fields are written as strings, and a malformed body is refused without quoting it. **Over REST, a code reaches a Go caller by its HTTP status**: gax maps HTTP 400 to INVALID_ARGUMENT, so FAILED_PRECONDITION (HTTP 400, as on Google) arrives as INVALID_ARGUMENT. The envelope's `status` still says FAILED_PRECONDITION, and the compat tests read it from there. A path that matches no Google binding is 404 over REST, where gRPC says INVALID_ARGUMENT: a malformed name, for example, or a version-name `:decrypt`. `TestKMSJSONIsServedOnTheSamePort` pins the routing. The six reads are transcoded too (#422): GetKeyRing, ListKeyRings, GetCryptoKey, ListCryptoKeys, GetCryptoKeyVersion and ListCryptoKeyVersions, the path giving `name` or `parent` to the same parsers gRPC uses, so a malformed segment is the same INVALID_ARGUMENT (`TestKMSResources` runs its reads as `grpc` and `rest` subtests; `TestKMSReadsAgreeOverREST`; `TestRESTReads`). **One query-parameter policy covers every transcoded method.** Request fields the path does not bind are query parameters, in camelCase or snake_case; whether Google accepts snake_case is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.keyRings.cryptoKeys/encrypt>). `alt=json` (or `$alt`), `prettyPrint` and `$.xgafv` are accepted; `$alt=json;enum-encoding=int`, which the GAPIC REST client sends on every call, makes enums numbers (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/api/http.proto>) for Google). The other system parameters (`fields`/`$fields`, `alt=proto`, `callback`, `$.xgafv`, `quotaUser`, ...) are applied as [REST system parameters](#rest-system-parameters-1954) describes; **any other parameter is INVALID_ARGUMENT naming it** (code UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/api/http.proto>)), unlike the Cloud Tasks and Secret Manager JSON APIs, which ignore unknown parameters, because a dropped KMS parameter would look as though it took effect. The creates are transcoded too (#423): CreateKeyRing, CreateCryptoKey, CreateCryptoKeyVersion and `:updatePrimaryVersion`. The new resource is the body (for `:updatePrimaryVersion`, the whole request, and a body `name` that differs from the path is INVALID_ARGUMENT, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/api/http.proto>) for Google). An empty body is an empty message, which is what Terraform's key ring create sends. Unknown body fields are INVALID_ARGUMENT (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/api/http.proto>)) and are never echoed; `skipInitialVersionCreation` takes `true` or `false`; a duplicate is HTTP 409, ALREADY_EXISTS; a verb nothing binds is 404 (`TestKMSResources`' `create-grpc`/`create-rest` subtests, `TestKMSCreatesOverREST`, `TestRESTCreates`, which replays Terraform's, gcloud's and the GAPIC client's bodies). The lifecycle is transcoded too (#424): `PATCH` UpdateCryptoKey and UpdateCryptoKeyVersion, with `updateMask` a protojson FieldMask of lowerCamelCase paths converted to proto paths before the server's mask checks (a path that does not convert is INVALID_ARGUMENT), and `:destroy` and `:restore`, which take `{}` or no body. A body `name` that differs from the path is INVALID_ARGUMENT (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/googleapis/master/google/api/http.proto>)). DeleteCryptoKey and DeleteCryptoKeyVersion return long-running operations, served since #1212 (the key deletion row). `TestKMSUpdateCryptoKey`, `TestKMSUpdateCryptoKeyVersion`, `TestKMSDestroyCryptoKeyVersion` and `TestKMSRestoreCryptoKeyVersion` run every case as `grpc` and `rest` subtests; `TestKMSLifecycleOverRESTWire` and `TestRESTLifecycle` cover the wire. The IAMPolicy mixin is transcoded too (#429, `TestRESTIam`). JSON requests appear in `/admin/events`; fault injection is not interposed on them.

Google publishes no specification or reference server of the protocol Cloud KMS speaks to an external key manager, and no open-source one exists (checked 2026-10-16: the Cloud EKM overview names only commercial partners; Cosmian KMS implements Workspace CSE and Azure EKM, not Cloud EKM), so no real EKM is run: **CloudBurrow acts as the EKM of every key URI and every EKM connection**. A version's key URI or key path is stored and returned as given and never dialled; its key material is generated and kept by the instance, as a SOFTWARE key's is, so nothing an external key protects is outside CloudBurrow. Each challenge is 32 random bytes; a reply must be the challenge signed RSASSA-PKCS1 v1.5 over SHA-256 (as `openssl dgst -sign` makes it) by the key it names, and a reply that is unsigned, does not verify, or names a key with no challenge is INVALID_ARGUMENT with nothing recorded: no unsigned approval is accepted. The instance states each operation needs are hsm_management.proto's (delete: DISABLED or PENDING_TWO_FACTOR_AUTH_REGISTRATION, the operation field's stricter reading); a proposal expires after `ttl` or at `expire_time` (default 1 day, 5 minutes to 7 days); one unexpired PENDING or APPROVED proposal per instance; Delete is soft (DELETED until `purge_time`, the expiry); DELETED resources are listed only with `show_deleted`; an ACTIVE instance past `disable_time` (730 days after creation, the last refresh or enable) reads DISABLED. An `HSM_SINGLE_TENANT` key needs `crypto_key_backend` naming an ACTIVE instance in the key ring's location (INVALID_ARGUMENT when absent or missing, FAILED_PRECONDITION when not ACTIVE), and every cryptographic operation and new version on it is FAILED_PRECONDITION while the instance is not ACTIVE ("keys in a DISABLED or deleted instance still show ACTIVE but fail cryptographic operations"). gcloud: `TestGcloudKMSSingleTenantHsm` runs `kms single-tenant-hsm create`, `describe`, `list`, `proposal create`/`describe`/`approve --quorum-challenge-replies`/`execute`/`list`/`delete`, and `kms keys create --protection-level hsm-single-tenant --crypto-key-backend`, then encrypt and decrypt. Terraform: the google provider (8.4.0) has no single-tenant HSM resource. **What differs:** there is no hardware: operations complete at once, so the transitional states (CREATING, DISABLING, DELETING; proposal CREATING and RUNNING) are never observed, and the keys are SOFTWARE keys underneath, as HSM ones are. `upgrade_key_trust` proposals and import jobs at HSM_SINGLE_TENANT are served since #1521 (the trusted key wrapping and import job rows). Key rings have no labels. Matches are counted before paging, so `total_size` is the number matched. A field the resource does not have, a value its field cannot hold, or a filter that does not parse is INVALID_ARGUMENT (error code UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/sorting-and-filtering>)). |

A malformed name is INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the field; a well-formed name that does not exist is NOT_FOUND. Google documents neither code for KMS. Unit-tested for every RPC (`TestMalformedNamesAreInvalidArgument`), and `TestKMSNamesAreValidatedBeforeLookup` checks GetCryptoKey against the CI instance. **Locations follow the rule the other services use**: lowercase words joined by single hyphens, so `1abc` and `us--east1` are refused. |

## Secret Manager — `google.cloud.secretmanager.v1`

An **owned implementation**: the upstream audit (#24) found no official Secret Manager
emulator. Measured against the published contract, never against another emulator.

> **It is not a secret store.** CloudBurrow authenticates nothing, so anything written here
> is readable by any caller that can reach the endpoint. It exists so an application whose
> code fetches configuration from Secret Manager can run locally. See
> [credentials.md](credentials.md).

Served on one port over **both gRPC and JSON**, as Google's own endpoint is.

### Control plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateSecret` | **Verified** | `TestSecretLifecycle`. Duplicate is `ALREADY_EXISTS`. |
| `GetSecret` | **Verified** | Missing is `NOT_FOUND`. Tests: `TestSecretErrorsUseGoogleCodes`, `TestMissingSecretIsNotFound`. |
| `ListSecrets` | **Verified** | Paged, ordered by name, scoped per project. Tests: `TestSecretLifecycle`, `TestCreateGetAndListSecrets`, `TestSecretsAreIsolatedPerProject`, and unit `TestListSecretsPagesInNameOrder` (#1567: secrets made `c`, `a`, `b` list, two to a page, `[a b]` then `[c]`). |
| `UpdateSecret` | **Verified** | `TestSecretUpdateAppliesOnlyTheMask`, `TestGcloudSecrets` (`gcloud secrets update --update-labels`) and `TestTerraformSecretLabelChangeInPlace` (a label change on `google_secret_manager_secret`, applied in place and planned clean; #691). `labels`, `annotations`, and `expire_time` or `ttl` (#1225, `TestSecretManagerExpiry`). An **empty update mask is refused** rather than treated as "replace everything", which would silently clear every label. A mask naming an immutable field is refused rather than ignored; `replication` is refused only when it would change (see Replication config, `TestSecretManagerUserManagedReplicasRoundTrip`). |
| `DeleteSecret` | **Verified** | Removes every version with it: an orphaned version could otherwise be listed by a later secret with the same ID. Tests: `TestDeleteSecretRemovesItsVersions`, `TestSecretLifecycle`. |
| Replication config | **Verified** | `automatic`, and `user-managed` with its replica locations, are **kept and returned as given** — the locations in the order sent — by `CreateSecret`, `GetSecret` and `ListSecrets` over gRPC and REST, and carried by state save and load (`TestSecretManagerUserManagedReplicasRoundTrip`, `TestStateSaveResetLoadRestoresEverything`; #857). Recorded, not enforced: there is one local store either way. Replication is **immutable**: an `UpdateSecret` whose mask names `replication` with a different policy is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**, and one sending it unchanged is accepted, per the field's `IMMUTABLE` behaviour and AIP-203 — **documented, not measured against Google** (same test). The one exception is the customer-managed encryption keys (next row, #1453). `SecretVersion.replication_status` is returned since #1453 for versions added since: the replicas (automatic, or each user-managed location) and the key version that encrypted each. |
| `customer_managed_encryption` on the automatic policy or a replica (CMEK) | **Verified** (error codes and messages UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/cmek>)) | `TestSecretManagerCMEK` (#1453), through `cloud.google.com/go/secretmanager/apiv1` over gRPC and REST and `cloud.google.com/go/kms/apiv1` against the instance's Cloud KMS; `TestGcloudSecretsCMEK` (`gcloud secrets create --kms-key-name`, `versions describe`, `secrets replication update --set-kms-key` and `--remove-cmek`); `TestTerraformSecretCMEK` (`google_secret_manager_secret` with `replication.auto.customer_managed_encryption` on a `google_kms_crypto_key`, and a `google_secret_manager_secret_version`; plan clean). As docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/cmek documents: automatic replication takes a key in the `global` location and a user-managed replica a key in its own location, otherwise **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**, as is an empty `kms_key_name`; each version is encrypted when it is added with each key's **primary** version, which `replication_status` reports as `kms_key_version_name`; while a key version it needs is disabled or destroyed, **`AccessSecretVersion` and `AddSecretVersion` are `FAILED_PRECONDITION`** naming the key, with Cloud KMS's message (a failed add uses no version number); an `UpdateSecret` whose mask names `replication` may change or remove the keys, the rest of the policy unchanged, and existing versions keep the keys they were encrypted with. It is envelope encryption through the instance's Cloud KMS `Encrypt` and `Decrypt` only: the payload is sealed (AES-256-GCM) under a fresh data key, which Cloud KMS encrypts under every replica's key; only the sealed payload and the encrypted data keys are stored. Choices Google does not document, pinned by unit `TestCMEKEncryptsAndFailsWhenTheKeyIsDisabled`, `TestCMEKEveryReplicaKeyMustDecrypt`, `TestCMEKKeysCanBeChangedNothingElse`, `TestCMEKKeyRules`, `TestCMEKOverREST`: a version is readable only while **every** replica's key can decrypt (Google routes an access to one replica); the key is not looked up at create or update, so a missing key fails the first `AddSecretVersion`; the Secret Manager service agent's grant on the key is not required (IAM is recorded, not enforced); without Cloud KMS on the instance a key is **`UNIMPLEMENTED`**. A Cloud Run or Cloud Functions `secretKeyRef` or secret volume to a version under a customer-managed key is mounted as its **plaintext**, decrypted by the instance (row `secretKeyRef` or secret volume under a customer-managed key, below; #1489). The `ListSecrets` filter fields `replication.automatic.customer_managed_encryption` and `replication.user_managed.replicas.customer_managed_encryption.kms_key_name` match the keys. From the console: the keys on Create secret and Change encryption keys on a secret's page, and the key versions on a version's page (`TestConsoleSecretCMEK`). |
| `Secret.expire_time` / `ttl` | **Verified** | `TestSecretManagerExpiry` (#1225), through `cloud.google.com/go/secretmanager/apiv1` over gRPC and REST: either is accepted on `CreateSecret` and on an `UpdateSecret` whose mask names `expire_time` or `ttl`; a `ttl` is answered as the `expire_time` it gives (it is input only), and a mask naming either with neither set **clears** the expiry. An expiry less than 60 seconds or more than 100 years away ("A secret's expiration cannot be less than 60 seconds away or more than 100 years away", <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/creating-and-managing-expiring-secrets>, read 2026-10-17), as an `expire_time` or a `ttl`, is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`** on `CreateSecret` and `UpdateSecret` (the page gives no code: UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/creating-and-managing-expiring-secrets>) code and wording). **At its `expire_time` the secret and every version of it are deleted**, on the service's clock: a read treats an expired secret as gone (`NOT_FOUND`, and its ID can be created again) and a sweep deletes it from storage at that time, the Kubernetes Secret holding it included; a 61-second `ttl` is `NOT_FOUND` over both transports once the service's clock passes it. Unit, on a fake clock: `TestSecretExpiresOnTheStoreClock`, `TestExpiredSecretIsGoneOnRead`, `TestUpdateSecretExpiry`, `TestRESTExpiry`, `TestKubeBackedSecretExpires`. Deletion is documented, not measured against Google. |
| `Secret.rotation` (rotation schedules) | **Verified** (error codes and messages UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/secret-rotation>)) | `TestSecretManagerRotationAndDelayedDestroy` (#1278), through `cloud.google.com/go/secretmanager/apiv1` and `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub/v2` against the instance's Pub/Sub: `next_rotation_time` and `rotation_period` are kept and returned by `CreateSecret`, `GetSecret` and `ListSecrets` (gRPC and REST), set, changed or (named with the field unset) cleared by an `UpdateSecret` whose mask names `rotation`, `rotation.next_rotation_time` or `rotation.rotation_period`, and filter `ListSecrets`. The rules are the Secret reference's and docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/secret-rotation's: `next_rotation_time` at least 5 minutes and at most 100 years ahead when it is set, `rotation_period` whole seconds from 1 hour to 100 years, a period needs a `next_rotation_time`, and rotation needs `topics`; each is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`** naming the rule. At `next_rotation_time` a **`SECRET_ROTATE`** notification (the Secret's JSON, with the attributes of the row below) goes to every topic, and `next_rotation_time` advances by the period; Secret Manager changes nothing else, the subscriber adds the version. Three choices UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/secret-rotation>) against Google, pinned by unit `TestRotationNotifiesAndAdvances`: a secret due several periods ago (nothing was running, or the clock was advanced) is notified once and moves to the next time after now; a `next_rotation_time` with no period notifies once and is cleared; the etag does not change when it advances. `rotation_period` is INPUT_ONLY in resources.proto; it is returned, as gcloud shows it. This runs on Secret Manager's clock, which the CloudBurrow extension `cloudburrow.secretmanager.v1.EmulatorClock/Advance` on the same port moves forward (never back) and sweeps before it answers, so a test can pass the documented minimums in a moment; it is the whole instance's clock, and a ttl counts on it. From the console: Create and Edit secret (`TestConsoleSecretRotationAndDestroyDelay`). |
| `RotateSecret`, `EnableManagedRotation` (managed rotation) | **Verified unsupported** | Since #1215, **`UNIMPLEMENTED`** saying why (`TestSecretsManagedRotationIsUnimplemented`). As documented, managed rotation takes Cloud SQL single-user credentials, and each rotation adds a version and changes that user's password in Cloud SQL; it is not the Pub/Sub notification of `Secret.rotation`. Google documents only the request, not what a rotation does to the user or to the secret's versions, and CloudBurrow's Cloud SQL Admin API (#1301) takes no password change from another service, so it is not guessed (#1530 updated the reason, which named no Cloud SQL Admin API, and the coverage page now shows it). Change the password with `users.update` and add a version with `AddSecretVersion` instead. No console Rotate now. |
| `Secret.topics` (event notifications) | **Verified** | `TestSecretManagerTopicNotifications` (#1259), through `cloud.google.com/go/secretmanager/apiv1` and `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub/v2` against the instance's Pub/Sub: up to 10 topics, `projects/*/topics/*`, are kept and returned by `CreateSecret`, `GetSecret`, `ListSecrets` and an `UpdateSecret` whose mask names `topics` (gRPC and REST; `topics` / `topics.name` also filter `ListSecrets`), and each change is published to every topic as docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/event-notifications documents: **`TOPIC_CONFIGURED`** (no data, `eventType` its only attribute) to every topic on a create or update that sets topics, before it is stored, then `SECRET_CREATE`, `SECRET_UPDATE`, `SECRET_DELETE` (`deleteType` `REQUESTED`, or `EXPIRATION` when `expire_time` passes), `SECRET_VERSION_ADD`, `SECRET_VERSION_ENABLE`, `SECRET_VERSION_DISABLE` and `SECRET_VERSION_DESTROY`, each with `eventType`, `dataFormat` `JSON_API_V1`, `secretId` (the secret's full name), `timestamp` (RFC 3339) and, on version events, `versionId` (the version's full name); the data is the Secret's or SecretVersion's JSON (no payload), after the change or, for a delete, before it. Published through the official Pub/Sub client, the path Cloud Scheduler's Pub/Sub targets take; the console sets topics on Create and Edit secret and shows them on the secret's page (`TestConsoleSecretTopics`). **What differs:** a topic that does not exist fails the create or update with Pub/Sub's **`NOT_FOUND`** naming the topic (Google documents only "an error message indicating why the publish failed": the code is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/event-notifications>)); there is no service agent, so no publish permission is checked; a publish that fails after the change was made is written to CloudBurrow's log rather than to the secret's. `SECRET_ROTATE` and `SECRET_VERSION_DESTROY_SCHEDULED` are sent by the rotation schedule and the delayed destruction (#1278, rows above and below). On an instance without Pub/Sub, topics are refused **`UNIMPLEMENTED`** saying so. |
| `Secret.version_destroy_ttl` (delayed destruction) | **Verified** (error codes and messages UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/delay-destruction-of-secret-versions>)) | `TestSecretManagerRotationAndDelayedDestroy` (#1278), through the official client: `version_destroy_ttl` from 1 day to 1000 days (the range docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/delay-destruction-of-secret-versions gives; anything else is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**) is kept, returned, filterable and changed or cleared by an `UpdateSecret` whose mask names it. With it, `DestroySecretVersion` moves the version to **DISABLED** with `scheduled_destroy_time` now plus the ttl, and publishes **`SECRET_VERSION_DESTROY_SCHEDULED`** (`versionId` set; the version's JSON); access is FAILED_PRECONDITION, as for any disabled version. `EnableSecretVersion` or `DisableSecretVersion` before then cancels it, as documented. At `scheduled_destroy_time` the version is destroyed, its payload cleared, and `SECRET_VERSION_DESTROY` is published. A changed or removed ttl applies to later destroys only; deleting or expiring the secret destroys every version at once, as documented. UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/delay-destruction-of-secret-versions>): a second destroy of a scheduled version is FAILED_PRECONDITION here; the version reads DISABLED until the sweep runs, which is at the scheduled time. Same clock as `rotation` above; unit `TestDelayedVersionDestroy`. From the console: Destroy (delayed) on the version's page, with the scheduled time on it (`TestConsoleSecretRotationAndDestroyDelay`). |
| `Secret.version_aliases` | **Verified** (error codes UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-19: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/assign-alias-to-secret-version>)) | `TestSecretManagerVersionAliases` (#1850), through `cloud.google.com/go/secretmanager/apiv1`: an `UpdateSecret` whose mask names `version_aliases` sets (or, with none, clears) the aliases, `GetSecret` returns them, and `GetSecretVersion` and `AccessSecretVersion` reach a version by its alias (`.../versions/ALIAS`), answering with its number. The rules are resources.proto's and the docs page's: at most 63 letters, numerals, hyphens and underscores, starting with a letter; never `latest` or `NEW`, case-insensitively; at most 50 on a secret; each is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**. Choices Google does not document, pinned by unit `TestVersionAliasesAreSetReadAndResolved`: an alias to a version that does not exist is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; an unknown alias is `NOT_FOUND`; the calls that change a version (enable, disable, destroy) refuse an alias with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, as the field says access by alias is only supported on `GetSecretVersion` and `AccessSecretVersion`; an alias to a destroyed version is kept. The `ListSecrets` filter field `version_aliases` matches the aliases' names (`TestVersionAliasFilter`). From the console: Version aliases on Create secret and Edit secret, the Overview and the Versions tab (`TestConsoleSecretParity`). On creating a secret the field stays refused (next row): no version exists for an alias to name yet. |
| `Secret.secret_type` (#1850) | **Verified** (error codes UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-20: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/creating-and-accessing-secrets>)) | `TestSecretManagerSecretType`, through `cloud.google.com/go/secretmanager/apiv1`: `CreateSecret` keeps the type (CLOUD_SQL_DB_CREDENTIALS, ACCESS_KEY, CERTIFICATE, OTHER_DB_CREDENTIALS or OTHER), `GetSecret` returns it (the REST resource as `secretType`), and an `UpdateSecret` whose mask names `secret_type` is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**, the field being "Optional. Immutable." and the docs saying the type can be set only when the secret is created. Choices Google does not document, pinned by unit `TestSecretTypeIsSetAtCreationAndImmutable`: a number the enum does not define is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; any defined type is accepted on a global or a regional secret. From the console: Secret type (Preview) on Create secret and Create regional secret, and the Overview (`TestConsoleSecretParityRound3`, `TestSecretManagerConsoleRound3`). |

Immutable.") maps a tag key, by its permanent ID (`tagKeys/N`) or namespaced name, to a value, by its permanent ID, namespaced name or short name; each is bound through the instance's Resource Manager to the secret's full resource name, `//secretmanager.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT/secrets/ID` (or `.../locations/LOCATION/secrets/ID` for a regional secret), where `ListTagBindings` and `ListEffectiveTags` find it; `GetSecret` returns no tags. An unknown key or value, a value of another key, or one key named twice is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and nothing is stored; `DeleteSecret` removes the secret's bindings. Without Resource Manager's registry, `tags` stays `UNIMPLEMENTED`. `version_aliases` at creation are checked as `UpdateSecret` checks them (the name rules, at most 50, positive version numbers); a new secret has no versions, so an alias naming one is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` (the message is CloudBurrow's). Unit: `TestCreateSecretBindsTags`, `TestCreateSecretChecksVersionAliases`, `TestBindTagsAtCreation`. |

Secret fields: `name`, `labels.KEY` (and `labels:KEY`), `annotations.KEY`, `create_time`, `expire_time`, `replication.automatic`, `replication.user_managed.replicas.location`, `topics`, `rotation`, `rotation.next_rotation_time`, `rotation.rotation_period` and `version_destroy_ttl` (#1278), and the documented customer-managed encryption and `version_aliases`, which no secret here can carry, so they are never set. Version fields: `name`, `state`, `create_time`, `destroy_time`. With a filter `total_size` is 0, as the page documents. A value list may join its values with `AND` (all match) as well as `OR`, each optionally `NOT` (#1943). **Anything else stays `UNIMPLEMENTED`** naming it, never ignored: an unknown field, and gcloud's `~` regular expressions, which the API itself does not take; a malformed filter, or a value list mixing `AND` and `OR`, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Unit `TestListSecretsFilters`, `TestListSecretVersionsFilters`, `TestUndocumentedListFiltersAreRefusedNotIgnored`. Equality on `name` compares the full resource name; that, and the case sensitivity of `=`, are UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/filtering>). |

An absent etag skips the check. `TestSecretManagerRefusesWhatItWouldDrop`, unit `TestEtagsAreCompared`. |
| **Regional secrets** (`projects/*/locations/*/secrets/*`, `secretmanager.{location}.rep.googleapis.com`) | **Verified** (error codes and messages UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/regional-secrets/regional-secrets-overview>)) | `TestSecretManagerRegionalSecrets` (#1519), through `cloud.google.com/go/secretmanager/apiv1` over gRPC and REST, pointed at the Secret Manager port as a program points it at the regional endpoint (the one port serves every location, since the location is in each resource name), and `cloud.google.com/go/kms/apiv1` against the instance's Cloud KMS: `CreateSecret` under `projects/*/locations/*`, `GetSecret`, `ListSecrets` (a location's own; a project's global listing never includes them, and a regional and a global secret of one ID are two secrets), `UpdateSecret`, `DeleteSecret`, `AddSecretVersion`, `GetSecretVersion`, `ListSecretVersions`, `AccessSecretVersion`, `DisableSecretVersion`, `EnableSecretVersion`, `DestroySecretVersion`, and `GetIamPolicy`, `SetIamPolicy` and `TestIamPermissions` (stored, not enforced, [ADR-0006](adr/0006-iam-policy-surface.md)). As documented, a regional secret has no replication policy (a `replication` on create, or in an update mask, is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`), and its CMEK is the secret's own `customer_managed_encryption`, a key in the secret's location (another location is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`), encrypting each new version through Cloud KMS as #1453 does; a version reports the key version in its own `customer_managed_encryption`, not `replication_status`; an `UpdateSecret` naming `customer_managed_encryption` changes the key for new versions or removes it. **gcloud:** `TestGcloudRegionalSecrets`, through gcloud-setup's `secretmanager` override, which gcloud uses for `--location` in place of the regional host: `gcloud secrets create --location=us-central1 --regional-kms-key-name`, `versions add`, `versions access`, `update --update-labels`, `describe`, `list` and `delete`. **Terraform:** `TestTerraformRegionalSecret`, through `cloudburrow terraform`, which sets `secret_manager_regional_custom_endpoint`: `google_secret_manager_regional_secret` with a `customer_managed_encryption`, `google_secret_manager_regional_secret_version` and `google_secret_manager_regional_secret_iam_member` apply, read back through the official client, plan clean, change in place (labels, the key, the member's role), plan clean and destroy. **Console:** Create secret takes a Location, the list shows each secret's location, and a regional secret's page, versions, Show value, Add version, Change encryption keys, Permissions and Delete reach it (`TestConsoleRegionalSecret`, `TestKMSKeyEncryptsARegionalSecretThroughTheBrowser`). | `GetIamPolicy`, `SetIamPolicy` on `projects/*/secrets/*` | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestSecretIamPolicyIsStoredNotEnforced` (#365, [ADR-0006](adr/0006-iam-policy-surface.md)): bindings set through the official client read back with a new etag, and a stale etag is **ABORTED**. **No RPC consults a stored policy**, so a binding grants and denies nothing here. Conditional bindings are stored with the version 3 rules (#1745, `TestIAMConditionsOnServicePolicies`; from the console, `TestConsoleIAMConditionsOnServicePolicies`); audit configs are **UNIMPLEMENTED** with the field named. A version 3 policy without conditions is accepted, and is read back as version 1. Policies are kept on the secret, so they follow `--mode`, go with `DeleteSecret`, are cleared by `/admin/reset` and are captured by `state save`. From the console's Permissions tab: `TestConsolePermissionsOnASecret` (#793). |
| `TestIamPermissions` on a secret | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | Same test: returns **every** requested permission, the literal truth when nothing is enforced. A test that asserts a principal *lacks* a permission fails here rather than passing falsely. |
| Durability | **Verified, measured** | CI's restart probe (#483): `TestSecretManagerRestartSetup` runs alone just before `stop` and leaves a secret with a version. After `stop` and `up` in persistent mode, `TestSecretManagerAcrossRestart` reads the version back; brought up again with `--mode ephemeral`, it requires the secret to be NOT_FOUND (error code UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/managing-secrets>)). The Secrets live in the workload namespace, which an ephemeral `up` keeps, so once the cluster answers and before `up` is ready an ephemeral run deletes every Secret Manager Secret of the instance not written by itself (each write carries the run's `cloudburrow.dev/epoch` label), and a persistent run deletes what an ephemeral run wrote. |

### Version plane

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AddSecretVersion` | **Verified** | Version numbers increment and are **never reused**, including after a destroy — reuse would let a stale reference resolve to different bytes. Tests: `TestVersionNumbersIncrementAndNeverRepeat`, `TestSecretVersionLifecycle`. |
| `AccessSecretVersion` | **Verified** | Returns the **concrete** version name even when asked for `latest`, so a client can record which bytes it got. The payload carries **`data_crc32c`**, which Google's samples verify (#580). Tests: `TestSecretVersionLifecycle`. |
| Payload checksums on `AddSecretVersion` | **Verified** | A supplied `data_crc32c` that does not match the data is **`INVALID_ARGUMENT`**; `TestSecretManagerRefusesWhatItWouldDrop`, unit `TestPayloadChecksums`. |
| `GetSecretVersion` | **Verified** | Metadata stays readable for a disabled or destroyed version. Tests: `TestSecretVersionLifecycle`, `TestDestroyIsTerminalAndClearsThePayload`. |
| `ListSecretVersions` | **Verified** | Newest first, across page boundaries, with a full-walk test proving no duplicates or gaps. Tests: `TestGRPCListVersionsIsNewestFirstAndPagesWithoutGaps`, `TestListVersionsIsNewestFirst`. |
| `EnableSecretVersion` / `DisableSecretVersion` | **Verified** | A disabled version is `FAILED_PRECONDITION` on access, **not** `NOT_FOUND`: it exists, and saying otherwise sends a caller looking for a creation bug instead of an enable call. Tests: `TestSecretVersionLifecycle`, `TestDisabledVersionIsFailedPreconditionNotNotFound`. |
| `DestroySecretVersion` | **Verified** | Terminal. The payload is **cleared, not flagged**, so a destroyed version cannot leak what it held; re-enabling is refused. Tests: `TestDestroyIsTerminalAndClearsThePayload`, `TestSecretVersionLifecycle`. |
| `latest` alias | **Verified** | The most recently **created** version, per `GetSecretVersionRequest.Name`. Deliberately not "the most recently enabled": a disabled latest fails rather than silently returning older bytes. Tests: `TestLatestIsTheMostRecentlyCreatedNotTheMostRecentlyEnabled`, `TestSecretVersionLifecycle`. |
| Payload limit (64 KiB) and empty payload | **Verified** | Both `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Tests: `TestPayloadLimitsAreEnforced`, `TestSecretErrorsUseGoogleCodes`. |
| **Client-side encryption / CMEK** | **Verified** | Customer-managed keys on a replica or the automatic policy encrypt each version's payload through Cloud KMS; see `customer_managed_encryption` above (#1453). Without them, payloads are stored as given. `Secret.customer_managed_encryption` is a regional secret's key (#1519, its row); on a global secret it is `UNIMPLEMENTED`. Tests: `TestSecretManagerCMEK`, `TestCMEKEncryptsAndFailsWhenTheKeyIsDisabled`. |

### Transport

| Concern | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| gRPC and JSON on one port | **Verified** | One `Store` behind both, so there is one implementation of the contract rather than two that drift. gRPC is served through `grpc.Server.ServeHTTP` behind `h2c`, which upstream documents as lower-performance than a dedicated listener — worth it to match the real service's shape locally. Tests: `TestRESTLifecycleSharesTheStoreWithGRPC`. |
| Google error envelope over REST | **Verified** | Google's JSON mapping of `google.rpc.Status`, `{"error":{"code":400,"message":"...","status":"FAILED_PRECONDITION","details":[...]}}`, with `details` when the status has them (#1470). `status` names the canonical code where the HTTP code cannot: gcloud prints it (`TestGcloudSecretManagerErrorStatus`: FAILED_PRECONDITION, ABORTED; ALREADY_EXISTS is read from the official REST client's error body, since gcloud words a 409 on `projects/P/secrets` itself), unit `TestWriteJSONCarriesStatus`. |
| Custom methods (`:addVersion`, `:access`, `:enable`, `:disable`, `:destroy`) | **Verified** | `net/http` cannot express a wildcard followed by a literal in one path segment, so the verb is captured with the ID and split by the handler. An unrecognised verb is `UNIMPLEMENTED`, not 404. Tests: `TestRESTLifecycleSharesTheStoreWithGRPC`, `TestRESTVersionStateEndpoints`. |
| Kubernetes-backed storage | **Verified** | One GCP secret is one Kubernetes Secret holding its metadata in an annotation, and **each version is a Kubernetes Secret of its own** (#1596), `<the secret's Secret>-v<N>`, its payload in `data["vN"]` and its metadata in an annotation, all labelled `cloudburrow.dev/owned=true`. Applied **server-side**, because a client-side apply copies every payload into `last-applied-configuration` — an annotation `kubectl describe` prints. Tests: `TestPayloadLandsInKubernetesData`, `TestOwnershipLabelsAreApplied`, `TestApplyIsServerSideSoPayloadsStayOutOfAnnotations`. **As many versions as Google allows** (#1596): Secret Manager documents no cap on a secret's versions (docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/quotas: a payload of at most 64 KiB), and until #1596 every version's metadata was an annotation on the one Secret, so Kubernetes' 256 KiB cap on annotations made the 905th `AddSecretVersion` `INTERNAL`. The Secrets are listed once, when the instance starts, and reads are answered from that copy, which every write updates once the cluster has taken it, so a read runs no kubectl and a write one small apply per record, however many versions there are: `TestSecretTwoThousandVersions` adds 2,000 versions through the official client, reads the first and the last back, and finds the p99 of the last 200 `AddSecretVersion` and `AccessSecretVersion` calls within twice that of the first 200 (unit `TestManyVersionsStaySmallAndFlat`). Deleting a secret is one DeleteCollection of its Secrets. **A secret stored in the earlier layout is migrated when the instance starts**: each version is written to a Secret of its own, then the version annotations are removed from the secret's Secret; its payloads stay there, since a revision deployed earlier references them, until the version is destroyed (`TestOldLayoutIsMigratedToASecretPerVersion`, `TestMigrationCutShortIsFinished`). A Cloud Run secret volume of several versions reads several Kubernetes Secrets, so it is rendered as a `projected` volume with a source per Secret; one version stays a `secret` volume: `TestRunJobMountsTwoVersionsInOneVolume` mounts versions 1 and `latest` of one secret in one volume of a job, through the official `run/apiv2` and `secretmanager/apiv1` clients, and the task exits 0 only when both files hold their payloads (unit `TestSecretVolumeOfSeveralVersionsIsProjected`). |
| `secretKeyRef` in a Cloud Run revision | **Verified** | `TestCloudRunRevisionReadsASecretManagerSecret`: the container reports the payload, and the test also asserts the payload is **not** in the deployed Knative Service — the revision reads it from the cluster rather than having it templated in. |
| `latest` in a `secretKeyRef` | **Verified, with a pinned result** | Kubernetes has no `latest` key, so the alias is resolved to a concrete version **at deployment**. A running revision does not pick up a version added later: `TestCloudRunRevisionReadsASecretManagerSecret` (#1576) adds a version under the running revision, which goes on answering the deployed version's value for 15 s, and no new revision is made. Cloud Run behaves the same way for environment variables. Tests: `TestResolveSecretRefPointsAtTheKubernetesObject`, `TestCloudRunRevisionReadsASecretManagerSecret` (the resolution at deployment). |
| Reference to a disabled or destroyed version | **Verified refused** | `FAILED_PRECONDITION` at deploy time. Accepting it would produce a pod that fails to start with Kubernetes complaining about a missing key — a message pointing nowhere near the cause. Tests: `TestSecretKeyRefToAnInaccessibleVersionIsRefused`, `TestResolveSecretRefRefusesAnInaccessibleVersion`. |
| Secret volume mounts | **Verified** | `TestRunServiceVolumesAndServiceAccount`, `TestRunJobMountsSecretAndMemoryVolumes` (#1297): a `secret` volume is a Kubernetes secret volume of the Secret holding the secret's versions, each item a version (`latest` resolved at deployment, as for `secretKeyRef`) at its path, with its mode; with no items, the latest version in a file named after the secret. The task reads the payload from the file; the Knative Service and batch Job carry the reference, not the payload. Mounts are read-only, as Knative requires and Cloud Run does. |
| `secretKeyRef` or secret volume to a version under a customer-managed key | **Verified** (error codes and messages UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/secrets>)) | `TestRunMountsASecretUnderACustomerManagedKey` (#1489), through `cloud.google.com/go/run/apiv2`, `cloud.google.com/go/secretmanager/apiv1` and `cloud.google.com/go/kms/apiv1`: a job's task reads a version under a `global` key (#1453) as a `secretKeyRef` variable and as a secret volume file and exits 0 only when both are the plaintext; with the key version **disabled**, `RunJob` and a service's `CreateService` are **`FAILED_PRECONDITION`** naming the key (a secret Cloud Run cannot access stops the deployment, and variables are read when an instance starts, as docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/configuring/services/secrets documents); once enabled again the job runs. The stored Secret keeps the sealed payload: the instance decrypts the version through its own Cloud KMS, as `AccessSecretVersion` does, and writes the plaintext to a second Kubernetes Secret, `<stored name>-plain`, which the pod references; the pod is never given a key. Cloud Functions' secret variables and volumes (#1464) are rendered into the same Cloud Run template, so take the same path. While deployed, every mounted version is re-checked every 10 s: with its key disabled or destroyed, or the version disabled or destroyed, its plaintext is removed, so an instance that starts then fails (Kubernetes reports the missing key) while running instances keep what they read; it is put back once the key decrypts again (unit `TestMountFollowsTheKeyAndTheVersion`, `TestResolveSecretRefMountsTheDecryptedPayload`). The copy goes with the secret (delete, expiry, `reset`). A secret volume mixing versions with and without a key reads two Kubernetes Secrets, and is rendered as a `projected` volume (#1596, as two versions without a key are, `TestRunJobMountsTwoVersionsInOneVolume`; the mix itself is not run end to end; it was `UNIMPLEMENTED` before). |
| Namespace | — | Secrets live in the **workload** namespace, not the managed one, because `secretKeyRef` cannot cross namespaces. `cloudburrow reset` removes them **by ownership label**, so it can never touch an object CloudBurrow did not create. |
| **Project ID validation differs from Cloud Run** | Known inconsistency | Secret Manager accepts any valid resource ID; the Cloud Run adapter enforces GCP's 6-30 character project rule. The same project string can therefore be valid for one and not the other. Recorded rather than silently changed. |

## Cloud Storage — notifications to Pub/Sub

The storage server serves `notificationConfigs` and **detects the events itself** (#506).
Every event is written to an outbox in the same transaction as the mutation that caused it; a
dispatcher then publishes it to the Pub/Sub emulator after commit and deletes it once
published, retrying a failed publish (up to 20 attempts, so a topic that never exists cannot
hold the queue forever), so an event is never lost between the mutation and the publish. In an
instance the emulator is the cluster's Pub/Sub; `storage-server --pubsub-emulator host:port`
names one, and without one, creating a configuration is 501.

| Capability | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `notificationConfigs` insert / get / list / delete | **Verified** | `TestNotificationConfigsCRUDThroughTheSDK`, through the official Storage client; delete is 204 with no body. IDs are per bucket and never reused. At most 100 configurations per bucket and 10 custom attributes each; the refusal's code, 400, is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/pubsub-notifications>). A configuration goes with its bucket. An identical configuration is not refused (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/pubsub-notifications>)). |
| Standard attributes and payload | **Verified** | `TestObjectUploadDeliversANotification`, uploaded with the Storage SDK and received with the Pub/Sub SDK: `eventType`, `bucketId`, `objectId`, `objectGeneration`, `payloadFormat`, `eventTime` and `notificationConfig`, with the Storage Object resource as the body. |
| Filters | **Verified** | `TestNotificationFiltersAreHonoured`: `object_name_prefix` and `event_types`, where an empty list means **all** types, as the API defines it. |
| `custom_attributes` and `payload_format: NONE` | **Verified in process** | `TestNotificationEventsAndFilters`: custom attributes are added and **cannot overwrite a standard attribute**; NONE sends attributes only. |
| Service-qualified topic form | **Verified** | The official client sends `//pubsub.googleapis.com/projects/{p}/topics/{t}` and parses it back; both spellings are accepted and the bare one stored. Tests: `TestNotificationConfigsCRUDThroughTheSDK`, `TestNotificationEventsAndFilters`. |
| `OBJECT_FINALIZE` | **Verified** for an upload and a copy, with `overwroteGeneration` when a live version was replaced, and (#1576) for a rewrite, a compose, a move's destination (after the source's `OBJECT_DELETE`) and a restore, each naming the new generation. Tests: `TestNotificationEventsAndFilters`, `TestNotificationOverwroteGenerationAttributes`, `TestNotificationFinalizeForRewriteComposeMoveAndRestore`, `TestObjectUploadDeliversANotification`. |
| `OBJECT_DELETE` | **Verified** | `TestNotificationDeleteAndMetadataUpdate`. Sent when a version leaves the bucket: a delete, an overwrite on an unversioned bucket (with `overwrittenByGeneration`), a lifecycle delete or a move's source. Under soft delete (#499) it is sent when the object is soft-deleted (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-10-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/pubsub-notifications>)). |
| `OBJECT_METADATA_UPDATE` | **Verified** | `TestNotificationDeleteAndMetadataUpdate`: a patch or update. |
| **`OBJECT_ARCHIVE`** | **Verified** | `TestNotificationArchiveOnVersionedOverwrite`: a live version made noncurrent by a delete or an overwrite, with `overwrittenByGeneration` naming the new one. |
| Payload | **Verified** | The Storage Object resource, with Google's `https://storage.googleapis.com` links, since a payload is built outside any request. Tests: `TestNotificationEventsAndFilters`, `TestObjectUploadDeliversANotification`. |
| Ordering and delivery | **At least once** | Events are published in the order they were committed. A failed publish is retried; one that fails 20 times is dropped and counted. |
| Across a restart | **Verified, measured** (configurations) | Configurations and undelivered events are in the server's store (`--data-dir`), so they follow `--mode`. CI's restart probe measures configurations (#701): `TestStorageAcrossRestart` creates one at setup against the in-cluster server, finds it, on the same topic, after `stop` and `up` in persistent mode, and finds it gone after `up --mode ephemeral`. Undelivered events are not probed. The check job's builtin server has no Pub/Sub emulator in its restart probe, so there it refuses the configuration (501) and the probe covers the rest. |
| Without Pub/Sub | **Excluded**, verified | `TestStorageNotificationsWithoutPubSub` (#1444), on an instance started with `--services storage` alone: `notifications.insert` is 501 naming the reason (a configuration needs a Pub/Sub emulator to deliver to), never accepted and dropped, since there is no topic to verify, as Google requires one to exist, or to publish to; `list` answers (empty) and `get` is 404. With Pub/Sub on the instance the rows above apply. |

## Resource Manager — `google.cloud.resourcemanager.v3` (Projects, Folders, Organizations, Tags, Liens)

**v3 Projects** (#298), **Folders and Organizations** (#1294), over gRPC and the v3 REST paths,
**v1 REST `projects.list/get/create/update/delete/getAncestry`** and `organizations.get/search`
(#301, #1265, #1294), which `gcloud projects`, `gcloud organizations` and Terraform's
`google_project` call, and **v2 REST folders** (#1294), which `gcloud resource-manager folders`
calls, are served on `--port-resourcemanager` (default `9007`) from the **same registry the
console lists**. Per-method status for v3 is generated in
[coverage/resourcemanager.md](coverage/resourcemanager.md), and for v1 REST and liens, by discovery ID, in
[coverage/resourcemanagerv1.md](coverage/resourcemanagerv1.md).

**The local organization** is fixed and the same on every instance: `organizations/100000000001`,
display name (domain) `cloudburrow.local`, directory customer ID `C0cloudburrow`, always `ACTIVE`.
It cannot be created or deleted, and any other organization is NOT_FOUND. Folders are created under
it or under other folders; projects may be created in, or moved to, either. A project created with
no parent, as every project was before #1294 (and the instance's own project), stays top-level:
its `parent` is empty and its ancestry is the project alone.

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `CreateProject`, `GetProject`, `SearchProjects`, `UpdateProject` (labels), `DeleteProject` | **Verified** | `TestResourceManagerV3Projects`, with `cloud.google.com/go/resourcemanager/apiv3` against the CI instance. Create, Update and Delete return **completed** long-running operations, since each change is made before the call returns. Update accepts `display_name` and `labels` in the mask and refuses anything else. |
| One store with the console | **Verified** | The same test: a project created through the API is in the console's project list, one created in the console is found by `SearchProjects`, and an API delete removes it from the console. Tests: `TestResourceManagerV3Projects`. |
| `ListProjects` | **Verified** | It lists a folder's or the organization's direct children, with `show_deleted` and paging (`TestResourceManagerV3Folders`, #1294). A folder or organization that does not exist is NOT_FOUND, an empty parent is INVALID_ARGUMENT pointing at `SearchProjects`, as in Google's API, and a top-level project is listed under no parent (`TestResourceManagerV3ListProjects`, #691). |
| `SearchProjects` query | **Partial** | Space-separated `key:value` terms, all of which must match: `id`, `projectId`, `name`, `displayName`, `state`, `parent` (`folders/N` or `organizations/N`), `parent.type`, `parent.id` and `labels.KEY`. `OR`, wildcards and any other key are INVALID_ARGUMENT, never ignored. |
| Delete and `UndeleteProject` | **Verified** | `TestResourceManagerV3Projects` (#1216): as on Google, a deleted project is kept in `DELETE_REQUESTED` for 30 days ([Shutting down projects](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-projects#shutting_down_projects)): `GetProject` reads it, its ID cannot be taken by `CreateProject` (ALREADY_EXISTS), and `UndeleteProject` makes it `ACTIVE` again. Undeleting an active project is FAILED_PRECONDITION, and so are a second delete and an `UpdateProject` of a deleted one (not measured against Google). `SearchProjects` leaves a deleted project out unless the query has a `state` term, and v1 `list` unless the filter has `lifecycleState`, as `ListProjects` needs `show_deleted` (not measured). After 30 days the record is purged and the ID is free again, where Google never reuses one. v1 `undelete` is served too. **A purge drops the project's state** (#1537, `TestAPurgedProjectsIDStartsEmpty`, with the official clients): its IAM policy and audit configs, org policies, liens, tag bindings on it and on resources in it, the tag keys it parents with their values, its Service Usage API states, and, through each service's per-project reset, its buckets, topics and subscriptions, queues (with CMEK configs), secrets, KMS resources, Scheduler jobs and Logging entries and configuration; and (#1540, `TestAPurgedProjectsDataGoesEverywhere`) its Cloud Run services, jobs with their executions, worker pools, instances and functions (with each function's Eventarc trigger) and its Cloud Build builds, triggers and worker pools, its Spanner instances and databases, its Bigtable instances and tables, its Firestore documents (in `(default)`, every database the Admin API made, and since #1550 every database a documents call named, which the call front shows the Admin API) with the Admin API's records, its Datastore entities in every namespace of the default database and (#1550) of every named database a call named (the call front keeps them as entities of its own in the emulator), its Bigtable tables under any instance a call named, made by the instance admin or not (#1550), its Memorystore instances with their servers, and what the Spanner, Bigtable and Firestore fronts keep for it; its BigQuery datasets go with their tables, routines and models and the front's undelete copies (the emulator serves one project, so this is measured with a project-scoped reset, `TestAProjectResetDropsItsBigQueryDatasets`); since #1781 (`TestBigQueryPurgedProjectStartsEmpty`, official Go client, a project of Resource Manager) every one of its datasets goes with its tables, views, SQL functions, table functions, procedures, routines `routines.insert` made, models and row access policies, and its jobs, every user's, so a project made again under the ID lists no job, reads none of the old ones (404) and makes `CREATE FUNCTION` of an old name anew (it was 409 Already Exists: the purge's deletes, which carry the linked writer's header, bypassed the front's purge path). A project created again under the ID reads none of it. Resource Manager, Service Usage, Logging, the metadata server, the Cloud Run, Functions and Cloud Build service agents, the console and Cloud Storage (its `projectNumber`, `project-<team>-<number>` ACL entities and service agent) and, since #1551, BigQuery's `projects.getServiceAccount` all report the record's number. The console lists a deleted project as `DELETE_REQUESTED` and offers **Restore** on its page (#1865; same test; unit `TestProjectUndeleteIsOfferedOnlyWhenDeleted`). |
| `Projects.GetIamPolicy`, `Projects.SetIamPolicy`, `Projects.TestIamPermissions` | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestResourceManagerProjectIAM` (#1368), with `cloud.google.com/go/resourcemanager/apiv3` `ProjectsClient` and `google.golang.org/api/cloudresourcemanager/v1`: a policy set through either reads back through both with a new etag; a stale etag is ABORTED (409 over REST), and a version 3 policy without conditions is accepted. **IAM Conditions** (#1742, `TestResourceManagerIAMConditions`, with the v3 `ProjectsClient` and the v1 REST client), as Google's "Policy versions" and "Overview of IAM Conditions" document them: a binding's `condition` (a required title, an optional description, a required CEL expression) is stored and read back in a version 3 policy when version 3 is requested; a conditional binding in a version 1 or unversioned policy, a condition without a title or an expression, an expression that does not compile or is not a boolean, more than 12 logic operators, and more than 20 conditions for one role and principal (IAM quotas) are INVALID_ARGUMENT (Google publishes no message text for these; UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/policies>)); a version 1 (or unversioned) read renders each conditional role as `ROLE_withcond_HASH` without its condition, a version 1 set of that rendering keeps the condition, and a policy mixing conditions and such roles is refused `Policy cannot contain both conditions and condition hashes`. The expression language is the CEL subset Google's attribute reference documents for `resource.name` (`==`, `!=`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `extract`), `resource.type` and `resource.service` (`==`, `!=`) and `request.time` (comparisons with `timestamp()`, `date()`, `± duration()`, and the `get*` functions with an optional time zone), with `&&`, `||`, `!` and `in`; other attributes (`request.path`, `request.host`, resource tags, `api.getAttribute`, `destination.*`, `principal.*`) are refused INVALID_ARGUMENT ([gaps.md](gaps.md)). A condition is evaluated where a check consults the policy: Firestore with MongoDB compatibility's sign-ins (below, `TestFirestoreMongoDBIAMConditions`) and Memorystore's IAM auth (#1745: per cluster or instance, `request.time` and its effective tags, its own and the project's, are evaluated; a `resource.*` part grants nothing, because Memorystore is not among the services Google's "Resource attributes for IAM Conditions" lists: "Other services and resource types do not recognize resource attributes"; `TestMemorystoreIAMConditions`, #1748). **Every attribute Google's attribute reference documents for a role binding compiles** (#1745, `TestIAMConditionAttributes`): resource tags (`resource.hasTagKey`, `hasTagKeyId`, `matchTag`, `matchTagId`), `request.path`, `request.host`, `request.auth.access_levels`, `destination.ip`, `destination.port`, `api.getAttribute` with `hasOnly` (`iam.googleapis.com/modifiedGrantsByRole` only on projects, folders and organizations, as Google accepts it), `api.getAttribute` with a map default (#1748: `aiplatform.googleapis.com/memoryScope`'s `{}`, with map literals, `==`, `in` and `[key]` as Google's "Control access to Memory Bank with IAM Conditions" writes them; a default of another type than the attribute's is refused), `compute.isForwardingRuleCreationOperation` and `compute.matchLoadBalancingSchemes`; `principal.type` and `principal.subject`, which the reference documents for Principal Access Boundary policies only, are INVALID_ARGUMENT. Where a check does not supply an attribute (no IAP, no Compute Engine forwarding rule here), the part that reads it grants nothing, as Google documents. Conditions on other services' own policies follow Google's "Services that allow conditions": Bigtable, BigQuery, Cloud KMS, Cloud Logging, Cloud Run, Resource Manager tags, Secret Manager, Spanner and Cloud Storage buckets store them (`TestIAMConditionsOnServicePolicies`, `TestSpannerIAMConditions`, `TestStorageBucketIAMConditions`); Pub/Sub, Cloud Tasks, Artifact Registry, Secure Source Manager and Cloud Functions refuse them INVALID_ARGUMENT (`TestPubSubIAMHandle`, `TestQueueIamPolicyIsStoredNotEnforced`); Google does not publish that refusal's text. The hash in `ROLE_withcond_HASH` is CloudBurrow's own (20 hex digits of a SHA-256 over the binding's role and condition); Google's is undocumented. **Audit configs are stored, not acted on** (#1486, `TestResourceManagerAuditConfigs`): set when the update mask names `audit_configs`, kept when it does not (with no mask, `bindings, etag` is used, as `iam_policy.proto` documents), cleared by a mask naming them with none, and an audit config without a service or a log type is INVALID_ARGUMENT; Cloud Storage writes its Data Access audit logs by them (#1979); no other service's audit log is written or withheld because of one. `TestTerraformProjectIAMAuditConfig` drives `google_project_iam_audit_config` (apply, clean plan, a changed exempted member, clean plan, destroy). The same holds for folders and the organization. A project is named by ID or number; one that does not exist is NOT_FOUND, one pending deletion keeps its policy and refuses a set (FAILED_PRECONDITION), and one purged loses it. `TestIamPermissions` answers every well-formed permission a project can hold (any service's), less `resourcemanager.folders.*` and `resourcemanager.organizations.*`; nothing is denied. **Nothing inherits it**: a resource's own `getIamPolicy` shows only its own bindings, and one project's policy is not another's ([ADR-0006](adr/0006-iam-policy-surface.md), amended by the maintainer on 2026-10-15). Kept in the registry's store, captured by `state save`; `/admin/reset` (component `resourcemanager`, also with `project=`) clears the policies, and the org policies, liens and tags (#1537), and keeps the projects and folders. In the console: **IAM & Admin > IAM**, the selected project's policy with Grant access, Remove principal and Test permissions (`TestConsoleProjectIAM`); the project's, a folder's and the organization's Permissions tabs list each binding's condition, Grant access takes one, and a row's **Add condition** / **Edit condition** changes it (`TestResourceHierarchyFolderIAMConditions`, #1742). |

## IAM custom roles — `google.iam.admin.v1`

**Built** (#1743, #1746). The IAM API's custom roles, `projects.roles` and `organizations.roles`,
Google's predefined roles (`roles.get`, `roles.list`), `roles.queryGrantableRoles` and
`permissions.queryTestablePermissions` are served on the Resource Manager port (`--port-resourcemanager`,
default `9007`), over gRPC (`google.iam.admin.v1.IAM`, the official `cloud.google.com/go/iam/admin/apiv1`
client) and the transcoded v1 REST paths (`google.golang.org/api/iam/v1`, gcloud, Terraform), always,
as Resource Manager is. `gcloud-setup` writes the `iam` override; `cloudburrow terraform` sets
`iam_custom_endpoint` and `iam_beta_custom_endpoint` (provider 8.4.0's IAM client for custom roles
reads the latter). Roles are kept in the registry's store beside the policies that grant them, with
its persistence and snapshots; a purged project's roles go with it, and `/admin/reset` clears them.
Per-method status is generated in [coverage/iam.md](coverage/iam.md). Behaviour follows Google's
[Roles and permissions](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-overview) and
[Create and manage custom roles](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/creating-custom-roles) (read
2026-11-17). Service accounts (#1747) follow [Create service accounts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-accounts-create), [Delete and restore service accounts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-accounts-delete-undelete), [IAM quotas and limits](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/quotas) and the `projects.serviceAccounts` reference (read 2026-11-17); they are kept in the registry's store with the roles, a purged project's go with it, and `/admin/reset` clears them.

A role is named `projects/{project ID}/roles/{id}` (a project number in a request is taken) or `organizations/100000000001/roles/{id}`. **Role ID**: 3 to 64 letters, digits, underscores and periods, else `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; an ID in use is `ALREADY_EXISTS`, and the ID of a deleted role whose deletion has not completed `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, as Google's `roles.create` sample catches it ("already exists and in deleted state", #1746). **Limits**: a title of at most 100 bytes, a description of at most 300, at most 3,000 permissions and 64 KB of title, description and permission names, `INVALID_ARGUMENT` beyond; at most 300 custom roles a project or the organization (the 301st is `FAILED_PRECONDITION`; the code Google answers is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-17: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/creating-custom-roles>)). A deleted role counts until it is scheduled for permanent deletion, which Google puts "7 to 14 days after the initial request", here when the 7 days to undelete it end (#1746); that it does not count after is Google's. **Permissions** must be listed SUPPORTED or TESTING on Google's [custom roles support page](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/custom-roles-permissions-support), all 14,527 of which are embedded (`internal/iamroles`); an unknown or NOT_SUPPORTED one, or, in a project role, a permission on an organization or folder (`resourcemanager.organizations.*`, `resourcemanager.folders.*`, `compute.organizations.*`, `cloudkms.folders.*`), is `INVALID_ARGUMENT` `Permission P is not valid.`, as Google documents. Deleting a deleted role and undeleting a live one are `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, the codes Google's `roles.delete` and `roles.undelete` samples catch (`TestIAMPredefinedRoles`, #1746).
