## Workload Identity Federation — `iam.googleapis.com` v1 pools, `sts.googleapis.com` v1

**Built** (#1941). The IAM API's workload identity pools, their providers and the providers' keys are
served as JSON on the Resource Manager port (the IAM endpoint: `google.golang.org/api/iam/v1`, gcloud's
`iam` override, Terraform's `iam_beta_custom_endpoint`), kept in the registry's store; the Security
Token Service's `POST /v1/token` is served on the metadata port, beside IAM Credentials. Per-method
status is generated in [coverage/workloadidentity.md](coverage/workloadidentity.md). Behaviour follows
Google's [Workload Identity Federation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation),
[Principal identifiers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/principal-identifiers), the IAM v1
`projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools` reference and the STS v1 `token` reference (read 2026-11-19).
Everything stays local: an issuer's keys are the provider's `oidc.jwksJson`, or are fetched from the
issuer's discovery document only when the issuer is a loopback address (CloudBurrow accepts an
`http://127.0.0.1` or `http://localhost` issuer for this; Google requires `https://`), and nothing is
asked of AWS or any remote IdP.

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.create`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.get`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.list`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.patch`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.delete`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.undelete`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.operations.get` | **Verified** | `TestWorkloadIdentityPools` (official REST client), `TestGcloudIAMWorkloadIdentityPools`, `TestTerraformIAMWorkloadIdentityPool`. A pool ID is 4 to 32 characters of `[a-z0-9-]`, not starting `gcp-` (`INVALID_ARGUMENT`); the only location is `global`; names are under the project number; a display name is at most 32 characters, a description 256; create, patch (`displayName`, `description`, `disabled`; any other mask path `INVALID_ARGUMENT`), delete and undelete answer a done Operation that `operations.get` reads. Delete is soft: `DELETED` with an `expireTime` 30 days on, listed only with `showDeleted`, still read by get, its ID not reusable (`ALREADY_EXISTS`) until it is purged. Only `FEDERATION_ONLY` pools: managed workload identity (`TRUST_DOMAIN`, `inlineCertificateIssuanceConfig`, namespaces, attestation rules) is 501, and the pools' own IAM policies (`getIamPolicy`, `setIamPolicy`, `testIamPermissions`) are 501. |
| `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.listAttestationRules` | **Verified** | `TestTerraformIAMWorkloadIdentityPool`: Terraform reads it after every apply; a federation pool has none (an empty list). |
| `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.create`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.get`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.list`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.patch`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.delete`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.undelete`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.operations.get` | **Verified** | `TestWorkloadIdentityPools`, `TestGcloudIAMWorkloadIdentityPools` (`create-oidc`, `update-oidc`), `TestTerraformIAMWorkloadIdentityPool`. Exactly one of `oidc`, `aws`, `saml` and `x509` (`INVALID_ARGUMENT` otherwise). OIDC needs `issuerUri`, at most 10 allowed audiences of up to 256 characters, a valid `jwksJson` when set (RSA or EC P-256 keys), and an attribute mapping with `google.subject`; AWS a 12-digit account ID and Google's default mapping (`google.subject=assertion.arn`, `attribute.aws_role` with `extract()`); SAML metadata (at most 128K characters) with an IdP entity ID and one to three signing certificates, one not expired; X.509 a trust store of PEM trust anchors and intermediates, and the default mapping `google.subject=assertion.subject.dn.cn`. Mappings and conditions are CEL (`assertion`, `google`, `attribute`, the strings extension and `extract()`): keys `google.subject`, `google.groups`, `google.display_name`, `google.posix_username` and up to 50 `attribute.NAME` (`[a-z0-9_]`, 100 characters), each expression at most 2,048 characters, a condition at most 4,096 and boolean. A disabled provider exchanges no token; a deleted pool's providers cannot be undeleted before it. `actorProviders` is 501. |
| `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.keys.create`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.keys.get`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.keys.list`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.keys.delete`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.keys.undelete`, `iam.projects.locations.workloadIdentityPools.providers.keys.operations.get` | **Verified** | `TestWorkloadIdentityPools`: an `ENCRYPTION` key of `RSA_2048`, `RSA_3072` or `RSA_4096` is generated here and its certificate returned as `RSA_X509_PEM`; soft delete and undelete as pools. A live key decrypts the provider's encrypted SAML assertions at the STS (#2065); its private key is kept by the instance and never answered. |
| `sts.token` | **Verified** | `TestWorkloadIdentityFederationSTS` (`google.golang.org/api/sts/v1`, and `golang.org/x/oauth2/google` and `cloud.google.com/go/auth` reading Google's `external_account` credential configuration with a file-sourced credential, `token_url` and `service_account_impersonation_url` pointing at this instance), `TestWorkloadIdentityFederationStorage`. Form-encoded (the auth libraries) or JSON (the discovery client). `grant_type` must be token exchange (`unsupported_grant_type`) and `requested_token_type` an access token; an OIDC token (`jwt` or `id_token`) is verified as Google documents: `RS256` or `ES256`, a `kid` in the provider's keys, `iss` the provider's issuer, `aud` one of the allowed audiences or, with none, the provider's own name with or without `https:`, `exp` in the future and `iat` at most 24 hours ago, each failure `invalid_grant` with Google's description; an attribute condition that refuses is `invalid_grant` "The given credential is rejected by the attribute condition."; an audience naming no provider, or a disabled or deleted pool or provider, is `invalid_target`. The token is opaque and lasts an hour (`expires_in` 3600); its account is the subject's `principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/N/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/P/subject/S`, and the `principalSet://` identifiers of its pool (`/*`), its groups (`/group/G`) and each custom attribute (`/attribute.NAME/VALUE`) are kept from its latest exchange. A SAML assertion (`saml2`) is verified and mapped (#2065, below, under Workforce Identity Federation). Not exchanged (501 with an OAuth error): AWS (`aws4_request`, which Google verifies with AWS), X.509 (`mtls`), a Google access token (Credential Access Boundary), `actor_token`; a workforce provider's audience is exchanged (#2056, below). |

Federated identities in IAM (#1941): a federated token is an access token this instance minted, so IAM
enforcement (`up --iam-enforcement=on`) checks it as the `principal://` identifier with its
`principalSet://` identifiers as its members, in allow policies (`TestWorkloadIdentityFederationStorage`:
Cloud Storage refuses with Google's 403 naming the `principal://`, and reads once the subject or its
group's `principalSet://` holds `roles/storage.objectViewer` on the bucket) and in deny policies.
Impersonation is IAM Credentials' `generateAccessToken` with the federated token as the caller: the
account's policy must grant `iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken` (`roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser`) to
the `principal://` or a matching `principalSet://` (403 otherwise). While its pool is disabled or
deleted, a federated token is refused (401) everywhere, and grants again when the pool is enabled or
undeleted, as Google documents. The console's IAM & Admin > Workload Identity Federation lists, creates,
edits, disables, deletes and restores pools and providers (`TestIAMWorkloadIdentityFederationPage`).

### Workforce Identity Federation (#2056)

The IAM API's `locations.workforcePools`, their providers (OIDC and SAML), the providers' keys and
the pools' subjects are served beside the workload pools, organization-scoped: a pool's `parent` is
the instance's organization (`organizations/100000000001`; another is 404), its name
`locations/global/workforcePools/ID`, and `list` needs `parent`. Behaviour follows Google's
[Workforce Identity Federation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workforce-identity-federation),
[Manage workforce pools and providers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/manage-workforce-identity-pools-providers),
[Principal identifiers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/principal-identifiers) and the IAM v1
`locations.workforcePools` reference (read 2026-11-20).

|---|---|---|

A pool ID is 6 to 63 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, starting with a letter, not ending with a hyphen, globally unique, `gcp-` refused; display name at most 32 characters, description 256; `sessionDuration` 900s to 43200s (3600s by default) is the exchanged token's lifetime; `accessRestrictions.disableProgrammaticSignin` refuses every STS exchange (`allowedServices` is immutable). Create, patch, delete and undelete answer a done Operation; delete is soft (DELETED, `expireTime` 30 days on, listed with `showDeleted`, the ID not reusable). A disabled or deleted pool exchanges no token and its tokens are refused (401) until it is enabled or undeleted. |

The STS exchange for a workforce provider (`sts.token`; `TestWorkforceIdentityFederationSTS`, with
`google.golang.org/api/sts/v1`, and `golang.org/x/oauth2/google` and `cloud.google.com/go/auth`
reading an `external_account` configuration with `workforce_pool_user_project`): the `audience` is
`//iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/POOL/providers/PROVIDER`, an OIDC token
(`subject_token_type` `id_token` or `jwt`) whose `aud` must be the provider's `clientId`
(`invalid_grant` otherwise), verified and mapped as for workload pools, with Google's workforce
limits (mapped attributes at most 16 KB, `google.display_name` 100 bytes). `options.userProject`
must name a project (ID or number, at most 32 characters; `invalid_request` otherwise). The token
lasts the pool's `sessionDuration`; its account is
`principal://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/POOL/subject/SUBJECT`, with the
`principalSet://` identifiers `/*`, `/group/G` and `/attribute.NAME/VALUE`, which IAM enforcement
honours in allow and deny policies (`TestWorkforceIdentityFederationStorage`: Cloud Storage refuses
with Google's 403 naming the `principal://`, reads once the subject or its group holds
`roles/storage.objectViewer`, and refuses again under a deny policy naming its attribute's
`principalSet://`) and on the organization (`TestIAMEnforcementWorkforceIdentity`: IAM Workforce Pool
Viewer and Admin granted to a `principal://`). A SAML assertion (`subject_token_type` `saml2`, #2065;
`TestWorkforceIdentityFederationSAML` on an enforcing instance, with `google.golang.org/api/sts/v1`,
`golang.org/x/oauth2/google` reading a file-sourced SAML `external_account` configuration, and Cloud
Storage) is a base64 SAML response or assertion, verified as Google documents ("Prepare your SAML
IdP", docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-other-providers, and
docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workforce-obtaining-short-lived-credentials, read 2026-11-20): the
assertion, the response or both signed (XML-DSig, exclusive C14N, by
`github.com/russellhaering/goxmldsig`) by a signing certificate of the provider's
`idpMetadataXml`, only the signed element's verified copy being read; a response with exactly one
assertion, `IssueInstant` less than an hour old and status Success; `Issuer` the metadata's entity
ID; a `NameID` and exactly one bearer `SubjectConfirmation` whose data has a future `NotOnOrAfter`
and no `NotBefore`, and whose `Recipient`, when present, is the provider's sign-in callback
(`https://auth.cloud.google/signin-callback/locations/global/workforcePools/POOL/providers/PROVIDER`)
or the STS token URL; `Conditions` `NotBefore` past and `NotOnOrAfter` future when set, an `Audience`
of `https://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/POOL/providers/PROVIDER`; an
`AuthnStatement`, whose `SessionNotOnOrAfter`, when set, must be future and shortens the token's
lifetime below the pool's session. An `EncryptedAssertion` is decrypted with one of the provider's
live encryption keys (RSA-OAEP, AES-CBC or AES-GCM). `assertion.subject` is the `NameID`,
`assertion.attributes['NAME']` the list of the attribute's values. A tampered, expired, unsigned or
foreign-signed assertion, another audience and a rejecting condition are `invalid_grant`. The
same verification serves a workload pool's SAML provider (audience
`https://iam.googleapis.com/projects/N/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL/providers/PROVIDER`;
Google documents no Recipient for it, so none is checked) (unit `TestVerifySAML`). UNVERIFIED (re-read 2026-11-20:
https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-other-providers publishes none): the error descriptions' texts. The console's IAM & Admin > Workforce Identity
Federation lists, creates, edits, disables, deletes and restores pools and providers, and revokes,
deletes and restores subjects (`TestIAMWorkforceIdentityFederationPage`); a pool's and a SCIM
tenant's Permissions tabs grant, remove and test their own policies, and a provider's SCIM tab
creates, edits, deletes, restores and permanently deletes its SCIM tenant and creates (showing the
security token once) and deletes its tokens (#2067, `TestIAMWorkforcePoolPermissionsAndScimPage`).

#### The SCIM provisioning endpoint (#2068)

A SCIM tenant's endpoint (Google's `iamscim.googleapis.com`, base URI
`https://iamscim.googleapis.com/v1alpha1/tenants/UID`) is served on the IAM API's port at
`/v1alpha1/tenants/UID`, as SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7643, RFC 7644) with the limits and deviations of
Google's [SCIM provisioning for Workforce Identity Federation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workforce-identity-federation-scim)
and [Configure SCIM in OIDC or SAML IdP](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/configure-scim-oidc-saml)
(read 2026-11-20). Measured by `TestWorkforceScimProvisioning` on an enforcing instance (a SCIM
client over net/http, since Google ships no SCIM SDK; the tenant and token made with
`google.golang.org/api/iam/v1`, the exchange with `golang.org/x/oauth2/google`, the read with
`cloud.google.com/go/storage`) and unit `TestWorkforceScimEndpoint`, `TestWorkforceScimUsersGroups`
and `TestWorkforceScimUsageProvider`:

- Every request carries one of the tenant's SCIM tokens as a bearer token; none, an unknown or
  deleted one, or a deleted tenant is 401 with a body that is not SCIM JSON, as Google documents.
- `/Users`: create (201), get, list, replace (PUT), PATCH and delete (204); `/Groups`: the same
  without PUT (501); `/Schemas` (User, Group, Enterprise User) and `/ServiceProviderConfig` (patch
  supported; no bulk, sort, ETags or password change; filters of at most 100 results; an OAuth
  bearer token) are read only; `/Me`, `/Bulk`, `.search` and `/ResourceTypes`, which Google does
  not support, are 501.
- Filters are `attrPath eq value` comparisons joined with `and` only (any other operator, `or`,
  `not` or grouping is 400 `invalidFilter`); `userName`, `emails.value` and `displayName` compare
  case-insensitively, `id`, `externalId` and `members.value` exactly. There is no pagination:
  `startIndex` is always 1, at most 100 resources (or `count`) are answered and `totalResults` is
  the number answered. `attributes` and `excludedAttributes` select top-level attributes.
- PATCH takes RFC 7644's `add`, `replace` and `remove` (any case), with or without a path, value
  filters (`emails[type eq "work"].value`, `members[value eq "ID"]`), sub-attributes and the
  Enterprise User extension's attributes; `remove` with a list of values removes those members.
- The tenant's claim mapping is evaluated on every write: `google.subject` (and, for a group,
  `google.group`; a tenant without it provisions no group) must be non-empty (400 `invalidValue`),
  unique in the tenant (409 `uniqueness`) and unchanged by an update (400 `mutability`). The
  mapping's forms are Google's: `google.subject` is `user.externalId`, `user.userName` or
  `user.emails[0].value` (the last two optionally `.lowerAscii()`), `google.group` is
  `group.externalId` or `group.displayName`, with `google.display_name`, `google.profile_photo`,
  `google.email`, `google.posix_username` and at most 50 `attribute.KEY` rules of at most 256
  characters. A user has at most one email, of type `work`; `password` is never stored; a user's
  `groups` is read only; a group's members must be users of the tenant.
- A group's get, and a list of groups without a `members` filter, answer an empty `members`; a
  list filtered on `members` answers them. Deleting a user removes it from every group; a tenant's
  hard delete removes its users and groups.
- A provisioned user's `google.subject` is a pool subject
  (`principal://iam.googleapis.com/locations/global/workforcePools/POOL/subject/SUBJECT`, listed on
  the pool's Subjects tab); a group's `google.group` is `principalSet://…/group/GROUP`. When the
  tenant's provider has `scimUsage` `ENABLED_FOR_GROUPS`, IAM reads a subject's groups from SCIM at
  every check instead of its sign-in token's `google.groups`; with `ENABLED_FOR_USERS_GROUPS` its
  custom attributes come from the tenant's `attribute.KEY` mappings too, and a subject without an
  active SCIM user exchanges no token (`invalid_grant`) and its tokens grant nothing. A provider with
  `scimUsage` set and no tenant fails sign-in (`invalid_grant`), as Google documents.
- The permissions of the SCIM methods are Google's (verified 2026-11-20 against "SCIM audit logging"
  and the IAM roles index): `iam.workforcePoolProviderScimUsers.{create,list,get,put,patch,delete}`
  and `iam.workforcePoolProviderScimGroups.{create,list,get,patch,delete}`, granted by SCIM Data
  Syncer (`roles/iam.scimSyncer`), which "Configure SCIM in Okta" grants the tenant's service agent;
  locally the token authenticates as that service agent, taken to hold the role.

## IAM enforcement

`cloudburrow up --iam-enforcement=on` (#1879; default `off`) checks the caller's permission on
the resource before each mapped method runs, against the stored allow policies, through one
evaluator (`internal/iameval`): the resource's own policy and its service parents' (a crypto
key's key ring, a task's queue), then the project's, its folders' and the organization's;
predefined roles from Google's IAM roles index (`internal/iamroles`), custom roles, and the basic
roles derived from the permission catalog (Owner every permission, Editor all but access
management, Viewer `get`, `list` and `getIamPolicy`; UNVERIFIED, as Google's pages do not list
them, docs re-read 2026-11-19: https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-overview#basic); conditions (`resource.name`, `resource.type`, `resource.service`, `request.time`, tags);
`group:` members through Cloud Identity groups, nested too, `domain:`, `allUsers` and
`allAuthenticatedUsers`. `status`, the startup banner and the console's Policy Troubleshooter and
Policy Analyzer pages report the mode.

The caller is the account its bearer token was minted for (IAM Credentials `generateAccessToken`,
a key file from `keys create`, the metadata server). The instance's own account (the ADC
fixture's) and a request with no bearer token are the project owner, as Google makes a project's
creator `roles/owner`, so every client, the console and `gcloud-setup` keep working; a token the
instance did not mint is `UNAUTHENTICATED`, as Google refuses one it did not issue. Cloud Run
invoke is the exception: a request with no bearer token is `allUsers` alone, as on Google (below).

IAM v2 deny policies (#1886) are evaluated first, as Google's "Deny policies" describes
(https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/deny-overview, read 2026-11-19): the deny policies attached
to the resource's project, its folders and its organization apply to everything below them, each
on its own; a rule denies a permission named in `deniedPermissions` (a permission or a group,
`svc/resource.*`, `svc/*.*`) and not in `exceptionPermissions`, to a principal named in
`deniedPrincipals` (`principal://goog/subject/EMAIL` a user, `principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/-/serviceAccounts/EMAIL`
a service account, `principalSet://goog/group/GROUP` through Cloud Identity groups, nested too,
`principalSet://goog/public:all` everyone) and not in `exceptionPrincipals`, when `denialCondition`
(resource tag functions only, over the resource's effective tags) is true or cannot be evaluated. A
denied permission is refused whatever the allow policies grant, to the instance's own account too
(it is checked as itself for deny policies), with each service's usual denial. A permission is named
in its v2 form, `SERVICE_FQDN/RESOURCE.VERB`, with the v1 names and aliases Google's "Permissions
supported in deny policies" lists (https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/deny-permissions-support,
read 2026-11-19, embedded in `internal/iameval/denypermissions.tsv.gz`). Not matched:
`principalSet://goog/cloudIdentityCustomerId/...` (no customer IDs are kept) and workforce pool
principals (no workforce pools are served); workload identity pool principals are matched (#1941); a request to Cloud Storage or Pub/Sub with
no bearer token is decided in the server as the owner without asking the host, so deny policies do
not apply to it there. Principal access boundaries and organization policies are not evaluated.

Cloud Storage and Pub/Sub's front run in the cluster. They do not keep copies of the policies: each
asks the host's evaluator (`internal/iamcheck`, `POST /cloudburrow/v1/iam:check` on the Resource
Manager port through `cloudburrow-host`, given to them only with `--iam-enforcement=on`) with the
caller's bearer token, the permissions, the resource and its own policies (a bucket's and its
managed folders', a topic's), and the host names the caller and adds the project's, folders' and
organization's. So every decision is the one evaluator's. A request with no bearer token is decided
in the server, as the owner, without a round trip.

Container Analysis: notes and occurrences, each keeping its own policy, the permission of the method's name (`containeranalysis.notes.*`, `containeranalysis.occurrences.*`), an occurrence's create also `containeranalysis.notes.attachOccurrence` on its note and `ListNoteOccurrences` `containeranalysis.notes.listOccurrences` (https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-analysis/docs/ca-access-control); `GetOccurrenceNote` `occurrences.get` and `GetVulnerabilityOccurrencesSummary` `occurrences.list` (no page names one); `GetIamPolicy` `getIamPolicy` (its page names `setIamPolicy`, which the viewer roles lack). Not checked: Secure Source Manager's Operations and Locations mixins (their pages name OAuth scopes only). Git over HTTPS: a clone or fetch needs `securesourcemanager.instances.access` on the instance and `securesourcemanager.repositories.fetch` on the repository, a push `.push`, the permissions of the Instance Accessor and Repo Reader or Writer roles the page asks for "to push to and pull from a repository"; a Developer Connect token is checked by its link's scope, as before. `TestIAMEnforcementSecureSourceManager`, `TestIAMEnforcementSourceManagerGit`, `TestIAMEnforcementDeveloperConnect`, `TestIAMEnforcementContainerAnalysis`. |
| BigQuery Data Transfer Service (gRPC and JSON) | Each method's REST reference (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/datatransfer/rest/v1, read 2026-11-20): `bigquery.transfers.get` for data sources' `get`, `list` and `checkValidCreds`, transfer configs' `get` and `list`, runs' `get` and `list` and `transferLogs.list`; `bigquery.transfers.update` for configs' `create` (on the parent) and `delete`, `scheduleRuns`, `startManualRuns` and runs' `delete`; `resourcemanager.projects.update` on the project for `enrollDataSources` and `unenrollDataSources`. `transferConfigs.patch` names none on its page: `bigquery.transfers.update`, which "Enable the BigQuery Data Transfer Service" (https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/enable-transfer-service) names to modify a transfer. A config's `serviceAccountName` needs `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` ("permissions to act as this service account"). Refused "Permission 'P' denied on resource 'R' (or it may not exist)." with ErrorInfo (UNVERIFIED wording, re-read 2026-11-20: the pages give none). Not checked: the Locations mixin (no page names a permission). `TestIAMEnforcementDataTransfer`; tag bindings on other services' resources `TestIAMEnforcementTagBindingsOnOtherResources`. |

The JSON (REST) transports of the same methods are checked the same way, matched to their
method by the protos' HTTP rules (and cloudkms_v1.yaml's IAMPolicy bindings), with the same
status in Google's JSON error envelope (403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, the ErrorInfo in `details`):
`TestIAMEnforcementJSON`, through the official clients' REST transports. Not enforced yet, and
served as before whatever the mode: every service not in the table.
`TestIamPermissions` answers the requested permissions the caller holds, as Google does, over gRPC
(`TestIAMEnforcementSecretManager`) and JSON (`TestIAMEnforcementJSONTestIamPermissions`), and so
do Cloud Storage's bucket and managed folder `testIamPermissions` and Pub/Sub's. With enforcement
on, the compat suites invoke Cloud Run services as the instance's own account (an ID token the
harness mints, `test/compat/ownerinvoke1879_test.go`), and CI's `iam` shard runs the enforcement
tests against an instance started with it. BigQuery,
Memorystore's IAM auth, Firestore with MongoDB compatibility and IAM Credentials keep their own
checks, which run whatever the mode (ADR-0006).

Policy Troubleshooter and Policy Analyzer, on the Resource Manager port, answer from the same
evaluator whatever the mode:

| Method | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `policytroubleshooter.iam.troubleshoot` v3 (`POST v3/iam:troubleshoot`) | **Verified** | `TestIAMEnforcementInherited`, with `google.golang.org/api/policytroubleshooter/v3`: `CAN_ACCESS` with the folder's policy `ALLOW_ACCESS_STATE_GRANTED`, its binding `ROLE_PERMISSION_INCLUDED` and the account `MEMBERSHIP_MATCHED`; `CANNOT_ACCESS` for a permission the role lacks. `TestIAMEnforcementDenyPolicies` (#1886): a folder's deny policy makes it `CANNOT_ACCESS` with `denyPolicyExplanation` `DENY_ACCESS_STATE_DENIED`, the folder's explained resource denied, and the rule's principal `MEMBERSHIP_MATCHED` and permission `PERMISSION_PATTERN_MATCHED`; `permissionDeniable` from Google's list. |
| `iam:troubleshoot` v1 and v2alpha1 (one shape) | **Verified** | `TestGcloudPolicyTroubleshoot`: `gcloud policy-troubleshoot iam`, which calls v2alpha1 in every release track (Cloud SDK 593.0.0), through `gcloud-setup`'s `policytroubleshooter` override: `GRANTED` and `NOT_GRANTED`. |
| IAM v2 deny policies in enforcement | **Enforced** | `TestIAMEnforcementDenyPolicies` (#1886), the official `cloud.google.com/go/iam/apiv2` client and Secret Manager's: a deny on the project's folder refuses a granted `AccessSecretVersion` with Secret Manager's `PERMISSION_DENIED` and ErrorInfo, and deleting it restores access; `principalSet://goog/public:all` with the account as an exception principal lets it through and refuses the instance's own account; a `resource.matchTag` denial condition denies only once the tag is bound to the project. Unit `TestDenyBeforeAllow` covers groups, permission groups, exception permissions and conditions that cannot be evaluated. Every enforced service's check (the in-cluster servers' too, through `iam:check`) and Cloud Run invoke go through the same evaluator. |
| `cloudasset.analyzeIamPolicy` (`GET v1/{scope}:analyzeIamPolicy`) | **Verified**, *subset* | `TestIAMEnforcementInherited`, with `google.golang.org/api/cloudasset/v1`: an identity and a permission find the folder's binding as an analysis result. The scope's policies and its project's ancestors' are analyzed, and a `resourceSelector`'s own policies; resources under a scope are not enumerated, and `analyzeIamPolicyLongrunning`, `expandGroups`, `expandResources` and service-account impersonation analysis are not served. |

## Cloud Identity groups — `cloudidentity.googleapis.com` v1

**Built** (#1812), as far as IAM membership needs it, with the groups' security settings and inbound SSO (#1959). Served in the CLI process on Resource
Manager's port, JSON only, at Google's paths (`/v1/groups...`); pass `http://<the Resource
Manager endpoint>/` to `option.WithEndpoint` of `google.golang.org/api/cloudidentity/v1`, the
official client (Google publishes no `cloud.google.com/go` client for it). Groups are Google
Groups (the `groups.discussion_forum` label, optionally `groups.security`) of the organization's
customer, `customers/C0cloudburrow`, with emails in its domain, `cloudburrow.local`; groups and
memberships persist in the project registry's store. A `group:` member of a policy, and a BigQuery
dataset's `groupByEmail` entry, name the group's members and those of groups nested in it;
`domain:cloudburrow.local` (and a `domain` entry) every account of the domain, wherever this
instance evaluates a policy ([ADR-0006](adr/0006-iam-policy-surface.md)). Per-method status is
generated in [coverage/cloudidentity.md](coverage/cloudidentity.md).

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cloudidentity.groups.create`, `cloudidentity.groups.get`, `cloudidentity.groups.list`, `cloudidentity.groups.lookup`, `cloudidentity.groups.patch`, `cloudidentity.groups.delete` | **Verified** | `TestCloudIdentityGroups1812`, with `google.golang.org/api/cloudidentity/v1`: create and patch answer a done Operation with the group; `lookup` finds a group by email, case-insensitively; `list` pages (`pageSize`, BASIC 200 and at most 1000, FULL 50 and 500). Refused as Google refuses: a taken email (409 `Error(4003): Cannot create group which already exists.`), a missing parent or Google Group label, an email outside the customer's domain (400), another customer, and a missing group (403 `Error(2028): Permission denied for resource … (or it may not exist).`, which Cloud Identity answers for both). Deleting a group removes it from the groups it was a member of. A parent may be spelled `customerId/C…`, as gcloud sends it. `initialGroupConfig` `WITH_INITIAL_OWNER` makes the account the bearer token was minted for the group's `OWNER` (and `MEMBER`), `EMPTY` adds nobody (`TestCloudIdentityInitialOwner1812`, a token minted through IAM Credentials); a token that names no account, such as the instance's admin token, adds no owner. `TestCloudIdentityMembershipRules` (2026-11-18): a group email follows a username's rules, as the Directory API says group emails do ("subject to the same character usage rules as usernames"; name guidelines, <https://support.google.com/a/answer/9193374>): at most 64 characters before the @, no period at the start or end or two in a row, none of `+ = & < > , !` (400); a display name is at most 73 characters ("Can be up to 73 characters"), on create and patch (400), and the description's 4,096 is counted in characters; the security label cannot be applied to a group that holds a Google Group ("You can't apply the security group label to a Google Group that doesn't meet these conditions", <https://docs.cloud.google.com/identity/docs/how-to/update-group-to-security-group>; 400 `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, Google states no error) and cannot be removed. Unit tests `TestGroupEmailRules`, `TestGroupDisplayNameLimit`, `TestSecurityGroupMembers`. |
| `cloudidentity.groups.memberships.create`, `cloudidentity.groups.memberships.get`, `cloudidentity.groups.memberships.list`, `cloudidentity.groups.memberships.lookup`, `cloudidentity.groups.memberships.delete` | **Verified** | `TestCloudIdentityGroups1812`: a member is a user, a service account (`SERVICE_ACCOUNT`) or a group (`GROUP`, nested); roles default to `MEMBER`, are `OWNER`, `MANAGER` or `MEMBER`, never twice (400), and always include `MEMBER`; a second membership of the same member is 409. The `MEMBER` role's `expiryDetail.expireTime` (in the future; only `MEMBER` takes one) ends the membership when it passes. `TestCloudIdentityMembershipRules` (2026-11-18): a security group takes users, service accounts and security groups, and a Google Group is refused 400 `FAILED_PRECONDITION` ("Security groups can only contain … Security groups inside of your domain"; Google states no error); an expiry on `OWNER` is 400 ("Expiry details are only supported for `MEMBER` `MembershipRoles`"); a group member may expire ("Expirations apply to users, groups, and service accounts with the `MEMBER` role", <https://docs.cloud.google.com/identity/docs/how-to/manage-expirations>), and a member whose `MEMBER` role expires may also be `OWNER` or `MANAGER`, as Google documents no rule against it ([gaps.md](gaps.md)). Unit test `TestMembershipExpiryRules`. |
| `cloudidentity.groups.memberships.checkTransitiveMembership`, `cloudidentity.groups.memberships.searchTransitiveGroups` | **Verified** | `TestCloudIdentityGroups1812`: both follow nested groups; `searchTransitiveGroups` (parent `groups/-`) needs `member_key_id == '…'` and a `'…' in labels` term, may add `parent == 'customers/…'`, and answers each group's `relationType` (`DIRECT`, `INDIRECT`, `DIRECT_AND_INDIRECT`) with the member's direct roles. Google serves these to Premium and Enterprise accounts only; the instance's customer is taken to be one. |
| `group:` and `domain:` members, `groupByEmail` and `domain` dataset entries | **Verified**, *this instance's own rule* | `TestBigQueryGroupMembers1812`, with the official `cloudidentity/v1` and `bigquery` clients: a minted token's service account in a group nested in another reads a table through a dataset's `groupByEmail` READER entry of the outer group, loses it when the nesting is deleted, and reads through a project binding of `group:` of its own group. The same expansion is applied by Memorystore's IAM auth, Firestore with MongoDB compatibility and IAM Credentials (unit tests `TestGroupsPrincipals1812`, `TestEntryNames1812`, `TestMemberIndex1812`, and the compat tests of the row below); `domain:` is unit-tested only, as the instance mints tokens for service accounts, which are in no domain. BigQuery remote models', object tables' and `AI.GENERATE`'s connection checks ask Cloud Identity for the checked account's groups (unit test `TestConnectionMembers1812`; `TestBigQueryConnectionGroupMembers1812` is written, gated on local AI like the remote-model tests, and has not run, [gaps.md](gaps.md)). |
| `cloudidentity.groups.search` | **Verified** | `TestCloudIdentitySearch1812`, and gcloud's `identity groups search` (`TestGcloudIdentityGroups`): the query, in CEL, must contain `parent == 'customers/…'` (400 without; another customer 403) and may add `'…' in labels`, `domain_name == '…'`, and `==`, `startsWith('…')` and `contains('…')` on `group_key` (case-insensitively) and `display_name`, joined by `&&`, as Google documents; pages as `groups.list` does. |
| `cloudidentity.groups.memberships.searchDirectGroups`, `cloudidentity.groups.memberships.searchTransitiveMemberships`, `cloudidentity.groups.memberships.getMembershipGraph` | **Verified** | `TestCloudIdentitySearch1812`: `searchDirectGroups` (parent `groups/-`, a member and a label required, 400 without) answers the member's direct groups with the membership and its roles, `orderBy` `group_key` or `group_name`, `asc` or `desc`; `searchTransitiveMemberships` every direct and indirect member of a group with its `relationType` (an account's `member` is `users/` and a stable number derived from its email, as the instance keeps no user directory; a group's is its `groups/…` name); `getMembershipGraph` a done Operation whose `GetMembershipGraphResponse` holds every membership path from the member up to the group (`groups/-` for every group), as an adjacency list, with the groups on them. Premium-only at Google, like the transitive searches. |
| `cloudidentity.groups.memberships.modifyMembershipRoles` | **Verified** | `TestCloudIdentitySearch1812`: `addRoles` and `removeRoles` (never `MEMBER`, 400), or `updateRolesParams` with `fieldMask` `expiry_detail.expire_time` on the `MEMBER` role alone, never mixed with the other two (400); answers the membership. `TestCloudIdentityMembershipRules`: an expiry on `OWNER` in `addRoles` or `updateRolesParams` is 400; `MANAGER` is added to, and the `MEMBER` expiry updated on, an `OWNER` whose `MEMBER` role expires. |
| IAM Credentials, Memorystore IAM auth, Firestore with MongoDB compatibility: `group:` members | **Verified**, *this instance's own rule* | With the official clients: `TestIAMCredentialsGroupMember1812` (`iam/credentials/apiv1`: a Token Creator binding of `group:outer` on a service account lets an account in outer through a nested group mint its token, and the nesting's removal takes it away), `TestMemorystoreIAMAuthGroupMember1812` (go-redis AUTH to a Valkey instance with IAM auth, `roles/memorystore.dbConnectionUser` granted to a group only), `TestFirestoreMongoDBGroupMember1812` (the MongoDB Go driver's access-token sign-in, `roles/datastore.user` granted to a group only); each refused before the grant and after the nesting's removal. |
| gcloud `identity groups create`, `describe`, `search`, `delete`, `memberships add`, `list`, `delete` | **Verified where gcloud is installed** | `TestGcloudIdentityGroups`, through `gcloud-setup`'s `cloudidentity` override alone, egress blocked (`--customer C0cloudburrow`; gcloud has no `groups list`, `search` lists a customer's groups by label). |
| Console | **Verified** | **IAM & Admin > Groups** (`TestConsoleIAMGroups`): groups with their type and member count, Create group, a group's members and the groups it belongs to, Edit group, Add member, Remove member, Delete; a group's Security settings and Edit group's Member restriction (`TestConsoleIAMSSO1959`, browser `TestIAMGroupMemberRestriction1959`). **IAM & Admin > SSO profiles** and **SSO profile assignments** (#1959, the Admin console's SSO with third-party IdP; `TestConsoleIAMSSO1959`, browser `TestIAMSSOProfilesAndAssignments1959`). |
| `cloudidentity.groups.getSecuritySettings`, `cloudidentity.groups.updateSecuritySettings` | **Verified** | `TestCloudIdentityMemberRestriction1959` (#1959), with `google.golang.org/api/cloudidentity/v1`: a group's settings (`groups/{id}/securitySettings`) start with no `memberRestriction`; `updateSecuritySettings` takes `updateMask` `member_restriction.query` alone (400 otherwise) and answers a done Operation. The query is Google's CEL subset: `member.type == 1`, `2` or `3` (user, service account, group) and `member.customer_id == groupCustomerId()`, joined by `&&`, `||` and parentheses; anything else is 400. `memberships.create` then refuses a direct member the query excludes (400 `FAILED_PRECONDITION`) and reports the `MEMBER` role's `restrictionEvaluations` (`COMPLIANT`, `NON_COMPLIANT`, or `FORWARD_COMPLIANT` for a nested group holding a violator whose own restriction admits nothing the parent excludes); members already present stay, and the restriction's `evaluation.state` says whether every transitive member adheres. A group and a user of `cloudburrow.local` are the customer's, a service account when its project is in the organization. The evaluation is synchronous, never `EVALUATING`. `readMask` takes `member_restriction` or `*`. |
| `cloudidentity.inboundSamlSsoProfiles.create`, `cloudidentity.inboundSamlSsoProfiles.get`, `cloudidentity.inboundSamlSsoProfiles.list`, `cloudidentity.inboundSamlSsoProfiles.patch`, `cloudidentity.inboundSamlSsoProfiles.delete`, `cloudidentity.inboundSamlSsoProfiles.idpCredentials.add`, `cloudidentity.inboundSamlSsoProfiles.idpCredentials.get`, `cloudidentity.inboundSamlSsoProfiles.idpCredentials.list`, `cloudidentity.inboundSamlSsoProfiles.idpCredentials.delete` | **Verified** | `TestCloudIdentityInboundSSO1959` (#1959): a SAML profile of the customer (`customers/C0cloudburrow` or `customers/my_customer`; another customer 403) needs `idpConfig.entityId` and an https `singleSignOnServiceUri` (400 for http; `logoutRedirectUri` and `changePasswordUri` https too), at most 1,000 per organization; it answers `spConfig` (entity ID and ACS URL under `https://accounts.google.com/samlrp/{id}`). `list` filters by `customer=="customers/…"` only and pages (at most 100, larger silently 100). `patch` takes `display_name` and `idp_config` (or its fields); `customer` is immutable. `idpCredentials:add` takes a PEM x509 certificate with an RSA or DSA key (400 otherwise; an ECDSA one is refused, unit test), up to 2 per profile (a third is 400 `FAILED_PRECONDITION`), and answers `rsaKeyInfo`/`dsaKeyInfo.keySize`. A profile an assignment uses cannot be deleted (400 `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, *this instance's own rule*). Every mutation is a done Operation; multi-party approval is not modelled. **No sign-in happens locally**: the instance has no Google sign-in page, so a profile is stored configuration only. Certificates in tests are generated locally. |
| `cloudidentity.inboundOidcSsoProfiles.create`, `cloudidentity.inboundOidcSsoProfiles.get`, `cloudidentity.inboundOidcSsoProfiles.list`, `cloudidentity.inboundOidcSsoProfiles.patch`, `cloudidentity.inboundOidcSsoProfiles.delete` | **Verified** | `TestCloudIdentityInboundSSO1959`: an OIDC profile needs an https `idpConfig.issuerUri`; `rpConfig.clientSecret` is input only (stored, never answered); `rpConfig.redirectUris` is answered (its shape is not documented by Google; CloudBurrow answers one URI under the profile's `samlrp` path). `patch` takes `display_name`, `idp_config` and `rp_config` (or their fields). No sign-in happens locally. |
| `cloudidentity.inboundSsoAssignments.create`, `cloudidentity.inboundSsoAssignments.get`, `cloudidentity.inboundSsoAssignments.list`, `cloudidentity.inboundSsoAssignments.patch`, `cloudidentity.inboundSsoAssignments.delete` | **Verified** | `TestCloudIdentityInboundSSO1959`: an assignment targets a group (`targetGroup`, which must exist, `rank` 1 or more, 400 for 0) or an org unit (`targetOrgUnit` `orgUnits/{id}`, `rank` 0), never both, one per target (409); `ssoMode` is required (`SSO_OFF`, `SAML_SSO`, `OIDC_SSO`, `DOMAIN_WIDE_SAML_IF_ENABLED`), with `samlSsoInfo` set if and only if `SAML_SSO` and `oidcSsoInfo` if and only if `OIDC_SSO`, naming an existing profile; `signInBehavior.redirectCondition` is unset or `NEVER`. Group ranks stay 1..n: a create or a `patch` of `rank` places the assignment there and shifts the others down, a delete moves them up; `list` answers group assignments by rank, then org units'. `customer` and the target are immutable. Org units are not modelled (the instance has no Admin SDK directory), so an org unit ID is taken as given. A deleted group's assignment is deleted with it. |

## Service Usage — `serviceusage.googleapis.com` v1

**Built** (#1352). Served in the CLI process on `--port-serviceusage` (default `9023`), JSON only,
always, as Resource Manager is. `env` exports `CLOUDBURROW_SERVICEUSAGE_ENDPOINT` and
`CLOUDSDK_API_ENDPOINT_OVERRIDES_SERVICEUSAGE`; `gcloud-setup` writes the `serviceusage` override, and
`cloudburrow terraform` sets `service_usage_custom_endpoint`. No client library reads the variable, so
pass `http://<it>/` to `option.WithEndpoint`. Per-method status is generated in
[coverage/serviceusage.md](coverage/serviceusage.md); the model is in [serviceusage.md](serviceusage.md).

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `serviceusage.services.list`, `serviceusage.services.get`, `serviceusage.services.batchGet` | **Verified** | `TestServiceUsageServices`, with `google.golang.org/api/serviceusage/v1`: every API the instance serves is listed under its `googleapis.com` name with its title, named `projects/{number}/services/{name}`, ENABLED in every project until disabled there, but for the Container Scanning API (`containerscanning.googleapis.com`, #1912), DISABLED until enabled, as Google's is; enabling it turns on Artifact Registry's vulnerability scanning in that project. `filter` takes `state:ENABLED` or `state:DISABLED` (anything else is INVALID_ARGUMENT); `pageSize` up to 200; `batchGet` up to 30 names. An API CloudBurrow could serve with other `--services` reads DISABLED; one it never serves is PERMISSION_DENIED, as Google answers an unknown service. A project number that names no registered project is PERMISSION_DENIED; any project ID is accepted, as every CloudBurrow service accepts it. |
| `serviceusage.services.enable`, `serviceusage.services.batchEnable` | **Verified** | `TestServiceUsageServices`, `TestTerraformProjectService`, `TestGcloudServices`: each returns a done operation, which `serviceusage.operations.get` answers. Enabling an API the instance does not serve is **refused** (400 FAILED_PRECONDITION) with the reason: `start the instance with --services spanner`, or that CloudBurrow serves no such API; a `batchEnable` with one such API changes nothing, as Google's fails as a whole. At most 20 per batch. |
| `serviceusage.services.disable` | **Verified** | Recorded per project, reported DISABLED, persisted in the project registry's store (durable with the instance, captured by snapshots), and enforced as Google enforces it (#1914): every call to the API in that project fails `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403) with Google's `SERVICE_DISABLED` message and ErrorInfo (`service`, `consumer`, `activationUrl`, `serviceTitle`, `containerInfo`), through gRPC and REST; see [serviceusage.md](serviceusage.md#disabling-is-enforced-as-on-google). An API enabled APIs depend on is refused `FAILED_PRECONDITION` without `disableDependentServices`, and with it is disabled together with them; Google documents no dependency among the served APIs. `checkIfServiceHasUsage` is accepted; no usage is tracked. Tests: `TestServiceUsageServices`, `TestServicesThroughTheOfficialClient`, `TestDisableDependentServices`, `TestServiceDisabledStorage`, `TestServiceDisabledPubSub`, `TestServiceDisabledSecretManager`, `TestServiceDisabledBigQuery`, `TestServiceDisabledFirestore`, `TestGcloudServicesDisableEnforced`. |
| `serviceusage.operations.get` | **Verified** | `TestServiceUsageServices`: the operation a change returned, done, with its `EnableServiceResponse`, `BatchEnableServicesResponse` or `DisableServiceResponse`. Neither Terraform nor gcloud polls it, as the operation is done. Operations are kept in memory. |

Console: the **Service Usage operations** page lists a project's operations with **Delete** (`TestConsoleServiceUsageOperations`); it has no Cancel, as every operation is done. gcloud and Terraform call none of these. |

Measured (TF_LOG=DEBUG, hashicorp/google 8.4.0): reads are `services.list` with `filter=state:ENABLED`, `pageSize=200`, `fields=services/name`; creates are `:enable` or `:batchEnable`; destroy is `:disable`; the provider also reads the project from Resource Manager v1 and drops the resource when it is not registered. |

Measured (`--log-http`, gcloud 587.0.0): `list --enabled` and `list --available` are `services.list` with and without `filter=state:ENABLED`; `enable` and `disable` of one API are `:enable` and `:disable`. |
| `serviceusage.services.generateServiceIdentity` (v1beta1) | **Verified** | `TestServiceUsageGenerateServiceIdentity` (#1834), with `google.golang.org/api/serviceusage/v1beta1`: a done operation (`operations/finished.DONE_OPERATION`) whose `ServiceIdentity` is the service's primary service agent as <https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-agents> lists it, `service-NUMBER@DOMAIN` with a 12-digit project number and a 21-digit `uniqueId`, the same at every call: run for Certificate Authority Service (`gcp-sa-privateca`), Cloud KMS (`gcp-sa-ekms`, its External Key Management agent, as <https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/create-ekm-connection> creates it), Pub/Sub, Secret Manager and Cloud Run (`serverless-robot-prod`) where the instance serves them; a served API with no primary agent (Cloud Storage, Cloud Logging run) answers an empty `ServiceIdentity`, as gcloud's `GenerateServiceIdentity` documents; an unserved API is refused as `enable` refuses it. the `apikeys` override, and `cloudburrow terraform` sets `apikeys_custom_endpoint`. No client library
reads the variable, so pass `http://<it>/` to `option.WithEndpoint` (`google.golang.org/api/apikeys/v2`,
or `cloud.google.com/go/apikeys/apiv2`'s REST client). Per-method status is generated in
[coverage/apikeys.md](coverage/apikeys.md); the model is in [apikeys.md](apikeys.md).

Restrictions are validated: one application restriction kind only, websites with `*` only for a subdomain or a path, IPv4/IPv6 addresses or CIDR subnets, Android package names with 20-byte SHA-1 fingerprints (colon form accepted, answered in plain hex), iOS bundle IDs, API targets with a service and methods whose `*` is last; at most 1,200 application restrictions and 300 keys per project; `displayName` at most 63 characters. A location other than `global` is 400. |

## Google Auth Platform — OAuth clients

**Built** (#2030), console only, as on Google: Google Auth Platform has no public API. The IAP OAuth
Admin API (`iap.projects.brands`, `identityAwareProxyClients`) was deprecated on 2025-01-22 and shut
down on 2026-03-19 (<https://docs.cloud.google.com/iap/docs/deprecations>), so it is not served, and
`gcloud iap oauth-brands` and `oauth-clients` stay refused. The console's Google Auth Platform pages
keep the app and its clients locally ([console-parity.md](console-parity.md)); the metadata server serves
the authorization endpoint (`/o/oauth2/v2/auth`, and `/o/oauth2/auth`), the token endpoint's
`authorization_code` and `refresh_token` grants for those clients (`/token`) and `/revoke`.

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| An OAuth client used with `golang.org/x/oauth2` | **Verified** | `TestOAuthClientSignsInTheInstanceUser`: a Web client made on the console's pages; the consent screen names the app and signs the instance's user in; Allow redirects with `code` and `state`; the exchange with PKCE (S256) answers an access token, a refresh token (`access_type=offline`) and an ID token (`openid`), whose audience is the client ID; a wrong secret is `invalid_client`; the refresh grant answers a new access token. Redirect URIs must match a Web client's exactly (a Desktop client takes any loopback port); an External app in Testing signs in only its test users (`access_denied`). Codes live 10 minutes in memory and are used once. |
| Brand verification, the Verification Center, logo upload, app monitoring | **Unimplemented** | Google's own review and console-only features with nothing to emulate locally. |

## Firebase Rules — `firebaserules.googleapis.com` v1

**Built** (#2048). `internal/service/firebaserules` serves the Firebase Rules API in the CLI process on
`--port-firebaserules` (default `9043`) whenever Firestore is enabled, JSON only (the gRPC surface is
not served). `env` exports `CLOUDBURROW_FIREBASERULES_ENDPOINT`, and `cloudburrow terraform` sets
`firebaserules_custom_endpoint`; no gcloud command calls the API, and `gcloud-setup`'s refusal keeps
its `firebaserules` property local. No client library reads the variable, so pass `http://<it>/` to
`option.WithEndpoint` (`google.golang.org/api/firebaserules/v1`). The Firestore emulator evaluates
the rules, exactly as it does for Firebase's own emulator suite; this API keeps the rulesets and
releases and sets them there. Per-method status is generated in
[coverage/firebaserules.md](coverage/firebaserules.md).

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `firebaserules.projects.rulesets.create`, `firebaserules.projects.rulesets.get`, `firebaserules.projects.rulesets.list`, `firebaserules.projects.rulesets.delete` | **Verified** | `TestFirebaseRulesReleaseEnforcesOnClientCalls`, `TestTerraformFirebaseRules`, with `google.golang.org/api/firebaserules/v1`: a ruleset is compiled by the emulator, on a scratch project (`cloudburrow-rules-check`), and one that does not compile is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT naming each `file:line:column` the emulator reports; a kept ruleset is `projects/{p}/rulesets/{uuid}` with `createTime` and `metadata.services` (`cloud.firestore`), its source read back as sent (a file's `fingerprint` only when given, and `language`); `list` pages (`pageSize` at most 100) and omits the source, as Google's does; a ruleset a release refers to cannot be deleted (400 FAILED_PRECONDITION). |
| `firebaserules.projects.releases.create`, `firebaserules.projects.releases.get`, `firebaserules.projects.releases.list`, `firebaserules.projects.releases.patch`, `firebaserules.projects.releases.delete`, `firebaserules.projects.releases.getExecutable` | **Verified** | `TestFirebaseRulesReleaseEnforcesOnClientCalls`, `TestTerraformFirebaseRules`: a release named `cloud.firestore` (or `cloud.firestore/{database}`) sets its ruleset as the project's rules in the emulator, which then evaluates every client-SDK call to the project's Firestore (a Firebase ID token, or no credentials with a Firebase `x-goog-api-client`) and answers a denied one 403 PERMISSION_DENIED; server client libraries are not subject to rules, as on Google. A second release of a name is 409; `patch` honors `rulesetName` only, as Google documents; `list` takes Google's `name=`, `ruleset_name=` filter (a trailing `*` matches a prefix). The emulator keeps one set of rules per project, so the latest-updated `cloud.firestore*` release of a project is in force for all its databases. With no release, before the first and after the last is deleted, every client-SDK call is denied 403 PERMISSION_DENIED, as on Google, while server client libraries still pass (`TestFirebaseRulesNoReleaseDeniesClients`, #2050): deleting the last release sets deny-all rules in the emulator, and the Firestore front, which sees the rules this API sets pass through it, sets deny-all rules itself for a project a client calls before any release (`internal/firestoreadmin/rulesgate.go`). `getExecutable` answers the ruleset's source as the executable: the emulator compiles rules in its own process and exposes none. Releases and rulesets are kept in the state directory in persistent mode and set in the emulator again when the instance starts. |
| `firebaserules.projects.test` | **Verified** | `TestFirebaseRulesReleaseEnforcesOnClientCalls`, `TestFirebaseRulesTestFunctionMocks`: each test case is evaluated by the emulator on a fresh scratch project: the case's `resource` is written as the emulator's owner, then its `request` (`get`, `list`, `create`, `update`, `delete` on `/databases/{database}/documents/...`, with `resource.data` for a write) is made with an unsigned Firebase ID token for `request.auth` (its `uid` and `token` claims), or with no credentials for a null auth. A 403 is DENY and any other answer ALLOW; a result is SUCCESS when it matches the expectation and FAILURE otherwise, with the emulator's denial in `debugMessages`. A source that does not compile is answered with its `issues`. `functionMocks` (#2050) answer cloud.firestore's service functions (`get`, `exists`, `getAfter`, `existsAfter`) as the API reference documents: the case runs a rewritten source in which each call of one is a call of a function answering the mocks' results, an `exactValue` argument matching the path it spells and `anyValue` any (after the exact ones), a `value` result returned and `undefined` an error; an unmocked call, or one no mock matches, is an error, as Google documents ("any service-defined Rules function is expected to return an error"). A mock of another function, of more or fewer than one argument, without exactly one result, or repeating another's matchers is 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. Not reported: `expressionReports`, `visitedExpressions` and `functionCalls`, which the emulator does not report. |

## Certificate Authority Service — `google.cloud.security.privateca.v1`

**Built, not reused** (#1834): Google publishes no Certificate Authority Service emulator. It runs in the CLI process and is opt-in: `--services privateca`, on `--port-privateca` (default `9028`), gRPC and JSON on one port as `privateca.googleapis.com` serves both (the shared `Transcoder`, with the `privateca_v1.yaml` Locations, Operations and IAMPolicy mixins). `env` exports `CLOUDBURROW_PRIVATECA_ENDPOINT` for `option.WithEndpoint`. CA keys are generated locally and certificates are signed for real with Go's `crypto/x509`, so any TLS stack verifies them against the CA; the keys are product data kept unencrypted in the instance's state file (not a security boundary, ADR-0004). Every long-running method answers an Operation that is already done, with `OperationMetadata` (`verb`, `target`) and the resource. Per-method status is generated in [coverage/privateca.md](coverage/privateca.md); the user's guide is [privateca.md](privateca.md). Over REST a FAILED_PRECONDITION arrives at a Go caller as HTTP 400; the compat test reads the code from the envelope's `status`.

| Claim | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| CA pools: `CreateCaPool`, `GetCaPool`, `ListCaPools`, `UpdateCaPool`, `DeleteCaPool` | **Verified** | `TestPrivateCAPoolsRootsAndCertificates`, with `cloud.google.com/go/security/privateca/apiv1` over gRPC and REST, waiting on each operation. `tier` is required; an ID outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,63}` is INVALID_ARGUMENT; a duplicate is ALREADY_EXISTS. `UpdateCaPool` takes `labels`, `issuance_policy` and `publishing_options`. A pool holding any CA, one in its 30-day grace period included, cannot be deleted (FAILED_PRECONDITION, UNVERIFIED: the delete page states no precondition, docs re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.caPools/delete>). `encryption_spec` (CMEK) is 501. |
| Trust anchors: `FetchCaCerts` | **Verified** | The same test: one chain per ENABLED, DISABLED or STAGED CA ("The CA will be part of the CaPool's trust anchor"). |
| Root CAs: `CreateCertificateAuthority`, `GetCertificateAuthority`, `ListCertificateAuthorities`, `UpdateCertificateAuthority` | **Verified** | The same test. A `SELF_SIGNED` CA is created **STAGED** ("All root CAs are created in the STAGED state by default", <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/managing-ca-state>, read 2026-11-18) with a key of its `key_spec.algorithm` (RSA PSS or PKCS #1 2048/3072/4096, EC P-256 or P-384) and a self-signed certificate of its `config` and `lifetime`; `ca_options.is_ca` must be true. At most 1,000 CAs per location per project (the quotas page's resource limit), RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED past it. `cloud_kms_key_version` keys and `gcs_bucket` are 501 (subordinate CAs: the row below). `UpdateCertificateAuthority` takes `labels` and `user_defined_access_urls`. |
| CA states: `EnableCertificateAuthority`, `DisableCertificateAuthority`, `DeleteCertificateAuthority`, `UndeleteCertificateAuthority` | **Verified** | The same test. Enable from STAGED or DISABLED; disable from ENABLED or STAGED (UNVERIFIED: the state page names none; docs re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/managing-ca-state>). Delete needs DISABLED, STAGED or AWAITING_USER_ACTIVATION (an ENABLED CA is FAILED_PRECONDITION, UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.caPools.certificateAuthorities/delete>)), and refuses a CA with active certificates, "both unrevoked and unexpired", unless `ignore_active_certificates`; it sets DELETED, `delete_time`, and `expire_time` 30 days on, or purges at once with `skip_grace_period`. Undelete restores DISABLED ("CA state changes from DELETED to DISABLED if successfully restored"). Only an ENABLED CA issues: a STAGED or DISABLED one is FAILED_PRECONDITION. |

The pool's `baseline_values` override the request's, `allowed_key_types` and `allowed_issuance_modes` are enforced, and `lifetime` is cut to `maximum_lifetime` and to the CA's expiry (the CA's cut UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.caPools>)). `subject_mode` other than DEFAULT, `rdn_sequence`, `custom_sans`, `subject_key_id`, `requested_not_before_time` and `identity_constraints.cel_expression` are 501. `UpdateCertificate` takes `labels`. |

As resources.proto documents them, each custom SAN's `value` "must contain an ASN.1 encoded UTF8String" (else `INVALID_ARGUMENT`); it is written into the subjectAltName extension as an RFC 5280 otherName with the custom SAN's `object_id` as its type ID, beside the DNS names, email addresses, IP addresses and URIs, the extension critical when a custom SAN is or the subject is empty; the description reports it back in `custom_sans`. `subject_key_id.key_id`, "encoded in lowercase hexadecimal" (else `INVALID_ARGUMENT`), is the certificate's subjectKeyIdentifier instead of the SHA-1 of its public key. The messages are CloudBurrow's. Unit: `TestCustomSANsAndSubjectKeyID`. |

A `SUBORDINATE` CA is created **AWAITING_USER_ACTIVATION** with its key and no certificate ("Certificates cannot be issued from this CA. CRLs will not be generated."); `FetchCertificateAuthorityCsr` answers its CSR (its subject and its `x509_config` as requested extensions, signed by its key), FAILED_PRECONDITION in any other state. Signed by a CA of this service, as gcloud and Terraform do it (`CreateCertificate` on the issuer's pool with that CSR, whose CA config is honoured, then `ActivateCertificateAuthority` with `subordinate_config.certificate_authority`), or by a third party (`subordinate_config.pem_issuer_chain`): the certificate must hold the CA's key (INVALID_ARGUMENT otherwise), be a CA certificate and verify against the chain to its root. The CA is then **STAGED** (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.caPools.certificateAuthorities/activate>): the state after activation), its `pem_ca_certificates` its certificate then the issuer chain, "the root issuer is the final element"; a second activation is FAILED_PRECONDITION. A leaf the enabled subordinate issues verifies through it to the root. Every `Subject` field (common name, organization, unit, country, province, locality, street address, postal code) is kept in the CA's certificate and its `ca_certificate_descriptions`; `rdn_sequence` is 501. (`reusable_config` is v1beta1's; v1 has `config`, served.) |
| Certificate templates: `CreateCertificateTemplate`, `GetCertificateTemplate`, `ListCertificateTemplates`, `UpdateCertificateTemplate`, `DeleteCertificateTemplate`; `certificate_template` on `CreateCertificate` | **Verified** | The same test. A template's `predefined_values` override the request's x509 values and the pool's `baseline_values` override both; its `identity_constraints` narrow the pool's (a subject not passed through is dropped); its `maximum_lifetime` caps the lifetime; a template outside the certificate's location is INVALID_ARGUMENT ("This template must be in the same location as the Certificate"). Update takes `labels`, `description`, `predefined_values`, `identity_constraints`, `passthrough_extensions` and `maximum_lifetime`. `passthrough_extensions` with any extension and `identity_constraints.cel_expression` are 501. |
| Cloud KMS CA keys, CMEK, `gcs_bucket`, subject modes, CEL, passthrough extensions: `CreateCaPool`, `CreateCertificateAuthority`, `CreateCertificate`, `CreateCertificateTemplate`, `GetCertificate` | **Verified** | `TestPrivateCAKMSKeysCMEKAndIssuanceRules` (#1834), with `cloud.google.com/go/security/privateca/apiv1` and `cloud.google.com/go/kms/apiv1` over gRPC and REST: a root CA whose `key_spec.cloud_kms_key_version` is an EC_SIGN_P384_SHA384 version of this instance's Cloud KMS holds that version's public key and is signed by it, as is every certificate it issues ("The key must be in the same location as your CA pool", "The key version that you plan to use must be enabled", ASYMMETRIC_SIGN RSA_SIGN_PSS/PKCS1 SHA-256 or EC_SIGN_P256/P384 only, <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/choosing-key-algorithm>, read 2026-11-18); a version in another location is INVALID_ARGUMENT and a disabled one FAILED_PRECONDITION when it signs. `encryption_spec`: a symmetric key in the pool's location, ENTERPRISE only (DevOps or a signing key is INVALID_ARGUMENT); certificates are kept encrypted in the state file and a disabled key fails issuance and reads with FAILED_PRECONDITION (<https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/creating-ca-pool>, read 2026-11-18); `UpdateCaPool` takes `encryption_spec`. `subject.rdn_sequence` is the subject in its order; `subject_mode` `RDN_SEQUENCE` keeps a CSR's RDN sequence; `REFLECTED_SPIFFE` is FAILED_PRECONDITION with Google's "the caller does not have a SPIFFE identity" message (the code is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/troubleshooting> names none)), since CloudBurrow serves no Workload Identity Federation. `requested_not_before_time` needs `allow_requester_specified_not_before_time` (else INVALID_ARGUMENT) and starts the validity. Pool and template `identity_constraints.cel_expression` in the dialect of <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/using-cel> (read 2026-11-18), with Google's cel-go, nested macros refused; a false result is INVALID_ARGUMENT (the code is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/using-cel> names none)). `passthrough_extensions` drop the request's other extensions; a template's `predefined_values` outside the pool's, or the pool's `baseline_values` outside the template's, are INVALID_ARGUMENT (the code is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.certificateTemplates> names none)). `TestPrivateCAPublishesToGCSBucket`: `gcs_bucket` publishes the CA certificate and CRL to the bucket in this instance's Cloud Storage, the access URLs, AIA and CDP are the objects' URLs, a revocation republishes the CRL, a `gs://` name is INVALID_ARGUMENT and a missing bucket FAILED_PRECONDITION; the object path under the bucket is UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.caPools.certificateAuthorities> names none). `TestTerraformPrivateCAKMSKeyAndTemplateRules`: Terraform's `key_spec { cloud_kms_key_version }`, `encryption_spec`, template `cel_expression` and `passthrough_extensions` apply and plan clean. A template without `ca_options` never plans clean, against any server: provider 8.4.0's `flattenPrivatecaCertificateTemplateConfigX509ConfigCaOptions` always returns a `ca_options` block (`null_ca = true`), whatever the response. gcloud's `--kms-key-version`, `--bucket` and `--encryption-key` have no test yet. |
| CRLs: `GetCertificateRevocationList`, `ListCertificateRevocationLists`, `UpdateCertificateRevocationList`; published CA certificates and CRLs | **Verified** | The same test. Each STAGED, ENABLED or DISABLED CA whose certificate allows CRL signing has one CRL resource, regenerated, signed by the CA's key, when the CA is created, enabled, disabled or activated and on each revocation of a certificate it issued: `sequence_number` grows, `revoked_certificates` names each unexpired revoked certificate with its serial and reason, `pem_crl` is the CRL, valid 7 days (UNVERIFIED (docs re-read 2026-11-18: <https://docs.cloud.google.com/certificate-authority-service/docs/revoking-certificates>): Google's lifetime). With the pool's `publishing_options.publish_ca_cert` and `publish_crl`, the CA's `access_urls` name this port's `/privateca-content/{ca}/ca.crt` and `crl.crl`, which serve them (PEM, or DER with `encoding_format` DER), the CRL's `access_url` is set, and every certificate the CA issues carries them as its AIA issuer URL and CRL distribution point; the test fetches both and checks the CRL's signature and the revoked serial with its reason code. Google publishes to a Cloud Storage bucket; here they are served locally and nothing is written to Cloud Storage. Update takes `labels`. |
| IAM on CA pools, certificate templates and CRLs | **Verified**, *stored, not enforced* | `TestPrivateCAPoolsRootsAndCertificates` sets a pool's policy and reads it back, `TestPrivateCASubordinatesTemplatesAndCRLs` a template's and a CRL's (the IAMPolicy mixin, ADR-0006). |

Every `list` takes an AIP-160 `filter` and an AIP-132 `order_by` (#1943, `TestListFiltersPrivateCA`: `tier = DEVOPS` by `name desc`), as do `ListOperations` (filter) and `ListLocations` (filter). `TestGcloudPrivateCAKMSKeyBucketAndCMEK` (gcloud 593.0.0): `pools create --tier enterprise --encryption-key` (a DevOps pool with a key is refused), and `roots create --kms-key-version --bucket --auto-enable`, whose calls were measured with `--log-http`: privateca `caPools.get`, Resource Manager v1 `projects.testIamPermissions` and Cloud KMS `cryptoKeys.testIamPermissions` (each answering the permission asked), Cloud Storage `buckets.get` with `projection=full`, Service Usage v1beta1 `generateServiceIdentity`, Cloud KMS `getIamPolicy` and `setIamPolicy` on the key and Cloud Storage bucket `getIamPolicy` and `setIamPolicy`, then `certificateAuthorities.create` and `:enable`, every one 200; the official clients find the agent granted `roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier` and `roles/viewer` on the key and `roles/storage.objectAdmin` and `roles/storage.legacyBucketReader` on the bucket, the CA's public key the KMS version's, its certificate the bucket's object, and a certificate `certificates create --csr` issues from the CMEK pool verifies under it. |
