an index past the end, an array inside an array and a property the entity already has are refused, and a reserved name with the emulator's own message; the emulator stores an array's values excluded from indexes after its indexed ones, measured at the top level and inside an embedded entity, so a change that would put an excluded value before an indexed one is refused rather than moved (#911, `TestConsoleDatastoreAddAndRemoveValues`; unit `TestDatastoreAddAndRemoveValueChangeOnlyThatValue`, `TestDatastoreValueActionsAreOfferedWhereTheyApply`); a blob is shown and edited as base64, standard encoding with padding as the v1 REST API's `blobValue`, by Edit property, Add property and Edit value — whose Exclude from indexes is prefilled with the value's own flag — and saved unchanged writes the same bytes back (proto-equal through `Lookup`), a change is read back by the official client as those bytes, and a blob over 1,500 bytes is refused indexed with the client's "too long to index" and written excluded, which the emulator enforces too (#912, `TestConsoleDatastoreBlobValuesAsBase64`; unit `TestDatastoreBlobValuesRoundTripAsBase64`; in headless Chrome, with Add value and Remove value, `TestDatastoreAddRemoveAndBlobValuesThroughTheBrowser`); Edit value, Add value, Remove value and Exclude from indexes address a value by its place in the property, so each carries a digest of the property as its page read it, in a hidden form field, and is refused inside the same `Lookup`/`Commit` transaction, before anything is written, when the property is not that any more, saying it changed since the page was loaded and to reload the page: after the official client inserted a value at the front of the array, and after the v1 API changed one value's index flag, all four drawn before the change are refused and the property reads back through `Lookup` as the other writer left it, while a change to another property of the entity refuses nothing and Remove value then removes the value its row showed; an action with no digest is refused (#923, `TestConsoleDatastoreValueActionsRefuseAConcurrentChange`; unit `TestDatastoreValueActionsRefuseAChangedProperty`, `TestHiddenFieldsAreSentBackAsTheyCame`; in headless Chrome `TestDatastoreStaleValueActionIsRefusedAndWholeArrayExcludedThroughTheBrowser`); **Exclude from indexes**, on an array or embedded entity property's page and on every array or embedded entity inside one, sets or clears the flag on every value inside it, at any depth, an embedded entity's own included, in one write: on an array the official client wrote, every value reads back excluded through `Lookup` in the same order and otherwise proto-equal, the client reads the property excluded, a 2,000-byte blob can then be added excluded at the front (which the ordering rule refused before), indexing it again is refused naming the blob and the 1,500-byte rule, and once it is removed indexing gives back the array proto-equal to what the client stored; on an embedded entity it excludes the entity and every value inside, and on the array inside it indexes that array alone; an embedded entity inside an array excluded before an indexed neighbour is refused as Add value refuses it (#924, `TestConsoleDatastoreExcludeWholeArrayFromIndexes`; unit `TestDatastoreExcludeFromIndexesSetsEveryValue`). Only the emulator's ordering was measured; whether production Firestore in Datastore mode reorders an array's excluded values the same way is not known; an indexed 1,600-byte string is refused with the client's "too long to index"; Delete property and Delete entity remove them, `Get` answering `datastore: no such entity`. Changes to an entity are a read and an update in one transaction, through the Datastore v1 API (`Lookup` and `Commit`) rather than the client: the client's read kept only a key value's namespace, so Add, Edit and Delete property had rewritten a key value naming another project or database to this project's default database, reproduced against the emulator; now every value the change does not touch is written back exactly as `Lookup` returned it, and `Lookup` reads it back so (#893, `TestConsoleDatastoreKeepsAKeyValuesProjectAndDatabase`). Maps, arrays and embedded entities are written as JSON, so a value holding bytes, a timestamp, a geopoint, a reference or a key inside one is shown and offered no Edit field or Edit property as a whole (`TestValuesTheFormCannotHoldOfferNoEdit`); in Datastore a value inside one is edited with Edit value (#905) and added or removed with Add value and Remove value (#911), and in Firestore likewise since #995 (the row "Firestore: values inside maps and arrays, and bytes"); subcollections, namespaces and child entities are the next row. Every delete is confirmed by typing the name back. The forms and actions are covered by these API tests and the unit tests `TestEditFormsRoundTripTheStoredType`, `TestTypedValuesAreReadAsTheirTypeNeverGuessed` and `TestDocumentAndEntityActionsAreOfferedWhereTheyApply`. |
| Firestore: values inside maps and arrays, and bytes | **Verified** | `TestConsoleFirestoreEditValuesInsideMapsAndArrays` (#995), in the emulators shard, through the console API, read back with the official `firestore` client. A map or array field's page has an **Elements** tab listing every value inside it, at any depth, as `meta.items[2]` or `meta.items[2]["odd name"]`, each with its own page; **Edit value** (string, number, boolean, null, timestamp, geopoint, reference or bytes, prefilled), **Add value** on a map (a new key) or an array (at an index, or appended), on the field's page and on each map or array inside it, and **Remove value**, confirmed by typing the value's name back. A document the client wrote, holding an array with a double and a map of a timestamp with microseconds, bytes, a geopoint, a reference in this project and one in another project, a boolean and a null: Edit value saved as prefilled on every value it is offered for leaves `DocumentRef.Get` equal to what the client wrote; the other project's reference, and a map or array, are offered no Edit value. Then a timestamp inside the array's map, the bytes and the geopoint are changed, a reference is inserted at index 1, a key added and the array's first value removed, and the client reads each new value as its type and every other value and field as written. Each change is read with `BatchGetDocuments` and written with one `Commit` masked to the changed value's field path as far as it runs through maps (an array is written whole: a field path cannot name an index), preconditioned on the document's update time; each action carries a digest of the field as drawn, and one drawn before another writer changed the field is refused with "changed since the page was loaded" and changes nothing. **Bytes** are shown and edited as base64 (standard encoding, padded, as the REST API's `bytesValue`): Add field `bytes` `AQID` is read back as the bytes 1, 2, 3, and its Edit field is prefilled `bytes` `AQID`. Unit: `TestFirestoreElementsAreListedAndAddressed`, `TestFirestoreEditValueSavedUnchangedWritesTheSameValue`, `TestFirestoreAddAndRemoveValueChangeOnlyThatValue`, `TestFirestoreValueWritesAreMaskedToWhatChanged`, `TestFirestoreValueActionsRefuseAChangedField`, `TestFirestoreBytesRoundTripAsBase64`; in headless Chrome `TestFirestoreEditAddRemoveAndBytesValuesThroughTheBrowser`. A Firestore vector value is not given an Elements tab. |
| Firestore: Edit field refuses a reference into another project or database | **Verified** | `TestConsoleFirestoreEditFieldRefusesAForeignReference` (#1050), in the emulators shard: a top-level field holding a reference to a document of another project, written with the official `firestore` client, is offered no **Edit field** on its page (#995), and a `PATCH /api/resources/firestore` posted by hand is refused 400 with the note the page shows, since the form writes a reference into this project's default database, which would change the document it names; the client reads the field back unchanged. A reference into this project's default database is still edited through the same route. Unit `TestFirestoreEditFieldRefusesAForeignReference` (another project, and another database of this one). Datastore refuses a key in another project or database the same way (#893). |
| Firestore subcollections, Datastore namespaces and child entities in the console | **Verified** | #854, in the emulators shard, read back through the official clients. **Firestore** (`TestConsoleFirestoreSubcollections`): a document's Collections tab lists its subcollections as `DocumentRef.Collections` (`ListCollectionIds`) does, each opening its own page by its path; **Start collection** on a document's page makes a subcollection with its first document, read back at `users/alice/orders/o1`; the subcollection's page names its parent document and lists its documents; Add document, Add field and Delete document work in it as at the top level; a nested document's breadcrumb leads back through each collection and document above it. A subcollection is not deleted with its document. A document that does not exist but holds subcollections is listed since #875 (next row). **Datastore** (`TestConsoleDatastoreNamespacesAndChildren`): Create entity with a namespace writes the entity in it and not in the default; a reserved namespace (`__…__`) is refused; the Datastore screen lists every namespace's kinds with a Namespace column, and a row in another namespace opens its kind there; a Namespaces page lists them and each one's page its kinds. **Create child entity** on an entity's page writes an entity whose parent is that one, in its namespace, with a name or an allocated ID; the parent's Children tab (a kindless ancestor query, bounded at 1,000 descendants) lists it by its key path and opens it; its page shows the key path and parent, and Add property and Delete entity act on it; a child of an entity that does not exist is refused with `no such entity`. A child is listed by its key path, with `/` and `%` in a name escaped (unit `TestDatastorePathsAddressNamespacesAndAncestors`); since #875 an entity's page is addressed by its encoded key (next row). In headless Chrome (`test/browser`, emulators shard): `TestFirestoreStartASubcollectionOnADocumentPage` and `TestDatastoreNamespaceAndChildEntityThroughTheBrowser`. |
| Firestore documents that do not exist, and Datastore entity addresses, in the console | **Verified** | #875, in the emulators shard, read back through the official clients. **Firestore** (`TestConsoleFirestoreListsMissingDocumentsWithSubcollections`): a collection's page is read with `ListDocuments` and `show_missing` — the client's `CollectionRef.DocumentRefs` — rather than a query, so a document that does not exist but has a subcollection is listed as `DocumentRefs` lists it, in italics with *no fields — has subcollections*, and paging continues with the API's page token (a page token can be issued for a page that ends the collection, so the next page can be empty). Its page says it does not exist and its Collections tab opens its subcollections; **Add field** on it creates it (`Create`, so one written meanwhile is `ALREADY_EXISTS`), which the client reads back; **Delete document** on it says there is nothing to delete. The documents that exist are then read in one `BatchGetDocuments` for their fields. The query builder still runs a query, which, as in Firestore, does not return a missing document. **Datastore** (`TestConsoleDatastoreOpensARootEntityNamedLikeAKeyPath`, unit `TestDatastoreEntityAddressIsUnambiguous`): an entity's page is addressed by its key encoded as Google's console encodes it — the URL-safe base64 of the key's protocol buffer, the client's `Key.Encode` — so a root entity named `Customer/alice/Order/x` in kind `Order` and the child that path names each open their own page, and Add property on each changes that entity only; so do a root named `id=7` and the numeric id 7. The page is headed by the key as the listing names it, and Delete entity asks for that back. A link in the older form (a name, `id=N` or a key path) still opens what it did. The precedence when a segment is both (#882, unit `TestDatastoreEncodedKeyPrecedence`): it is an encoded key only when it is the canonical encoding — what `Key.Encode` writes, or that with the page's own project named — of a complete key with the page's namespace and kind and the default database; otherwise it is the older form, so another project's, namespace's or kind's key, a non-canonical encoding and an incomplete key are names here. The only older link this changes is a root entity whose name is itself such an encoding, and its row opens it by its own encoded key. The listing named a root entity by its name, so that root and that child shared a Key cell; since #882 a **Parent** column on a kind's entities and the query builder's results — *none (root entity)*, or the parent's key path, as Google's console lists an entity's parent — tells the rows apart (`TestConsoleDatastoreRowsNameTheirParent`, which also opens the child by its key with this project named and reads another project's key as a name no entity has; unit `TestDatastoreEntityRowsTellARootFromTheChild`). Since #885 entities are listed in a **Name/ID** column rendered as Google's console renders it — `name=…` for a name, `id=…` for a numeric ID — so a root named `id=7` (`name=id=7`) and the numeric ID 7 (`id=7`), which both have no parent and read the same before, differ in the list, in the query builder's results and in their pages' headings and breadcrumbs; key paths (the Parent column, Key path, a child's heading) use the same rendering, `Customer/name=alice/Order/id=7`, and Delete entity asks for the heading back. Create entity's Key identifier reads that rendering too, so `name=id=7` makes the name `id=7`. An older `/datastore/Order/id=7` link still opens the numeric ID 7 (`TestConsoleDatastoreNameIDTellsANameFromAnID`, unit `TestDatastoreNameIDTellsANameFromAnID`; in headless Chrome, `TestDatastoreNameIDColumnTellsANameFromAnID`). The Firestore screen's Documents count, and a Collections tab's, count the same `ListDocuments` list as the collection's page, so a document that does not exist but has subcollections is counted, and the lists' notes say so (`TestConsoleFirestoreCountsMissingDocuments`, #882). In headless Chrome (`test/browser`, emulators shard): `TestFirestoreMissingDocumentIsListedInItalics`, `TestDatastoreRootEntityNamedLikeAKeyPathOpens`, `TestFirestoreCollectionCountIncludesMissingDocuments` and `TestDatastoreKindListShowsEachRowsParent`. |
| **Cloud Tasks attempt history on a task's page** | **Not supported** | A task's page shows its attempt and response counts and last response code, not a history of attempts. |
| Deploy a Cloud Run service from the console | **Verified** | Through the **Cloud Run v2 adapter**, not by applying a Knative manifest — applying directly would let the console accept a configuration the API refuses, which is the console inventing support. The deploy **waits for readiness**: a service reported created and never ready is the failure the console exists to make visible. Verified end to end, including invoking the deployed service through the ingress. Tests: `TestCloudRunEditFormIsPrefilledAndGivesFocusBack`, `TestCloudRunPredictorAnswersOnlinePredictionInTheBrowser`. |
| Delete a Cloud Run service from the console | **Verified** | Through the same adapter, waiting for the operation. Tests: `TestTheRunProviderReachesTheAdapterAtItsBoundPort`. |
| Kubernetes pods, services, jobs and events | **Verified** | Scoped, **read-only**, across namespaces, each row showing whether CloudBurrow owns it. Events are what turn "the pod is Pending" into a reason. Tests: `TestConsoleReadsKubectlArguments`, `TestPodStatusReportsWhatIsActuallyWrong`, `TestEventTimeFallsBackThroughEveryShape`. |
| Ownership shown per object | **Verified** | A developer can tell what CloudBurrow created from what they created: the `cloudburrow.dev/owned` label is the CloudBurrow column on pods, services and jobs (`cmd/cloudburrow/consoleproviders.go`, `ownedBy`). `TestOwnershipColumnOnPodsServicesAndJobs` (#1576): each of the three screens lists the column, and a row says `yes` only for `cloudburrow.dev/owned=true`, `no` for another value, other labels or none. |
| **GKE cluster metadata** | **Not supported** | This is a kind cluster. No node pools, autopilot or release channels are presented, because presenting them would be fabricating exactly what the issue forbids. |
| **Creating Kubernetes workloads from manifests** | **Not supported** | Read-only by design: a console that could apply arbitrary manifests would create workloads CloudBurrow does not track and cannot clean up. |
| Kubernetes Engine pages (#1857) | **Verified** | Google's menu over the instance's own kind cluster: Kubernetes clusters (its one cluster, Details, Nodes, Storage, Observability, Logs, Connect), Workloads with Kubernetes system objects hidden by default and **Deploy** (one Deployment from an image, `kubectl create deployment`, never into a system namespace), Secrets & ConfigMaps (keys only for a Secret), Gateways, Services & Ingress, Storage (claims and storage classes) and Object Browser. **No Kubernetes Engine API is served** (#1913): Create cluster, Edit, Upgrade and Delete are drawn and refused. Tests: `TestGKEWorkloadsHideSystemObjectsByDefault`, `TestGKEDeployRefusesBeforeKubectl`, `TestGKEClusterPage`, `TestGKESecretsShowKeysNotValues`; in headless Chrome, `TestKubernetesEnginePagesThroughTheBrowser`. |
| Logs Explorer, live | **Verified** | Real pod logs followed from the cluster, streamed over **Server-Sent Events** (#88). Verified in a real browser: 88 live rows, `live` state, pause control, severity filter. Tests: `TestStreamSendsBacklogThenLiveEntries`, `TestLogCollectorKubectlArguments`, `TestTheLogStreamStatesItsOwnHealth`. |
| Stream logs / Stop stream | **Verified** (`internal/console/assets/console.js`) | As Google's Logs Explorer (#1863): a query's results are drawn when it runs (the stream's backlog, ended by a `ready` event), and later entries only while **Stream logs** is on; with the stream stopped they are held, and Stream logs shows them rather than skipping them. `TestLogsExplorerStreamLogsAndStopStream` (#1576, #1863, headless Chromium): two entries written through the Logging API after the query ran are not drawn and the status reads `stream stopped — 2 new`; Stream logs draws both beside the earlier line, a later entry is drawn as it arrives, and after Stop stream one more is held until Stream logs. |
| Logs Explorer query editor | **Verified** (`internal/console/logquery.go`) | The query pane takes the Logging query language over the LogEntry fields the console's entries carry (`insertId`, `timestamp`, `severity`, `logName`, `resource.type`, `resource.labels.source`, `resource.labels.name`, `resource.labels.project_id`, `textPayload`, `operation.id`): comparisons `=` `!=` `:` `>` `>=` `<` `<=`, a bare value searching every field, `NOT` or `-`, implicit or explicit `AND`, `OR` binding tighter than `AND` as in the language, `--` comments, severity by level or number and timestamps as RFC 3339; parentheses, regular expressions and other fields are refused naming the term, on the query pane. The query applies to the results, the Timeline and the Log fields counts alike. `TestCompileQuery`; in headless Chromium `TestLoggingExplorerAsGoogleLaysItOut` (#1863). |
| Reconnect and resume | **Verified** | Every event carries an id; a reconnecting client sends `Last-Event-ID` and the **gap** is replayed rather than everything, which would make a reconnect look like a flood of new activity. Tests: `TestStreamResumesFromLastEventID`, `TestSinceResumesRatherThanReplaying`. |
| Filters: severity, source, resource, operation, text | **Verified** | Applied to both the backlog and the live stream. Tests: `TestFiltersNarrowTheView`, `TestStreamHonoursFilters`. |
| **Credential redaction** | **Verified** | On the way **in**, not on the way out: an entry stored with a token in it has already been written somewhere a later change might expose. Covers `ya29.` and `cbl_` tokens, `Authorization`, api-key/password/secret/token assignments, PEM private keys and JWTs. Operation failure causes are redacted too. Tests: `TestCredentialsAreRedactedBeforeStorage`, `TestOperationErrorsAreRedacted`. |
| Message truncation | **Verified** | 2 KiB, marked. An application logging a whole request body would otherwise push out everything that explains it. Tests: `TestLongMessagesAreTruncatedAndMarked`. |
| Bounded retention | **Verified** | 2000 entries in memory. Nothing is persisted: keeping logs would make CloudBurrow responsible for data it never promised to keep. Tests: `TestRecorderIsBounded`. |
| **System namespaces are not followed** | **By design** | Measured: the control plane, kourier and Knative's own components were **90% of the buffer**, pushing out the lines that explain a developer's failure. Only `default` and the managed namespace are followed; the Events screen and `kubectl logs` still reach the rest. |
| Cloud Tasks attempt history | **Verified** (`taskLogger.Attempt`, `cmd/cloudburrow/consolelogs.go`) | Each dispatch attempt is logged with its outcome. A queue that says "1 task" tells a developer nothing; the attempt says why it is still there. `TestConsoleTasksAttemptHistory` (#1576), with the official Cloud Tasks client: a task whose target answers 500, on a queue of two attempts, is two `WARNING` lines (`attempt 1 of … returned 500`, `attempt 2 …`), and one answered 200 an `INFO` line, under the queue and its project. The lines carried no project before #1576, so the queue's page and a project's Logs Explorer, which filter on it, showed none. |
| Activity: operations with states and causes | **Verified** | PENDING / SUCCEEDED / FAILED from the **backend's verdict**, never from the console's optimism. A failed operation links to its own logs. Tests: `TestOperationsRecordTheBackendsVerdict`, `TestAFailedActionRecordsItsCause`, `TestTheLogsScreenHonoursAnOperationScope`. |
| **Severity of container logs is inferred** | Partial | Container logs carry no structured severity, so it is a heuristic over the words applications conventionally use. Used for filtering, never to claim an application said something it did not. |
| **Billing, quota, SLA or cost metrics** | **Not supported** | Nothing of the kind is displayed. There is no billing here to report. |
| **Request-rate, latency and resource metrics** | **Partial** | **Cloud Tasks, Secret Manager, the Cloud Run v2 adapter, Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Logging, Resource Manager, Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub, Bigtable, Spanner, Firestore and Datastore**, the services CloudBurrow serves itself or fronts: every call is counted by service, method and canonical code, with a latency histogram, at `GET /metrics` on the loopback control port in the Prometheus text format (`TestCreateTaskCallsAreCounted`, which parses it with Prometheus's own parser). `/monitoring` charts request rate, error rate and p50/p95 latency per service. A service with no observer (Cloud SQL, Memorystore, BigQuery) is labelled not measured, never charted at zero. That set is derived from the services that registered a call observer, not kept by hand, so a measured service is never also reported unmeasured (`TestMetricsSchedulerAndLoggingAreMeasured`, #600). Cloud Run workloads' own requests need Knative's queue-proxy metrics, which are off (#181). Storage (#513): each request is counted and recorded in `/admin/events` by API method (`storage.objects.insert`, `xml.PUT`), with its bucket, object, status and duration, and never its query string or body, so no upload_id, token, signature or secret (`TestStorageEventsRecorded`, `TestStorageEventsRedactUploadIDs`, `TestMetricsStorageIsMeasured`). The server also keeps its last 1000 calls at `GET /_cloudburrow/events?after=N`, for the CLI to scrape from the in-cluster server (#514). Pub/Sub (#1266): the front before the emulator keeps its last 1000 calls, gRPC and REST, at `GET /_cloudburrow/calls?after=N`, with their method, the topic, subscription, snapshot or project the request names, the gRPC code or HTTP status, start, duration and `traceparent`, and never a payload; the CLI reads it through the tunnel every two seconds into `/metrics` (`GetTopic`, `JSON GET`), `/admin/events` and the console's request log, and with tracing on one span each. Every client is seen, the host's, a pod's and the storage server's notifications alike, since all reach the emulator through the front. `TestPubSubCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, through the official `cloud.google.com/go/pubsub/v2` client: `CreateTopic`, `Publish` and a `NOT_FOUND` `GetTopic` are counted in `/metrics` and recorded in `/admin/events`, `/api/requests` and `/api/metrics/requests` with their code, resource and duration, no payload, and Pub/Sub is no longer unmeasured. Unit `TestCallLogRecordsGRPCAndREST`, `TestCallLogRecordsStreamingPull`, `TestPubSubCallsAreMeasured` (spans continue the client's trace), `TestPubSubCallsAfterAFrontRestart`. Bigtable (#1267): its front keeps the same call log (`internal/calllog`), so every client's calls are seen, the ones the front refuses `UNIMPLEMENTED` itself among them, which name no resource since they are answered unread (`TestBigtableCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, unit `TestCallLogRecordsBigtableCalls`). Firestore and Datastore (#1267): the host tunnel's guard, which already reads each request's headers, tells the CLI each call's method, gRPC code (`grpc-status`) or HTTP status, duration, `traceparent` and the database or project its routing headers name (`google-cloud-resource-prefix`, `x-goog-request-params`); a pod's calls reached the Service directly and were not seen (`TestFirestoreCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, unit `TestGuardObservesEachRequest`). Spanner, Firestore and Datastore (#1288): a call front (`internal/callfront`, `cloudburrow-storage call-front`) now serves each one's Service port in its pod, the emulator on the pod's loopback behind it, and passes every request through unread in the protocol it came in (gRPC over h2c with its streams and trailers, REST over HTTP/1.1), keeping the same call log as the Pub/Sub and Bigtable fronts from the routing headers and the outcome; the host tunnel's guard no longer records, so no call is counted twice. Every client is seen: Spanner's, whose raw tunnel nothing read before, and a pod's. `TestSpannerCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, through the official `cloud.google.com/go/spanner` client from the host: `CreateDatabase`, `Commit` on its database and a failed `ExecuteStreamingSql` are in `/admin/events` with their code and duration and in `/metrics`, and Spanner is no longer unmeasured; `TestAPodsFirestoreCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`: a one-off pod's `Commit` and `BatchGetDocuments`, with the official Firestore client at `firestore.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local:8080`, are recorded with its project's database. The front adds about 0.1 ms to a unary call (median of 300 `GetTopic` calls to an in-memory gRPC server, 138 µs through it against 40 µs direct, `TestGRPCPassesThroughAndAddedLatency`); unit `TestRESTPassesThroughAndIsLogged`, `TestReadinessFollowsTheEmulator`, `TestCallFrontCallsAreMeasured`. `/monitoring` charts each one's request rate, error rate and latency, and each in-cluster emulator pod's container CPU and memory from the kubelet's per-pod readings (`TestFirestoreOnMonitoringChartsItsCallsAndContainer`, `TestSpannerOnMonitoringChartsItsCalls`). |
| **Traffic splitting** | **Verified** | A Cloud Run service's page shows where its traffic goes, with each tag and its URL, and **Manage traffic** sets splits, pinned revisions and tags through `UpdateService` (#1224, `TestCloudRunManageTrafficThroughTheBrowser`). |
| Pagination | **Verified** | Tables page, with rows per page and a range out of the filtered total (`TestTablesPaginate`). Cloud SQL, Firestore, Datastore and Bigtable listings continue past their first page with a cursor, and a cursor the provider did not issue is refused rather than read as the end (`TestEveryPagedListingRefusesACursorItDidNotIssue`). |
| **Bucket listing is not scoped by project** | **Inherited limitation** | The storage backend accepts the project parameter and returns every bucket. The screen **says so** rather than presenting the rows under a project heading. |
| Console walkthrough on a fresh stack | **Verified** | [console-verification.md](console-verification.md): the walkthrough is now `test/browser`, run in headless Chrome against the compat storage shard's instance in CI (#594): landmarks and the LOCAL badge, the theme switch, a bucket created through the form, the error card under an injected fault, a row opened by keyboard, and no request off loopback; since #700 also the four viewport widths, dialog focus and Escape, and the Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler, Subscriptions and Cloud Run edit screens, the KMS and Run tests against the run shard's instance. Focus indicators and colour contrast are no longer walkthrough claims: `TestOutlineSuppressionHasAFocusVisibleRule` and `TestTokensMeetContrast` assert them from the stylesheet. |
| Form validation actually runs in a browser | **Verified** | It did **not** before this walkthrough. An HTML `pattern` is compiled with the RegExp `v` flag, where a literal `-` in a character class must be escaped; an unescaped one makes the pattern invalid and the browser then **silently skips validation**. Every create form had shipped that way. A regression test now compiles each shipped pattern under the `v` rule, and `TestCreateBucketThroughTheForm` (`test/browser`) submits a name the bucket pattern rejects in headless Chrome and asserts nothing is sent before creating a valid bucket through the same form; with the `-` unescaped it fails (#594). The regression test covered only the first four products' forms, so the Cloud KMS key ring and key, Cloud Scheduler job and Secret Manager secret patterns shipped the same way; `TestKMSCreateKeyRingThroughTheForm` found the first in Chrome's error log, and the unit test now reads every product's create form (#700). |
| Subscription creation from the UI | **Verified** | From a topic's page; see the Pub/Sub actions row above (`TestConsolePubSubActions`). |
| Visual regression against reference fixtures | **Not possible today** | No reference screenshots exist, so there is nothing to diff against — a threshold measured against our own output would only prove the console still looks like itself. This is what keeps visual fidelity at `Partial`. |
| Model catalogue screen | **Verified** | Shows the real catalogue with publisher, access, modality, licence, runtime and a **per-model** reason it is unavailable — the reasons differ, and one blanket message would hide that. Tests: `TestRunnableReportsTheRuntimeGap`, `TestEveryCatalogueEntryIsFullyDescribed`, `TestModelGardenNoteMatchesTheCatalogue`. |
| Generation playground | **Verified** | Offered only when local AI is configured, and relayed to the same API path the SDK calls (`TestPlaygroundGeneratesThroughTheRealAPIPath`); see [Console playground](#console-playground). Embeddings have a screen of their own (`TestEmbeddingsScreenSendsBothMethods`, `TestConsoleEmbeddingsPlaygroundMatchesTheOfficialSDK`; [playground.md](playground.md) §7); custom prediction requests are the Online prediction page ([playground.md](playground.md) §8). |
| Gemma results labelled as Gemini | **Cannot occur** | The playground shows the model and its publisher, and says, where the output appears, that a community conversion's output is not a Gemini result (`TestPlaygroundReportsReadinessFromALiveProbe`). |

**Visual fidelity and API compatibility are separate claims with separate evidence**, and
neither implies the other. A screen that renders correctly proves nothing about the API
behind it, and a verified API proves nothing about the screen.

## Cross-cutting

| Concern | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Google-style error bodies and gRPC status codes | **Verified** | `internal/apierror`: one cause renders a consistent gRPC code and HTTP status, plus the JSON envelope a Google client parses. Used by Cloud Tasks, Secret Manager, Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Logging, Resource Manager, Cloud Storage and the Cloud Run v2 adapter. Tests: `TestCodeAndHTTPStatusAgree`, `TestWriteJSONCarriesStatus`, `TestWriteJSONCarriesDetails`. |
| Pagination with deterministic ordering | **Verified** | `internal/paging`: full-walk coverage proves no duplicates or gaps; invalid and cross-listing tokens are rejected. Used by the list methods of Cloud Tasks, Secret Manager, Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Logging, Resource Manager and the Cloud Run v2 adapter. Tests: `TestPagesCoverEveryItemExactlyOnce`, `TestInvalidTokensAreRejected`, `TestTokenFromAnotherListingIsRejected`. |
| Long-running operations | **Verified** | `internal/lro`: pending, succeeded and failed are all reachable and terminal states are final. Used by the Cloud Run v2 adapter's operations. Tests: `TestAllStatesAreReachable`, `TestTerminalStatesAreFinal`. |
| Project isolation | **Verified** | `TestPubSubProjectIsolation`; `internal/resource` makes it structural — identical IDs in different projects or locations produce different keys by construction. |
| REST and gRPC transport | **Verified** | `internal/transport`: unknown REST paths return a Google 404 envelope and unknown gRPC methods return `Unimplemented`; request sizes are bounded and unknown JSON fields rejected. Cloud Tasks, Secret Manager, Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler, Cloud Logging, Resource Manager and the Cloud Run v2 adapter are served on it. Tests: `TestUnknownMethodReturnsNotFound`, `TestRequestBodyIsBounded`, `TestDecodeJSONRejectsUnknownFields`, `TestUnknownMethodIsUnimplemented`. |
| Background workers registered after startup | **Verified** | A worker registered after `Start` used to sit in the list and never run, because `Start` snapshotted the list once. **Cloud Tasks dispatch was wired into `up` and never dispatched anything.** Found while building the Logs Explorer: a deliberately failing task showed `dispatches=0` after minutes. Now started immediately, sharing the coordinator's lifetime. Tests: `TestWorkerRegisteredAfterStartStillRuns`, `TestLateWorkerStopsWithTheCoordinator`. |
| Scheduling, retry and backoff over an injected clock | **Verified** | `internal/sched`: retry timing is proven by advancing virtual time, never by sleeping. Concurrent duplicate attempts are prevented, and shutdown drains in-flight work. Tests: `TestRetryUsesBackoffWithoutSleeping`, `TestNoConcurrentDuplicateAttempts`, `TestRunDrainsInFlightWork`. |
| Metadata storage, memory and durable modes | **Verified** | `internal/store`: both modes share one test body; durable state survives restart, a second instance is refused, a failed commit leaves state unchanged, and unsafe keys are rejected. Tests: `TestDurableSurvivesRestart`, `TestDurableRefusesSharedDirectory`, `TestDurableCommitFailureLeavesStateUnchanged`, `TestUnsafeKeysAreRefused`. |
| Resource-name parsing and traversal safety | **Verified** | `internal/resource` rejects `..`, encoded separators, NUL and path separators in IDs. Tests: `TestValidIDRejectsTraversal`. |
| Installation and release packaging | Partial | `docs/install.md`, `docs/status.md` and a release workflow that builds and checksums four platforms. v0.1.0 and v0.2.0 were published by it. The post-publish smoke install (#603), added after v0.1.0, ran on v0.2.0 and passed on all four platforms (release run 44326099460), as did the action's self-test against that release; v0.2.0's darwin binaries were signed and notarized in the same run (#605). |
| Reset / seed / event inspection | Partial | `internal/admin`, served on the loopback-only control port and refused on service ports. **Reset covers Cloud Tasks, Cloud Storage (buckets, objects and notification configurations), Pub/Sub, Secret Manager, Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler (jobs), Cloud Logging (entries, and since #1226 log-based metrics, sinks and exclusions) and Resource Manager's IAM policies (on projects, folders and the organization, #1368; the projects and folders themselves are kept, since the other services' state is scoped by them)**, and Cloud SQL for MySQL's databases when it is enabled, and, since #1541, #1542 and #1543, the Cloud SQL Admin API's created instances, backups, client certificates and operations (`sqladmin`), Backup and DR (`backupdr`) and Artifact Registry (`artifactregistry`), each also by project, which a project's purge uses (`TestAPurgedProjectsSQLBackupAndRegistryStartEmpty`), narrowable with `service=` and `project=`. Measured 2026-10-16 on an instance of the default services less Cloud Run, plus Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler and Cloud Logging: `POST /admin/reset` answered `{"reset":["tasks","storage","pubsub","scheduler","logging","kms","secretmanager","resourcemanager"]}`, and afterwards the official clients found the topic, the secret and the Scheduler job `NOT_FOUND`, no entry of the log written, and no binding of the project's IAM policy set through v1 `setIamPolicy`, while a project created through v1 was still there; an unknown `service=` is 400 naming these (MySQL's reset was not measured) (`TestAProjectResetClearsOnlyThatProject`). Storage buckets record their project (#510), so a project-scoped reset clears that project's buckets only (`TestAProjectResetIncludingStorage`). The storage server's reset clears its store directly: live, noncurrent and soft-deleted objects, soft-deleted buckets, upload sessions, rewrite tokens, notification configurations and undelivered events, multipart uploads, IAM policies and HMAC keys, with no API delete and so no soft delete or notification (`TestAStorageResetEmptiesEveryBucketOnBuiltin`, `TestAStorageProjectResetOnBuiltin`). A Pub/Sub reset deletes a project's subscriptions, snapshots, topics and, since #889, schemas (`TestPubSubResetDeletesSchemas`: a schema is `NOT_FOUND` after its project's reset, its ID can be created again, and another project's schema is kept; unit `TestPubSubResetDeletesSchemas`). Pub/Sub state in a project CloudBurrow has never seen survives a full reset. **Seed covers Cloud Tasks, Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub, Secret Manager and Cloud Scheduler** from one document validated whole before anything is created (`TestOneSeedDocumentIsReadBackByTheOfficialSDKs`, `TestAnInvalidSeedDocumentSeedsNothing`, `TestSchedulerSeedIsReadBackByTheOfficialClient`). Pub/Sub fields the emulator is not known to honour are refused by name. Pub/Sub **schemas** (Avro, and since #1446 Protocol Buffer) and a topic's **`schemaSettings`** are seeded since #890: `TestPubSubSeedSchemaAndBoundTopic` seeds a schema and a topic bound to it, both read back by the official clients, a conforming message is published and a non-conforming one refused `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, a repeat is a 409 and `ifNotExists` skips it, and, since #1446, a `PROTOCOL_BUFFER` schema is seeded through CloudBurrow's Pub/Sub front with a topic bound to it, read back by the official clients, a non-conforming message refused `INVALID_ARGUMENT`, while one whose definition the API refuses is a 400 before anything is seeded (unit `TestPubSubSeedCreatesSchemasAndBindsTopics`, `TestPubSubSeedValidatesSchemasFirst`, `TestPubSubSeedProtocolBufferSchema`). A subscription's **`expirationPolicy`, `messageRetentionDuration` and `retainAckedMessages`** are seeded since #899: `TestPubSubSeedExpirationAndRetention` seeds a 1-day ttl with a 1-hour retention and acknowledged messages kept, and a policy without a ttl, each read back by the official client; the 1-day one is gone 25 hours on by the front's clock and the other kept; a 12-hour ttl, and a 1-day ttl under the default 7-day retention, are refused 400 before anything is seeded, by the front's own check (unit `TestPubSubSeedSetsExpirationAndRetention`). Bucket labels, location and storage class are seeded and kept (`TestStorageSeedAcceptsLabels`, #503). **Events record every API call on the ports CloudBurrow serves itself** — Cloud Tasks (gRPC and JSON, #591), Secret Manager (gRPC and JSON), the Cloud Run v2 adapter (gRPC and JSON, #591), Cloud KMS, Cloud Scheduler and Cloud Logging (gRPC and JSON, #591), and Cloud Storage, whose calls the CLI scrapes from the in-cluster server (#513, #514) — with method, resource, project, canonical status code and duration, and never a payload or query string (`TestSecretManagerCallsAreRecordedWithoutTheirPayloads`). **Pub/Sub, Bigtable, Spanner, Firestore and Datastore are recorded too**, from the front in each emulator's pod, which every client's call passes through and which the CLI scrapes the same way (Pub/Sub #1266, Bigtable #1267, the others' call fronts #1288): measured 2026-10-16, the official Pub/Sub client's `CreateTopic` and `Publish` were in `/admin/events?service=pubsub` within the scrape's 2 s, with code, duration, project and topic (`TestFaultsPubSubIsRefusedForWhereItRuns`; `TestFirestoreCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, `TestBigtableCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`, `TestSpannerCallsReachMetricsAndTheRequestLog`; Datastore's front is scraped the same way, and no test reads its events). **BigQuery, Cloud SQL and Memorystore are not recorded**: no call observer is registered for them. |
| Go SDK compatibility harness | **Verified** (`test/compat/harness.go`) | `test/compat`. Refuses non-loopback endpoints and fails outright if cloud credentials are present in the environment. `TestHarnessGuards` (#1576) runs the harness in a child of the test binary: `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` or `GCLOUD_PROJECT` set fails `New`; a `*.googleapis.com` or `*.google.com` endpoint, a private address, a hostname and `0.0.0.0` fail `Endpoint` before any dial; `127.0.0.1` and `localhost` are served. It needs no instance, so it runs in every shard. |

| Workstation preflight (`cloudburrow doctor`) | **Verified** | `internal/doctor`: binaries, daemon reachability, memory, CPUs, disk and every port `up` would bind, each with a remedy. Only genuine blockers exit non-zero; an unmeasurable check reports `unknown`, never `ok`. On macOS, and on Linux when the daemon is in a VM (Docker Desktop for Linux), the disk figure is the host volume backing the VM disk, and says so. It names the container engine from `docker info` and warns on rootless and non-Desktop VM engines ([install.md](install.md#container-engines), #712). Windows is not built ([install.md](install.md#prerequisites)). Tests: `TestMissingBinaryBlocks`, `TestUnreportedResourcesAreUnknown`, `TestBusyPortBlocksAndSuggestsTheEscape`, `TestDoctorClassifiesTheEngineFromDockerInfo`. |

A stopped instance is covered by a unit test. Redaction is pattern-based (`console.Redact`) plus removal of pod env values; a credential an application logs in a form those patterns do not recognise is not caught, so read a bundle before sharing it. Tests: `TestDiagnoseBundleHoldsNoCredentials`, `TestDiagnoseStoppedInstance`, `TestWithoutEnvValues`. |
